info.title: Check Networks API
info.description:
The Check Networks API lets you run your services from your own systems:
qualify and order NBN and Opticomm data services, manage phone numbers,
SIP trunks and SMS, raise support tickets, receive webhooks, and read your
account and billing.


The reference is published at `https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs`. The
OpenAPI document behind it, for generating a client, is at
`https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs/openapi.json`.


Endpoints marked **Coming Soon** are published early so you can build
against them. Until they go live they answer `501 - Not Implemented`.

# Getting Started

1. **Create an API Client** in the Wholesale Portal, under Company
   Settings → Integrations → API Keys, and choose the scopes it may use.
   The Client Secret is shown once.
2. **Request an access token** from `POST /oauth/token` with
   `grant_type=client_credentials`, your `client_id` and `client_secret`,
   and the scopes you need as a space-separated `scope`
   (e.g. `scope=data:read tickets:read`).
3. **Call `GET /ping`** with the token to confirm it works and see the
   key, account and scopes it carries, the address we saw and which
   environment answered.
4. **Send the token on every request**:
   `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. Tokens last one hour; request a
   new one when it expires.

The API is for Check Networks customers. If you do not have access to the
Wholesale Portal, contact your Account Manager or our Sales Team.

**Build against the sandbox** (`https://api.checknetworks.dev/v2`): a
separate copy of the platform, with its own account, keys and test
addresses, where nothing reaches a carrier. Orders there move through the
carriers' own steps in minutes and fire your webhooks as production does.
Ask your Account Manager for one. In production every call runs against
your real account, and a carrier write places a real order. A few calls
that act on our live network answer `501` in the sandbox.

To test your retries, send `CN-Sandbox-Simulate: 429`, `502` or `503` on
any sandbox call: it answers that status in the usual error shape, with
`Retry-After: 60` on a 429 or 503, and runs nothing. Production ignores
the header.

# Scopes

Each endpoint lists the scope it needs. A token carries only the scopes
you asked for **and** your API Client is allowed; any others are dropped
without an error. With no `scope` at all, a token carries none and every
endpoint refuses it. The `scope` field of the token response is the
record of what a token carries, so check it first when you get a
`403 - Forbidden`.

Every data endpoint, under `/nbn`, `/opticomm` and `/data` alike, uses the
`data:*` scopes.

# Conventions

- Field names are `camelCase`.
- Money is a decimal string in Australian dollars (`"49.95"`), with a
  `currency` field alongside (always `AUD` today).
- A single object comes back in `result`, and a list in `results`.
- Every list of your own records takes `page` and `perPage` and returns
  `total`, `page` and `perPage` with `results`. `perPage` defaults to
  **50** and runs from 1 to **200**; a value outside that, or a `page`
  that is not a whole number of at least 1, is `422 - Unprocessable
  Entity` naming the field, never quietly changed.
- Lists take `sort` (a field the list names, `-` in front for
  descending), `q` (a case-insensitive search, at most 100 characters,
  over the fields the list names), `updatedSince`, `createdFrom` and
  `createdTo` (an ISO 8601 date or date-time; a date alone is that day in
  UTC, or in your zone when you send `CN-Time-Zone`). A filter such as `status` takes one or several values,
  comma-separated, in any case. An unknown sort field or filter value is
  `422`.
- Lists that grow while you read them (payments, tickets, SMS, webhook
  deliveries, call records) also return `nextCursor`, newest first: pass
  it back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page carries `perPage`,
  `nextCursor` and `results` only. A sorted list has no cursor.
- An end user is named by its number, as `endUser`, everywhere a
  response or a request names one; where a response shows its name too,
  that is `endUserName`.
- `expand` inlines a related record in full where a list or read names
  it, such as `expand=endUser` on your services, which adds
  `endUserDetail`.
- Every time is UTC unless you ask for your own zone: send
  `CN-Time-Zone` with an IANA zone name, such as `Australia/Perth`, and
  every time in a JSON response comes in that zone with its offset
  (`2026-11-22T09:30:00+08:00`), a date alone in a list filter is that day
  in that zone, and the response echoes the header. A name that is not a
  zone is `422` naming `CN-Time-Zone`. Downloads (CSV, NDJSON, PDF),
  webhook deliveries and the carrier-shaped `/nbn` and `/opticomm` bodies
  stay as they are. What you set comes back as you set it, whatever it
  looks like: `metadata`, `externalRef`, your references
  (`orderReference`, `customerReference`, `customerRef`,
  `salesReference`, `paymentReference`, `paidReference`) and your own
  `name`, `description`, `note` and `notes` text.
- A create answers `201 - Created` with the new resource. Every other
  success answers `200 - OK`.

**Carrier-shaped endpoints.** Some `/nbn` and `/opticomm` endpoints mirror
the carrier's own API, so an integration written for the carrier works here
unchanged. These return the carrier's own bodies and status codes, without
the `result` wrapper, and are not paginated: the `/nbn` service
qualifications (`single_site`, `fibre_uplift`, `enterprise_ethernet`),
`/nbn/address/search`, `/nbn/address/geocode`, `/nbn/address/{locId}`,
`/nbn/planning/{locId}`, the `/nbn/product_qualification` `service_types`
and `bandwidths`, the diagnostic test catalogue and Opticomm
`productOrders`. Our account identifiers are removed and links point at this
API. The `/nbn` ones also take Kinetix's query parameter names (`loc_id`,
`service_ref`, `customer_authority_date`, `location_ref`, `service_type`)
as well as ours. Lists of your own records under those paths, such as your
NBN inventory, are paginated as usual. Where we add to a carrier's shape,
the field or parameter says "Ours": the premises `address` and
`fibreBuildCategory` on an EE quote, and the search, filters, sort and
paging of `GET /nbn/quotes`.

# Errors

Errors use standard HTTP status codes. The body tells you more:

- **`code`** says what went wrong, such as `not_found`,
  `key_revoked` or `duplicate_order`. Your code should check this. The
  full list is on the `Error` schema.
- **`reason`** explains it in words, for a person to read. The wording
  can change.
- **`messageId`** is this request's id, the same as the `CN-Message-Id`
  header. Quote it to Support.
- **`docUrl`** links to the code's entry in the
  [error reference](https://help.checknetworks.tools/api/errors/),
  which says what to do about it.
- **`fields`** appears when the request failed validation, and names
  each input that was wrong.
- **`carrierCode`** appears when nbn or Opticomm refused the request,
  and holds their own error code.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `400` | The body could not be parsed, or a required header is missing. On the carrier-shaped `/nbn` and `/opticomm` endpoints, also a bad input, as the carrier answers. |
| `401` | The access token is missing, expired or invalid, or its key is past its end date (`key_expired`). |
| `403` | Refused: `code` says why, such as `missing_scope`, `key_revoked`, `ip_not_allowed` or `account_suspended`. |
| `404` | Not found. We give the same answer for something on another account. |
| `405` | The path exists, but not for this method. |
| `409` | The resource isn't in a state that allows this right now. |
| `422` | An input was wrong (`validation_failed`, with `fields` naming it), or the request was refused on its merits. `reason` says why. |
| `429` | Too many requests. See Rate Limits. |
| `501` | The endpoint is Coming Soon, or isn't offered in the sandbox. Only the operations that list it can answer it. |
| `5xx` | A problem on our side, or with the carrier. Try again shortly. |

Every error, an unknown path included, comes back as this JSON body,
whatever your `Accept` header says.

# Idempotency

A write (`POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`) can carry an
`Idempotency-Key` header so that retrying it never does the work twice,
for example after a timeout where you never saw the response. Use a new
unique value, such as a UUID, for each operation:

`Idempotency-Key: 1f8e6b1a-9c4d-4a2e-8b3a-2f6d0c9e7a51`

The key is required wherever a repeated request could do real harm, in
three groups.

**Calls that reach a carrier**, where a repeat could place a second real
order: placing, answering, changing or cancelling an order
(`/data/orders`, `/nbn/orders/...`, `/opticomm/productOrders`),
submitting a bundle (`POST /bundles/{id}/submit`), ordering a number
(`POST /numbers`), reserving, changing or cancelling a technician
appointment, the carrier service tests and health reports (and
`POST /data/services/{ref}/sessions/refresh`,
`POST /data/services/{ref}/diagnostics` and
`POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check`), and Opticomm's
`static_ip` GET. These share a limit of **30 per minute per account**,
on top of the general rate limit. A replay of a stored answer does not
count against it. A batch qualification (`POST /data/sq/batches`) asks
the carrier once for each row, so it needs the key too, but is not on
that limit.

**Calls that bill or send**, where a repeat could charge you twice or
send twice: creating a trunk (`POST /trunks`), ordering a fax plan
(`POST /fax/plans`), sending a fax (`POST /fax/documents`), requesting
an NBN quote (`POST /nbn/quotes`), sending an SMS (`POST /sms`),
ordering colocation (`POST /colocation/orders`), and rotating a webhook
secret (`PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}` with `rotateSecret: true`).

**Writes on our side that must not run twice**: recording an end user's
usage (`POST /end-users/{endUser}/usage` and `POST /usage/batch`), which
would bill them twice; importing end users (`POST /end-users/imports`),
which would import the file twice; rotating your own API key
(`POST /account/api-keys/self/rotate`), which would rotate it twice;
a bulk change to numbers (`POST /numbers/bulk`), which could release
them twice; and hanging up a call (`POST /voice/calls/{callId}/hangup`),
which could hang up a second one.

Each of these operations lists the header as required (the webhook
secret rotation says so in its description, as it needs the key only
with `rotateSecret`). Without a key they all answer `400` with the same
body.

Every other write (users, tickets, webhooks, a single number, RADIUS,
provisioning and the rest) accepts the key and honours it the same way,
but runs without one.

How a key behaves:

| You send | You get |
|---|---|
| A new key | The request runs, and its response is stored. |
| The same key and the same request | The stored response, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Nothing runs again. |
| The same key with a different request | `422` `idempotency_key_reused`. |
| The same key while its first request is still running | `409` `idempotency_in_progress`, with `Retry-After`. Retry then. |
| A key longer than 255 characters | `400`. |

A `5xx` is stored like any other response, so retrying with the same key
returns the same `5xx` rather than running the write again. A request that
timed out may still have **succeeded**, so we keep the key spent rather
than risk a duplicate. Once you know the operation did not happen, send it
under a **new** key. If a key keeps answering `409` long after the first
call, contact Support: we never release a key on our own, because we
can't tell a slow request from one that stopped.

Keys belong to your API Client and are kept for 30 days. A write sent
without the header, where it is optional, is not deduplicated.

# Rate Limits

Each API Client may make **120 requests per minute** across the whole API,
and your account **600 per minute** across all its API Clients together,
so adding clients does not add capacity. Over either, requests answer
`429 - Too Many Requests` until the minute passes. If you need more,
contact Support: we can raise your account's figure.

Three groups of calls have a lower limit of their own, per account, on
top of those. Each of these operations names its limit in its
description, as `Limit: ... (carrier write)`, `(webhook send)` or
`(domain verify)`:

| Calls | Limit |
|---|---|
| Carrier-reaching writes (listed under Idempotency) | 30 per minute. A replay of a stored answer does not count. |
| Webhook test, redeliver and replay-dead, and sending an event again (`POST /events/{eventId}/deliveries`) | 10 per minute, shared |
| Verifying an end-user portal domain | 5 per minute |

`POST /end-users/lookup` allows 20 per minute for each API key, and says
so as `Limit: 20 per minute for the key.`

`POST /oauth/token` has its own limit: **30 per minute for each
`client_id` from one address**, so systems behind one NAT do not share
it, and 120 per minute from one address whatever the `client_id`.

Every response carries the limit that will stop you first, whichever of
these it is:

| Header | What it says |
|---|---|
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | The calls that limit allows in its minute. |
| `X-RateLimit-Remaining` | The calls you have left in it. |
| `X-RateLimit-Reset` | When it starts again, as a Unix time. |
| `Retry-After` | On a `429` only: the seconds to wait before retrying. |

A `429` always means a rate: wait and retry. A cap on what you hold, such
as the 5 open install reservations, answers `409` instead, because
waiting does not change it.

# Versioning

The current version is **v2**, at `/v2`
(`https://api.checknetworks.tools/v2/account`). Every path also answers
without the prefix (`https://api.checknetworks.tools/account`), and those
unprefixed paths mean v2 **for good**: a later version gets its own
prefix (`/v3`) and never changes what an unprefixed call does.

Every response, errors included, names the version that answered:

```
API-Version: 2
```

There is no `/v1` here. v1 is the legacy API at `api.checknetworks.au`, a
separate platform being retired over time. If you still use it, talk to us
about moving across.

**What counts as a breaking change.** Within v2 we only add: a new
endpoint, a new optional parameter, a new field in a response, a new
webhook event type or a new error `code`. Build your client to ignore
fields it does not know. Removing or renaming a field, endpoint or parameter, changing a
field's type or meaning, making an optional input required, or refusing
a request we used to accept is breaking, and happens only through the
deprecation below or a new version.

# Deprecation

Nothing is deprecated today. When an endpoint or field is to be retired,
you get **at least 12 months' notice** before it stops working. We tell
you three ways: an entry here and in the changelog saying what to use
instead, an email to your account, and three headers on every response
from the call:

```
Deprecation: @1798761599
Sunset: Fri, 31 Dec 2027 23:59:59 GMT
Link: <https://api.checknetworks.tools/docs#section/Deprecation>; rel="deprecation"; type="text/html"
```

The `Sunset` is at least 12 months after the `Deprecation`. The one
exception is a security fix: when keeping a call would put accounts at
risk, we may retire it sooner, and say why.

| Header | What it says |
|---|---|
| `Deprecation` | When it was deprecated: `@` and a Unix timestamp ([RFC 9745](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9745.html)). |
| `Sunset` | The last moment it answers, as an HTTP date ([RFC 8594](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8594.html)). After that it answers `404`. |
| `Link` | This section, which says what to use instead. |

It keeps working normally until the `Sunset`. We suggest logging a warning
whenever a response carries `Deprecation`, and raising an alert when the
`Sunset` falls inside your next release cycle. Deprecated operations are
also marked `deprecated: true` in this document, so a generated client can
flag them.

# Support

Every response carries a **`CN-Message-Id`** header, our identifier for that
request. Quote it when you contact Support about a call and we can find the
exact request. It is on error responses too. We issue it; you can't set it.
For your own handle on a write, use `Idempotency-Key`.

For help with the API, email support@checknetworks.com.au. Our team can
answer questions and help you understand the API, but can't write your
integration for you.

tags.name: Webhook Delivery
tags.description:
Each event is sent as a `POST` with a JSON body to every endpoint subscribed to it. Reply with any `2xx` status to acknowledge it, including for an event type you do not handle.

### What a delivery carries

The body has `eventId`, `eventType`, `occurredAt`, `sequence` and `data`, plus `apiVersion` (`2`), `livemode` (`false` from the sandbox), `test` (`true` for a delivery you asked for with `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test`), `accountId` (your `clientNumber`) and `resourceUrl`, where to read the current state of what the event is about. Events can arrive late or out of order, so re-read `resourceUrl` before acting on one.

The headers carry `X-CN-Event-Id` (the `eventId`) and `X-CN-Delivery-Attempt` (`1` for the first try, counting up on each retry; a redelivery or replay is a new delivery and starts again at `1`).

Within a version, events only gain fields and new event types are only added. Ignore a field or type you do not know, and answer `2xx` to it.

### Checking a delivery came from us

Every delivery carries an `X-CN-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<signature>` header. Check it: it is the only proof a delivery came from us. The secret itself is never sent, so nothing that logs your request headers can forge a delivery.

The signature is an HMAC-SHA256, in hex, of `<t>.<raw body>`, keyed with your endpoint secret. Work it out over the exact bytes you received, compare it in constant time, and reject a delivery whose `t` is more than 5 minutes old.

For a while after you rotate the secret, the header carries a second `v1` signed with the old one. Accept the delivery if any `v1` matches.

### Retries

What happens next depends on the status your endpoint answers:

- A `5xx`, a timeout or a connection failure is tried again: 6 attempts in all over about 8.6 hours, waiting 1 minute, 5 minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 6 hours between them. After the last one it is marked `dead`.
- A `429` is tried again when your `Retry-After` header says, or on the same ladder if you send none.
- A `408` is treated like a timeout and tried again on the ladder.
- Any other `4xx` is **not retried**: it is marked `dead` at once, since the endpoint would answer the same way in six hours.
- A `3xx` is **not followed and not retried**: it is marked `dead` at once. Register the final URL instead.

Every `dead` delivery counts toward the auto-disable below, whichever way it got there, with one exception: for 30 days after an event type is added, a `4xx` to it does not count, so an endpoint that does not know the new type yet is not turned off for it. The endpoint's `lastError` still shows the rejection.

After 20 dead deliveries in a row, the endpoint is turned off (`disabledReason: auto`), your technical contact is emailed, and your other endpoints that take it get a `webhook.endpointDisabled` event. Events are still recorded while it is off. Turn it back on with `PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}`, then replay the dead deliveries to catch up.

### Duplicates and order

An event can arrive more than once, and out of order. Use `eventId` to ignore repeats, and `occurredAt` to put them in order: a redelivered or replayed event keeps both. `sequence` counts up for each endpoint as each delivery is queued, and a redelivery or a replay is a new delivery with a new `sequence`, so do not order by it. Better still, treat an event as a hint and re-read `resourceUrl`.

### Answering

We wait 10 seconds for an answer, 5 of them to connect, and each endpoint has at most two deliveries in flight at once. Answer `2xx` quickly and do the work afterwards.

tags.description: Check Networks' legacy Opticomm provisioning lane — not an upstream mirror.

tags.description: Mirrors Opticomm NPIS `npis-appointments` v1.0.1.

tags.name: Numbers
tags.description:
Your phone numbers: their labels, inbound routing and emergency address.

An Australian number (geographic, mobile, 1300, 1800 or 13) needs an emergency address before it can be routed or used as an outbound caller ID. Link one with `emergencyAddressId`.

To get a number: find the area for a customer's address (`GET /numbers/areas`), see what is available and its price (`GET /numbers/available`), hold one if you like (`POST /numbers/holds`), order it (`POST /numbers`) and read the order until it is set up (`GET /numbers/orders/{id}`). `POST /numbers/lookup` says who holds and who serves a number before you port it.

tags.name: Emergency Addresses
tags.description: The addresses emergency services are given for your numbers: in Australia, the number's IPND listing. Create one, then link numbers to it with `PATCH /numbers/{number}`.

tags.name: SIP Trunks
tags.description:
Create and manage SIP trunks, their IP allow-lists and registrations.

**Webhooks:** a trunk going live, suspended, resumed or disconnected sends [Services events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Services), and a trunk going down or coming back sends [Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice).

tags.name: Fax Plans
tags.description:
Fax is an ordered service. A number sends and receives faxes only while
it is on a fax plan, and faxes go to Australian landlines, mobiles and
13, 1300 and 1800 numbers only. Order a plan, put numbers on it, and
authorise the email addresses that may send as them. A number on a plan
has no separate monthly number charge.

tags.name: Fax
tags.description:
Send a fax, read your fax history, and set your fax domain and cover
page. History is metadata only, never the documents.

**Webhooks:** faxes received, sent or failed send [Fax events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Fax).

tags.name: Voice
tags.description:
Call records (with filters, a summary and one call), the scheduled call
record exports, live calls and hanging one up (never an emergency call).

**Webhooks:** completed calls send [Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice).

tags.name: SMS
tags.description: Send SMS and read your message history.

tags.name: Number Ports
tags.description: Bring numbers to us from another carrier, and follow numbers leaving you. Request a port-in, confirm a mobile port's verification code, withdraw a port before its cutover is booked, and read every port with who it is waiting on and what has happened so far, as the portal's Number Ports pages do. A port is named by its `reference`; another account's answers 404. Each step also arrives as `order.statusChanged`.

tags.name: IP Transit Blackholes
tags.description:
Drop the traffic to one address of an IP transit service, to stop an
attack on it reaching you. The traffic is dropped at our border.

**Webhooks:** a blackhole placed, released or expired sends [IP Transit events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Transit).

tags.name: End-User Price Book
tags.description:
What you charge your end users for each product: your default markup,
a price per product, a voice product's default call plan, and the
products you sell that are not priced yet. Only for an account that
bills its end users: every route answers 404 otherwise.

Prices are ex-GST, as in the portal. GST is added on the end user's
invoice under your own tax settings.

tags.name: End-User Call Plans
tags.description:
Your own call plans for your end users: build one, edit its draft
destinations, and publish a version.

tags.name: End-User Service Billing
tags.description:
How one service you have given an end user bills: a call plan pinned to
it, its own price and setup fee in place of your price book, or not
billed at all.

tags.name: End-User Charges
tags.description:
Your own recurring and one-off charges on an end user's bill, such as a
support fee or a site visit.

tags.name: End-User Usage
tags.description:
Usage you rated yourself (managed-service hours, seats, a third-party
feed), billed on your end users' invoices.

tags.name: End-User Spend
tags.description: An end user's spend this month against its monthly limit.

tags.name: End-User Billing Settings
tags.description:
The settings on every invoice to your end users, the payment reminder
schedule, the wording of the notices they receive, and whether your
payment gateways are working.

tags.name: End User Billing
tags.description:
The invoices, credit notes and payments on your end users' accounts:
approve, release and resend invoices, credit them, record payments,
pause reminders, issue a final invoice, and read an end user's ledger.
Only for an account that bills its end users: every route answers 404
otherwise.

tags.name: End User Cases
tags.description:
Your end users' billing disputes and financial hardship cases: review,
credit and close a dispute, and assess and close a hardship case, as
the portal does.

tags.name: Xero
tags.description:
Your own Xero organisation, which your end-user invoices, credit notes
and payments are sent to. Connecting and disconnecting stay in the
portal, as they need a browser sign-in to Xero.

tags.name: End Users
tags.description:
Your end users: your own customers, who use your services. Create and
change them, give them services, suspend, archive and restore them, and
manage their notes, representatives and logins to the end-user portal,
as the End Users pages of the portal do.

An end user is named by its number (`endUser`), never an internal id.
An end user of another account answers 404, as an unknown number does.

While a family violence safety record withholds an end user's contact
details, every end-user call masks them, as the portal does.

tags.name: Residential Lines
tags.description:
Home phone lines: one SIP line each on our residential domain, billed as
a PAYG or Ultimate plan. Order one, move it between plans, and set its
call forwarding, Do Not Disturb, anonymous call reject, call waiting and
voicemail, as the portal's Residential Lines pages do.

A line is named by its SIP username, the `trunk` that call records and
numbers carry with `trunkType: residentialLine`. A SIP trunk's username
answers 404 here, and a line's answers 404 under `/trunks`.

**Webhooks:** a new voicemail sends [Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice).

tags.name: Caller ID Authorisations
tags.description:
Ask for the right to present a number your account does not hold as a
trunk's caller ID, with proof that you may use it. We review each
request; until one is approved, setting that number as a trunk's
`defaultCallerId` answers `422` with the code
`caller_id_authorisation_required`.

**Webhooks:** each decision sends `callerId.statusChanged` ([Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice)).

tags.name: Call Recordings
tags.description:
The recordings of calls on trunks with call recording on: list them and
fetch one with a download link that lasts 5 minutes. Recordings are call
content, so they need their own scope, `recordings:read`, never
`voice:read`; every fetch is audited. Recordings are deleted by our
staff only.

**Webhooks:** a stored recording sends `voice.recording.ready` ([Voice events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Voice)).

tags.name: Delegated Steps
tags.description:
Hand one step of an order to a person with no login: the mobile
number's holder who must confirm a port, or someone at the site who
must pick an install time. Name them and their email; they get a
one-use link to a page on your end-user portal, in your branding.
They pass a code sent to that email, then see only that step and do
it once. Resend the link (a new link; the old one stops working) or
cancel it. A link works for 7 days.

The page opens on your end-user portal, so an account without one
answers `403` with the code `no_end_user_portal_access`.

**Webhooks:** a step done sends `delegation.used` ([Delegated Steps events](#tag/Webhook-Events-Delegated-Steps)).

post.description:
Exchange your API Client credentials for an access token. This is the
first call any integration makes, and the only one that does not carry a
bearer token.

Tokens are valid for **one hour**. Request a new one when it expires;
there is no refresh token in the client-credentials flow.

### Scopes

Ask for the scopes the token needs, space-separated. A token requested
**without** a `scope` carries none, and every endpoint refuses it with
`403`. Request only the set each job needs, especially for anything
running unattended.

Scopes outside your Client's allowance are dropped silently rather than
rejected, so **the `scope` field in the response is the source of truth
for what your token can actually do**. Check it first when an endpoint
answers `403`; that error names the scope it wanted.

### IP allowlist

A Client with an IP allowlist gets tokens only from an address on it. A
request from anywhere else answers `403` with code `ip_not_allowed`
before the secret is checked, so the answer says nothing about whether
the secret was right.

### Rotation and end dates

While a rotation's overlap runs (`POST /account/api-keys/self/rotate`,
or Roll Secret in the portal), both the old and the new secret are
accepted here. A token the old secret mints then ends when the overlap
does, even if that is under an hour away.

A key may have an end date. Past it, the right secret answers `401` with
code `key_expired`; a wrong one answers as any wrong secret does. Tokens
the key minted before then stop at the end date too.

### Rate limit

**30 requests per minute for each `client_id` from one address**, so
systems behind one NAT or cloud address each keep their own, and 120 per
minute from one address whatever the `client_id`. A token lasts an hour,
so a client that reuses its token never comes near either.

### OAuth apps

A registered OAuth app uses this endpoint for the authorization code
grant (`grant_type=authorization_code`, with the `code` from the consent
screen, the same `redirect_uri` and the PKCE `code_verifier`) and to
refresh (`grant_type=refresh_token`). Both send the app's `client_id`
and `client_secret`. The response then carries a `refresh_token` as well.
Each refresh replaces the refresh token and the access token: use the
new ones. A refresh token lasts 30 days from the refresh that issued it,
so an app that refreshes at least every 30 days stays connected, and one
left idle longer must be connected again. Sending a replaced refresh
token again is treated as a stolen copy: it is refused, the app is
disconnected from the account with all its tokens, and the account's
Owners are emailed. A refresh after the account revoked the app, or
after we disabled it, is refused.
An app's client cannot use `client_credentials`. See
[OAuth Apps](https://help.checknetworks.tools/api/oauth-apps/).

grant_type.description: `client_credentials` for an API key. An OAuth app sends `authorization_code` to exchange a code, and `refresh_token` to refresh.

code.description: The code from the consent screen (`authorization_code` only). Lasts ten minutes and works once.

redirect_uri.description: The redirect URI the code was issued for (`authorization_code` only).

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose S256 hash the authorise step was sent (`authorization_code` only).

refresh_token.description: The app's latest refresh token (`refresh_token` only).

client_id.description: Your API Client's id, from the Wholesale Portal. Required, here or as the user of an `Authorization: Basic` header (RFC 6749 2.3.1) with `client_secret` as its password.

client_secret.description: Your API Client's secret. Shown once when the client is created; if it is lost, rotate it in the portal. A production secret starts `cn_live_` and a sandbox one `cn_test_`. Required, here or in an `Authorization: Basic` header.

scope.description: Space-separated; ask for the scopes the token needs. A token requested without a scope carries none, and every endpoint refuses it with `403`.

access_token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` on every other endpoint.

refresh_token.description: OAuth apps only. Send it with `grant_type=refresh_token` for the next access token. It is replaced on every use and lasts 30 days from that use.

scope.description: Space-separated, and authoritative — the scopes this token actually carries, which may be narrower than requested.

400.description: The request is malformed or the grant is unsupported. Uses the OAuth2 error shape (RFC 6749), not this API's standard error envelope.

401.description: The client id or secret is wrong: the OAuth2 error shape (RFC 6749), not this API's standard error envelope. The right secret of a key past its end date answers in this API's standard error envelope instead, with code `key_expired`.

403.description: The request came from an address outside the Client's IP allowlist (`ip_not_allowed`). No token is issued. This API's standard error envelope.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none; any valid token

The first call to make with a new token, and the one to make when a call
is refused: it answers `200` when the token and your API Client are good,
and shows which key and account answered, the scopes the token actually
carries, the address we saw you call from, whether the key's IP allowlist
is on, which environment answered and when the token expires. A token
from a revoked client, or one issued before its secret was rotated, is
refused here exactly as on every other endpoint, with `403`.

keyId.description: Your API Client's id, the `client_id` you requested the token with.

name.description: Your API Client's name, as set in the Wholesale Portal.

scopes.description: The scopes this token carries. A scope you requested but your Client is not allowed is not listed.

accountId.description: The account the key belongs to, its `clientNumber` on `GET /account`.

ip.description: The address we saw this call come from, as your IP allowlist is checked against.

ipAllowlistActive.description: Whether the key has an IP allowlist. When it does, only addresses on it may call or request tokens.

environment.description: Which environment answered. A production secret starts `cn_live_` and a sandbox one `cn_test_`.

tokenExpiresAt.description: When this token expires. Request a new one before then.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none; any valid token

Finds Australian addresses in our copy of G-NAF, best match first. It
does not call a carrier, so it is quick enough for type-ahead.

Send some of the address in `q`, the structured parameters, or both. The
unit, level and road parameters are matched with `q`. `localityName`,
`stateTerritoryCode` and `postcode` must match exactly. You need `q` or
at least one of the unit, level or road parameters.

Each match carries its G-NAF id. Use it for the carrier step: for NBN,
`GET /nbn/address/search?gnaf=`; for Opticomm, the match's `opticommOpcId`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text, such as `12 smith st parramatta`.

parameters.name: roadTypeCode
parameters.description: The road type, in full or abbreviated, such as `STREET` or `ST`.

parameters.name: stateTerritoryCode
parameters.description: Any letter case.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many matches to return.

200.description: The matches, best first. An empty list when nothing matches.

get.description:
Names the service and its version, and points at this reference, its
OpenAPI document and the token endpoint. It needs no token, so it is a
simple first check that you are talking to the right host.

documentation.description: Path to this reference on the same host.

openapi.description: Path to this reference's OpenAPI document, bundled as JSON.

get.description:
Answers `200` while the API can serve requests, and `500` when it cannot.
It needs no token and does no work on your account, so it suits a load
balancer or uptime monitor. The body is a small HTML page, not JSON:
check the status code only.

500.description: The API is not able to serve requests.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Use this endpoint to get your Account Details. This can be handy for ensuring that we have the most up-to-date
details on file for you.

The credit position (`amountOwed`, `creditLimit`, `creditUsed`, `availableCredit`, `creditUsedPercent`,
and the deprecated `credit` or `balance`) and `billingEmail` in `billingDetails` are billing data: they
are returned only when your token also holds **billing:read**. Without it, `billingDetails` carries only
`accountType` and `currency`. The fields mean the same as on
[Get Account Balance](#tag/Account/operation/get_account_balance).

200.description: A JSON Object containing your Account Details.

clientNumber.description: Your Client Number with Check Networks

status.description: Your Current Account Status

isSuspended.description: True while the account is suspended. A suspended account can read but not change anything: every write answers 403 with code `account_suspended` until it is restored.

entityDetails.description: Your Legal Entity Details as recorded with Check Networks

businessName.description: Your Entity's Trading Name. Null when you trade under your legal name — it is not repeated here.

abn.description: Your Entity's ABN - Only valid for AU Clients. Null when we hold none.

acn.description: Your Entity's ACN - Only valid for AU Clients. Null when we hold none.

entityType.description: Your Entity Type. Null when it is not recorded.

address.description: Your Primary Address as we have it on file.

address1.description: Address Line 1 for your Primary Address on File. Null when we hold no such line.

address2.description: Address Line 2 for your Primary Address on File. Null when we hold no such line.

address3.description: Address Line 3 for your Primary Address on File. Null when we hold no such line.

locality.description: The City/Suburb for your Primary Address on File. Null when we hold no such line.

state.description: The State for your Primary Address on File. Null when we hold no such line.

postcode.description: The Postcode/Zip Code for your Primary Address on File. Null when we hold no such line.

country.description: The Country for your Primary Address on File. Null when we hold no such line.

billingAddress.description: The address printed on our invoices to you, in the same shape as `address`; every line is null when none is on file. Change it with [Update Billing Details](#tag/Account/operation/patch_account_billing_details). Returned only when your token also holds **billing:read**.

billingContact.description: Your billing contact, where invoices and billing notices go. Each field is null when not on file. Returned only when your token also holds **billing:read**.

features.description: What your account may order and use, so a call that would be refused can be predicted from this read. An order is accepted only when its product is `true` in `orderable`, `orderChecksOutstanding` is empty and `ordersHeld` is false; otherwise every order answers 403.

orderable.description: Each product and whether your account may order it. A product that is `false` answers 403 on its order routes; your account manager can enable it. A voice product that needs numbers is `false` while numbers are.

orderChecksOutstanding.description: The onboarding checks still to pass before your account may order anything. Empty when every check has passed or been waived.

ordersHeld.description: True while every order is refused because your account is on hold: a hold on your outbound calls, or a suspension. `ordersHeldReason` says which. Contact support to have a hold reviewed.

ordersHeldReason.description: Why orders are held, or null when they are not: `spend_velocity` (call spend rose unusually fast), `calling_pattern` (an unusual calling pattern), `credit` (over your credit limit) or `suspended`.

numberTypes.description: The number types a number order takes (the `type` of [Search Available Numbers](#tag/Numbers/operation/search_available_numbers)). Empty while numbers are not orderable.

retailBilling.description: Your account bills its own end users. While false, the `retail:*` and `retail-cases:*` routes answer 404.

endUserPortal.description: Your end users have their own portal on your hostname.

fax.description: Fax to email and email to fax are offered.

invoiceDisputes.description: Invoice disputes are offered, on our invoices and on your end users' bills.

callerScopes.description: The scopes of the token making this call, and the scopes its API key may ask for. A call needing a scope outside `token` answers 403 with code `missing_scope`; one in `key` but not `token` needs a new token that asks for it.

createdAt.description: When the account was opened, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the account's details last changed, in UTC.

oneOf.title: Prepaid Account
oneOf.description: Billing Details when you have a Prepaid Account. The credit position fields need billing:read.

credit.description: Your current Credit Balance, as a decimal string in dollars: `amountOwed` with its sign turned round. Deprecated: read `amountOwed`. Needs billing:read.

currency.description: The currency of the amounts on your account.

billingEmail.description: The Billing Email linked to your account, where you receive notifications. Null when no billing contact has an address on file. Needs billing:read.

oneOf.title: Postpaid Account
oneOf.description: Billing Details when you have a Postpaid Account. The credit position fields need billing:read.

balance.description: Your Current Account Balance, as a decimal string in dollars, the same as `amountOwed`. Deprecated: read `amountOwed`. Needs billing:read.

currency.description: The currency of the amounts on your account.

billingEmail.description: The Billing Email linked to your account, where you receive notifications. Null when no billing contact has an address on file. Needs billing:read.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

The figures on your portal dashboard in one call: how many trunks, numbers
and data services you have, how many orders, tickets and outages are open,
and what needs you. The numbers are the dashboard's own, from the same reads.

`needsAttention` lists only the groups with something in them. Each entry's
`link` opens the list filtered to exactly the rows it counted, or is null
where there is no API list for that group yet.

`endUser` (an end user's number) narrows every figure to that end user's
services, orders and tickets. Outages affect the whole network, so
`openOutages` is your account's either way, and the port groups, which
belong to your account, are left out.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: An end user's number. An unknown number answers 422.

200.description: Your account's headline figures and what needs you.

trunks.description: SIP trunks (residential lines are not counted).

byNetworkAndState.description: Your data services counted by network and state, largest first.

openOrders.description: Every kind of order still in progress.

openOutages.description: Outages affecting your services that are not yet resolved.

link.description: The list filtered to this group, e.g. `/data/orders?needsAttention=orderAwaitingAction`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Every notice we sent you and your end users (invoices, statements, payment
notices, overdue and suspension warnings, outage notices and others), newest
first, with what happened to it. Use it to answer "I never got that notice":
whether it went, to which address, and whether it bounced.

Paged like every list: by `page`, or by cursor, passing the `nextCursor` of
one page as `cursor` for the next. A notice sent while you walk by cursor
never shifts a row into or out of a page. `nextCursor` is null on the last
page.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Sent at or after this date or time.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Sent at or before this date or time. A date alone covers the whole day.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only notices of this kind, e.g. `overdue_notice`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only notices sent to this end user (its number). An unknown number answers 422.

total.description: Notices matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page or a page that was not full.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

One notice we sent you or one of your end users, by its `id`.

>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Use this endpoint to see where your account stands with us: what you owe,
your credit limit, how much of it is used and how much is left. Your
system can warn before your services are held.

200.description:
A JSON Object containing your Current Account Balance.

`amountOwed` means the same on every account: positive when you owe us,
negative when you hold credit with us. It is your **billed** position:
invoices raised, less payments and credits applied, with GST.

`creditUsed`, `availableCredit` and `creditUsedPercent` are your credit
line as credit control reads it and the portal dashboard shows it:
without GST, and credit used is what you owe plus usage not yet
invoiced. Your services are held when `availableCredit` reaches zero.

`unbilledUsage` is metered usage that has **not** been invoiced yet,
with GST: calls and messages since your last invoice. It is not in
`amountOwed`. On a postpaid account, `amountOwed` plus `unbilledUsage`
is roughly what you would owe if invoiced now. On a prepaid account,
your credit left after that usage is `unbilledUsage` taken from the
credit you hold (`-amountOwed`). Read `availableCredit` for the figure
that holds your services.

`unbilledUsage` is null when the figure is not available. Treat null as
**unknown**, never as zero.

balance.description: The amount owed on a postpaid account, and the credit left on a prepaid one, so its meaning turns with the account type. Deprecated: read `amountOwed` and `accountType`.

currency.description: The currency of every amount here.

unbilledUsage.description: Metered usage not yet invoiced, with GST, as a decimal string in dollars. Always present; null when the figure is unavailable. Not in `amountOwed`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns a paginated list of invoices for your account, ordered newest first.
`q` searches the invoice number.

### Bulk export

For bulk pulls, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson` to stream the **entire**
matching result set (the `status`, `number` and date filters still apply) as a single download
instead of paged JSON. `page`/`perPage` are ignored in this mode. `csv`
returns `text/csv` (header row + one row per invoice); `ndjson` returns
`application/x-ndjson` (one JSON object per line, each identical to a
`results[]` item). An unrecognised `format` returns `422`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Bulk export format. Omit for paged JSON; `csv` or `ndjson` streams the full matching result set as a download.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Filter by the status an invoice shows; several, comma-separated (`status=unpaid,overdue`). Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`. `unpaid` is issued and not yet overdue; `overdue` is issued and due before today on the invoice's own calendar, so no invoice is both.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Invoices whose number contains this text, as the portal's invoice search matches it. Not case-sensitive.

parameters.name: issuedFrom
parameters.description: Invoices issued on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. The day is the one the invoice shows: on the time zone it was cut in (its `timezone`). Send `CN-Time-Zone` to read the date on your own zone instead. Leave either end open. A date that is not a real date, or a start after the end, answers `422`.

parameters.name: issuedTo
parameters.description: Invoices issued on or before this date, the whole day included.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing invoices.

total.description: Total number of invoices matching the query.

perPage.description: The number of invoices per page.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. The full matching result set as CSV — a header row followed by one row per invoice, with the same columns as a `results[]` item.
Present only when `format=ndjson`. The full matching result set as newline-delimited JSON — one object per line, each identical to a `results[]` item.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's `id`, as `GET /account/invoices` gives it.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Returns the full details for a single invoice: what is paid, owed and held
by a dispute, any card or direct debit charge still processing, and every
line with the service, end user and period it bills and the rows behind it.

`amountDue` is what is still owed now. While `amountInFlight` is more than
zero, a charge is already under way: do not pay the same invoice again in
the portal.

### One invoice as CSV

Set `format=csv` for the invoice's lines as `text/csv`, one row per line,
with the invoice number and dates on each row and the money as
`unitPriceExGst`, `unitPriceGst`, `unitPriceIncGst`, `totalExGst`,
`totalGst` and `totalIncGst`. The lines' `totalIncGst` add up to the
invoice's. No cell begins with a character a spreadsheet reads as a
formula. Any other `format` returns `422`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit for JSON; `csv` for the lines as a spreadsheet.

200.description: A JSON object containing the invoice and its line items.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:create

Use this endpoint to invite a new user to your Wholesale Account, as the
Users page in the portal does.

This is to be used to add new staff, not client accounts.

The person is sent the normal invitation email. No login exists until
they accept it, and they choose their own password when they do; a
`password` in the request is refused with `422`. The invitation lasts 72
hours. Inviting the same address again replaces the open invitation.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required, so a retry returns the first answer
instead of sending a second email that cancels the link in the first.
Without it the request answers `400`. A client written before 2.0.0-pre.3,
when the key was optional here, must now send it.

`role` is `admin`, `billing` or `readonly`. An API key assigns what an
Administrator may, so it can never make an Owner. The account's Owners
are emailed when a user is invited, naming the API key that made the
request. Only an Owner can grant a key the `account:create` scope.

firstName.description: The first name of the person to invite.

lastName.description: The last name of the person to invite.

email.description: The email address to invite. It must not already be in use by another login.

role.description: What the user may do: `admin` manages the account, its services, users and API keys; `billing` sees invoices and payments; `readonly` reads only.

202.description: The invitation is sent. The user exists once the invitation is accepted, and then appears in `GET /account/users` with its own `id`.

result.description: The pending invitation. It has no user id yet: the login, with its own `id` in `GET /account/users`, exists once the invitation is accepted.

inviteId.description: The invitation's id, as `/account/invites/{inviteId}` takes it to resend or revoke it.

status.description: Always `pending`; the invitation has not been accepted.

expiresAt.description: When the invitation lapses unaccepted, in UTC.

>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

The active Layer 2 link destinations available to your account — the outer
VLANs (S-Tags) on your customer interconnects, where a Layer 2 service can
be handed off to you.

**Not offered at the moment.** Layer 2 handoff is unavailable, so there is
nothing to order on, and every request answers 422 with the reason, as
`POST /data/provisioning/layer2` does.

Each destination's carrier is derived from its Point of Interconnect. A
single-tag interconnect carries all your services on one outer VLAN across
every POI and carrier; it is presented under the reserved POI code `0NAT`
and serves both NBN and Opticomm.

get.description:
Your orders, whichever network delivers them, newest first, one summary
row each: enough to act on without reading every order. The whole order
is its `href` (GET /data/orders/{orderId}).

An order still open is always listed, however long since it last
changed: a parked or waiting order stays until it ends. Without `status`
or `updatedSince`, completed and failed orders are listed for the
**last 30 days**; ask for `status=completed`, `status=failed` or an
`updatedSince` to reach older ones. Paged like every list.

Filter by `status` (`open` is every order not finished), `type`,
`network`, `locationId`, `orderReference`, `endUser`, `tag` and
`updatedSince`. Each narrows the list, and a value outside its set or
its form is `422`, never a quietly wider list. `q` searches the order
id, PND, your order reference and the location id.

`expand=service` gives each order's service in full, in the same call.

An order appears here once it has been placed with the carrier, or once
it is waiting for your appointment or port, under its PND.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only orders of these types, one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter, so the `type` an order shows (`Connect`) is accepted as it is; any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only orders in these statuses, one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter, so the `status` an order shows (`InProgress`) is accepted as it is; `open` is every order not finished, the same as `inProgress`. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: network
parameters.description: Only orders on these networks, one or several, comma-separated. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Only orders for this premises: an NBN location id (`LOC` and 12 digits) or an Opticomm one (`OPC` and 12 digits), any case. Any other form is `422`.

parameters.name: orderReference
parameters.description: Only the orders placed with this reference of yours, matched whole, ignoring case.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `service` inlines each order's service in full. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: Only the orders in this needs-attention group, exactly as `GET /account/summary` counted them. With it, `endUser` (an end user's number) narrows the group to that end user.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the orders for this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is `422`, not an empty list. With `needsAttention`, it narrows the group to that end user.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

One Connect order for every data network and technology, so you need
no separate endpoint for each. The location picks the order: an NBN
Location ID is placed as an NFAS (Fibre), NWAS (Fixed Wireless), NHAS
(HFC) or NCAS (FTTB, FTTN, FTTC) order by its access technology, and an
Opticomm Property ID as an Opticomm order. Satellite and Enterprise
Ethernet are not ordered here.

Take the plan and the resource from the Service Qualification
(GET /data/sq/{locId}). The order takes what the portal's order page
takes: the end user it is for, its add-ons, the restoration SLA, a
static IPv4 address and IPv6, a new or additional install, and a
transfer. NTD delivery and the other options of each network are on the
network's own order endpoints under /nbn and /opticomm.

The order is checked against the Service Qualification before it is sent,
so a mistake comes back as a 422 with the reason and no order is placed.
A 201 means the order is accepted; follow it with GET
/data/orders/{orderId}.

An order that needs something only you can give is accepted and waits on
our side, with nothing sent to the carrier: a technician appointment
(`order.appointmentRequired`), or, where every port on the NTD is in use,
a new NTD or a port to take over (`order.ntdFull`). Its `actionRequired`
says what it needs and its ID is a PND. Answer it with PATCH
/data/orders/{orderId}; one still waiting after 7 days is cancelled.

With `bundleId`, the order is checked the same way and joins that bundle
as a draft instead (see `POST /bundles`): nothing is sent until the
bundle is submitted. The answer is the bundle item, with the bundle at
`Location`; a retry with the same `orderReference` is that item again.

200.description: An order with this `orderReference` was already placed; this is that order. With `bundleId`, it is already in the bundle; this is the item.

201.description: The order was placed with the carrier, or accepted to wait for your appointment or port (see `actionRequired`). With `bundleId`, it joined the bundle; this is the item.

get.description:
One order, whichever network delivers it, in the same shape for all of
them. Use the ID from the order list.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order ID, as returned by the order list.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `service` inlines the order's service in full. Any other value is `422`.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Give an order waiting for you (`actionRequired` on the order, and the
`order.appointmentRequired` or `order.ntdFull` webhook) what it needs,
and it is placed with the carrier, keeping its ID.

- **Appointment required:** `appointmentId`, an appointment you reserved
  from the order's timeslots.
- **NTD full:** `appointmentId` for a technician to install another NTD,
  or `resourceId` for the port to take over, with `serviceId` (the AVC on
  NBN) and `customerAuthorityDate`.

The order is checked again as when it was placed, so a mistake comes back
as a 422 with the reason and the order keeps waiting.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order ID (the PND in `order.appointmentRequired` or `order.ntdFull`).

200.description: The order was placed with the carrier.

The technician timeslots for an order waiting for an appointment, read

starts at the order's `preferredAppointmentDate`, or today, and looks two

Reserve a slot on the network's appointment endpoint (/nbn/appointments
or /opticomm/appointments), then attach it with PATCH
/data/orders/{orderId}. `timeslots` is that network's own timeslot
document, as its appointment search returns it.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The order ID (the PND in `order.appointmentRequired` or `order.ntdFull`).
