post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

The simplified provisioning step for an IPoE (DHCP) Layer 3 service.
Call it after placing the order; only the IP preferences are needed —
everything else is derived from the order.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself — if no provisioning step is called for an
order, the service never goes live.

Accepted until the service is built; after that, changes require a
Modify Order.

orderNumber.description: The Order to provision (your PND reference or the carrier order number).

staticIp.description: Hold the service's IPv4 address stable (and allow custom reverse DNS).

ipv6.description: Provision IPv6 (a /64 on-link prefix and a delegated prefix). The delegated prefix size is plan-dependent: /56 by default, or /48 where your plan or service is configured for it. Set false for an IPv4-only service.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

The simplified provisioning step for a Layer 2 pass-through service.
Call it after placing the order.

**Not offered at the moment.** Layer 2 handoff is unavailable, and every
request answers 422 with the reason. Provision the order as IPoE instead.

The optional `handoff` names one of your Layer 2 link destinations
(as listed by `GET /data/layer2/destinations`). Omit it and the
service is handed off on your default destination for the order's
POI.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself — if no provisioning step is called for an
order, the service never goes live.

Accepted until the service is built; after that, changes require a
Modify Order.

orderNumber.description: The Order to provision (your PND reference or the carrier order number).

handoff.description: (Optional) The interconnect to hand this service off on, from GET /data/layer2/destinations. Omit to use your default destination for the order's POI. The outer VLAN (S-Tag) on it is chosen for you from that POI.

cTag.description:
(Optional) The inner VLAN (C-Tag) to use for this service, if
you want to pick it — it only has to be unused on the handoff
it lands on.

Left out, the next free one is allocated and returned to you.

Either way the tags are allocated as soon as you ask, not when
the carrier finishes — so you can configure your own side
immediately, and no other order can take the tag meanwhile.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

The simplified provisioning step for a PPPoE Layer 3 service. Call it
after placing the order; only the IP preferences are needed —
everything else is derived from the order.

PPPoE logins live in your account's realm, so they cannot collide with
another provider's: the username is always `<name>@<your realm>`. Your
realm is set up by Check Networks — PPPoE cannot be provisioned until it
is in place.

Choose a login by supplying `username` and `password`, or leave both out
and one is created with the service: the carrier's service ID as the name
and a generated password. Either way the username appears on the Radius
User Status endpoint and the password via the dedicated RADIUS Password
endpoint.

A chosen login can only be set once the carrier has accepted the order
and the service exists — the login belongs to the service.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself — if no provisioning step is called for an
order, the service never goes live.

Accepted until the service is built; after that, changes require a
Modify Order.

orderNumber.description: The Order to provision (your PND reference or the carrier order number).

staticIp.description: Hold the service's IPv4 address stable (and allow custom reverse DNS).

ipv6.description: Provision IPv6 (a /64 on-link prefix and a delegated prefix). The delegated prefix size is plan-dependent: /56 by default, or /48 where your plan or service is configured for it. Set false for an IPv4-only service.

username.description:
(Optional) The name part of the PPPoE login — your realm is
appended, so do not include "@".

Letters, numbers, full stops, underscores and hyphens. Must
not already be in use.

password.description: (Optional) The PPPoE password. Generated for you when not supplied. 8 to 64 printable ASCII characters, with no single quote (') or backslash (\): the same rule as a later change with PATCH /data/radius/{ref}/password.

get.description:
Every data service you hold, on NBN and Opticomm, in one shape, the most
recently requested first, as the portal's Services list opens. Filter by
`network`, `status`, `endUser`, `technology`, `customerReference`, `plan`,
`locationId` or `tag`, as the portal's filters of the same names do; each
narrows the list, and a value outside its set or its form is `422`, never
a quietly wider list. `q` searches what the portal's search does: the
product and service references, the RADIUS username, the carrier order,
the address, your customer reference, and the end user's reference and
name.

`expand=endUser` gives each service's end user in full, as
`endUserDetail`, in the same call.

A connect still in flight is an order (GET /data/orders), not a service:
it appears here once it is live.

A service with no request date, such as one taken over from another
provider, comes after every service that has one, in the default order
and in any `sort`. So does any service with no value in the field a
`sort` names, such as `activatedAt` before it is live.

parameters.name: network
parameters.description: Only services on these networks, one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter; any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only services in these statuses, one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter, so the `status` a service shows (`Live`) is accepted as it is; any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `endUser` adds each service's end user in full, as `endUserDetail`. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: technology
parameters.description: Only services on these access technologies, one or several, comma-separated, as the `technology` a service shows. Case does not matter; any other value is `422`. A technology none of your services has gives an empty list.

parameters.name: customerReference
parameters.description: Only the services with this customer reference, matched whole, ignoring case.

parameters.name: plan
parameters.description: Only the services on this plan, by its SKU (the `plan.sku` a service shows), ignoring case.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Only the services at this premises: an NBN location id (`LOC` and 12 digits) or an Opticomm one (`OPC` and 12 digits). Any other form is `422`.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: Only the services in this needs-attention group, exactly as `GET /account/summary` counted them. With it, `endUser` (an end user's number) narrows the group to that end user.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description:
Only the services of this end user, by its public number (the
`endUser` each service returns). A number that is not one
of your end users is a 422, not an empty list. With `needsAttention`,
it narrows the group to that end user.

total.description: Every service that matches, across all pages.

get.description:
One of your data services, with its speed and whether it is connected
right now.

Address it by its product reference (`id`: an NBN PRI or an Opticomm
product) or its service reference (`serviceId`, such as an AVC).

The live status is read from our RADIUS, or live from the network for a
service on Kinetix's. Where a network can only tell us by running a test,
`session.status` is `OnRequest`: ask GET /data/radius/{ref}/online with
the service's `radiusUser`.

`contract` is the term end and what disconnecting today would charge,
or null with no term.

Where a carrier reference was reused, the live service answers, then a
suspended one, then the newest.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: expand
parameters.description: `endUser` adds the service's end user in full, as `endUserDetail`. Any other value is `422`.

patch.description:
Your own `externalRef` and `metadata` on the service, so you can find it
by your customer or job id without keeping a map of ours. Send either or
both; one you leave out is kept, and null clears it. Everything else on
a data service is the carrier's, and changes through an order.

An `externalRef` another of your data services holds is `422`. Find the
service again with `GET /data/services?externalRef=`.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

200.description: The service as it now is.

get.description:
One month of a service's data usage, in total and by day: the figures
your portal's usage card shows. Usage is reported, never charged.

`period` is a month, `YYYY-MM`, in the last 13 months; the current month
by default, counted up to now (`complete` is false).

Months and days follow your bill's calendar, not UTC: your account's
time zone, the zone your invoices are cut in (set in the Wholesale
Portal's Company Settings; Brisbane until you set another). A sample at 2 am on the 1st there counts
in the new month and on that day. Send `CN-Time-Zone` to have the months
and days on your own zone instead. `from` and `to` carry the zone's
offset.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The month, `YYYY-MM`. Defaults to the current month.

get.summary: List a Service's Outages, Planned Work and Degradations
get.description:
Is anything wrong at this service right now? Three lists in one answer,
as your portal's service page shows them, on either network:

- `outages`: the entries on our outage register that cover the service's
  address, in the shape `GET /outages` gives. Each carries what you need
  to report it: `cause`, `premisesAffected`, and `serviceCounts`, the
  count of services hit by each affected type (null for a type we have
  no count of).
- `plannedWork`: the maintenance windows you were sent notice of whose
  area takes in the service's address. A window that names no area
  covers every service it was noticed for.
- `degradations`: the Potential Service Degradations at the service's
  point of interconnect: slower at peak, not down.

Open ones only by default. `include=resolved` adds those resolved in the
last 30 days. A service with nothing on it answers three empty lists.
Every time is UTC.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `resolved` adds what was resolved in the last 30 days. Any other value is `422`.

serviceCounts.description: The count of services the outage hit, by each of its `affectedServiceTypes`; null for a type we have no count of.

post.summary: Run a Line Test on a Service
post.description:
Run one of the tests `GET /data/services/{ref}/diagnostics/types` lists
for the service, on either network, with that test's `inputs`. An input
you leave out takes its `default`; one the test does not take, or a
missing required one, is `422`. The service must be live.

It answers `202` with the test's id; the result comes from the carrier
later and is on `GET /data/diagnostics/{id}`. While the same test is
still running on the service, a second is `409` and `error.runningTestId`
names the one running: nothing is asked of the carrier. When the
carrier's test system is down, `503` with `Retry-After`.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

202.description: The test was asked for.

409.description: The same test is already running on the service.

runningTestId.description: The id of the test still running.

get.description:
The service's line tests, newest first, paged, on either network.
Session History is not listed: it is `GET /data/services/{ref}/sessions`.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only tests in these statuses, comma-separated. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only these tests, by code, comma-separated, in any case. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: result
parameters.description: Only tests with these results, comma-separated. Any other value is `422`.

get.summary: List the Line Tests a Service Allows
get.description:
The line tests the carrier allows for this service now, on either
network, as your portal's Run Test offers them. Each says when to use it
(`description`), when to raise a fault ticket rather than test again
(`escalateIf`), and the inputs it takes. Asking reads the carrier live.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

escalateIf.description: When to raise a fault ticket instead of running the test again.

name.description: The key to send it under in `inputs`.

default.description: Used when you leave the input out.

options.description: For an `enum` input, the values it takes.

get.description:
One of your line tests, on either network, with the inputs it was run
with, the carrier's reason for a rejected or cancelled test, and the
carrier's detailed results once it has them.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The test's id.

reason.description: Why the carrier rejected or cancelled it.

details.description: The carrier's detailed results, once it has them; their fields depend on the test.

get.description:
What disconnecting the service would charge if it ceased on `ceaseOn`,
from the same early termination quotes the cease bills, so you can tell
your customer before you place it. One line per open subscription: the
plan and each add-on; a line past its term charges nothing.

`ceaseOn` is a Sydney calendar day from today to 90 days ahead, the
window a disconnect accepts; today by default. Reading the quote books
nothing and changes nothing.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: ceaseOn
parameters.description: The day the service would cease, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Any other value, or a day outside the window, is `422`.

chargeExGst.description: The whole early termination charge, in dollars ex GST.

chargeWaived.description: True when we waived the early termination charge, so the charge is `0.00` though the service is still in its term.

chargeable.description: Whether ceasing on `ceaseOn` charges anything for this line.

chargeWaived.description: True when we waived this line's charge, so it is `0.00` though still in term.

get.description:
The service's connection sessions, newest first, as the portal's service
page shows them: when each started and ended, how long it ran, its
address, the bytes each way, the router's MAC and why it ended. Use it
when your customer says the internet keeps dropping.

- A service on our own network: our RADIUS accounting (`source`
  `checknetworks`).
- An Opticomm Layer 3 service: the sessions in the last Session History
  test Opticomm answered (`source` `opticomm`), and `retrievedAt` says
  when. Reading never starts a test at Opticomm; POST
  /data/services/{ref}/sessions/refresh asks for a new one.
- A service whose sessions another carrier holds, such as a Kinetix
  Layer 3 service, has no history here: `422`. Its current session is on
  GET /data/radius/{ref}/session.

`from` and `to` keep the sessions that ran in that window: started by
`to`, and still open or ended at or after `from`. One request covers at
most 90 days: `to` defaults to now and `from` to 90 days before `to`,
and a longer window is `422` naming `from`. Read an older or longer
period 90 days at a time.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 date or date-time; a date alone is the start of that day (UTC). At most 90 days before `to`; 90 days before `to` when absent. Not ISO 8601, or further back, is `422`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: An ISO 8601 date or date-time; a date alone includes that day. Now when absent. Before `from` is `422`.

retrievedAt.description: For `opticomm`: when Opticomm answered the test these sessions are from; null when none has been answered yet. Null for `checknetworks`, which is current.

endedAt.description: Null while the session is open.

mac.description: The router's MAC address, as the network reported it.

terminateCause.description: Why the session ended, as RADIUS reports it (`Lost-Carrier`, `User-Request`…). Null while open.

post.description:
Ask Opticomm for the service's sessions now, by starting a Session
History test there. For an Opticomm Layer 3 service only: our own
network's sessions are always current. This is a request to the
carrier, so it needs `data:update`.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

`202` says the test is asked for. The sessions are on GET
/data/services/{ref}/sessions once Opticomm answers, usually within a
minute or two, and the `data.radius.sessionRetrieved` webhook says when.
`409` says a test is already on its way: `error.testId` names it, and
its answer will be on the read.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

202.description: The test is asked for.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before reading the sessions.

409.description: A Session History test is already on its way.

testId.description: The running test's reference. Absent when it was started elsewhere and is not yet known here.

post.description:
Ask the carrier for a new health report on the service, as the portal's
service page does. The same call for an NBN and an Opticomm service.
This is a request to the carrier, so it needs `data:update`.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

`202` says the report is asked for, and gives its `id`. It is on GET
/data/health/{id} once the carrier answers, and the
`serviceHealth.reportReady` webhook says when. `409` says a report is
already on its way: `error.reportId` names it. A report still not
answered after an hour no longer blocks a new one.

The carrier's own calls (POST /nbn/service_health/service/{serviceRef},
POST /opticomm/serviceHealth) still work, with the carrier's bodies.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC, OAC).

202.description: The report is asked for.

serviceId.description: The service's product reference.

409.description: A health report is already on its way.

reportId.description: The id of the report on its way. Absent when it was asked for elsewhere and is not yet known here.

get.description:
The service's health reports, newest first, pending ones included, in
the same shape on every network. `overall` is the result the portal's
service page shows.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC, OAC).

get.summary: Get a Service's Latest Health Report
get.description:
The service's newest health report, pending or complete, in the same
shape on every network. `404` when none has been asked for.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC, OAC).

get.description:
One health report on one of your data services, by the `id` that
POST /data/services/{ref}/health answered or the
`serviceHealth.reportReady` webhook named.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The report's id.

put.description:
Your own tags on the service, so you can map it to your sites, cost
centres or customers. The list you send replaces the whole list; `[]`
clears it. Filter the services and orders lists by tag with `tag`.

Each tag is trimmed, at most 255 characters, and matched ignoring case:
`Brisbane Office` and `brisbane office` are one tag, kept as first
written. A service carries at most 20. Anything else is `422`.

Tags you send with POST /data/orders are carried to the service the
order builds.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product) or service reference (AVC).

tags.description: The tags the service now carries.

get.description:
Every tag on your data services and orders, each once (matched ignoring
case, in the spelling first written), with how many services and orders
carry it, by name. Use a name with `tag` on GET /data/services or GET
/data/orders.

services.description: How many of your services carry it.

orders.description: How many of your orders carry it.

get.description:
Your active RADIUS users, one row each with its realm, by username, paged
like every list. `realm` narrows the list to one realm. `q` searches the
username and the user reference.

Services that authenticate on their access circuit rather than a login
have no realm: their `realm` is `null`.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: Only users in this realm, such as `example.net.au`. Case does not matter. A value that is not a realm name is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

realm.description: Everything after the `@` in the username; null for a user with no realm.

post.description:
Request a PPPoE realm for your account.

Every PPPoE username is namespaced into your realm, so a realm is
globally unique and effectively permanent once services are built on it.
Requests are reviewed by Check Networks rather than granted immediately,
and PPPoE services cannot be provisioned until yours is in place.

Use a domain you control.

realm.description: The realm you would like, as a domain name.

202.description:
Requested, not granted. The realm is held as `Pending` until Check Networks confirms it, and PPPoE ordering stays closed until then — which is why this is `202` rather than `201`.

The `Location` header names where to poll: *Retrieve a Realm* reports the request as `Pending`, `Approved` or `Rejected` (with the reason), and `Active` once the realm is on your account. The `data.realm.approved` and `data.realm.rejected` webhooks carry the decision if you subscribe to them, so polling is optional.

Location.description: Where to poll for the decision.

get.description:
Your realm and how many active users sit in it, or a realm you have
requested and where that request stands.

This is the resource the `Location` header of *Request a Realm* points
at. Poll it until `status` leaves `Pending`: `Active` means the realm is
yours and PPPoE can be ordered; `Rejected` carries the reason. A realm
neither yours nor requested by you is a `404`.

parameters.name: realm
parameters.description: The realm.

status.description: `Active` once the realm is on your account. A request you have made is `Pending` until Check Networks decides it, then `Approved` (and `Active` from the next read) or `Rejected`.

reason.description: Why a request was rejected; null otherwise.

users.description: Active RADIUS users in this realm (0 for a request).

get.description:
One RADIUS user.

Address it by its own reference, or by any reference you already hold for
the service — the order id, the product reference, or the service id.
There is one user per service, so all of them resolve to the same record.

The record carries the RADIUS detail: whether the address is static, the
CGNAT public address and ports, IPv6, the last authentication and recent
dropouts. For a service on Kinetix's RADIUS it is read live from Kinetix
on each request; if Kinetix does not answer, `detailAvailable` is false
and the detail fields are null.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

get.summary: Check Whether a User Is Online
get.description:
Whether the user has a session up right now. A session that has stopped
reporting accounting is treated as gone.

For a service on Kinetix's RADIUS, the answer is read live from Kinetix
on each request. If Kinetix does not answer, the request fails with a 502
rather than guess.

For a service on Opticomm's RADIUS, the answer comes from the latest
session check at Opticomm, with `retrievedAt` saying when Opticomm
reported it. Reading never asks Opticomm: a check is asked for with
`POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check`. While one is on its way this
answers `202`: call again after `Retry-After`, or subscribe to
`data.radius.sessionRetrieved`. With no check held it answers
`status: NotChecked`, and neither online nor offline.

A service handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect never logs on to
our RADIUS: it answers `status: NotOnOurRadius`, and neither online nor
offline.

Limit: 2 a second and 30 a minute for the account, shared with
`DELETE /data/radius/{ref}/session`.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

source.description: Where the answer came from: our own RADIUS sessions, Kinetix's RADIUS, read live, or Opticomm's session history.

retrievedAt.description: For an `opticomm` answer only: when Opticomm reported it.

get.description:
The password this user authenticates with.

A password is a secret, so this call needs the `data:credentials` scope;
a `data:read` key gets `403`. Only a live service answers: a cancelled or
suspended one is `404`.

Every read is recorded against the service. A service that authenticates
on its access circuit has no password to return.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

patch.description:
Set a new password for this user.

A change is accepted only where it takes effect: a live PPPoE service
that logs on to Check Networks' own RADIUS, while PPPoE is offered.
Anything else is `422` and nothing is changed:

- PPPoE is not offered yet (every service logs on over IPoE today);
- the service is not live (suspended or cancelled);
- the service logs on at the carrier, which holds its password;
- the service does not log on with a password at all (IPoE).

A reference that is not one of your services is `404`, whatever the
body holds.

The password is 8 to 64 printable ASCII characters (letters, digits,
spaces and symbols), with no `'` or `\`; the same rule as a password
chosen at provisioning.

The service keeps its current session and re-authenticates with the new
password the next time it connects, so the CPE has to be reconfigured to
match. Changes are recorded against the service in the same way as reads.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

password.description: The new password: 8 to 64 printable ASCII characters, with no single quote (') or backslash (\).

get.description:
The user's current session — when it came up, how long it has been up,
the address it holds and the traffic it has passed.

`result` is null where nothing is connected.

For a service on Kinetix's RADIUS, the session is read live from Kinetix
on each request. If Kinetix does not answer, the request fails with a 502,
so a null `result` always means nothing is connected.

For a service on Opticomm's RADIUS, the session comes from the latest
session check at Opticomm; its `lastSeenAt` is when Opticomm reported
it. Reading never asks Opticomm: a check is asked for with
`POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check`. While one is on its way this
answers `202`: call again after `Retry-After`, or subscribe to
`data.radius.sessionRetrieved`. With no check held it answers
`status: NotChecked`, never a null that would read as not connected.

A service handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect never logs on to
our RADIUS: it answers `status: NotOnOurRadius`, never a null.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

delete.description:
Drop the user's live session, so the service connects again on its own
and picks up a new password or plan. For a live service on our own
network; a service on a carrier's RADIUS keeps its session there. A
suspended account cannot reset a session.

Limit: 2 a second and 30 a minute for the account, shared with GET
/data/radius/{ref}/online. Past it the answer is `429` with
`Retry-After`.

`202` says the session was dropped. `409` with `no_live_session` says
nothing is connected. `422` with `session_not_resettable` says the
session is on a network where it cannot be reset (the legacy NAS, a
carrier's RADIUS, or a service handed to you at layer 2, which has no
session here), and a plain `422` that the service is not live.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

202.description: The session was dropped.

post.summary: Check a User's Session at Opticomm
post.description:
Ask Opticomm for the user's session now, by starting a Session History
test there. For a live service on Opticomm's RADIUS only: the other
services' GET /data/radius/{ref}/online and /session are read live. This
is a request to the carrier, so it needs `data:update`, and a suspended
account cannot make it.

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

`202` says the check is on its way; a check already on its way is
reused, not asked for twice. The answer is on GET
/data/radius/{ref}/online and /session once Opticomm gives it, usually
within a minute or two, and the `data.radius.sessionRetrieved` webhook
says when. If Opticomm refused the last check under five minutes ago,
or does not answer, this fails with a 502.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A RADIUS user (USR…), order, product or service reference.

get.summary: List Every Service's Usage for a Month
get.description:
One month of data usage for every data service on your account, one row
per service, paged: what you need to bill or warn your end users, in one
call rather than one per service. Each row's totals are the ones
`GET /data/services/{ref}/usage` gives for the same month. Usage is
reported, never charged.

`period` is a month, `YYYY-MM`, in the last 13 months; the current month
by default, counted up to now (`complete` is false). Months follow your
bill's calendar, as on the per-service read. A service disconnected
before the month began has no row.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: The month, `YYYY-MM`. Defaults to the current month.

parameters.name: network
parameters.description: Only services on these networks, one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter; any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the services of this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

total.description: Every service that matches, across all pages.

to.description: The month's end, or now for the current month.

parameters.name: locId
parameters.description: The premises to qualify — an NBN Location ID (LOC…) or an Opticomm Property ID (OPC…). Use the address search endpoints to find these.

get.summary: Qualify a premises on whichever network serves it
get.description:
One carrier-neutral qualification document. An NBN Location ID runs the NBN single-site qualification plus an Enterprise Ethernet check; an Opticomm Property ID runs the Opticomm qualification and, where the premises also has an NBN footprint, the Enterprise Ethernet check against it. The carrier-shape endpoints under /nbn/service_qualification and /opticomm/service_qualification stay available for the fuller per-carrier documents.

The Service Transfer parameters apply to NBN locations only — either with an Opticomm Property ID is rejected with a 422 naming the field.

parameters.name: serviceRef
parameters.description: (Conditional, NBN only) Existing Service ID for Service Transfer — the entire AVC # or its last 5 digits. Requires `customerAuthorityDate`; indicates the matching resource via `serviceIdMatch` on the `resources` entries, with validation issues surfaced in `siteRestrictionError`.

parameters.name: customerAuthorityDate
parameters.description: (Conditional) The date Customer Authority was obtained for the premises, as `YYYY-MM-DD` (a date-time is read as its date); must be less than 45 days old. Mandatory with `serviceRef`.

parameters.name: potsInterconnect
parameters.description: (Optional, NBN only) Existing Full National Number (FNN) or ULL ID to check against.

parameters.name: latitude
parameters.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the address.

parameters.name: longitude
parameters.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the address.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Limit the amount of locations returned. Leave empty to return all available results.

schema.description: Locations matching the supplied coordinates.

get.summary: Request nbn™ Location IDs (LOC #) for a Latitude and Longitude
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Kinetix's own answer: a bare array of addresses, without a `results`
wrapper.

parameters.name: secondaryComplexName
parameters.description:
Name associated with a building or area within a complex site.
This data element may represent the name given to an entire building within an address site that has its own separate address.

limit, so retrying without releasing one gets the same answer.

post.summary: Request nbn™ run a test for a TC4 Service (AVC #)
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Request nbn™ run a diagnostic test against an Access Virtual Circuit
(AVC). Use the /diagnostics/{testRef} endpoint to retrieve the results.
A webhook subscribed to `diagnostic.completed` is told once the test
finishes, with its result, so you need not poll.

Every request here reaches nbn™, and some tests (a Port Reset, an NTD
Reset) drop the end user's service while they run. To try this call
without reaching the carrier, use the
[sandbox](https://help.checknetworks.tools/api/sandbox/).

serviceRef.description:
Access Virtual Circuit (AVC) ID Reference.
For Example: "AVC000000000000"

test.description: The test to be run against this AVC service

trafficClass.description:
This field is for the "Network Performance Test" test only. It is mandatory for that test.
The traffic class on which to perform the test:
  - "TC-1" - Traffic Class #1
  - "TC-2" - Traffic Class #2

monitoringDuration.description:
(Optional) This field is for the "Line Quality Diagnostic" test only.
The monitoring duration in minutes. If not provided, the test will run with the default duration of 6 minutes.

packetSize.description:
(Optional) This field is for the "Loopback" test only.
The packet size for performing a loopback test, if not provided the test will be run with a pre-configured default packet size.
The minimum accepted value is 64 and the maximum accepted value is 1500.

forceTest.description:
This field is for the "Metallic Line Test" test only. It is mandatory if the AVC is on a NFAS (Fibre) line, but must not be specified if the AVC is on a NCAS (FTTB, FTTC, FTTN) line.
Whether or not to force a test if there is a call in progress on the target line:
  - "true" - the test will run even if there is a call in progress, resulting in the call being dropped.
  - "false" - the test will not be progressed if there is a call in progress.

technology.description:
This field is for the "Metallic Line Test" test only.
The test parameters differ based off the line technology. If this AVC is known to Check Networks the technology will be detected automatically, if the AVC is unknown to Check Networks you must specify the line technology here, otherwise the test request will be rejected.

forceMeasurement.description:
This field is for the "Single End Line Test" test only. It is mandatory for that test.
Forces the testing platform to provide detailed measurements on the associated Copper Loop.

parameters.description:
NBN Location ID of the premises.
Either the locId or the serviceRef must be specified.

parameters.name: serviceRef
parameters.description:
NBN Access Virtual Circuit (AVC) ID.
Either the locId or the serviceRef must be specified.

The order is accepted immediately and processed in the background, so the
service is not disconnected at the moment this call returns. The response
contains the order number and its current status.

A service still in its contract term is charged early termination. To
see what before you disconnect, GET /data/services/{ref}/disconnect-quote.

get.summary: Retrieve an order using its Order ID
get.description:
Retrieve the current detail of one of your orders by its Order ID.

Once an order has completed, its final detail is returned. While an order
is still in progress, the latest available detail is returned so you can
poll its status through to completion.

An order that nbn does not hold yet is found by its PND and answered from
Check Networks' own record, with no nbn detail: `state` Acknowledged while
it is on its way to nbn, PendingReview if nbn could not accept it as Check
Networks sent it (Check Networks will correct and resubmit it), or

never a 404. Once nbn holds the order its `id` is the Order ID; a PND that
was PendingReview keeps returning nbn's detail, and any other PND then
finds nothing, so poll by the Order ID.

post.summary: Submit an Order to NBN for a NCAS Product
post.description:
NCAS Products include: FTTB, FTTC and FTTN

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).


A successful submission will result in an "Acknowledged" response.
The order status can be checked when viewing the Order Details.

If nbn cannot accept an order as Check Networks sent it, the answer is
still a success, with `state` "PendingReview" and the order's PND as its
`id`: the fault is ours, and Check Networks will correct and resubmit it.
Poll the PND on the Order Details. A genuine refusal from nbn, such as
informed consent not evidenced or no NTD capacity, is a 422 instead.

Use the Callbacks API to register a callback URL for receiving
notifications when the order is "Accepted", "Complete" or "Rejected".

Use the Service Qualification API first — it lists the copper pairs at the
premises with the Service Class of each, which determines what this order
needs.


VALIDATION>

An order runs over a copper pair rather than an NTD, so `copperPairId`
names the pair it uses: an existing CPI, or "NEW" for a new line. An order
is then one of three things: a connection on that pair, a Service Transfer
(adding `transferType`, `serviceRef` and `customerAuthorityDate`), or a
Connect Outstanding (as a transfer, but without `serviceRef` — the
previous occupant's AVC is unknown).

Orders are checked against the Service Qualification for the Location
before they are sent to nbn, so a mistake comes straight back as a 422
with the reason — no order is created at nbn when an error is found in
pre-validation. The reasons are:

 - `location_not_serviceable` the Location cannot take a service
 - `wrong_access_technology` the Location is not FTTB, FTTC or FTTN — use the order endpoint for its access technology
 - `copper_pair_id_required` supply a copper pair (CPI #) or "NEW"
 - `unknown_copper_pair` no such copper pair at this Location
 - `copper_pair_not_available` that pair carries a service — transfer it, or choose another pair
 - `new_pair_not_allowed` the premises has a spare pair, so a new line cannot be ordered
 - `appointment_required` this order needs an appointment — see the `appointmentId` field for the Demand Type it takes
 - `appointment_not_allowed` no appointment is required for this order
 - `appointment_wrong_demand_type` the appointment is not the Demand Type this order needs
 - `transfer_type_invalid` / `transfer_type_unsupported` see the `transferType` field for the accepted values
 - `service_ref_required` / `service_ref_not_allowed` only a Service Transfer names the AVC being taken over
 - `avc_mismatch` nbn does not report that AVC on that copper pair — check both
 - `authority_date_required` / `authority_date_invalid` / `authority_date_in_future` / `authority_date_expired` the Customer Authority must be dated within the last 45 calendar days
 - `pots_interconnect_required` a Service Class 12 Active line must name the phone service being transitioned
 - `pots_interconnect_not_allowed` the line does not transition a phone service
 - `central_splitter_not_allowed` a central splitter can only be installed on a Service Class 12 line
 - `installation_workforce_not_allowed` no installation is being performed
 - `installation_workforce_invalid` see the `installationWorkforce` field for the accepted values
 - `bandwidth_sku_required` / `bandwidth_sku_not_eligible` / `sla_sku_not_eligible` use the Product Qualification APIs for the selectable options
 - `order_reference_required` / `order_reference_invalid` up to 35 characters of letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens and periods
 - `informed_consent_required` confirm the End User has given Informed Consent
 - `vlan_mode_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_required` / `uni_vlan_id_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_not_allowed` `uniVlanId` applies only when `vlanMode` is "Tagged"

locId.description: The NBN Location ID for the premises the order is for.

bandwidthProductSku.description:
Product SKU of the Bandwidth Product being ordered.
This controls which Service Layer (Layer 2 or Layer 3) this Order can be Provisioned with.
Use the Product Qualification > Eligible Bandwidth Products API to find selectable options for the Location (LOC #)

restorationSlaSku.description:
(Optional) Product SKU of the Service Restoration SLA.
If omitted, the Standard SLA ("NBN-SLA-TC4-STD") is applied.
Indicates how quick NBN responds should this service be affected by an issue, depending upon the SLA Region.
Response times are Business Hours unless a (24/7) SLA is selected.
Enhanced or Premium SLAs may incur an additional monthly cost.
Bundled SLA Product SKUs will only be accepted when provided with an eligible Bandwidth Product SKU.
Use the Product Qualification > Eligible Restoration SLA Products API to find selectable options for the Location (LOC #).

copperPairId.description:
The copper pair (CPI #) this order runs over, or "NEW" to
order a new line.

Use the Service Qualification API to see the pairs at the
premises. "NEW" is not accepted where the premises already has
a spare pair — the existing one must be used.

(Conditional) NBN Appointment ID to attach to this order.

Service Class 13 and 33: no appointment — unless you are
ordering a new line ("NEW") because every pair at the premises

appointment with Demand Type "Non EU Jumper Only" — the work is
at the exchange, not the premises.

informedConsent.description: Verification that the End User has provided Informed Consent for this order to be placed.

transferType.description:
(Conditional) Service Transfer Type.
Only applicable to, and is mandatory for Service Transfers.
 - "Service Transfer" - transfer an existing nbn service from another provider to you.
 - "Service Transfer Reversal" - recover an existing service that was incorrectly transferred away from you.
 - "Connect Outstanding" - connect a new service over a line that still has an existing active service not controlled by the End User.  This requires time to legally cancel the existing service.

Required for a Service Class 12 Active line. Must NOT be
supplied for a Service Class 13 or 34 line, or for an Inactive
Service Class 12, 31, 32 or 33 line.

(Conditional) Who performs the installation.

"NBN Co Install End User" is only available at a Service Class
33 premises. Everywhere else an installation is required, it
is "NBN Co Install" — a technician attends.

installOptionCentralSplitter.description:
(Optional) Install a central splitter.

Only applicable to a Service Class 12 line, and rare even
there. Defaults to false.

vlanMode.description:
(Optional) The VLAN Mode determines which Product Template will be used when ordering this connection.

IMPORTANT> Do not specify unless explicitly needed.

When this field is not specified, "Default-Mapped" will be the assumed value.
Intended mainly for transitioning existing "Tagged" PPPoE services without needing to change the client CPE configuration.

IMPORTANT> You cannot change this value with a Modify Order. Instead, the service must be cancelled and reordered, potentially bringing the service down for 24-48 hours.

uniVlanId.description:
(Conditional) Required if `vlanMode` is "Tagged"
The UNI VLAN ID # used to tag the service traffic.
The value should be between 1 and 4094.

post.summary: Submit an Order to NBN for a NFAS Product

NFAS Products include: Fibre and FTTP

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).


A successful submission will result in an "Acknowledged" response.
The order status can be checked when viewing the Order Details.

If nbn cannot accept an order as Check Networks sent it, the answer is

notifications when the order is "Accepted", "Complete" or "Rejected".

Use the Service Qualification API first — the Service Class, the NTDs at
the premises and the UNI-D port status determine which fields this order
needs.


VALIDATION>

An order is one of four things: a new install (`ntdId` "NEW" with a
"Standard Install" `appointmentId`), taking a spare port on an installed
NTD (`ntdId` and optionally `unidPortId`), a Service Transfer (adding
`transferType`, `serviceRef` and `customerAuthorityDate`), or a Connect
Outstanding (as a transfer, but without `serviceRef` — the previous
occupant's AVC is unknown). A transfer moving to a different UNI-D
Port without downtime adds `overlapPeriod` "4" and `fromPortId`.

Orders are checked against the Service Qualification for the Location
before they are sent to nbn, so a mistake comes straight back as a 422
with the reason — no order is created at nbn when an error is found in
pre-validation. The reasons are:

 - `location_not_serviceable` the Location cannot take a service
 - `wrong_access_technology` the Location is not FTTP — use the order endpoint for its access technology
 - `ntd_id_required` supply an NTD ID or "NEW"
 - `ntd_must_be_new` Service Class 1 or 2 has no NTD installed yet, so `ntdId` must be "NEW"
 - `unknown_ntd` no such NTD at this Location
 - `appointment_required` a new NTD needs a "Standard Install" appointment
 - `appointment_not_allowed` an installed NTD needs no technician
 - `unknown_port` no such UNI-D Port on that NTD
 - `port_not_free` the Port carries a service — transfer it, or choose a free Port
 - `port_not_in_use` a transfer needs the Port the existing service is on
 - `no_free_port` the NTD is full — order an additional NTD with `ntdId` "NEW"
 - `transfer_type_invalid` / `transfer_type_unsupported` see the `transferType` field for the accepted values
 - `unid_port_required_for_transfer` a transfer must name the Port
 - `service_ref_required` / `service_ref_not_allowed` only a Service Transfer names the AVC being taken over
 - `avc_mismatch` nbn does not report that AVC on that Port — check both
 - `authority_date_required` / `authority_date_invalid` / `authority_date_in_future` / `authority_date_expired` the Customer Authority must be dated within the last 45 calendar days
 - `overlap_requires_service_transfer` / `overlap_period_invalid` / `overlap_period_required` the overlap applies only to a Service Transfer
 - `from_port_required` / `from_port_same_as_target` / `unknown_from_port` / `from_port_not_in_use` an overlap moves the service between two different Ports
 - `bandwidth_sku_required` / `bandwidth_sku_not_eligible` / `sla_sku_not_eligible` use the Product Qualification APIs for the selectable options
 - `order_reference_required` / `order_reference_invalid` up to 35 characters of letters, numbers, underscores, hyphens and periods
 - `informed_consent_required` confirm the End User has given Informed Consent
 - `vlan_mode_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_required` / `uni_vlan_id_invalid` / `uni_vlan_id_not_allowed` `uniVlanId` applies only when `vlanMode` is "Tagged"

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Provisions a Connect Order as a service on the Check Networks network —
its authentication identity, addressing, VLAN tags and edge configuration.

This is a separate step from ordering the tail. The Connect Order APIs
(NFAS, NWAS, NHAS, NCAS) order the access service from nbn™; this builds
the service on our side and links it to that order.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself — if this is never called for an order,
the service never goes live. You may call it at any point after the order
is placed: ask before the carrier has finished and the service is built as
soon as it delivers; ask afterwards and it is built immediately.

The same endpoint serves both delivery modes — supply `destination` for a
Layer 2 handoff, or the Layer 3 fields (`fixedIp`, `ipv6Method`,
`protocol`) for a Layer 3 service. Do not mix the two.

Your settings can be changed by calling this again, up until the service
is built. After that, changes require a Modify Order.

If the order is later rejected or cancelled by the carrier, the
provisioning request is cancelled with it.

orderRef.description:
The Reference ID of the Connect Order to be provisioned.
Orders that are marked "Rejected" will have any provisioning requests rejected too.

fixedIp.description:
(Optional) Assign a Fixed IPv4 address to a Layer 3 Service.
NOTE: Fees and charges may apply - refer to your Agreement for details.
Leave empty to have Check Networks assign a Dynamic address instead.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

ipv6Method.description:
(Optional) Enable IPv6 for a Layer 3 service.
Left unspecified, IPv6 is enabled.
NOTES:
 - There is no charge for enabling IPv6 for a service.
 - Can be applied whether `fixedIp` is specified or not.
 - The End User's CPE may need configuring to enable IPv6.
 - You can safely assign IPv6 to services without IPv6 support.
 - IPv6 Addresses and Prefixes will be assigned at processing.
 - Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

OPTIONS:
 - 'Disabled' - Do not enable IPv6 for this service.
 - 'DHCPv6' - Enable IPv6 via DHCPv6 with Prefix Delegation.

protocol.description:
(Optional) The protocol used to connect and authenticate the Layer 3 service within RADIUS.
The default "IPoE" is preferred.  If using "PPPoE" you must provide the EXACT username and password configured on the end-user's device.
PPPoE requires a realm on your account. Contact support if you do not have one.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

The PPPoE Username the user will authenticate with, without a realm —
your realm is appended for you.
Leave it out and a username is generated with the service.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

(Optional) - For `protocol` = "PPPoE" only.

The Peer NNI to use as the "Destination" of the Layer 2 link for this Service, where its traffic will be handed over to you.
Use the Provisioning Layer 2 Destinations API (`GET /nbn/provisioning/layer2/destinations`) for allowed values.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 3 Order.

>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

The Enterprise Ethernet Fibre Build Contribution quotes attributed to your
account that are still in date: the ones you requested, and any our staff
attributed to you. A build cost belongs to the location, so a quote someone
else requested for the same location is listed only once it is attributed
to you. Expired quotes are not listed; request a new one with
`POST /nbn/quotes`.

An account with no in-date quote gets an empty list.

Search, filter and sort it as the portal's NBN Quotes page does: the same
choice gives the same quotes in the same order. Soonest to expire first
unless you ask for another order; the quote id breaks every tie, so the
order is stable between pages. Paged by `page` and `perPage` like every
list of your own records.

The search, filters, sort and paging are ours, not the carrier's: the
carrier has no list of quotes, so this list is our own register of yours
rather than a relay.

post.summary: Create an Enterprise Ethernet (EE) Fibre Build Contribution (FBC) Quote
post.description:
A successful request will return an "Acknowledged" response. A repeat request for a location with an in-date quote, or one the carrier is still working, returns that quote instead of asking again.
The carrier works the quote over hours or days. When it is priced, held waiting on you ("Action Required"), or ends unpriced, the `quote.completed`, `quote.actionRequired` or `quote.closed` webhook is sent, and your users with EE quote updates on are emailed. Read it any time with `GET /nbn/quotes/{quoteId}`.

To try this call without reaching the carrier, use the [sandbox](https://help.checknetworks.tools/api/sandbox/) with one of your account's [test addresses](https://help.checknetworks.tools/api/sandbox/#addresses).

NBN error codes surfaced via the 400 response include:
|Type|Code|Message|
|---|---|---|
|ValidationException|001000|The following mandatory field is not provided: %fieldName%|
|ValidationException|001003|Incorrect enumeration of %enumeration% provided for field %fieldName%|
|ValidationException|001012|The value for %fieldName% : %fieldValue% is in an invalid format|
|ValidationException|001015|The value of %fieldName% %value% is invalid|
|InvalidAddressException|005036|The requested location is currently not serviceable|
|InvalidAddressException|012000|The NBN Location ID provided in the request : %NBN Location ID% does not result in a valid NBN Location Address match|

locId.description: NBN Location ID for the site/premises the quote is for

rspReference.description: RSP Reference ID, specified by the Access Seeker

201.description: The quote request has been acknowledged.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Reserve a technician slot (upstream `createAppointment`) — the body is
the carrier's own `Appointment` create shape. The carrier answers the
appointment RESERVED with a sunset timer; attach it to a Connect order
before the timer lapses to book it. Answers `200` with the created
document in a single-element array, exactly as upstream.

`externalId` is YOUR reference and is held on the Check Networks side;
the carrier-side correlation key is ours. `accessSeekerContact` is
server-owned and refused. `Service Restoration` and `Single Truck
Roll` require the caller to hold a service at the property.

An account may hold at most **5 open install reservations**
(`Standard Install` or `Additional Install`, RESERVED, not yet attached
to an order, timer not lapsed). The next one answers `409`: waiting does
not free a place, so attach one to a Connect order or cancel it first. Like every carrier
write, it needs an `Idempotency-Key`.

priorityAssist.description: (Optional) Sent to the carrier as its priority assist flag. "Yes" is accepted only for a customer on our Priority Assistance register; otherwise the reservation is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist` before the carrier is asked.

validFor.description: The slot as `GET /opticomm/timeSlots` returned it: a date-time with or without an offset, passed to Opticomm as given.

400.description: The request was malformed, carried a server-owned field, or the carrier rejected it outright (the carrier's own error object is relayed).

409.description: The account already holds 5 open install reservations. Release one first, by attaching it to a Connect order or cancelling it; retrying unchanged gets the same answer.

`accessSeekerContact` is server-owned and refused. Answers `200` with
the updated document in a single-element array, as upstream.

A test the service's delivery layer cannot run (the RADIUS-side tests
on a service where Check Networks provides the Layer 3) is refused

>**Required Scope(s):** data:create (a Modify also requires data:update, a Disconnect data:delete)

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Submit an order of type Connect, Modify or Disconnect — one endpoint,
the carrier's own semantics. Use the Service Qualification read first:
it confirms serviceability, whether an installation appointment is
required, and which Bandwidth Products (and NTD ports) are selectable.
A live qualification also runs at submission and refuses an order the
carrier would reject.

A Disconnect of a service still in its contract term is charged early
termination. To see what before you place it, GET
/data/services/{ref}/disconnect-quote.

Returns `200` with the carrier's accepted `ProductOrder`, as upstream
does. A carrier rejection is relayed as the carrier's own error object
at the carrier's status code.

400.description: The request was malformed, carried a field Check Networks sets itself, or the carrier rejected it outright (the carrier's own error object is relayed).

422.description: The order cannot be placed — the carrier rejected it (their error object is relayed), or the service cannot take this order type.

the Check Networks side only — the carrier-side reference is Check

The active Layer 2 link destinations available to your account for Opticomm
services — the outer VLANs (S-Tags) on your customer interconnects, where a
Layer 2 service can be handed off to you. Use an `interconnectRef` from
here as the `destination` when provisioning a Layer 2 order.

**Not offered at the moment.** Layer 2 handoff is unavailable, and every
request answers 422 with the reason.

A single-tag interconnect carries all your services on one outer VLAN
across every POI and carrier; it is presented under the reserved POI code
`0NAT` and appears here as well as under nbn™.

This is the carrier-scoped view of `GET /data/layer2/destinations`, which
returns the same destinations across every carrier at once. New
integrations should prefer that one.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Provisions a Connect Order as a service on the Check Networks network —
its authentication identity, addressing, VLAN tags and edge configuration.

This is a separate step from ordering the tail. The Product Order API
(`POST /opticomm/productOrders`, orderType Connect) orders the access
service from Opticomm; this builds the service on our side and links it
to that order.

**A service is not built until you ask.** Completing at the carrier does
not provision anything by itself — if this is never called for an order,
the service never goes live. You may call it at any point after the order
is placed: ask before the carrier has finished and the service is built as
soon as it delivers; ask afterwards and it is built immediately.

The same endpoint serves both delivery modes — supply `destination` for a
Layer 2 handoff, or the Layer 3 fields (`fixedIp`, `ipv6Method`,
`protocol`) for a Layer 3 service. Do not mix the two.

Your settings can be changed by calling this again, up until the service
is built. After that, changes require a Modify Order.

If the order is later rejected or cancelled by the carrier, the
provisioning request is cancelled with it.

orderRef.description:
The Check Networks Reference ID of the Opticomm Connect Order to be provisioned.
Orders that are marked "Rejected" will have any provisioning requests rejected too.

fixedIp.description:
(Optional) Assign a Fixed IPv4 address to a Layer 3 Service.
NOTE: Fees and charges may apply - refer to your Agreement for details.
Leave empty to have Check Networks assign a Dynamic address instead.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

ipv6Method.description:
(Optional) Enable IPv6 for a Layer 3 service.
Left unspecified, IPv6 is enabled.
NOTES:
 - There is no charge for enabling IPv6 for a service.
 - Can be applied whether `fixedIp` is specified or not.
 - The End User's CPE may need configuring to enable IPv6.
 - You can safely assign IPv6 to services without IPv6 support.
 - IPv6 Addresses and Prefixes will be assigned at processing.
 - Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

OPTIONS:
 - 'Disabled' - Do not enable IPv6 for this service.
 - 'DHCPv6' - Enable IPv6 via DHCPv6 with Prefix Delegation.

protocol.description:
(Optional) The protocol used to connect and authenticate the Layer 3 service within RADIUS.
The default "IPoE" is preferred.  If using "PPPoE" you must provide the EXACT username and password configured on the end-user's device.
PPPoE requires a realm on your account. Contact support if you do not have one.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

username.description:
(Optional) - For `protocol` = "PPPoE" only.
The PPPoE Username the user will authenticate with, without a realm —
your realm is appended for you.
Leave it out and a username is generated with the service.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

password.description:
(Optional) - For `protocol` = "PPPoE" only.
The PPPoE Password the user will authenticate with.
Leave it out and a password is generated with the service.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 2 Order.

destination.description:
(Conditional) - Required for Layer 2 Orders. Layer 2 is not offered at the moment: a request with a destination answers 422.
The Peer NNI to use as the "Destination" of the Layer 2 link for this Service, where its traffic will be handed over to you.
Use the Layer 2 Destinations API (`GET /opticomm/provisioning/layer2/destinations`) for allowed values.
Do not specify this field for a Layer 3 Order.

in headers: `X-Total-Count`, `X-Page` and `X-Per-Page`.
