get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Qualifies an Opticomm property for service — the carrier's own
`SiteQualification` document: serviceability status and class, access
technology, NTD and port inventory, applicable charges, and (with
`productAvailability=true`) the bandwidth products offered at the
premises.

Served from Check Networks' qualification cache, fresh until 01:00
Sydney the next day. A request carrying `customerAuthorityDate` (a
transfer qualification — the carrier's answer depends on it) is always
answered live and never served from, or written over, the cache.

parameters.name: customerAuthorityDate
parameters.description: (Conditional) The date Customer Authority was obtained from the end user. Supply when qualifying for a Service Transfer; must be less than 45 days old.

parameters.name: productAvailability
parameters.description: Display the products available at this property. Absent behaves as false, as upstream.

400.description: The request was malformed, or the carrier rejected the qualification parameters (the carrier's own error object is relayed).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of all DID (Direct Inward Dialing) phone numbers assigned to your account,
in number order. The filters below narrow it and combine; they match the same numbers as the
portal's Numbers page. Filter by `endUser` for the numbers one end user holds.

For the whole list, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson` to stream **every** match in one response,
ignoring `page` and `perPage`. `csv` returns `text/csv` (a header row and one row per number, the
columns of a `results[]` item, with `routing` and `ipnd` as JSON); `ndjson` returns
`application/x-ndjson` (one `results[]` item per line).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of a number or of its description. A national number matches too: `07` finds numbers stored as `617`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: The number type.

parameters.name: szu
parameters.description: The standard zone unit (SZU) of the number's block, by name.

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only the numbers on this trunk, by its `sipUsername`. A trunk that is not yours is a 422.

parameters.name: routeType
parameters.description: Only the numbers whose first route is of this type.

parameters.name: assigned
parameters.description: `false` for the numbers on no trunk; `true` for those on one.

parameters.name: hasEmergencyAddress
parameters.description: `false` for the numbers with no emergency address linked; `true` for those with one.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit for paged JSON; `csv` or `ndjson` streams every match.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the numbers this end user holds, by its public number: those tagged to it, and untagged ones on its trunks. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list. With `needsAttention`, it narrows the group to that end user.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: Only the numbers in this needs-attention group, exactly as `GET /account/summary` counted them. With it, `endUser` (an end user's number) narrows the group to that end user.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of phone numbers.

total.description: Total number of phone numbers matching the query.

perPage.description: The number of records returned per page.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. Every matching number as CSV: a header row, then one row per number with the columns of a `results[]` item.
Present only when `format=ndjson`. Every matching number as newline-delimited JSON, one `results[]` item per line.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Order a number, or a block of 10 or 100, as the portal's Order Numbers page
does. Say the type and, for a geographic number, the area (`szu`, from
`GET /numbers/areas`), and where it goes: a trunk and the emergency
address it is listed at, or `spare: true` to keep it on no service, routed
to Disconnected until you route it.

Which number: a `holdId` from `POST /numbers/holds` orders the number you
held; an `offerId` from `GET /numbers/available` orders a number our
supplier offered, which is bought now; neither takes the next number (or
the first complete block) we hold. If an order buys a supplier number and
then cannot be placed (say, the trunk's account is on credit hold), the
`422` carries `error.holdId` and `error.heldUntil`: fix the cause and order
again with that `holdId`, and the number you bought is used, not bought
again.

With `bundle`, the order is recorded as a `draft` in that bundle and
nothing is allocated until the bundle is released. A bundle that has been
submitted takes nothing more, and a bundle's numbers are always ones we
hold, on a trunk.

The order is set up in the background: the answer is `202` with the order
and a `Location` to read it from. Poll it until it is `completed` or
`failed`. The `Idempotency-Key` is required, so a retry never orders twice.

type.description: The number type: an Australian geographic, mobile, 1300 or 1800 number, or a New Zealand geographic or 0800 number. 13 and premium numbers are by request through your account manager.

szu.description: The numbering area, required for `fixed` and `nz_geographic`.

blockSize.description: Consecutive numbers to order. Blocks are for geographic types only.

holdId.description: A hold from `POST /numbers/holds`, for a single number, or the `error.holdId` of an order that bought a supplier number but could not be placed, for the same area and block size. A hold that has run out answers `422` with the code `hold_expired`.

offerId.description: A `supplier` offer from `GET /numbers/available` for the same area and block size. Not with `holdId`, and not in a bundle.

spare.description: Keep the numbers on no service, routed to Disconnected. Leave `trunk`, `emergencyAddressId` and `routeType` out. Not in a bundle.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk the numbers go on. Required unless `spare`. In a `bundle`, the `id` of a trunk drafted in the same bundle puts them on that trunk once it is set up: they always start after it.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the numbers are listed at. Required unless `spare`.

routeType.description: Where calls go: the trunk, forwarded to a number (`redirect`), or a SIP address (`sip_address`). Time of day, geographic routes and failovers are set on the number once it is live.

routeTarget.description: The forward number, or a `sip:`/`sips:` URI that is not a private address. A forward to 000, 112 or 106, in any form, is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

bundle.description: The bundle to add the order to.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the number, set on it once it is allocated. A reference names one number, so a block (a `blockSize` above 1) is a 422 with one: give a block metadata only. One another number holds, or another open order holds for its number, is a 422 before anything is ordered.

metadata.description: Your own metadata, set on each number the order allocates.

202.description: The order is recorded. Read it at `Location` to see it set up.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The E.164 phone number (e.g. `61299999999`).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the full details for a single DID phone number on your account.

200.description: A JSON object containing the phone number details.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Update the label, inbound routing and/or emergency address for a DID phone number on your account.

You may update any combination of the fields below. Fields not included in the request body are left unchanged:
a request with only `description` leaves the routing as it is. Every field is checked before any is applied,
so a `422` means nothing changed.

**One route.** `routeType` and `routeTarget` set a single route. `routeTarget` is interpreted per `routeType`:
  - `trunk` — the target trunk's `sipUsername` (as returned by `GET /trunks`).
  - `redirect` — the destination phone number.
  - `sip_address` — a SIP URI (`sip:user@host`). Private/reserved hosts are rejected.
  - `fax2email` — the destination email address. Only a number on one of your fax plans (`faxEnabled`) can be
    routed here; any other answers `422` on `routeType`.
  - `disconnected` — no target; `disconnectResponse` says what the caller hears (`hangup` when omitted).

A single route replaces the number's whole chain. When the number has more than one route (`hasAdvancedRouting`:
a failover, time-of-day or geographic routing), `routeType` answers `409` and changes nothing, unless you also send
`replaceRouting: true`.

**The whole chain.** `routing` sets every route at once: a first route, up to three failovers, time-of-day windows
and geographic rules, each step checked by the same rules as the portal. Read `routing` from `GET`, change it and
send it back. `routing` cannot be sent with `routeType`.

**Emergency address.** On a spare number the new address applies at once. On a number in use it goes to the
IPND record shortly after the call: the response shows `emergencyAddressChange` with `status: pending`, and
`emergencyAddressId` keeps the old address until the change is done; `GET /numbers/{number}` then shows the new one.

**SMS delivery.** `smsDelivery` sets where a mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered (a
`422` on any other number), with the portal's rules:
  - A field left out of `smsDelivery` keeps what is stored; `method: null`
    turns forwarding off (messages are still received and stored).
  - `webhook` needs a public HTTPS `destination`; a private or reserved
    address is refused. `email` needs a valid email address.
  - Every webhook request is signed (see the `SmsDelivery` schema). For
    `yeastar`, send the `secret` set on the PBX; it is required while none
    is stored. For `generic` and `3cx`, leave `secret` out and one is
    generated: it is returned once, as `smsDelivery.secret` in this answer.
    A blank `secret` keeps the stored one; switching to `email` or off
    removes it. `secret` is write-only and never returned on a read.

description.description: A label or description for this number, up to 80 characters. Null or empty clears it.

routeType.description: How incoming calls to this number should be routed, as one route.

routeTarget.description: The target for the route, interpreted per `routeType` (see above). Omit it, or send null, for `disconnected`. A `redirect` to 000, 112 or 106, in any form, is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

disconnectResponse.description: For `routeType` `disconnected`, what the caller hears. Defaults to `hangup` when omitted or null.

replaceRouting.description: Send `true` with `routeType` to replace a chain of more than one route with the single route. Without it, such a number answers `409`.

routing.description: The whole routing chain, first route first. Replaces the number's chain.

emergencyAddressId.description: List the number at another of your emergency addresses. An Australian number needs one before it can be routed, so send it with the first `routeType` on a spare number.

smsDelivery.description: Where this mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered (see above).

vendor.description: The webhook payload shape; `generic` when left out.

destination.description: The webhook URL or email address.

secret.description: The signing secret. Required for `yeastar` while none is stored; generated for `generic` and `3cx` when left out.

200.description: Number updated successfully. Returns the updated number details.

emergencyAddressChange.description: Present when the request changed the emergency address of a number in use: the IPND record is updated shortly after, and `emergencyAddressId` shows the new address once it is.

emergencyAddressId.description: The address the number is moving to.

409.description: The request sent `routeType`, and the number has more than one route (a failover, time-of-day or geographic routing) that a single route would delete. The message names the steps. Nothing changed: send `replaceRouting: true` to replace them, or the whole chain as `routing`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Cancel (release) a phone number by specifying it in the path.

The release runs shortly after the call. Until then `GET` shows the
number as `releasing`; once it is done, `GET` answers `404` and the
`number.released` webhook is sent.

**What a release does.** When it runs, the number stops working and its
billing stops, and an IPND disconnect record is sent for a number that
is listed in the IPND. The number
then cools off for 30 days, during which no one can order it, you
included; after that it can be issued to anyone. **There is no undo in
the API**: a number released by mistake is a request to Support, and
once it has cooled off it may already be someone else's. If your end
user is moving to another provider, have them port the number out
instead.

**Refusals.** Each answers `409` with `code` `conflict` and a `reason`,
and the number stays yours, unchanged:
  - a number Check Networks has suspended: only Check Networks can lift
    the suspension, so contact Support;
  - a number a trunk presents as its default caller ID: change that
    trunk's default caller ID first (`PATCH /trunks/{username}`), then
    release the number.

The same checks run again when the release runs. If the number was
suspended, or made a trunk's default caller ID, after the `202`, the
release is dropped: `GET` no longer shows it as `releasing`, and no
`number.released` webhook is sent.

202.description: The cancellation is queued.

409.description: Check Networks has suspended the number, which only Check Networks can lift, or a trunk presents it as its default caller ID. Nothing changed.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of your emergency addresses, ordered by label.
`q` searches the label, customer name, long name, street and locality.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated list of emergency addresses.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Create an emergency address. It is lodged with the emergency register when
a number is linked to it.

To fill the address from an address search, send the `gnafId` of a
`GET /addresses/search` result as `serviceAddress.gnafPid` (and, for a
separate directory listing, `directoryAddress.gnafPid`) with no other
address fields: the building, unit, level, street number, street name and
type, locality, state and postcode are filled in the shape the emergency
register needs, as the portal does. A field sent beside the PID wins.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The emergency address's `id`.

get.description: >**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Send only the fields to change; the others are kept. The address that
results is checked whole, as on create. A change to an address your
numbers are listed at is lodged with the emergency register for each of
them.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

An address cannot be deleted while any of your numbers are listed at it
(`liveNumbers` above zero): the call answers `409`. Move those numbers to
another address first.

204.description: The address is deleted. The response has no body.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the account's fax plans, oldest first, paged like every list.
Open plans by default; pass `status=closed` for closed ones, or
`status=all` for both. `q` searches the plan's numbers and its end user's
reference.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The statuses a plan shows, `open` (the default) or `closed`, one or both comma-separated, or `all`. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of fax plans.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Opens a fax plan for your account, or for one of your end users. The plan
starts billing today. Put numbers on it with
`POST /fax/plans/{planId}/numbers`.

Refused with `422` when the account cannot take new orders (over its
credit limit, or overdue).

kind.description: `bundle`: one number, pages included. `service`: any number of numbers, each charged monthly, and each page sent charged.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the plan is for. Omit it for your own plan. An end user's plan takes that end user's numbers only, and its charges go on their invoice.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns one fax plan, with the pages it has sent this month.

pagesCharged.description: Pages sent this month that are charged per page.

pagesIncluded.description: Pages sent this month that the plan includes.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Closes the plan. Every number comes off it and stops sending and receiving
faxes: its sender addresses are removed and its Fax to Email route is
cleared. The plan stops billing today. A fax already queued still sends.

Closing a plan that is already closed changes nothing and returns `204`.

204.description: The plan is closed. The response has no body.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

post.summary: Add a Number to a Fax Plan

number.description: One of your numbers, as E.164 digits.

201.description: The number is on the plan.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: A number on the plan, as E.164 digits.

delete.summary: Remove a Number from a Fax Plan
delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Takes the number off the plan. It stops sending and receiving faxes: its
sender addresses are removed and its Fax to Email route is cleared. A fax
already queued still sends. The plan is charged for the days it held the
number.

To change plans without losing the sender addresses and the route, use
`POST /fax/plans/{planId}/numbers/{number}/move`.

204.description: The number is off the plan. The response has no body.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The ID of the fax plan the number is on now.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: A number on the plan, as E.164 digits.

post.summary: Move a Number to Another Fax Plan
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Moves the number to another of your open fax plans in one step. Its sender
addresses and Fax to Email route move with it, and each plan is charged
for the days it held the number.

Refused with `422` when the target plan cannot take the number: a Fax
Bundle that already has its number, or an end user's plan when the number
is not on that end user's services.

toPlan.description: The ID of the plan to move the number to.

200.description: The number is on the target plan, which is returned.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

get.summary: List a Fax Plan's Sender Addresses
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the email addresses that may send faxes by email under this plan,
and the number each sends as, by email, paged like every list. `q`
searches the email.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of sender addresses.

id.description: The sender address's id, as `DELETE /fax/plans/{planId}/senders/{senderId}` takes it.

sendsAs.description: The plan's number faxes from this address are sent as.

createdAt.description: When the address was added, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the address last changed, in UTC.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Authorises an email address to send faxes by email as one of the plan's
numbers. Mail from any other address is rejected.

Refused with `422` when `sendsAs` is not a number on this plan, or the
address is already authorised on your account.

sendsAs.description: A number on this plan, as E.164 digits.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The fax plan's ID.

parameters.name: senderId
parameters.description: The sender address's `id`, as the plan's sender list gives it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Removes a sender address from the plan. Faxes emailed from it are rejected
from then on.

204.description: The sender address is removed. The response has no body.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of all SIP trunks assigned to your account, oldest first.
`q` searches the name, handle, description and SIP username. Filter by
`endUser` for one end user's trunks and by `status`, as the portal's trunk
list does. A trunk's `connection.allowList` is on `GET /trunks/{username}`
only, not here.

For bulk pulls, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson` to stream **every**
matching trunk as a single download instead of paged JSON. `page`/`perPage`
are ignored in this mode. `csv` returns `text/csv` (a header row and one row
per trunk, with arrays and objects as JSON in their cells); `ndjson` returns
`application/x-ndjson` (one JSON object per line, each identical to a
`results[]` item). An unrecognised `format` returns `422`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only trunks with this `status`.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Bulk export format. Omit for paged JSON; `csv` or `ndjson` streams the full result set as a download.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the trunks of this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of SIP trunks.

total.description: Total number of trunks matching the query.

perPage.description: The number of records returned per page.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. Every matching trunk as CSV — a header row followed by one row per trunk, with the same columns as a `results[]` item.
Present only when `format=ndjson`. Every matching trunk as newline-delimited JSON — one object per line, each identical to a `results[]` item.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Create a new SIP trunk on your account.

The SIP domain, username and password are platform-assigned: the trunk
is created on the shared wholesale SIP domain and the generated
credentials are returned in the response. The password is revealed
**only once**, in the `201` response — store it securely.

With `bundleId`, the trunk is checked the same way and joins that bundle
as a draft instead (see `POST /bundles`): it is set up when the bundle is
submitted, and the answer is the bundle item, with the bundle at
`Location`. Order numbers onto it in the same bundle with the item's `id`
as `trunk`. Once it is set up, its `href` reads it; take its password with
`POST /trunks/{username}/credential/rotate`. A description, recording,
number formats and calling limits are set on the trunk then, so a request
in a bundle that sends them is a 422. `externalRef` and `metadata` are
taken now and held for the trunk: a reference another trunk holds, or one
another open order holds for its trunk, is a 422 now, and one another
trunk takes before the bundle sets this one up is left off it, with the
reason in the bundle item's `outcomeReason`.

schema.description: `sipUsername`, `sipDomain`, `cpsLimit` and `faxEnabled` are set by Check Networks; a request that sends any of them is refused.

name.description: A friendly name for this trunk.

description.description: An optional description for this trunk.

type.description: The plan to provision on. Omitted means `payg`. On `ultimate` each channel is a recurring billed assignment; on `payg` outbound calls are metered per use.

channels.description: Maximum concurrent calls on this trunk. On `ultimate` this is also the number of channels billed, and is required. On `payg` it is a ceiling and defaults to 5.

maxInternational.description: Maximum concurrent international calls. Only for a trunk that may call internationally: a limit sent without `International` in `callingPermissions` is refused with a 422.

callingPermissions.description: The calling-permission classes to enable. Omitted means `AUNational`, `AUMobile` and `AU13`. `AUEmergency` and `AUFreecall` are always on: you may send them, as a fetched trunk lists them, and they cannot be left out.

defaultCallerId.description: Default outbound caller ID: a number on your account with an emergency address linked, or one approved through `POST /caller-id-authorisations`. Digits, which may include `+` and spaces. Any other number is a 422 with the code `caller_id_authorisation_required`.

forceOutboundCli.description: Present `defaultCallerId` on every outbound call, whatever caller ID the PBX sends.

recordingEnabled.description: Order call recording with the trunk, a monthly charge per trunk. Every call is recorded, with no announcement: you are responsible for telling your callers that calls may be recorded. Needs `acknowledgeRecording: true`, and an account that may place orders.

acknowledgeRecording.description: With `recordingEnabled: true`, confirms that you accept the monthly recording charge and are responsible for telling your callers. Without it the request answers `422` `charge_acknowledgement_required`, with `error.consent` (the text you are agreeing to) and `error.charge` (the monthly price). The acknowledgement is kept on the trunk's history with the API key that sent it. A credit hold or a suspended account answers `422` and nothing is ordered.

endUser.description: The end user this trunk is for, by its public number: the trunk's calls are billed to that end user. One of your end users that is not archived; any other number is a 422. Omitted or null makes the trunk your own.

allowedCountries.description: The trunk's own list of countries it may call, as ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes. Omitted or null, the new trunk follows your account's list (Get Allowed Countries), later changes included.

dailySpendCapExGst.description: The most the trunk's outbound calls may cost in a day, ex GST, as a dollar string. Omitted or null is no cap. 000 always connects.

calledNumberFormat.description: How the dialled number arrives on calls to this trunk. Omitted means `international`.

callerNumberFormat.description: How an Australian caller's number arrives on calls to this trunk. Omitted follows `calledNumberFormat`'s plus: with a plus for `international`, digits only otherwise.

bundleId.description: An open bundle to add the trunk to, as a draft that is set up when the bundle is submitted. A bundle that has been submitted, or is not yours, is a 422.

201.description: SIP trunk created successfully. Includes the one-time SIP password. With `bundleId`, the trunk joined the bundle; this is the item.

sipPassword.description: The generated SIP password. To read it again later, call `GET /trunks/{username}/credential`, which needs `secrets:read`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username. A trunk with no SIP credential has only its `id`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the full details for a single SIP trunk on your account, including
its IP ACL entries and, in `connection.allowList`, the addresses to allow
through your firewall (read from DNS, so returned here and not on the list).

200.description: A JSON object containing the SIP trunk details.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Update settings on an existing SIP trunk. Fields not included in the request body will remain unchanged.

### Changing plan or channels

`type` and `channels` are billing-affecting on an `ultimate` trunk — each
channel is a recurring charge — so they follow the upgrade/downgrade rule
rather than applying as a plain edit:

* **Upgrades take effect immediately** and are billed from today. Moving
  `payg` → `ultimate` is an upgrade whatever the channel counts say, as is
  raising the channel count on an `ultimate` trunk.
* **Downgrades take effect at the start of your next billing cycle.**
  Lowering the channel count, or moving `ultimate` → `payg`, is a
  downgrade. Channels in use above the new limit are never cut mid-period.

When a plan change happens the response carries a `planChange` block. On a
scheduled downgrade `result` still shows the plan the trunk is on **today**
— `planChange.effectiveOn` is when the new one starts.

Requesting a change supersedes any change already scheduled on the trunk,
so an upgrade also clears a pending downgrade that would otherwise reverse
it on the 1st. A scheduled change shows in the trunk's `pendingPlanChange`
on every read until it applies, and `DELETE /trunks/{username}/plan-change`
cancels it.

Every field is checked before anything is applied, and the whole request
applies in one step: a `422` (for example a caller ID you may not present)
leaves recording, the plan and every other field as they were.

schema.description: `cpsLimit` and `faxEnabled` are managed by Check Networks; a request that sends either is refused.

description.description: Your free-text notes on the trunk, up to 500 characters. Null clears them.

type.description: The trunk's billing plan. Omit to leave it unchanged. Moving onto `ultimate` requires `channels`, since each channel is a recurring charge and one will never be assumed for you.

channels.description: Maximum concurrent calls on this trunk. On `ultimate` this is the number of billed channels, and changing it is an upgrade or a downgrade (see above); omit it to leave the count alone. On `payg` it is a concurrency ceiling only, with no billing effect. An `ultimate` trunk needs at least 1.

maxInternational.description: Maximum concurrent international calls; null removes the trunk's own limit. Only for a trunk that may call internationally: a limit sent while `International` is not among the calling permissions (after this request's change) is refused with a 422. Removing `International` clears the limit.

callingPermissions.description: The trunk's call barring: the calling-permission classes it may dial, replacing the current list. Remove `International` to cut international calling in one call. 000 and freecall are never barred: `AUEmergency` and `AUFreecall` stay on whether sent or not, and the answer's `callingPermissionsKept` names any this list left out.

defaultState.description: The trunk's default state; null clears it.

defaultCallerId.description: Default outbound caller ID: a number on your account, or one approved through `POST /caller-id-authorisations`. Digits, which may include `+` and spaces. Any other number is a 422 with the code `caller_id_authorisation_required`. The change is in the trunk's history with its before and after values.

forceOutboundCli.description: Present `defaultCallerId` on every outbound call, whatever caller ID the PBX sends. The caller ID must pass the same checks as `defaultCallerId`.

forcePrivateCli.description: Force all outbound calls to present as Private/Anonymous.

recordingEnabled.description: `true` orders call recording, a monthly charge per trunk; `false` cancels it, and recordings already made are kept. Every call is recorded, with no announcement: you are responsible for telling your callers that calls may be recorded. Turning it on needs `acknowledgeRecording: true`, and an account that may place orders.

acknowledgeRecording.description: With `recordingEnabled: true` on a trunk without recording, confirms that you accept the monthly recording charge and are responsible for telling your callers. Without it the request answers `422` `charge_acknowledgement_required`, with `error.consent` and `error.charge`. A credit hold answers `422` and nothing is ordered. Not needed to turn recording off.

allowedCountries.description: This trunk's own list of countries it may call, as ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes (the United Kingdom is `GB`). `null` drops the override, so the trunk follows your account's list again (Get Allowed Countries). It applies when `International` is in `callingPermissions`; calls to Australia and New Zealand follow their own permissions, high-risk destinations stay blocked, and 000 always connects.

dailySpendCapExGst.description: The most this trunk's outbound calls may cost in a day, ex GST, as a dollar string. At the cap its new outbound calls stop until midnight Brisbane time; calls already up carry on. Spend counts a call when it ends. A cap at or below `spendTodayExGst`, `"0.00"` included, holds the trunk at once, and the answer reads `spendCapHeld: true`; raising it above `spendTodayExGst` resumes calls at once. `null` removes the cap. 000 always connects.

calledNumberFormat.description: How the dialled number arrives on calls to this trunk.

callerNumberFormat.description: How an Australian caller's number arrives on calls to this trunk. A number's own inbound format still overrides it.

200.description: Trunk updated successfully. Returns the updated trunk details.

callingPermissionsKept.description: Present only when `callingPermissions` left out a class that is always on: the trunk keeps it, since 000 and freecall are never barred.

planChange.description: Present only when the request changed the trunk's plan or its billed channel count. Absent for an ordinary edit.

direction.description: Which way the change moves your entitlement.

appliedImmediately.description: True for an upgrade (already live). False for a downgrade, which starts on `effectiveOn`.

effectiveOn.description: The date the new plan applies from — today for an upgrade, the first day of your next billing cycle for a downgrade.

type.description: The plan the trunk moves to.

channels.description: The billed channel count the trunk moves to (0 on `payg`).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Permanently delete a SIP trunk from your account.

**Warning:** This action cannot be undone. Re-route or cancel the trunk's
numbers first; until then the request answers `422`. New calls are
refused at once, and calls already in progress are ended within a minute.
The one exception is the trunk's `defaultCallerId`, which cannot be
cancelled while the trunk is up: when it is the trunk's only number, the
delete releases it with the trunk. If that number can't be released just
then, the answer is `503` and nothing changes; try again shortly.

A trunk still in contract has an early termination charge. The first
request answers `422` with the code `charge_acknowledgement_required` and
the charge in `error.charge`; send `acknowledgeEarlyTermination=true` to
accept it and delete the trunk. The accepted charge is billed shortly
after, on your next invoice.

parameters.name: acknowledgeEarlyTermination
parameters.description: Accept the early termination charge on a trunk still in contract.

204.description: The trunk is deleted. The response has no body.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the IP ACL entries for a SIP trunk, in address order, paged like
every list. `q` searches the address or host name and its description.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of IP ACL entries.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Add a new IP address, CIDR range or host name to a trunk's IP ACL. Calls
from an address on the list are accepted without registration.

A **host name** (such as `pbx.example.com`) is resolved now and again on
its DNS TTL, and allows the public addresses it resolves to. It is stored
lower-cased and listed with `type: host`. It must be a full name with a
dot; one already on another trunk is refused.

An address must be:
  - **An IPv4 host or a range no wider than `/24`** (256 addresses), **or
    a single IPv6 host** (`/128`; IPv6 ranges are refused). A bare
    address is stored, and returned, as `/32` or `/128`.
  - **Public.** Private, CGNAT (`100.64.0.0/10`) and reserved ranges are
    refused.
  - **Not on any other trunk**, yours or another account's: a source
    address identifies the trunk a call belongs to, so ranges cannot
    overlap. If an address has moved to you, contact support.

ipAddress.description: The IPv4 address or CIDR range from `/24` to `/32`, the single IPv6 address, or the host name, to allow.

description.description: An optional label for this IP entry. Defaults to `API`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

parameters.name: ipId
parameters.description: The IP ACL entry's `id`, as the trunk's IP list gives it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Remove an IP address from a trunk's IP ACL.

204.description: The entry is removed. The response has no body.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the live SIP registration status for this trunk, read from the
platform's real-time registration state.

A registration-based trunk lists its currently active contacts (the SIP
devices/gateways registered against it). An IP-ACL-only trunk authenticates
by source IP rather than registering, so it has no registrations
(`registered` is `false`).

This data is live and reflects the current state of the trunk in real time.

username.description: The trunk's SIP digest username. Null for a trunk with no SIP credential, which authenticates by IP and never registers.

registered.description: Whether the trunk currently has at least one active SIP registration.

registrations.description: The trunk's currently active SIP registrations (empty for IP-ACL trunks).

aor.description: The SIP Address of Record the registration is bound to.

sourceIp.description: The source address the REGISTER was received from.

parameters.name: serviceNumber
parameters.description: The IP transit service's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** transit:read

Returns the blackholes in force on an IP transit service, oldest first,
paged like every list. It includes any that Check Networks placed on the
service's addresses (`placedBy` is `staff`), which count toward the
service's limit and which only Check Networks can release.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing an array of blackholes.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** transit:create

Drop all traffic to one of the service's addresses, to stop an attack on
it reaching your service. The traffic is dropped at our border within a
minute or two. It is not signalled to our upstream carriers.

The blackhole must be:
  - **One address**, IPv4 or IPv6, with no prefix length.
  - **Inside one of the service's own prefixes.** For a BGP service
    ordered with an AS-SET, that includes any route registered under the
    AS-SET in the routing registry (IRR), which is asked when you place
    the blackhole. Any other address is refused, and so is every address
    if the registry cannot be reached: try again, or signal the blackhole
    over BGP.
  - **On a live service.**
  - **Given an expiry**, of at most 24 hours. It lifts by itself then;
    place it again if the attack is still running.

A service holds at most 10 blackholes at once. Release one, or wait for
one to expire, to place another.

expiresInHours.description: How many hours until the blackhole lifts by itself.

reason.description: An optional note on why, shown with the blackhole.

parameters.name: serviceNumber
parameters.description: The IP transit service's number.

parameters.name: blackholeId
parameters.description: The blackhole's ID.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** transit:delete

Release a blackhole now, before it expires. Traffic to the address
resumes within a minute or two. A blackhole that has already been
released or has expired answers `404`.

You can release a blackhole you placed (`placedBy` is `customer`). One
Check Networks placed answers `422`; contact support to have it lifted.

204.description: The blackhole is released. The response has no body.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of Call Detail Records (CDRs) for your account.

Results can be filtered by date range using the `from` and `to` query parameters. Dates must be provided in ISO 8601 format (e.g. `2024-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Invalid `from`/`to` values return `422`.
When `from` is omitted the window is the **31 days** before `to`; when `to`
is omitted it is now. `period=unbilled` starts the window at the start of
this month instead (it cannot be combined with `from`), and `invoice` with
no `from` has no lower bound: the invoice bounds the calls. Every response
says the window it used in `window`, and a cursor keeps the first page's
window, so a walk does not drift as new calls arrive.

Filter further with `trunk`, `endUser`, `direction`, `disposition`,
`invoice` and `q`; `GET /voice/cdrs/summary` gives the totals for the same
filters, and `GET /voice/cdrs/{cgrid}` one call. An unknown trunk, end
user or invoice, or a value outside an enum, is a `422`.

A maximum of 200 records can be returned per page. `q` searches the source
and destination.

A re-rated call is listed once, under its `cgrid`, at its new price, with
`rerated: true` and the price before the most recent re-rate in
`previousCostExGst`, `previousCostGst` and `previousCostIncGst`. The
summary counts it once.

### Walking a large window

Page numbers reach at most 10,000 records into the window (`page × perPage`);
a deeper page returns `422`. `total` is exact up to 10,000 and reported as
10,000 with `totalIsBounded: true` beyond it. To walk every record, follow
`nextCursor`: pass it back as `cursor` to get the next page, until it is
`null`. A cursor page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results` only,
and each record is returned exactly once, however many there are.

### Bulk export

For bulk pulls, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson` to stream the **entire**
filtered result set (the `from`/`to` window still applies) as a single
download instead of paged JSON. `page`/`perPage` are ignored in this mode.
`csv` returns `text/csv` (header row + one row per call); `ndjson` returns
`application/x-ndjson` (one JSON object per line, each identical to a
`results[]` item). An unrecognised `format` returns `422`. An export
covers at most **93 days**: a longer window answers `422` on `from`. Each
export is audited with the API key that made it.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Bulk export format. Omit for paged JSON; `csv` or `ndjson` streams the full filtered result set as a download.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Filter CDRs on or after this datetime (ISO 8601), or from the start of this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Defaults to 31 days before `to`, or before now.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page. Walks the window by keyset rather than page number, with no depth limit; `page` is ignored when it is given.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Filter CDRs on or before this datetime (ISO 8601), or to the end of this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Defaults to now.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: `unbilled`: from the start of this month. Not with `from`.

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only this trunk's calls, by sipUsername. A trunk that is not yours is a 422.

parameters.name: invoice
parameters.description: Only the calls billed on this invoice of ours to you, by its `id` in your invoice list. Not one of yours is a 422.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search the source and destination numbers; a national number (07 …) matches too.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the calls on this end user's trunks, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`. `page × perPage` may not exceed 10,000; use `cursor` beyond that. A value that is not a whole number of at least 1 is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending, in place of newest call first. A sorted list has no cursor: `nextCursor` is `null`, and `sort` with `cursor` is `422`. An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing call detail records.

total.description: Number of CDRs matching the query, counted no further than 10,000. Absent on a cursor page.

totalIsBounded.description: True when more than 10,000 records match, so `total` reads 10,000. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The current page number. Absent on a cursor page.

perPage.description: The number of records returned per page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` when this is the last page, the page was not full, or the list was sorted.

window.description: The window the records were read over. `from` is null for an invoice with no `from`.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. The full filtered result set as CSV — a header row followed by one row per call, with the same columns as a `results[]` item.
Present only when `format=ndjson`. The full filtered result set as newline-delimited JSON — one object per line, each identical to a `results[]` item.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the current number of active call sessions on your account. This is useful for real-time capacity monitoring and integrations that need to track concurrent call usage.

The count is the calls the platform is rating on your account right now, across every trunk. If the count cannot be read the endpoint returns `503` rather than a misleading `0`.

200.description: A JSON object containing the current active call count.

activeCalls.description: The number of currently active call sessions across your account.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:read

Every SMS on your account, newest first — sent and received, whatever
sender it went out from.

This is the endpoint to use when you want your account's traffic rather
than one number's. It also covers senders that `GET /sms/{number}` cannot
reach on their own. To follow one message you sent, read
`GET /sms/messages/{messageId}` (the `Location` of the send).

Filter by `direction`, a `from`/`to` range on when the message was sent,
a `q` search over the numbers and the text, and `status`. For a large pull,
`format=csv` or `format=ndjson` streams every match as one download.

To walk every message while new ones arrive, follow `nextCursor`: pass it
back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page carries `perPage`,
`nextCursor` and `results` only.

Reads of message content are audited, an export once with its filters and
count, never the text.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: (Optional) Limit to messages sent or received. Case does not matter; any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending, in place of newest first. A sorted list has no cursor (`nextCursor` is `null`). An unknown field is `422`.

total.description: Messages matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page, a page that was not full, or a sorted list.

statusReason.description: Present only where the status alone is ambiguous.

createdAt.description: When the message was recorded, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the message last changed (its status), in UTC.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`: a header row, then one row per message (see `format`).
Present only when `format=ndjson`: one JSON object per line, with the same fields as a CSV row.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:send

Send an SMS message from a sender on your account.

The `from` sender must be either a DID on your account that has SMS enabled (check via `GET /numbers` — the `smsEnabled` field), or another sender approved for your account (a number ported for SMS, or an alphanumeric Sender ID). Request approval for any other sender with `POST /sms/senders`. An unapproved sender is rejected with a `403` whose `code` is `sender_not_approved`.

**`Idempotency-Key` is required** on this endpoint (`400` without one). At a flat rate-limit tier, a stuck client-side retry loop against an un-deduplicated send can bill and deliver the same message hundreds of times over; sending the header — the same mechanism documented in the Idempotency guide above — makes a retry with the same key return the original send's result instead of sending again.

from.description: The sender — an E.164 number that is an SMS-enabled DID on your account, or another sender (ported number or alphanumeric Sender ID) approved for your account.

to.description: The recipient number in E.164 format.

message.description: The body of the SMS message, up to 1600 characters. A longer body is rejected with `422` — that ceiling has always been enforced and was simply never published (#3102). A message over one segment is sent and billed as several: 160 characters per segment in plain GSM text, or 70 if it contains any character outside that set (emoji, most accented letters), and one fewer per segment once the message is long enough to be concatenated.

202.description:
Accepted for delivery. The message has been submitted and is awaiting a delivery receipt — it is **not** delivered yet, which is why this is `202` rather than `201`.

A `statusReason` of "Held for review before sending" means the message was additionally screened and will be sent once it clears. Either way the message is accepted: **do not retry**, because a retry creates a second message that will also be sent and billed.

The `Location` header names where to poll: the message itself, `GET /sms/messages/{messageId}`. The message reaches `delivered`, or `failed` if it is rejected or not released.

Location.description: Where to poll for this message's outcome (`/sms/messages/{messageId}`).

messageId.description: A unique identifier for the message.

statusReason.description: Present when the message needs more than "pending" to explain it — most often that it is held for review.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The E.164 DID phone number to retrieve SMS history for (must be on your account).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:read

Returns the SMS message history (inbound and outbound) for a DID phone number on your account.

Results are returned in reverse chronological order (newest first). To
walk every message while new ones arrive, follow `nextCursor`: pass it
back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page carries `perPage`,
`nextCursor` and `results` only.

The filters and the `format` export are those of `GET /sms`, within this
number's messages.

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Filter by message direction. Case does not matter; any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending, in place of newest first. A sorted list has no cursor (`nextCursor` is `null`). An unknown field is `422`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing SMS messages.

total.description: Messages matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page, a page that was not full, or a sorted list.

status.description: `delivered` and `failed` are final. `pending` means the message may still move — queued, awaiting a delivery receipt, or held for review; `statusReason` says which.

statusReason.description: Present only where the status alone is ambiguous — most usefully to tell a message held for review before sending from one merely in flight.

createdAt.description: When the message was recorded, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the message last changed (its status), in UTC.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`: a header row, then one row per message (see `format`).
Present only when `format=ndjson`: one JSON object per line, with the same fields as a CSV row.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Check Networks outages affecting services on your account, as published on
our outage register under the Telecommunications (Customer Communications
for Outages) Industry Standard 2024, with the planned maintenance windows
you were sent notice of. Unplanned outages come first, newest first, then
planned windows by start time. Paged like every list: `total`, `page`,
`perPage` and `results`.

An outage is included when it covers the service address of at least one
live service on your account — including services you have attributed to
your own end users. This is the same matching that decides who we
notify, so this endpoint will not disagree with the outage notifications
we send you. Each unplanned outage names which of your services it hit
(`yourAffectedServices`), and the end user each belongs to, so you can
tell them without matching addresses yourself.

Only published register entries are returned.

Every time is UTC, as everywhere in the API; `timezone` names the affected
area's zone, for showing the times locally.

`q` searches the reference, title, affected suburbs and postcodes.

This is distinct from the carrier outage endpoints (`/nbn/outage/...`,
`/opticomm/outage/...`), which report a single carrier's view of a single
carrier reference. Use this endpoint for "what is affecting my services",
and those for carrier-specific detail.

The full public register — including outages that do not affect your
services — is available without authentication at
<https://status.checknetworks.tools>.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` (the default) returns only outages still in progress, `resolved` the resolved ones still within the register's retention period, and `all` both. Several, comma-separated; case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only planned maintenance, or only unplanned outages. Both by default. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the outages that reach this end user's services, by its public number. Planned maintenance is noticed to you, not to an end user, so a list filtered by end user holds no planned windows. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

get.description:
Lists your account's support tickets, newest first. `sort=-lastActivityAt`
gives the portal's order, most recent activity first.

To walk every ticket while new ones are raised, follow `nextCursor`: pass
it back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page carries `perPage`,
`nextCursor` and `results` only. `q` searches the reference and subject.
`createdFrom` and `createdTo` bound the list by when tickets were raised;
`GET /tickets/summary` gives the figures over a range.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The statuses a ticket shows, one or several, comma-separated (`status=open,pending` is the portal's open group). Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: One or several categories, comma-separated. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the tickets about this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

parameters.name: isComplaint
parameters.description: `true` lists only complaints, `false` only the tickets that are not. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending, in place of newest first. `status` orders as the portal does (open, pending, resolved, closed) and `priority` from low to urgent. A sorted list has no cursor (`nextCursor` is `null`). An unknown field is `422`.

total.description: Tickets matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page, a page that was not full, or a sorted list.

post.description:
Opens a new support ticket on your account with its first message.
The response includes the ticket's `reference` (`INC-XXXXXX`), which
addresses the ticket in all other endpoints.

attachments.description: Files to attach to the opening message. Allowed types are PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images, PDF, plain text, CSV, ZIP, and Word (.doc, .docx) and Excel (.xls, .xlsx) files; the per-file size limit is 10 MB.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

get.description:
Returns the ticket with its public conversation thread, oldest
message first. Internal Check Networks notes are never included.

patch.description:
Self-service status change: mark your ticket `resolved`, or set it
back to `open` to re-open a resolved ticket. Tickets are closed by
Check Networks; there is no customer delete.

Read `canResolve` and `canReopen` on the ticket first. A resolve the
ticket's `resolveBlockedReason` refuses answers 422 with that reason's
`code` (`ticket_not_open`).

Resolving a complaint records its outcome: `complaintOutcome`, default
`resolved`. `closed_no_further_action` is recorded by Check Networks only.

`comment` is posted as a public reply before the status changes, in
the same step.

schema.description: `status`, or `externalRef` and `metadata` alone to change only your own reference on the ticket.

status.description: Required unless the request sends `externalRef` or `metadata`.

complaintOutcome.description: The outcome recorded when resolving a complaint. Default `resolved`; ignored for other tickets.

comment.description: A public reply posted with the status change.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.description:
Appends a reply to the ticket's conversation thread. Replying to a
resolved or closed ticket automatically re-opens it. To attach files,
send `multipart/form-data` with an `attachments[]` field. `body` is
required unless `attachments[]` is sent: a reply may be just a file,
such as a screenshot or a log.

body.description: The reply, as Markdown. Required unless `attachments[]` is sent; a reply may be files alone.

attachments.description: Files to attach to the reply. Allowed types are common image, document and archive formats; the per-file size limit is 10 MB.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

parameters.name: attachmentId
parameters.description: The attachment `id` from the message's `attachments` metadata.

get.description:
Streams the attachment's content. The response's `Content-Type` is the
file's stored MIME type; images are served inline, other files as a
download (`Content-Disposition`). Only attachments on the ticket's
public messages are available.

parameters.name: ticketRef
parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.description:
Submits a satisfaction rating for a resolved or closed ticket. A
ticket can be rated once; a `409` is returned if it is still open
or has already been rated.

get.description:
The figures the portal's Support Reports page shows, over the tickets
raised in a date range: counts by status, priority and category, volume
by month, how often the first response and the resolution met their
targets, the average response and resolution times, and satisfaction.
Without `from` and `to` the range is the last 90 days to today. The days
are calendar days in your account's time zone (Australia/Brisbane unless
you set another), and months in `volumeByMonth` are too. A
safety-sensitive complaint is in none of the figures, as it is in no
ticket list. `GET /tickets/export` gives the rows behind them.

parameters.name: from

The rows behind `GET /tickets/summary`, as the CSV the portal's Support
Reports page downloads: one row per ticket raised in the range, oldest

post.summary: Mark a Ticket as a Complaint
post.description:
Marks the ticket a complaint, as the portal's ticket page does. The
complaint's deadlines start from when the ticket's first message
arrived and show on the ticket's `complaint`; the acknowledgement is
sent to the consumer. Marking a complaint again changes nothing and
answers the ticket as it stands. A network outage complaint, which our
staff handle on its own track, is `409`. A safety-sensitive complaint is
`404`, as on every ticket call. The audit log names the API key.

Sets or clears the complaint's urgency, which moves its resolution
deadline. A ticket that is not a complaint is `409`.

The ticket was not a complaint after all: removes the complaint and its
deadlines and any TIO case logged on it. The ticket itself stays. A
ticket that is not a complaint is `409`.

Records that the complaint was acknowledged to the consumer, for one
acknowledged another way (by phone, say), and sends the acknowledgement
again. The first acknowledgement's time stays as `acknowledgedAt`. A
ticket that is not a complaint is `409`.

parameters.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`.

post.summary: Log a TIO Case on a Complaint
post.description:
The consumer took the complaint to the Telecommunications Industry
Ombudsman. Records the TIO's case reference and starts the deadline to
respond to the TIO, shown as `complaint.tioDueAt`: fewer working days
for an urgent complaint. A ticket not yet a complaint is marked one
first, as in the portal. Logging the case again updates the reference
and leaves the deadline where it is. A network outage complaint is `409`.

>**Required Scope(s):** tickets:update

Asks for more attention on one of your open tickets, with your reason.
The ticket's `priority` goes up one level (`low` to `normal`, `normal` to
`high`, `high` to `urgent`; an `urgent` ticket stays `urgent`), with its
response targets worked out again for the new priority. The engineer
looking after it, or our support team if no one is yet, is emailed; our
staff see it flagged on their ticket list with the reason; and it is
added to the thread. The ticket read shows the latest as `escalation`.
Escalating again replaces the reason there and raises the priority
again; each one stays on the thread. A resolved or closed ticket is
`409`: re-open it first.

reason.example: The end user's business has been offline for two days.

>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

The email addresses and mobiles your keys have subscribed to our outage
notices, newest first, pending or active. An address someone signed up on
the public status page, or another account subscribed, is never listed.

post.summary: Subscribe an Address to Outage Notices
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Subscribes a team mailbox or an on-call mobile to our outage notices, as
the sign-up on the public status page does. The person is sent a link to
confirm, by email or by text, and the subscription stays `pending` until
they follow it: notices start only then. Asking again for a pending
address sends a new link once 5 minutes have passed since the last one;
a mobile is sent at most 3 links, after which subscribe it by email.

The subscription is your account's own, with its own confirmation: an
address also signed up on the public status page, or by another account,
is confirmed again for your list, and theirs is left as it is. Someone on
more than one list is sent each notice once. Stop yours with
`DELETE /outages/subscriptions/{id}`, which leaves the address's other
lists as they are. The unsubscribe link in a notice is the person's own
choice, and stops every status notice to the address: the public list,
yours and every other account's. Their subscription then leaves
`GET /outages/subscriptions`, as one you removed does.

address.description: An email address for `email`; an Australian mobile for `sms`, in any common format.

scope.description: Which outages to be told of.

202.description: Accepted. The subscription waits for the person to confirm it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The subscription's id, as `GET /outages/subscriptions` returns it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Stops our outage notices to one of your subscriptions, pending or
active, at once. One your keys did not subscribe is a 404, as an unknown
id is.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:read

Everything your account is currently watching.

Removed watches are kept as `disabled` records rather than deleted; they
are excluded by default. Pass `status=disabled` for them alone, or
`status=all` for both. Newest first; `q` searches the reference and its
type.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: The statuses a watch shows, `active` (the default) or `disabled`, one or both comma-separated, or `all`. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:create

Start watching a reference. We email every address on the watch as updates
arrive — **one email per event**, never a batched digest, and never twice
for the same event.

### One watch per reference

Posting a reference you already watch **replaces** that watch's addresses
rather than creating a second one, and re-enables it if it had been
removed. The call is therefore safe to repeat. It answers `201` when it
created a watch and `200` when it replaced one. To change a watch you
already hold, `PATCH /watch/{watchId}` is the direct way.

An account can have at most 250 active watches.

### Where the emails go

`emails` is optional. Omit it and we use your account's default
notification address — which is what an integration usually wants, since
an API client has no address of its own. If your account has no default
notification address set and you omit `emails`, the request is rejected
rather than creating a watch that could never deliver anything.

### Which updates you get

`eventTypes` is optional. Omit it — or send `null` — and you are told about
everything, which is the default. Send a list to narrow it down;
`GET /watch/event-types` returns the values you can use, with the labels
that appear in the emails.

Like `emails`, the list **replaces** what the watch had rather than adding
to it, so re-posting without `eventTypes` puts a watch back to every event.

### What you may watch

Four kinds of thing, all through this one field — we work out which from
the reference, and tell you in `referenceType` on the response:

* an **order**, by the carrier's reference or ours;
* a technician **appointment**, by its carrier reference;
* a **service**, by its carrier service id or a trunk's SIP username;
* an **outage**, by its register reference.

The reference must belong to your account. Anything else returns `404`,
including a reference that exists on another account — so a `404` here
never confirms whether something exists.

An outage counts as yours when it affects services you hold, decided the
same way `GET /outages` decides what to show you: you can watch exactly the
outages you can already read, and no others.

reference.description: What to watch: an order (the carrier's reference or ours — both work), an appointment, a service, or an outage. See "What you may watch" above.

emails.description: Where to send notifications. Omit to use your account's default notification address.

eventTypes.description: Which updates to send. Omit or null for every update. See `GET /watch/event-types` for the accepted values.

200.description: The watch already on this reference, replaced.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:read

The values `eventTypes` accepts when creating a watch, with the labels that
appear in the notification emails.

Fetch this rather than hardcoding a list — it grows as we support more of
what the carriers send, and a value that is not on it is rejected.

### Each event names what it applies to

Which events exist depends on the kind of thing the watch is on, so each
item carries a `referenceType`, the same value the watch itself reports
back to you. The items are in the shape `GET /webhooks/event-types` uses.
An order's events are the carrier's own, finer-grained
lifecycle; an appointment, a service and an outage each carry the events
the corresponding webhook carries, spelled identically, so the emailed and
the pushed version of one happening never go by two different names.

You do not have to match the `referenceType` yourself: send whatever you want to hear
about, and anything that cannot happen to that reference simply never
fires.

Not everything we record is offered here. Telemetry and internal
bookkeeping events are excluded because they say nothing about the progress
of what you are watching.

200.description: The subscribable event types, each with the kind of reference it applies to; within a kind, in lifecycle order.

parameters.name: watchId
parameters.description: The watch's identifier, as returned when it was created.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:read

A single watch on your account.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:update

Change where a watch's emails go, or which updates it sends. Only the
fields you send change; the reference and whether the watch is active stay
as they are. Each field you send **replaces** what the watch had: send
`eventTypes: null` to go back to every update.

eventTypes.description: Which updates to send, or null for every update. See `GET /watch/event-types` for the accepted values.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** watch:delete

Stop watching. No further emails are sent.

The watch is marked `disabled` rather than erased, so it still appears
under `GET /watch?status=all` and creating a watch on the same reference
again re-enables this one.

204.description: The watch is disabled. The response has no body.

get.description: Lists your account's registered webhook endpoints, oldest first, paged like every list. `q` searches the URL.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

post.description:
Registers an HTTPS endpoint to receive event notifications. The
response includes the endpoint's `secret` **once** — store it; it is
not readable afterwards (it can be rotated via PATCH). The secret is
the HMAC key for the `X-CN-Signature` body signature on every
delivery. It is never sent itself: check the signature, not a header.

Endpoint URLs must use `https` on port 443 or 8443, carry no username
or password, and name a host that already resolves to a public address
when you register it (a private, loopback or link-local address, or a
name that does not resolve, is refused with `422`). An account can
register at most 25 endpoints.

A URL the account already has is a `409` whose `error.existingWebhookId`
names the endpoint: change its events with `PATCH /webhooks/{webhookId}`,
or get a new secret with `rotateSecret`. This is checked before the
25-endpoint limit.

secret.description: The endpoint's signing secret — shown only in this response.

409.description: The account already has an endpoint at this URL.

error.reason: This URL is already registered as webhook endpoint 12. Change its events with PATCH /webhooks/12, or get a new secret with rotateSecret.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** webhooks:read

The values `events` accepts when you register or update a webhook. `*`
subscribes to every event, including ones added later.

Fetch this rather than hardcoding a list: it grows as we add events, and a
value that is not on it is rejected. `ping` is not listed because you never
subscribe to it; the test call sends it to any webhook.

Each item has the shape `GET /watch/event-types` uses, with a label to show
a reader. `referenceType` is always null here.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint's `id`.

patch.description:
Change the URL or subscribed events, re-enable a disabled endpoint
(`isActive: true` — resets the failure streak), or rotate the secret
(`rotateSecret: true` — the new secret is returned once in this
response).

**Rotating without dropping a delivery.** The previous secret stays valid
for `rotationOverlapHours` (default `24`, at most `168` — 7 days; `0`
ends it at once). During that window every delivery's `X-CN-Signature`
carries two signatures, the new secret's first:
`t=<timestamp>,v1=<new>,v1=<old>`. Accept a delivery if **any** `v1`
matches a secret you hold, so you can deploy the new secret whenever
suits within the window. `previousSecretExpiresAt` on the endpoint says
when the old one stops. Once your receiver checks the new secret, send
`endRotationOverlap: true` to stop the old one at once.

`filters` replaces the endpoint's filters; empty lists remove them.

`rotateSecret: true` REQUIRES an `Idempotency-Key` header (`400`
without one) — rotation is not naturally idempotent, so a client retrying
a request whose response it never saw must not silently rotate a secret
it never read. With the header set, a retry of the exact same request
replays the already-rotated secret instead of minting another one. An
update that does not rotate the secret runs without the header too, but
send one on every update so a client never has to tell them apart.

url.description: Same rules as when registering — `https` on port 443 or 8443, no credentials in the URL, and a host that already resolves to a public address.

rotationOverlapHours.description: With `rotateSecret`: how many hours the previous secret keeps signing deliveries alongside the new one.

endRotationOverlap.description: `true` once your receiver checks the new secret: the previous one stops signing deliveries now. Does nothing outside a rotation window.

secret.description: Present only when `rotateSecret` was true — shown once.

delete.description: Removes the endpoint. Pending deliveries settle without being sent; delivery history is retained.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint's `id`.

post.description:
Limit: 10 per minute for the account (webhook send), shared by test, redeliver, replay-dead and event re-send.

Queues a `ping` event delivery to the endpoint (regardless of its
subscribed event list) so you can verify connectivity and
authentication. With an `eventType`, it queues a sample of that event
instead, in the event's own shape, so you can test your handler for it.
Either way the delivery has `test: true` and its `data` describes
nothing real. A `409` is returned if the endpoint is disabled, or
already holds 100 queued deliveries.

eventType.description: The event to send a sample of. Any subscribable type except `*`. Leave it out for a `ping`.

202.description: Queued

get.description:
Every delivery to every one of your endpoints, removed ones included, most
recent first. Each delivery's `webhookId` says which endpoint it went to.
Filter to one with `endpoint`, and by the same fields as an endpoint's own
list. Paged like it too: by `page`, or by following `nextCursor` (pass it
back as `cursor` until it is `null`); a cursor page carries `perPage`,
`nextCursor` and `results` only. `q` searches the event type and event id.

parameters.name: endpoint
parameters.description: Return only deliveries to this endpoint, by its `id`. Another account's endpoint, or anything that is not an endpoint id, matches nothing.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only deliveries in these states, one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Return only the deliveries of this event.

parameters.name: eventType
parameters.description: Return only deliveries of this event type (`ping` included). An unknown type is a `422`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Return only deliveries made at or after this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day, on your `CN-Time-Zone` calendar when you send one, UTC's otherwise.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Return only deliveries made at or before this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone includes the whole of that day, on your `CN-Time-Zone` calendar when you send one, UTC's otherwise. Not before `from`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending, in place of newest first. A sorted list has no cursor (`nextCursor` is `null`). An unknown field is `422`.

total.description: Deliveries matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page, a page that was not full, or a sorted list.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint's `id`.

get.description:
The endpoint's delivery history, most recent first — what we sent, when,
what your endpoint answered, and why an attempt failed.

Use it to answer "did that event reach us?" without raising a support
ticket. Filter to `dead` to see only what exhausted its retries — or
was never attempted: a `dead` delivery with `attempts: 0` is an event
that occurred while the endpoint was disabled. It was recorded, not
sent; replay-dead after re-enabling delivers it.

History is retained even after the endpoint is removed.

To walk the whole history while new deliveries are made, follow
`nextCursor`: pass it back as `cursor` until it is `null`. A cursor page
carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results` only. `q` searches the event
type and event id.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Return only deliveries in these states, one or several, comma-separated. Case does not matter. Any other value is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending, in place of newest first. A sorted list has no cursor (`nextCursor` is `null`). An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: Return only the deliveries of this event, to answer "did you send event X?".

parameters.name: eventType
