parameters.description: Return only deliveries of this event type (`ping` included). An unknown type is a `422`.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Return only deliveries made at or after this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day, on your `CN-Time-Zone` calendar when you send one, UTC's otherwise.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Return only deliveries made at or before this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone includes the whole of that day, on your `CN-Time-Zone` calendar when you send one, UTC's otherwise. Not before `from`.

total.description: Deliveries matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page, a page that was not full, or a sorted list.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint id.

parameters.name: deliveryId
parameters.description: The delivery id.

get.description:
One delivery: what we sent, when, and what your endpoint answered. A
delivery of another endpoint or another account is a `404`.

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint's `id`.

parameters.name: deliveryId
parameters.description: The delivery's `id`, from `GET /webhooks/{webhookId}/deliveries`.

post.description:
Limit: 10 per minute for the account (webhook send), shared by test, redeliver, replay-dead and event re-send.

Sends a past event to the endpoint again.

The replay carries the **same `eventId`** as the original, so a handler
that de-duplicates on `eventId` — as the webhooks guide recommends — sees
the same event rather than a new one. It also carries the **original
`occurredAt`** (when the event actually happened, not when it was
replayed) but gets its own, later `sequence` number, since delivering it
again is a new event in your endpoint's delivery order. It is recorded as
a new delivery with its own id; the original is left untouched, so the
history stays a faithful record of what happened.

Any settled delivery may be replayed, including one that was delivered
successfully — useful when your side acknowledged an event and then lost
it. A delivery still `queued` cannot: its first attempt has not resolved
yet, and a replay would race it (`409`).

Redelivery is allowed even while the endpoint is currently disabled
(auto-disabled after 20 consecutive failures) — that is precisely the
state the dead letters you are trying to recover are stuck in, and making
you re-enable the endpoint first would reset the failure count that is
the evidence of what went wrong.

A delivery is replayed once. Redelivering one that was already replayed
sends the newest replay of that event again, and is refused with `409`
while that replay is still `queued`. It is also refused with `409` while
the endpoint holds 100 queued deliveries.

202.description: Queued

parameters.name: webhookId
parameters.description: The webhook endpoint's `id`.

post.description:
Limit: 10 per minute for the account (webhook send), shared by test, redeliver, replay-dead and event re-send.

Redelivers every currently `dead` delivery for this endpoint in one call,
mirroring `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/deliveries/{deliveryId}/redeliver`
for the whole backlog instead of one at a time.

Allowed even while the endpoint is disabled — an endpoint auto-disabled
after 20 consecutive failures is exactly the situation with dead letters
worth replaying, and requiring a re-enable first would reset the failure
count that is the evidence of what broke.

Each individual redelivery follows the same rules as the single-delivery
endpoint (new row, same `eventId`, original `occurredAt`, a fresh
`sequence`); a delivery that stops being eligible between listing and
replay (e.g. it settled, or its endpoint was removed) is skipped rather
than failing the whole batch.

Each delivery is replayed once. A dead delivery that was already
replayed is skipped; if that replay died too, the replay is the one
retried. Calling this again therefore queues nothing for deliveries it
already replayed.

An endpoint holds at most 100 queued deliveries. The call replays up to
that many and is refused with `409` while the endpoint is already at it;
wait for the queue to settle, then call again.

202.description: Queued

replayed.description: How many dead deliveries were requeued.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Your end users, by name. Archived end users are left out unless you ask
for them with `status`.

`q` matches part of the name, the number, or the email. The email of an
end user whose contacts a family violence safety record withholds is
never matched, so the search cannot confirm it.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only end users with this status. Left out lists active and suspended ones.

parameters.name: externalRef
parameters.description: Only the end user with exactly this reference of yours.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:create

Creates an end user with the fields and rules of the End User form in
the portal. They are sent a welcome email in your branding, as when you
add one in the portal.

billingAddress.description: Left out or null, bills go to the service address.

post.summary: Find an End User by Identity Details
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Limit: 20 per minute for the key.

Finds the one end user a caller is, from the details they give you, such
as a name, an email and a mobile. Built for a front desk or phone tool
that should find one caller without listing everyone.

It answers only when **at least three** of the details you send match
the same end user exactly. The name counts as one. Case and spacing are
ignored, a phone number is compared in one format (0400 000 001 and +61
400 000 001 are the same), and an ABN by its digits.

Every miss answers the same `404`: too few details, a wrong one, no end
user, or more than one. The call cannot tell you which detail was wrong.

- A POST, so the details never appear in a URL or a log.
- Each call is audited with the names of the details sent, never their
  values, and whether it matched.
- The answer carries no contact details, so it is the same for an end
  user whose contacts a family violence safety record withholds.
- For such an end user, their email, phone and service address never
  count as a match, so a lookup that needs one of them is the same `404`
  as for no end user. Their name and ABN alone are too few.

serviceAddress.description:
The service address, as text ("12 Example Street, Brisbane City
QLD 4000"), or `{"gnafId": "..."}` for one picked from
`GET /addresses/search`.

200.description: The one end user the details match.

contactsMasked.description: True while a family violence safety record withholds their contacts. Read the end user with care.

404.description: No single end user matches enough of the details. Every miss answers this way.

error.reason: No single end user matches those details.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

One end user, archived ones included. While a family violence safety
record withholds their contacts, the contacts and addresses are null and
`contactsMasked` is true.

It also says whether the end user's final invoice can be issued now,
the same check as `GET /end-users/{endUser}/invoices/final` and the
portal's Final Invoice button: `finalInvoiceAllowed`,
`finalInvoiceEarliestDate` and `finalInvoiceReasons`. The list does not
carry these fields.

finalInvoiceAllowed.description: Whether the final invoice can be issued now.

finalInvoiceEarliestDate.description: The earliest it can be issued, when that is known.

finalInvoiceReasons.description: What is still open, each with a stable `code`. Empty when allowed, except for one `already_billed_through_end` when the last invoice already billed everything, so issuing makes no new invoice.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Changes any of the end user's details; a field you leave out stays as
it is. The rules are those of the End User form in the portal.

- **Addresses** are refused here (422). Change them with
  `PATCH /end-users/{endUser}/addresses`, which also updates the
  emergency services (IPND) record of their numbers.
- **Masked contacts**: while a family violence safety record withholds
  the end user's contacts, a change to `email`, `phone`, `billingEmail`,
  `altContactName` or `altContactPhone` is refused (422).
- **Archived** end users are not changed (409). Restore them first.
- **Time zone**: their bills are cut on `timezone`, and their portal shows
  times in it. A change applies from their next billing period: the
  period already open keeps the zone it started in. Null is your zone.

timezone.description:
The end user's own time zone, one of `Australia/Brisbane`, `Australia/Sydney`,
`Australia/Melbourne`, `Australia/Adelaide`,
`Australia/Perth`, `Australia/Darwin` or `Australia/Hobart`.
Any other is refused (422). Null clears it, so they are in
your zone.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Changes the end user's service address, billing address, or both, as
the end user can on their Profile page in the end-user portal. This is
the only call that changes an end user's addresses.

The service address is also the address emergency services are given
for the end user's numbers (their IPND record). When it moves, `ipnd`
says what happened to that record:

- `applied`: the address was picked from `GET /addresses/search` (send
  its `gnafId`), and the record is being updated.
- `referred`: the address was typed in, so it cannot be carried into
  the record. Confirm the end user's emergency address yourself.
- `unchanged`: the service address did not move. A billing-only change
  never touches the record.

While a family violence safety record withholds the end user's
contacts, the change is made but the addresses are not returned.
An archived end user is not changed (409).

schema.description: Send at least one of the three. A field you leave out stays as it is.

gnafId.description: The address's id from `GET /addresses/search`, when picked from it.

billingSameAsService.description: True to send bills to the service address.

billingAddress.description: The billing address. Null is the service address.

contactsMasked.description: True when the addresses below are withheld by a family violence safety record.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

The end user's default screening of international calls to their lines,
as they see it on their Profile page in the end-user portal, whether
they get billing texts, and whether you bill them through the platform.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Sets the end user's default for international calls to their lines,
for example after a scam-call complaint. It screens incoming calls only:
it never affects an outgoing call, and never a 000 call. A field you
leave out stays as it is. An archived end user is not changed (409).

`billingSms: false` stops their billing texts when they ask you to,
as the switch on their page in the portal does; `true` starts them again.
Their billing emails still go.

`isBilled: false` stops billing them through the platform, for an end
user you bill some other way; `true` bills them again from their next
bill, which covers its whole period, never an earlier one. While you
bill your end users, `true` is refused (422) until every service of
theirs has a retail price, a call plan or a markup that covers it; the
error says what to set. Each change is in your Audit Log.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Your own notes on the end user, as on the Notes tab of their page in the
portal: pinned first, then newest. The end user never sees them.

post.summary: Add a Note to an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Adds a note. Notes are append-only: to correct one, add another. The
note names this API key as its author, in the portal too. Its text is
never written to the audit log.

parameters.name: noteId
parameters.description: The note's `id`.

patch.summary: Pin or Unpin an End User's Note
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Pins or unpins a note. A note's text never changes (422 if you send
`body`): add a new note to correct one.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Removes a note written in error. The audit log records that it went,
not what it said.

get.summary: List an End User's Safety Records
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:read

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** These are family violence
safety records under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship and
Family Violence) rules (F2025L00664). Read the End users safety help
page before you use it.

The end user's records, active first, then newest, with every field the
portal shows.

post.summary: Raise a Safety Record on an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Raises a safety record when the end user discloses domestic or family
violence. With `suppressContactDisclosure` (the default), their contacts
are masked on every end-user read from then on, here and in the portal.
Audited, naming this key.

get.summary: Get an End User's Safety Record
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:read

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

One record, with the time and the person of each step. A step taken by
API names no person here; the audit log names the key.

patch.summary: Change an End User's Safety Record
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Changes the record's fields. A field you leave out stays as it is. A
closed record is not changed (409).

post.summary: Confirm It Is Safe to Communicate
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Records that the person confirmed it is safe for them to communicate
(s8(1)). Support can be recorded only after this. A closed record is not
changed (409).

>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Records that the available support was explained to the person (s8(2)).
Refused (409) until it is confirmed safe to communicate, and on a closed
record.

post.summary: Record Whether Further Support Is Wanted
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Records whether the person wants further information and support
(s8(3)). Refused (409) until it is confirmed safe to communicate, and on
a closed record.

post.summary: Close an End User's Safety Record
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:update

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Closes the record. It is never deleted: `retentionExpiresAt` is set to
the earliest it may be disposed of (s31). A record already closed is not
changed (409).

post.summary: Reveal an End User's Masked Contacts
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** safety:read

**Legal obligations attach to this endpoint.** Read the End users safety
help page before you use it.

Returns the contacts a family violence safety record masks on every
other end-user read. Every call is audited as a reveal, naming this key,
whether or not anything was masked. Without this scope, no call shows
them.

post.summary: Send an End User a Verification Code
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Sends a six digit code to the end user's own mobile (`sms`) or email,
so you can check the person you are talking to controls it. You never
supply the address: the code goes to the contact on file. While a family
violence safety record is active on the end user, it goes only to the
record's agreed safe contact for that channel, or not at all (422).

The SMS goes from one of your approved SMS senders. With more than one,
name it in `smsFrom`. The email goes in your branding.

The code is advisory: a right code records `lastVerifiedAt` on the end
user, and no other call needs it. It expires in 10 minutes. At most five
codes go to one end user in an hour (429 after that). Each send is
audited with the reason and this key's name, never the code.

reason.description: Why the code is being sent, for the audit log.

smsFrom.description: The approved sender to send the SMS from, when you have more than one.

202.description: The code was sent.

destination.description: Where it went, masked, such as `*******001` or `j***@example.com`.

parameters.name: verificationId
parameters.description: The `verificationId` the send returned.

post.summary: Check an End User's Verification Code
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Checks the code the person read back. A right code answers `verified:
true` and records `lastVerifiedAt`. A wrong code, one already used, one
expired, one with five wrong tries, or an unknown verification all
answer the same `verified: false`. Each check is audited with its
outcome and this key's name, never the code.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

The logins to the end user's own portal, and the invites not yet
accepted, as on the Logins card of their page in the portal.

post.summary: Invite a Login for an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update, end-users:sign-in

Emails an invite, in your brand, to set up a login to the end user's
portal. A login is a way into the portal, so it needs `end-users:sign-in`
as well as `end-users:update`, as a portal session does. Refused (422) when a login or an open invite already has that
email. 409 when your end-user portal is off or has no domain yet.

parameters.name: loginId
parameters.description: The login's `id`.

patch.summary: Change an End User Login's Role
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update, end-users:sign-in

Changes the login's role. A role can widen a way into the portal, so it
needs `end-users:sign-in` as well as `end-users:update`. Their portal keeps an Owner while it has
other logins, so taking the role from their only Owner is refused (422).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Removes the login: it can no longer sign in. Removing their only Owner
while other logins remain is refused (422); removing the last login of
all is allowed.

parameters.name: loginId
parameters.description: The login's `id`.

post.summary: Send an End User Login a Password Reset
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update, end-users:sign-in

Emails the login a password reset link, in your brand: the answer to
"I'm locked out". No call ever sets a password. When a link was sent a
moment ago, `sent` is false: that link is still live, and no second one
goes. Where the end user has a family violence safety record, the link
goes to the safe contact on it (`outcome` is `sent_to_safe_contact`), or
is held when the agreed contact method allows no email (`outcome` is
`held`, `sent` is false, and our staff are alerted to contact them the
agreed way). 409 when your end-user portal is off or has no domain yet.

parameters.name: inviteId
parameters.description: The open invite's `id`.

delete.summary: Revoke an End User Login Invite
delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Revokes an open invite: its link stops working.

parameters.name: inviteId
parameters.description: The open invite's `id`.

post.summary: Resend an End User Login Invite
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update, end-users:sign-in

Sends an open invite again, with a fresh link.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

The people the end user has authorised to act for them, as on their
page in the portal: active ones first, then newest. A revoked one is
kept as history and confers no authority. Check this before acting on
the word of someone who says they speak for the end user.

post.summary: Appoint a Representative for an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Records someone the end user has authorised to act for them, with at
least one area. `full` covers every area. Audited, naming this key.

parameters.name: repId
parameters.description: The representative's `id`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Ends the representative's authority at once. The record is kept as
history. Revoking one already revoked changes nothing. A representative
of another end user is a 404.

>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Suspends the end user, as **Suspend** on their page in the portal does,
for your own non-payment or abuse cases. Their voice services and VPN
seats are cut off; their data services keep running (only we suspend a
data service, and one we suspend says how soon in `suspensionTakesEffect`
on GET /data/services/{ref}). A 000 call still
goes through. An end user already suspended is answered as it stands.

- An end user on the Priority Assistance register is suspended too,
  with the `reason` you give. The suspension and its reason are recorded
  against their registration, naming your API key.
- An archived end user cannot be suspended (409).

reason.description: Why, shown on the end user as `suspendReason`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Lifts a suspension you placed, restoring only what it cut off. A
suspension Check Networks placed is refused (409) until we lift it. An
end user that is not suspended is answered as it stands.

>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Puts away a former end user. Their history stays, and their sign-in to
the end-user portal is closed. Only once nothing is live or owed: a live
service, an open order, or a balance either way is refused (409), with
each reason in `error.blockers`. A suspension Check Networks placed is
refused too (409).

409.description: The end user cannot be archived yet.

blockers.description: What stands in the way, one sentence each. Absent for a refusal that is not about blockers.

error.reason: This end user cannot be archived yet.
blockers: They have 1 live service. Cease or move them first.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Brings an archived end user back as active. An end user that is not
archived is answered as it stands.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

The services the end user owns, each with the billed assignment it
carries, and the numbers they hold. Not paginated.

post.summary: Give an End User a Service
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Gives the end user one of your data services, trunks or numbers. A
service another end user holds moves to this one. It then shows in the
end user's portal, and its charges and usage go on their bills.

This is a link on our side only: nothing changes at the carrier, such as
the nbn end user of record. A cancelled data service, a terminated trunk,
and another account's service are refused (422). An archived end user
takes no service (409); restore them first.

reference.description: A data service's service reference, a trunk's SIP username, or a number.

200.description: The service, now the end user's.

parameters.name: assignmentId
parameters.description: The assignment's `assignmentId` (a uuid), from `GET /end-users/{endUser}/services`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:update

Ends the assignment today: the end user is billed for it to the end of
today, on your calendar, and not after. The service itself is not
cancelled. An assignment already ended, today or before, keeps its end
date, so calling this again changes nothing.

Only for an account that bills its end users; otherwise this answers
404. An assignment of another end user answers 404 too.

post.summary: Sign an End User In to the End-User Portal
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:sign-in

A link that signs one of the end user's logins in to your end-user
portal and opens the page you choose: their dashboard, their bills, one
bill, one service or their support tickets. Send the end user to it from
your own app, for example to pay by card or direct debit, which only the
end-user portal takes.

The link works once, for 5 minutes, on your portal's own domain.
Opening it shows a page with a **Continue to your portal** button, and
only pressing the button uses the link, so a mail scanner or link
preview that fetches it leaves it working. It replaces the password
only: when the login has two-factor on, the portal
asks for the code first, and no page opens until it is given
(`twoFactor` says so). It signs in as `portalUser`, one of the end
user's active logins (see List End-User Logins). There is no default:
always name the login.

With `returnUrl`, the end user is sent there once signed in (after the
two-factor code, when asked for) instead of to `landing`. It must be an
`https` address on your own website's host or your end-user portal's
domain; any other is a `422`.

Refused with `403` and the code `no_end_user_portal_access` when the end
user cannot use the portal: the portal is off or has no domain, the end
user is archived, or they have no active login. A `portalUser`,
`invoiceId` or `assignmentId` that is not theirs is a `422`.

Each link is recorded in the end user's activity, naming the API key
and the login.

invoiceId.description: The bill to open, by its `id` (a ULID) on the end-user invoice calls. Required for `bill`, and only taken with it.

assignmentId.description: The service to open, by its `assignmentId` (a uuid) from List an End User's Services. Required for `service`, and only taken with it.

portalUser.description: The login to sign in as, by its `id` (a uuid) from List End-User Logins.

returnUrl.description: (Optional) Where to send the end user once signed in, instead of `landing`. An `https` URL on your own website's host or your end-user portal's domain.

url.description: Send the end user here. It works once.

portalUser.description: The login it signs in as.

twoFactor.description: Whether the portal asks that login for its two-factor code before the page opens.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

Every end-user import on the account, newest first: the ones sent by API
and the ones uploaded in the portal, partners' included.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:create

Make many end users at once, as the portal's End User import does, with
the same checks, duplicate rules and welcome email. Send the portal's
CSV file as `file` (multipart), or the same columns as JSON `rows`, up
to 2,000 rows.

Columns: `name` (required), `type` (`residential`, the default, or
`business`), `business_name` (required for a business), `email`,
`phone`, `external_ref` (your own reference) and `invite` (`yes` sends a
login invite to the end-user portal to `email`). In `rows`, the API's
camelCase names (`businessName`, `externalRef`) are taken too.

A row is passed over (`skipped`) when an end user with its email is
already there, or one with its name and external reference when it has
no email, or a row earlier in the file is the same. A row that fails a
check is `failed`, with the reason. The other rows are still made.

`validateOnly: true` runs every check and makes nothing (the portal's
Check File), answering `200` with what an import would do.
`sendWelcome: false` holds the welcome email to each new end user.

Up to 200 rows run at once and answer `201` with each row's outcome.
More run on the queue and answer `202` with the import `processing`:
read it with `GET /end-users/imports/{importId}` until it is `finished`,
or `failed` if its run stopped part-way.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required: a retry with the same key answers the
first import and never imports the rows twice.

file.description: The CSV file, as the portal takes it. Up to 10 MB.

business_name.description: Required when `type` is `business`, as this or `businessName`.

businessName.description: The same as `business_name`, in the API's own case.

external_ref.description: Your own reference for the end user.

externalRef.description: The same as `external_ref`, in the API's own case.

invite.description: Send a login invite to `email`, which is then required.

200.description: What an import of these rows would do (`validateOnly`). Nothing was made.

wouldSkip.description: Rows an import would pass over or fail.

201.description: The import, finished, with each row's outcome.

202.description: The import, processing on the queue.

parameters.name: importId
parameters.description: The import's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** end-users:read

One import: its status, its counts, and each row's outcome, the end
user made from it and the reason it was skipped or failed, as the
portal's import page shows them. An import of another account answers
`404`.

post.summary: Create End Users from Xero Contacts
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update, end-users:create

Create an end user from each contact you name in your Xero organisation
(see Search Xero Contacts), linked to that contact, as the portal's
Create End Users from Xero does. Each is a business, named after the
contact, with its email and, when it is a valid ABN, its tax number. Each
gets the welcome email, as any new end user does, and its invoices,
credit notes and payments go to the contact from then on.

A contact already linked to one of your end users, archived in Xero, or
not found is passed over and listed in `skipped`, so sending the same
list again makes no second end user.

Up to 50 contacts a call. Answers `409` while the account has no working
Xero connection.

The contacts are read from Xero one at a time, in the order sent. If
Xero fails part way, the end users already made stand (each has had its
welcome email): the answer is still `201`, with them in `created`, the
failure in `error`, and the contact it failed on and every one after it
in `notTried`. Send the list again to finish: the ones made are passed
over. If Xero fails before any end user is made, the answer is the error
alone, as for any other Xero call.

201.description: The end users made, the contacts passed over, and any contacts not tried because Xero failed part way.

contactId.description: The Xero contact it was made from, and is linked to.

endUser.description: The new end user's number.

skipped.description: Contacts already linked, archived or not found.

notTried.description: When Xero failed part way, the contact it failed on and every one after it; empty otherwise.

error.description: Why Xero stopped part way; `null` when every contact was tried.

message.example: Xero could not answer just now: Service Unavailable

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none; each type needs its own read scope

Find the number, trunk, data service, order, end user, port, emergency
address, ticket or invoice for a phone number, email, name or
reference in one call, as the portal's header search does, with the
same matches. Up to 5 hits of each type, in this order of types.

| Type | Matches | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `number` | the number in any format, or its alias | voice:read |
| `trunk` | its handle, alias or SIP username | voice:read |
| `dataService` | its service id, address, username or your reference | data:read |
| `order` | its PND, the carrier's ORD, or your reference | data:read |
| `endUser` | name, number, email or phone | end-users:read |
| `port` | its reference, the carrier's, or a number in it | voice:read |
| `emergencyAddress` | its label, customer name or street | voice:read |
| `ticket` | its reference or subject | tickets:read |
| `invoice` | its number (issued, paid or void) | billing:read |

Without `types`, every type the key holds the scope for is searched, and
the rest are left out. A type named in `types` without its scope is
refused with `403`, as is a key that holds none of these scopes.

An end user whose contact details a family violence safety record
withholds is found by name or number only, never by email or phone, and
a hit never shows a contact.

`href` is the API call that reads the hit, or null where there is none:
a port, a residential line, and an order not yet placed with the
carrier.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: What to look for. At least 2 characters.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: The types to search, comma separated. Every type the key may read when left out.

200.description: The hits, grouped by type in the order above.

id.description:
How the API names it: the number, the trunk's SIP username,
the service id, the order id, the end user's number, the
port's reference, the emergency address id, the ticket
reference or the invoice id.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: The outage's or maintenance window's reference, as `GET /outages` returns it.

get.summary: Get an Outage affecting your Services
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

One outage or planned maintenance window that touches your account,
open or resolved (within the register's retention period), in the same
shape as each item of `GET /outages`. One that does not touch your
account is a 404, as an unknown reference is; the public status site
shows every outage on the register.

post.summary: Assign Services to an End User
post.description:
Link up to 100 of your data services to one end user in one call, or
unlink them all with `endUser: null`. This is the portal's bulk
**Assign to End User** on the Data Services list, with the same rule and
the same audit entry for each service changed. The link is local: it
shows the service in the end user's portal and puts its charges and
usage on their bill; nothing changes at the carrier.

Each service is answered on its own, in the order sent:

- `assigned`: now linked as asked (to the end user, or to none).
- `unchanged`: it already was.
- `notFound`: no service of yours has that reference. Another account's
  service is `notFound` too.

One unknown reference does not stop the rest. An end user that is not
yours, or is archived, refuses the whole call with a 422 and changes
nothing.

The `Idempotency-Key` is required, as on the other bulk writes: a retry
with the same key answers as the first call did.

endUser.description: The end user to link the services to, by its public number; null to unlink them. Required, so an omitted field is never read as "unlink".

services.description: The services, each by its product reference (an NBN PRI or an Opticomm product) or its service reference (an AVC), as `GET /data/services` returns them.

endUser.description: The end user the services were linked to; null when they were unlinked.

service.description: The reference as you sent it.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Where automated mail goes, and whether your residential end users are
sent data usage notices, as Company Settings shows them in the portal.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Change the notification address, the usage notices, or both: only the
fields you send change. A sender must be one of `availableSenders`.

smsSender.description: Left out, the current sender is kept.

200.description: The settings as they now stand.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

The end-user portal's name, colour, support details, ticket switch,
email logo position and logos, as Portal Branding shows them in the
portal.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Change any of the branding fields: only the fields you send change, and
the portal's rules apply to the result. The display name is required,
so set it with your first change. A brand colour that does not reach
4.5:1 contrast against white is refused with its ratio. Logos are set
with `PUT /end-user-portal/logos/{variant}`. Each change is in your
audit log under this key's name.

200.description: The branding as it now stands.

parameters.name: variant
parameters.description: `light`, the main logo (also on your end users' invoices), or `dark`, the dark-mode logo.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

The stored logo image. 404 when none is set.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Replace a logo. Send the image as the multipart field `logo`. The light
logo is PNG or JPEG, as it is also your invoice logo; the dark logo is
PNG, JPEG or WebP. SVG is never accepted. The format is read from the
file's content, not its name, and the size cap is the portal's (1 MB
unless we have told you otherwise).

200.description: The branding, with the new logo.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Remove a logo. Removing one that is not set does nothing. A variant
other than `light` or `dark` answers `404`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

The custom domain claimed for your end-user portal, the DNS records to
publish and each record's last check. 404 when no domain is claimed.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Claim a hostname for your end-user portal, replacing any earlier claim.
Publish the records in the response, then call
`POST /end-user-portal/domain/verify`. A hostname already in use on the
platform, or our own edge hostname, is refused with a 422. An unverified
claim holds the hostname for seven days.

domain.description: A hostname, with no scheme or path.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Release the domain and any claim on it. The end-user portal stops
answering on it, and open end-user invites, whose links are built on
it, are revoked. 404 when no domain is claimed.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Limit: 5 per minute for the account (domain verify), as each call makes DNS lookups.

Check the claimed domain's DNS records now. When both pass, the domain
is verified and the end-user portal answers on it; otherwise the
response says which record is missing. 404 when no claim is waiting
to be verified.

200.description: The claim after the check, passed or not.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Your own family violence statement, its support channels, its approval
and whether it is ready to publish, as the portal's Retail Settings
shows it. Approve and publish it in the portal, at `portalUrl`. 404 while
the end-user portal is off on your account.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Save the statement's text. A field you leave out keeps its value; send
null or an empty string to clear one. Approval belongs to the wording
that was approved, so changing any of the six wording fields revokes it
and takes the statement off your portal until it is approved and
published again; `approvalRevoked` says when that happened.
`interimNotice` and `supportAvailableFrom` do not touch approval.

200.description: The statement as it now stands.

approvalRevoked.description: This change revoked an approval and unpublished the statement.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Add a way for an affected person to reach you, last in order. A web form
never counts as reaching a person, so `connectsToIndividual` is stored
false for one. 404 while the end-user portal is off on your account.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The channel's `id` (a uuid), as `GET /compliance/dfv-statement` lists it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Remove a support channel. 404 when your statement has no such channel,
or while the end-user portal is off on your account.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Your own complaints process, its contact details, its approval and
whether it is ready to publish, as the portal's Retail Settings shows
it. Approve and publish it in the portal, at `portalUrl`. 404 while the
end-user portal is off on your account.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Save the process. A field you leave out keeps its value; send null or an
empty string to clear one. Approval belongs to the summaries that were
approved, so changing either summary revokes it and takes the process
off your portal until it is approved and published again;
`approvalRevoked` says when that happened. The contact details do not
touch approval. `contactUrl` must be an `http` or `https` address, as it
is published as a link.

200.description: The process as it now stands.

approvalRevoked.description: This change revoked an approval and unpublished the process.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

The card and direct debit charges we started on your account, newest
first, so your system can see a payment under way before it reaches your
balance. A direct debit stays in flight for a few business days. Settled
charges appear on List Payments as well.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` for the charges still in flight, or one settled status. Any other value answers `400`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Your statement for a period, the same one the portal's Statement page
shows: the opening balance, every invoice, credit note, payment and
reversal in date order with the running balance, and the closing
balance. Amounts include GST. A debit is what you owed us more; a credit
is a payment or credit note.

Dates are in your account's own timezone. Leave both out for the
portal's default period. A date that is not a real date, or a `from`
after `to`, answers `422`. Set `format=csv` for the portal's CSV export.

>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Your credit warning settings, as the portal's Credit Alerts page holds
them: whether warnings are on, the percentages of your credit limit they
are sent at, the channels, and who receives them. With no recipients,
warnings go to `fallbackEmail`, your billing contact.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Change any of `enabled`, `thresholds` and `channels`; what you leave out
stays as it is. Thresholds come from `availableThresholds`. A setting the
portal would refuse answers `422`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Add one person to receive credit warnings: send `email` or `mobile`, not
both. A mobile that is not an Australian mobile answers `422`.

parameters.name: recipientId
parameters.description: The recipient's `id` (a uuid).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Stop sending credit warnings to one recipient. One that is not on your
account answers `404`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

The cards and direct debit authorities stored on your account, as the
portal's Payment Methods page lists them. Revoked ones are left out.
Adding a method stays in the portal, because it takes your card or bank
details on the payment provider's own page.

autopayMethodId.description: The `id` of the method autopay charges, or null when autopay is off.

parameters.name: methodId
parameters.description: The method's `id` (a uuid) from List Payment Methods.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Remove a stored method, as the portal does. When it was the default,
another stored method becomes the default. A method not on your account
answers `404`. This never takes a payment.

parameters.name: methodId
parameters.description: The method's `id` (a uuid) from List Payment Methods.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Make a stored method the default. A method not on your account answers
`404`. This never takes a payment.

200.description: The method, now the default, with the same fields as a List Payment Methods row, inside `result`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Every dispute you have raised on our invoices, newest first. While
invoice disputes are switched off, this answers `404`.

>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

The disputes on one invoice, and whether you can raise another: how much
is still disputable and when the window closes. `refusal` says why not
when `canDispute` is false. While invoice disputes are switched off, this
answers `404`.

200.description: The disputes and what can still be disputed.

disputable.description: The most a new dispute may be for, with GST.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Dispute all or part of an invoice, or one line of it, as the portal does.
The disputed amount is held off collection and reminders while the
dispute is open, and a support ticket is opened. Past the dispute window,
or for more than is disputable, this answers `422` naming `amount` or
`reason`. This never takes or refunds a payment.

amount.description: The amount disputed, with GST, up to two decimals.

lineId.description: The line disputed, by its `id` (a uuid) from the invoice's `lineItems`. Leave it out for the invoice as a whole.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

The groups that section our invoice to you, by name. Each group prints
as its own section with its PO number and subtotal; lines in no group
print under Other.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Add a group to our invoice. A name already used (ignoring case) answers
`422`. It applies from the next invoice.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: The group's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

One group on our invoice, with the services in it.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Rename a group or change its description, PO number or cost centre.
Only the fields sent change. It applies from the next invoice; issued
invoices keep the values they were issued with.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Remove a group with no services in it. A group that still has services
answers `422`: move them to another group, or out of groups, first.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: The group's `id` (a uuid).

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Make the group's services exactly this list. A listed service moves in
from any other group (a service is in at most one); a service left off
the list leaves groups and prints under Other. An empty list empties the
group. A service not on your account answers `422`. It applies from the
next invoice.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Every live service on our invoice to you, with its invoice group and its
own billing label, PO number and cost centre.

parameters.name: serviceRef
parameters.description: The service's reference, as invoice lines' `serviceRef`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

One service's place on our invoice. A service not on your account
answers `404`.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Set the service's own billing label, PO number and cost centre on our
invoice. Only the fields sent change; null or blank clears one, and a
cleared PO or cost centre falls back to the group's. Place the service
in a group with `PUT /account/invoice-groups/{groupId}/services`. It
applies from the next invoice.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Your partners' monthly commission runs, newest first, as the portal's
Partners page lists them. Read only: rates, finalising and recording a
payout stay in the portal. While partner commissions are switched off,
this answers `404`.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: One partner's user id. One that is not your partner answers `422`.

gstShown.description: Whether the portal shows these figures with GST.

parameters.name: runId
parameters.description: The run's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

One run with its breakdown by client and product, and the clawbacks it
took. Another account's run answers `404`.

repayment.description: An invoice paid again after a clawback, earning its commission back.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Clawbacks still to come off your partners' commission.

parameters.name: partner
parameters.description: One partner's user id. One that is not your partner answers `422`.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: The partner's user id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

One partner's commission rates: the default, any rate for a product type,
and any rate for one product. The most specific applies. A user who is
not your partner answers `404`.

>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The invoices you issued to your end users, newest first: issued, paid
and void ones. An invoice held for approval is on
[/end-users/invoice-approvals](#tag/End-User-Billing/operation/list_end_user_invoice_approvals)
until it is released. The invoices Check Networks issues to you are on
/account/invoices, and never here.

Answers 404 unless your account bills its end users.

`?format=csv` or `?format=ndjson` streams every matching invoice instead
of a page.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's invoices, by their number. An unknown number is a 422.

parameters.name: issuedFrom
parameters.description: Issued on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. The day is the one the invoice shows: on the time zone it was cut in (its `timezone`). Send `CN-Time-Zone` to read the date on your own zone instead. Leave either end open. A date that is not a real date, or a start after the end, answers `422`.

parameters.name: issuedTo
parameters.description: Issued on or before this date, the whole day included.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Invoice number contains this.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The end-user invoice's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

One invoice you issued to an end user, with its lines. An invoice of
Check Networks', a draft, one held for approval or another account's
answers 404.

>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The PDF the end user was sent, under your brand.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Sends an issued or paid invoice again, the same email the bill run sent,
to the end user's billing email address (or their email address if they
have no billing one). The call takes no address: a body naming one (`to`,
`email`, `cc`, `bcc` or `recipient`) is a 422, so an invoice never goes
anywhere else. An invoice can be resent three times an hour; a fourth is
a 422 that says when to try again.

For an end user with a family violence safety record it goes to the
safe email on that record. Where the method agreed with them does not
allow email, nothing is sent and the call is a 422 saying so; our team
is told to deliver it the agreed way.

get.summary: List Payments on an End-User Invoice
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The payments applied to this invoice, oldest first. Payments settle an
end user's invoices oldest first, so one payment can be part-applied
here and part to another invoice: `appliedToInvoice` is this invoice's
part. A payment later reversed is left off.

post.summary: Record a Payment on an End-User Invoice
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Records money the end user paid you outside the portal against an
issued invoice, as **Record Payment** does in the portal. It comes off
what they owe; more than the invoice's balance stays on their account
as credit. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: it names the payment, so a retry
with the same key records it once and answers 200 with `duplicate: true`.

amount.description: Inc. GST, as a dollar string.

paidOn.description:
The day the money was received: today or earlier, on
Brisbane's calendar. A later day is refused with a 422 on
`paidOn`.

amountDue.description: What is still owed on the invoice.
What is still owed on the invoice.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

How much of this invoice is left to credit: its total less the credit
notes already issued against it. Zero on a void invoice.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Issues a credit note against an issued or paid invoice, the one way to
correct it, as **Credit** does in the portal. The credit note is raised
on our side and answers 202; it is listed on
[/end-users/credit-notes](#tag/End-User-Billing/operation/list_end_user_credit_notes)
once issued, and emailed to the end user. More than is left to credit
is a 422 naming the amount left. 503 means billing could not be reached:
retry with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

The decision is the API key's own: the key's scopes are its authority,
and the audit log names the key, not a user.

amount.description: Inc. GST, as a dollar string. At least 0.01.

reason.description: Printed on the credit note.

202.description: The credit note is being issued.

post.summary: Pause Payment Reminders on an End-User Invoice
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

No payment reminder about this issued invoice goes out until `until`,
when reminders start again. The due date does not change, and the
invoice still shows as overdue. Pausing again replaces the date.

until.description: The day reminders start again. After today, on your calendar.

post.summary: Resume Payment Reminders on an End-User Invoice
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Lifts a pause at once. An invoice that is not paused answers as it is.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Invoices the bill run held instead of sending, because something on
them had no price, oldest first. Nothing is posted to the end user's
account or emailed while one is held. Release it as it stands, or price
what is listed in `unpriced` and rerun it.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Issues and sends a held invoice as it stands: what had no price is not
on it. Runs on our side and answers 202; the invoice then appears on
/end-users/invoices. An invoice no longer held, or already being
released or rerun, is a 409. 503 means billing could not be reached:
retry. The API key's own decision; the audit log names the key.

202.description: Being released.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Rebuilds a held invoice with your current prices and sends it. If
something is still unpriced it is held again. Runs on our side and
answers 202. An invoice no longer held, or already being released or
rerun, is a 409. 503 means billing could not be reached: retry. The API
key's own decision; the audit log names the key.

202.description: Being rerun.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The credit notes you issued to your end users, newest first. The
credit notes Check Networks issues to you are on /account/credit-notes.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's, by their number. An unknown number is a 422.

parameters.name: issuedFrom
parameters.description: Issued on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. The day is the one the credit note shows: on the time zone it was cut in (its `timezone`). Send `CN-Time-Zone` to read the date on your own zone instead. Leave either end open. A date that is not a real date, or a start after the end, answers `422`.

parameters.name: issuedTo
parameters.description: Issued on or before this date, the whole day included.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

One credit note you issued to an end user, with its lines.

>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The PDF the end user was sent.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: Preview an End User's Next Invoice
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

What the bill run would put on this month's invoice if it ran now,
built from the bill run's own lines and saving nothing. Usage is to
`usageTo`, so the figures can change before the invoice issues. `held`
says the bill run would hold it for approval, with what is `unpriced`.
`status` other than `preview` says why there is nothing to show: the
month is already invoiced, there is nothing to bill, the end user is
suspended, or their final invoice has issued.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: Check an End User's Final Invoice
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Whether the end user's final invoice can be issued now. It can once
every service assigned to them and every recurring charge of your own
has an end date, and the usage window after the last of them has
passed (three days by default, as usage takes that long to arrive).
Otherwise `finalInvoiceReasons` says what is still open, each with a
stable `code`, and `finalInvoiceEarliestDate` the earliest it can be
issued when that is known.

Codes: `final_invoice_already_issued`, `service_without_end_date`,
`charge_without_end_date`, `nothing_to_bill`, `usage_window_open`. New
codes may be added.

When your last invoice to the end user already billed everything through
the last end date (the monthly bill run got there first),
`finalInvoiceAllowed` is true and `finalInvoiceReasons` holds one
reason, `already_billed_through_end`: issuing makes no new invoice, and
marks the end user finally invoiced.

post.summary: Issue an End User's Final Invoice
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Bills the end user for everything since their last invoice up to the
end of their last service or charge, issues the invoice and emails it
now; the monthly bill run skips them from then on. It cannot be undone:
correct it with a credit note. Answers 201 with the invoice, whose
`status` is `held` when part of it had no price (release or rerun it
under /end-users/invoice-approvals). Refused with a 422 whose error
carries `reasons` (as the check above) and `earliestIssueDate`. 503
means billing could not be reached: retry. The API key's own decision;
the audit log names the key.

When the last invoice already billed everything through the last end
date, no invoice is made: the end user is marked finally invoiced
through that date, usage after it is refused from then on, and the
answer is a 200 with `code` `already_billed_through_end` and a
`message` saying so.

200.description: Nothing was left to bill. The end user is marked finally invoiced, with no new invoice.

finallyInvoicedThrough.description: The last service's end date, the day they are finally invoiced through.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Every invoice, payment, credit note and adjustment on the end user's
account between `from` and `to` (dates on your calendar), oldest first,
with the opening, running and closing balance. Defaults to the first of
the month two months back up to today. Pages by cursor: pass
`nextCursor` back as `cursor` until it is `null`.

One request covers at most 12 months: `to` may be up to 12 months after
`from` (1 January to the next 1 January is the longest). A longer range
answers 400; ask for it a year at a time.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

post.summary: Post an Adjustment to an End User's Account
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Changes what the end user owes without an invoice or credit note, for
example to write off a small balance. A positive `amount` adds to what
they owe; a negative one takes off it and pays their oldest unpaid
invoice first. The amount includes GST. It shows on their statement
with your `reason`. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: it names the adjustment,
so a retry with the same key posts it once and answers 200.

amount.description: Signed, inc. GST, as a dollar string. Not zero.

date.description: The day it was posted, on your account's time zone.

balance.description: What the end user owes now.

date.description: The day it was posted, on your account's time zone.

balance.description: What the end user owes now.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

Your end users' financial hardship cases, newest first.
`assessmentDueBefore` lists the applications still to assess whose
deadline falls on or before that day.

**Your obligations.** A hardship case read or decided through the API
carries the same obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial
Hardship) Industry Standard 2024 as one in the portal. You are the end
user's supplier and responsible for meeting them: the deadlines, the
options you offer, and the notices.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's, by their number. An unknown number is a 422.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: List an End User's Hardship Cases
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

One end user's hardship cases, newest first.

**Your obligations.** A hardship case read or decided through the API
carries the same obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial
Hardship) Industry Standard 2024 as one in the portal, and you are
responsible for meeting them.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Records an arrangement agreed with the end user (`status: active`), or
an application to assess (`status: proposed`), which then has an
assessment deadline in business days on your calendar. The end user is
sent the acknowledgement or the written confirmation under your brand,
as from the portal. `options` must be ones you offer
(/retail/hardship-options); a payment plan needs `instalmentAmount` and
`instalmentCount`, and fee or debt relief `reliefAmount`.

An end user has one case at a time: while one is under assessment
(`proposed`) or `active`, opening another answers `409` and sends
nothing. Assess or close that case first. Send an `Idempotency-Key`: it
is required, so a retry after a timeout replays the first answer and
never opens a second case or sends a second notice.

**Your obligations.** Opening a case through the API carries the same
obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship) Industry
Standard 2024 as opening it in the portal. You are responsible for
meeting them, and the case is recorded as made by the user who created
the API key.

parameters.name: caseId
parameters.description: The case's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

The outcome of an application under assessment: `approve` makes it an
active arrangement and sends the end user the written confirmation;
`decline` closes it and tells them the outcome. A case not under
assessment is a 409.

**Your obligations.** An assessment made through the API carries the
same obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship)
Industry Standard 2024 as one made in the portal, and you are
responsible for meeting them. It is recorded as the API key's own
decision, with no user.

parameters.name: caseId
parameters.description: The case's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Closes a case as `completed`, `cancelled` or `declined`. A closed case
is a 409.

**Your obligations.** Closing a case through the API carries the same
obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship) Industry
Standard 2024 as closing it in the portal, and you are responsible for
meeting them. It is recorded as made by the user who created the API
key.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

The financial hardship assistance you offer your end users.

**Your obligations.** The Telecommunications (Financial Hardship)
Industry Standard 2024 applies to these options set through the API as
in the portal, and you are responsible for meeting it.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Replaces the assistance you offer. At least six options (s18(1) of the
Standard); fewer is a 422. Stored in the catalogue's order.

**Your obligations.** Setting these through the API carries the same
obligations under the Telecommunications (Financial Hardship) Industry
Standard 2024 as setting them in the portal, and you are responsible
for meeting them.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

Disputes your end users raised about charges on their invoices, newest
first. While one is open, the disputed amount is not taken by
automatic payment and is left out of payment reminders.

**Your obligations.** A dispute handled through the API carries the
same obligations as one handled in the portal (the complaints-handling
and financial hardship rules you are bound by as the end user's
supplier), and you are responsible for meeting them.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's, by their number. An unknown number is a 422.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:read

One dispute, with what the end user said and where your decision is.

**Your obligations.** A dispute handled through the API carries the
same obligations as one handled in the portal, and you are responsible
for meeting them.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Shows the end user you are looking at an open dispute. It stays open,
so the disputed amount is still held. Runs on our side and answers 202.
A dispute not open is a 409; 503 means billing could not be reached.

**Your obligations.** A decision made through the API carries the same
obligations as one made in the portal (the complaints-handling and
financial hardship rules you are bound by as the end user's supplier),
and you are responsible for meeting them. It is the API key's own
decision, and the audit log names the key.

202.description: The dispute, with the decision in progress.

post.summary: Credit and Resolve an End-User Dispute
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

The end user was right: a credit note for `amount`, up to the amount
disputed, is issued against their invoice and the dispute is resolved.
Runs on our side and answers 202; `resolution` shows the outcome and
the credit note. A resolved dispute, or one with a decision already in
progress, is a 409. 503 means billing could not be reached.

**Your obligations.** A decision made through the API carries the same
obligations as one made in the portal, and you are responsible for
meeting them. The end user is emailed the decision. It is the API
key's own decision, and the audit log names the key.

amount.description: Inc. GST, as a dollar string.

notes.description: Shown to the end user with the decision.

202.description: The dispute, with the decision in progress.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Resolves a dispute without a credit: `reject` (the charge stands) or
`no_change` (nothing owed either way, for example they withdrew it).
Collection of the amount resumes. Runs on our side and answers 202. A
resolved dispute, or one with a decision already in progress, is a 409.
503 means billing could not be reached.

**Your obligations.** A decision made through the API carries the same
obligations as one made in the portal, and you are responsible for
meeting them. The end user is emailed the decision. It is the API
key's own decision, and the audit log names the key.

202.description: The dispute, with the decision in progress.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail-cases:update

Sends the last decision again, exactly as it was asked, after
`resolution.error` says it could not be completed. With no failed
decision to send, or one still in progress, it is a 409.

**Your obligations.** A decision made through the API carries the same
obligations as one made in the portal, and you are responsible for
meeting them.

202.description: The dispute, with the decision in progress.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The groups that section the invoices you send this end user, by name.
Each group prints as its own section with its PO number and subtotal;
lines in no group print under Other. `404` unless you bill your end
users.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Add a group to this end user's invoices. A name already used by this
end user (ignoring case) answers `422`. It applies from the next invoice.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: The group's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

One of this end user's groups, with the services in it.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Rename one of this end user's groups or change its description, PO
number or cost centre. Only the fields sent change. It applies from the
next invoice; issued invoices keep their values.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:delete

Remove one of this end user's groups with no services in it. A group
that still has services answers `422`: move them first.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: groupId
parameters.description: The group's `id` (a uuid).

put.summary: Set End User Invoice Group Services
put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Make the group's services exactly this list, as
`PUT /account/invoice-groups/{groupId}/services` does. Only this end
user's own services can be listed; any other answers `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

This end user's live services, each with its group and its own billing
label, PO number and cost centre on the invoices you send it.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

One of this end user's services and its place on their invoices. A
service that is not this end user's answers `404`.

put.summary: Set End User Invoice Service Details
put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Set the service's own billing label, PO number and cost centre on this
end user's invoices. Only the fields sent change; null or blank clears
one. It applies from the next invoice.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Your markups and every product you have priced for your end users. A
product given to an end user bills, in order, at the service's own
price, else its price here, else its type's markup on what we charge
you, else your default markup, else nothing (and the end user's invoice
is held for you to approve). Calls are priced by a call plan only.

Answers 404 unless your account bills its end users.

defaultMarkupPct.description:
Your default markup, a percentage of what we charge you.
Null when none is set.

markupsByType.description:
Your markups by product type (service category), each a
percentage of what we charge you. A type not listed uses
the default markup. Empty when none is set.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Set or clear your default markup, your markups by product type, or
both. A product you have not priced bills at what we charge you plus
its type's markup, else the default markup. With neither, a product you
have not priced bills nothing, and its end user's invoice is held for
you to approve. A price you set for a product or a service always wins
over a markup.

A call with no call plan bills at what we charged you for it plus its
call category's markup (such as `au_mobile_calls`), else the default
markup; a call plan always wins. Send at least one of the two fields; one you leave out stays as it is.

While you bill your end users, clearing the default or a type's markup
is `422` on `defaultMarkupPct` when it would leave a live service of an
end user you bill with nothing to price it. The error counts them and
names up to five; nothing is changed. Both fields are checked together,
so a type's markup set in the same request counts.

defaultMarkupPct.description:
The markup, a percentage of what we charge you, as a number or
a numeric string ("30.00"), from 0 to 9999. Null clears it.

markupsByType.description:
Your markups by product type, the whole set: a type left out,
or sent as null, uses the default markup. Keyed by the
product's service category (for example `hosted_pbx`,
`data_and_internet`, `payg_sip_channels`,
`au_geographic_numbers`, `sms`, `au_mobile_calls`).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Price a product for your end users. The product must be one of ours on
sale, and not already in your book: change its price instead.

`price` and `setupFee` are **ex-GST** dollar amounts, as the portal takes
them. GST is added on the end user's invoice under your tax settings.

productId.description: The product's public id, as the unpriced queue and the price book return it.

price.description: The price each period, ex-GST, in dollars, up to two decimals.

setupFee.description:
The setup fee, ex-GST, in dollars. Leave it out or null for
none set; 0 is a free connection.

effectiveFrom.description: The day the price applies from. Today when left out or null.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The price's `id` (a uuid), from the price book.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Change a product's price. `price` is **ex-GST**. Every end user on the
product moves to the new price: there are no grandfathered prices. A
month already invoiced keeps what it was charged.

price.description: The price each period, ex-GST, in dollars.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:delete

Take a product out of your price book. Its end users then bill at your
markup for its type, else your default markup. While you bill your end
users, removing it is `422` on `itemId` when nothing else would price a
live service of an end user you bill: the error counts them and names up
to five. Price them another way first, or mark the service or the end
user not billed.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The price's `id` (a uuid), from the price book.

put.summary: Set a Product's Default Call Plan
put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

The call plan that prices a voice product's calls for end users whose
service has no plan of its own. Only one of your own published call
plans; null clears it. While you bill your end users, clearing it is
`422` on `planId` when no markup would price those calls on a live
service of an end user you bill; the error counts them and names up to
five.

planId.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid) from List Retail Plans.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Products you have given your end users that your price book does not
price. One billing at your default markup carries that price as
`proposedPrice`, to accept in one call. One nothing prices
(`bills: false`) holds its end users' invoices until you price it.

endUsers.description: How many live services of your end users are on it.

bills.description: True when it bills at your default markup; false when it holds invoices.

proposedPrice.description: The default markup's price, ex-GST with its GST under the product's GST treatment (none on a GST-free product), as the price it becomes when accepted. Null when nothing prices it.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The product's `productId` (a uuid), from the queue.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Write a queued product's proposed price (your default markup's) into your
price book from today, as a price of your own. It leaves the queue.
A product nothing prices has no proposal, and is refused (422): price it
with `POST /retail/price-book/items`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns a paginated list of your own call plans for your end users, by
name, each with its versions and their state. The destinations of a
version are at
[List Plan Destinations](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/list_retail_plan_destinations).

Only for an account that bills its end users: the route answers `404`
otherwise.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of plans per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing call plans.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Creates a call plan as a draft, one of three ways, as the portal's New
Plan page does:

  - **`blank`**: an empty plan. Add destinations, or import a CSV.
  - **`clone`**: a copy of a base card's version in effect (else its
    latest).
  - **`margin`**: your sell rates worked out from a base card you are
    billed on (your buy rates), with the `margin` you give. The connection
    fee is marked up too with a `percent` margin; a `fixed` margin adds to
    the per-minute rate only.

The base card is one from
[List Base Cards](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/list_retail_plan_base_cards):
one of your own plans, or a card you are billed on. Any other is refused
with `422`.

Nothing prices calls until you publish the draft with
[Publish a Call Plan](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/publish_retail_plan).

code.description: A code unique across all plans: letters, digits, underscore and hyphen. Leave it out or null for one made from your account number.

baseCardId.description: The card to start from, by its `id` from List Base Cards. Required for `clone` and `margin`.

margin.description: The margin over the base card. Used with `margin` only, and then `value` is required.

type.description: `percent` marks the per-minute rate and the connection fee up by `value` per cent. `fixed` adds `value` dollars to the per-minute rate.

value.description: Per cent for `percent`; dollars per minute, ex-GST, for `fixed`. Up to 6 decimal places.

roundingStep.description: Sell rates round up to this step, in dollars, at most 5 decimal places. Defaults to `0.00001`.

minMargin.description: The least the per-minute sell rate is above the buy rate, in dollars ex-GST, applied after the markup.

201.description: The plan was created as a draft.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns the cards a new plan may start from, by name, in one response:
your own plans, and the cards you are billed on. Pass one's `id` as
`baseCardId` to
[Create a Call Plan](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/create_retail_plan).

200.description: A JSON object containing the cards.

ownPlan.description: True for one of your own plans; false for a card you are billed on.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns one of your own plans with its versions. `draftDrift` compares a
draft made from a supplier deck with the deck's current buy rates, as the
portal's publish step does; it is null for any other plan, and when
nothing is below cost.

Another account's plan, or a card that is not yours, answers `404`.

belowCost.description: Prefixes that sell below their buy rate.

belowFloor.description: Prefixes that sell above cost but below the margin floor.

orphaned.description: Prefixes with no buy rate in the deck.

acknowledgementNeeded.description: True when publishing needs `acknowledgeDrift: true`: some prefix is below cost or below the floor.
