buyPerMinuteExGst.description: The deck's buy rate per minute, ex-GST.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Changes the plan's name, code, description or currency. Send only the
fields to change. These belong to the plan, not a version, so the change
is live at once and opens no draft.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Returns a paginated list of one version's destinations, by name then
prefix. Without `version`, the working version: the draft, else the
version in effect, else the latest.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version number. An unknown one is refused with `422`.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Only destinations whose name or prefix matches.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of destinations per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

200.description: A paginated JSON object containing destinations.

version.description: The version listed; null for a plan with no version yet.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Adds a destination to the plan's draft. When the plan has no draft, one
is opened first as a copy of its latest version: a published version
never changes. A prefix already on the draft is refused with `422`.

Rates are dollar amounts, **ex-GST**, to at most 5 decimal places.

connectionFee.description: The charge for each answered call, ex-GST. Defaults to `0`.

minimumCharge.description: The least an answered call costs, ex-GST. Defaults to `0`.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Loads a CSV into the plan's draft, opening the draft first when there is
none. The file has the portal's columns, with a header row, in any order:

```
name,prefix,per_minute_rate,connection_fee_rate,minimum_charge_rate,first_increment_seconds,subsequent_increment_seconds
Australia Mobile,614,0.03,0.05,0,60,60
```

`name`, `prefix` and `per_minute_rate` are required on each row; the fee
and minimum default to `0` and the increments to `60`. Rates are dollars,
**ex-GST**, to at most 5 decimal places. At most 20,000 rows.

The import is all or nothing: a file with any bad row is refused with
`422`, naming the first ten bad lines, and the draft is left as it was.

`mode` is `replace` (the draft becomes exactly the file) or `merge` (the
file's rows are added or replace those with the same prefix; the rest
stay).

200.description: The file was loaded into the draft.

importedVersion.description: The draft the file was loaded into.

destinationCount.description: The draft's destinations after the import.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: The destination's prefix, which names it on every version.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Changes a destination on the plan's draft, opening the draft first when
there is none. Send only the fields to change. The prefix cannot change:
remove the destination and add the new prefix. A prefix not on the
working version answers `404`.

Rates are dollar amounts, **ex-GST**, to at most 5 decimal places.

connectionFee.description: The charge for each answered call, ex-GST.

minimumCharge.description: The least an answered call costs, ex-GST.

200.description: The destination as changed, on the draft.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Removes a destination from the plan's draft, opening the draft first
when there is none. The published versions keep it until the draft is
published. A prefix not on the working version answers `404`.

parameters.name: planId
parameters.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Publishes the plan's draft as a version that never changes, pricing
calls from `effectiveFrom` (today when left out) for every service on the
plan. A published version it replaces from that date is marked
`superseded`, and still prices the calls made before it.

Refused with `422` when:
  - the plan has no draft, or the draft has no destinations;
  - the draft, made from a supplier deck, prices some prefix below the
    deck's buy rate or below its margin floor, and `acknowledgeDrift` is
    not `true`. See `draftDrift` on
    [Get a Call Plan](#tag/End-User-Call-Plans/operation/get_retail_plan).

effectiveFrom.description: The date the version prices calls from. Defaults to today when left out or null.

acknowledgeDrift.description: Publish although the draft prices below cost or below its floor.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: assignmentId
parameters.description: The service's `assignmentId` (a uuid), from List an End User's Services.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The call plan pinned to the service, its own price and setup fee, whether
it is billed, and the price that will bill with where it comes from.
Answers 404 unless your account bills its end users.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Set all four at once, as the portal's Service Billing dialog does:

- `planId`: one of your own published call plans, or null for the
  product's default plan. Any other plan is refused (422) and nothing is
  changed.
- `price` and `setupFee`: this service's own price each period and setup
  fee, **ex-GST** dollar amounts. Null goes back to your price book; 0 is
  free. At most 999,999.99. A month already charged keeps its price.
- `notBilled`: true leaves the whole service, its fees and its usage, off
  the end user's invoices from the next one built.

While you bill this end user, clearing `price` or `planId` is `422` on
`price` when nothing else (your price book, a markup or a call plan)
would price the service; nothing is changed. The four are checked
together, so clearing the price with `notBilled` true is allowed.

planId.description: The plan's `id` (a uuid) from List Retail Plans.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: assignmentId
parameters.description: The service's `assignmentId` (a uuid), from List an End User's Services.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

End the end user's billing for the service today, on your account's
calendar: it is billed to the end of today and not after. The service
itself is not cancelled with us.

A service whose billing has already ended, today or before, keeps its
end date, so calling this again changes nothing.

200.description: The service's billing, with its end date.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: List an End User's Own Charges
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Your own charges on the end user's bill, newest first, in one response.
Answers 404 unless your account bills its end users.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Add a recurring or once-off charge to the end user's next bill. Send an
`Idempotency-Key` so a retry does not add it twice.

`amount` is an **ex-GST** dollar amount, as the portal's form takes it,
from 0.01 to 999,999.99. GST is added on the invoice.

A recurring charge that starts in an earlier month must say what to do
with the months since then, so nothing back-bills by default: `billing`
`start` bills every month since `startsOn`; `later` bills from
`billFrom` (months you billed elsewhere are not billed again). Leaving
`billing` out for such a charge is refused (422). A charge that starts
this month or later bills from its start.

An archived end user is refused (422).

amount.description: Ex-GST, in dollars, up to two decimals.

startsOn.description: The start date (recurring) or the date of the charge (once-off).

endsOn.description: Recurring only. The last day it bills.

billing.description: Recurring only. Required when `startsOn` is in an earlier month.

billFrom.description: With `billing` `later`, the first day to bill from. Not before `startsOn`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

parameters.name: chargeId
parameters.description: The charge's `id` (a uuid).

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Change any of the fields sent; the rest stay. `amount` is **ex-GST**.

Once an invoice carries the charge:
  - a **once-off** charge can no longer change (422);
  - a **recurring** charge can change only its `description`, `amount`
    (for months not yet charged) and `endsOn`. Sending `startsOn`,
    `billing` or `billFrom` is refused (422).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:delete

Remove a charge no invoice carries. An invoiced charge is refused (422):
end a recurring one with `PATCH` and `endsOn` instead.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The settings printed on every invoice to your end users: the name and
ABN you bill as, default payment terms and delivery, the copy address,
summary or detailed format, the number prefix and next number, and how
end users pay you outside a gateway.

Only for an account that bills its end users: otherwise this answers 404.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Change any of your end-user invoice settings. Send only the fields to
change; null clears a field that can be blank. The next end-user
invoice uses the new values.

The running invoice number changes only when you send
`invoiceNextNumber`. Each bill run moves it on, so a PATCH of any other
field never winds it back.

abn.description: 11 digits that pass the ATO check digit. Spaces are allowed.

bpayBillerCode.description: Your own BPAY biller code, 3 to 10 digits. Spaces are allowed and removed, so `12 3456` is stored as `123456`.

200.description: The settings saved, all of them.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

When your end users are reminded of an overdue invoice, as Company
Settings → Payment Reminders sets it in the portal.

Only for an account that bills its end users: otherwise this answers 404.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Set the whole schedule. Days are from 1 to 365, and the final notice
must come after the first reminder. The change applies from the next
nightly reminder run and is recorded in your audit log as a change in
the portal is.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The notices your end users receive that you may reword: the compliance
notices (complaints and the like) and the end-user billing emails, as
Company Settings → Notice Wording lists them. In one response: the list
is not paginated.

Only for an account that bills its end users: otherwise this answers 404.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The notice's key, from List Notices.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

One notice's subject and body in effect (Markdown), and the Check
Networks default wording.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Save your own subject and body (Markdown) for a notice. The wording is
checked as in the portal, and refused with a 422 listing each problem
when it:
  - drops a placeholder in `requiredContent`;
  - uses a placeholder the notice does not offer;
  - types a working-days timeframe as text where the notice has a
    placeholder for it.

A notice's statutory footer is added on every send and cannot be
changed. To test a notice, send it to yourself from the portal.

body.example:
Hi {{ customer_name }},

Invoice **{{ invoice_number }}** is attached.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:update

Remove your own wording, so the notice is sent with the Check Networks
default. A notice you have not reworded is unchanged.

200.description: The notice, back on the default wording.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

Whether each payment gateway you take your end users' payments through
(Stripe, Square, GoCardless) is connected and working, and which payment
methods it is on for: one row per gateway, connected or not. Use it to
spot a broken gateway before your end users fail to pay.

Keys are checked when they are saved in the portal or a gateway is
switched back on; this read does not call the gateway. No key, webhook
secret or callback address is returned. Connecting, changing and
removing a gateway stay in the portal.

Only for an account that bills its end users: otherwise this answers 404.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

How much of the monthly spend limit you set on an end user is used this
month: the limit, spent so far with and without GST, the per cent, and the
alert tiers already reached. Spent is the end user's Next Bill Estimate,
the figure their spend alert emails and your portal show. Once the month's
invoice is issued, the estimate starts again from nothing.

An end user with no limit answers `result: null`. Set the limit on the
end user. `endUser.spendThreshold` tells you as each tier is reached.

200.description: The end user's spend this month.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

get.summary: List an End User's Own Usage
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:read

The usage you rated yourself for one end user, newest usage first, and
whether each record is billed yet. Only for an account that bills its
end users.

parameters.name: billed
parameters.description: `true` for billed records only, `false` for those still to bill.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first usage date to list.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last usage date to list.

200.description: A page of the end user's usage records.

post.summary: Add Own Usage for an End User
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Add one record of usage you rated yourself (managed-service hours, seats,
a third-party feed). It is billed on the end user's next invoice, at
your unit price ex GST, and locked once a held or issued invoice carries
it. Refused for a usage date in the future, or in a bill period the end
user already has a held or issued invoice for, and for a `reference`
already added on your account. Once the end user is finally invoiced,
a usage date after their last end date is refused too ("This end user
has had their final invoice, so usage after ... can't be added."), as no
invoice would bill it.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required: a retry with the same key returns the
first answer and never adds the record twice.

post.summary: Add Own Usage in a Batch
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:create

Add up to 500 records of usage you rated yourself, across your end
users, each naming its end user. All or none: if any row is refused,
nothing is added, and the `422` names every bad row by its index from 0
(`rows.3.reference`). The rules for each row are those of
`POST /end-users/{endUser}/usage`; a reference repeated within the batch
is refused too.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required: a retry with the same key returns the
first answer and never adds the batch twice.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

201.description: Every record was added, in the order sent.

parameters.name: usageId
parameters.description: The usage record's `id` (a uuid).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** retail:delete

Remove a record no held or issued invoice carries yet. A billed record is
refused with `422`: correct the invoice with a credit note instead.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:read

Whether your own Xero connection works, and why an end-user invoice,
credit note or payment has not reached Xero: the mapping problems still to
fix, how many entries are waiting, waiting on a contact or failed, and the
last push and error. It answers whether or not Xero is connected.

Only for an account that bills its end users: it answers `404` otherwise.
Connect and disconnect Xero from Integrations in the portal: they need a
browser sign-in to Xero.

>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:read

The end-user ledger entries behind one of the counts in Get Xero Status,
newest first, each with the end user, the invoice, credit note or payment
it is for, and why it is not in Xero:

  - `waiting`: not tried yet. The nightly push, or Send to Xero, sends them.
  - `unmatched`: the end user has no Xero contact yet. Link one with Link
    Xero Contact, or create one.
  - `partial`: sent in part. The next push finishes them.
  - `failed`: Xero refused them; `reason` says why. Fix it in Xero or here,
    and the next push tries again.

Answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Which list.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of entries per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:read

The accounts and tax rates your end-user documents go to in Xero, the
choices your chart of accounts offers for each, and what still stops a
push. Answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection, and
`502` when Xero cannot be read just now.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update

Choose the accounts and tax rates your end-user documents go to, as Save
does on Integrations → Xero in the portal. Only the mappings you send
change; send `null` or `""` to clear one. Each value must be one your
chart of accounts offers for that kind of mapping today (see `choices` in
Get Xero Mapping): any other is refused with `422` and nothing is saved.
Your chart is read from Xero again first.

The answer is the mapping as saved, with `problems` listing what still
stops a push. Answers `409` while the account has no working Xero
connection.

products.description: A sales account by product ID.

charges.description: A sales account by your own charge's ID.

pushPayments.description: Send payments you record to Xero too.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update

Send what is waiting to Xero now, rather than at the nightly push: the
same push as Send Now in the portal, which also retries anything failed,
sent in part or waiting on a contact. It is queued, and the answer is
`202` at once; Get Xero Status shows the counts and any error once it has
run, usually within a minute. A second ask while one is queued is the same
push. Each ask is in the account's Audit Log against the API key that
made it.

Answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection, and `503`
when the push could not be queued just now: nothing was sent, so ask
again shortly.

202.description: The push is queued.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:read

Contacts in your Xero organisation, to link an end user to. With
`search`, the contacts whose name matches; without it, a page of 100 in
name order. `endUser` names the end user already linked to a contact.

Answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection, and `502`
when Xero cannot be read just now.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: A name, or part of one.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Without `search`, which page of 100. Defaults to `1`.

id.description: The contact's Xero ID. Link it with Link Xero Contact.

status.description: Xero's status for the contact, `ACTIVE` or `ARCHIVED`.

endUser.description: The number of your end user already linked to this contact.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: The end user's number.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update

Link an end user to a contact in your Xero organisation, so their
invoices, credit notes and payments go to it. Entries waiting on a contact
for them are sent on the next push.

  - Send `contactId` to link a contact you chose (see Search Xero
    Contacts). One Xero does not have is refused with `422`.
  - Send `create: true` to create them in Xero instead. As the portal
    does, a contact with their number, or exactly their name, is linked
    rather than a second one made, and an archived one is refused with
    `422`.

Answers `409` while the account has no working Xero connection.

contactId.description: The Xero contact's ID. Needed unless `create` is `true`.

create.description: Create the end user as a new Xero contact.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** integrations:update

Remove an end user's link to their Xero contact, so the next push matches
them again (by their number, then exactly by name) or waits for you to
choose one. Nothing already in Xero changes.

200.description: The end user, now with no contact.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Pause a trunk at once, as the portal's Suspend Trunk does: for example to
stop a compromised PBX. A suspended trunk makes and receives no calls:
new outbound calls are refused, and calls to its numbers are refused
before they reach your PBX. It **still places 000 (and 112 and 106)
calls**, and for an hour after one, calls to its numbers are delivered so
the emergency service can call back. Its PBX stays registered, calls
already up carry on, and billing is unchanged. `POST /trunks/{username}/resume` reverses it.

Suspending a trunk that is already suspended answers `200` with the trunk
as it stands. The trunk then reads `status: suspended` and, when you
suspended it, `suspendedBy: account`.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Resume a trunk you suspended, as the portal's Resume Trunk does. Only your
own pause can be resumed: a trunk Check Networks suspended
(`suspendedBy: checkNetworks`, for example for non-payment) answers `409`
with the reason, and stays suspended until we lift the hold.

Resuming a trunk that is already active answers `200` with the trunk as it
stands.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Cancel the plan or channel change booked for the trunk's next billing
cycle (its `pendingPlanChange`), as the portal's Cancel does. The next
cycle keeps the trunk's current plan. Answers `404` when nothing is
booked. Sends a `trunk.planChangeCancelled` event.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's SIP digest username.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** secrets:read

Returns a trunk's current SIP username and password, for setting up a PBX
on an existing trunk without rotating its password.

Reading a secret has its own scope: `voice:read` does not reveal it. Each
reveal is recorded in the trunk's history with the API key that read it
(never the password itself), as a reveal in the portal is.

A cancelled trunk answers 404, as does a trunk whose password cannot be
read back: rotate it to get a new one.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's handle, as the portal shows it: a trunk with no credential has no SIP username yet. A SIP username is accepted too, and answers 409, since that trunk already has a credential.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Gives a trunk that was set up without a SIP credential (IP-only) its
first one, so it can register. The platform sets the username and
password, and the password is returned **only once**, in the `201`
answer, as on a new trunk.

A trunk that already has a credential answers 409: rotate its password
instead. A cancelled trunk answers 422. Send an `Idempotency-Key` so a
retry replays the first answer.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's SIP digest username.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Rolls a new, platform-generated SIP password onto the trunk's credential
and returns it **once**. The username does not change.

**The old password stops working at once**: a PBX still using it fails
its next registration or call until it has the new one.

Send an `Idempotency-Key`: a retry with the same key replays the first
answer, with the same password, rather than rotating twice. A cancelled
trunk answers 422.

200.description: The trunk's SIP credential with its new password.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's SIP digest username.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns where the trunk's SIP credentials may be used from: source
addresses and countries. Both lists empty means no restriction.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Replaces both lists. Send both every time; empty lists lift every
restriction you set. The change reaches the SBC on its next policy reload
and is recorded in the trunk's history, with the entries it removed.

Entries Check Networks added (for example to stop fraud) are returned in
the lists but are not yours to remove: a replace keeps them, so they are
still in the lists it returns. Contact support about one.

Addresses must be public: private, CGNAT and reserved ranges are refused.
A refused entry answers 422 naming the entry and its place in the list
(for example `cidrs.1` or `countries.0`); nothing is changed.

So a typo cannot lock you out, a `cidrs` list that is not empty and does
not hold the address this request came from answers 422 on `cidrs`,
naming the address, and nothing is changed. A source in an allowed
country is still accepted, but the check does not look the country up.
Send `confirmLockout: true` to save the list anyway. Empty lists always go
through.

cidrs.description: Source addresses or CIDR ranges: IPv4 no wider than `/24`, IPv6 single hosts only.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, in any case.

confirmLockout.description: Save a `cidrs` list that leaves out the address this request came from. Without it, that list answers 422.

200.description: The source restrictions now in force.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update, and voice:delete for `release`

Release, route or re-address up to 100 numbers in one call. Each number
goes through the same checks as the single call, and gets its own
result: one number refused never stops the rest.

- `release`: as `DELETE /numbers/{number}`, which says what a release
  does: billing stops, the number cools off for 30 days before anyone
  can order it, and the API has no undo. A number Check Networks has
  suspended, one a trunk presents as its default caller ID, or one whose
  release is already asked for, is skipped with the reason. Each release
  then runs shortly after, as a single one does.
- `route`: every number straight to `trunk` (a `sipUsername`), each on its
  own routing, so the rest of its block is untouched. This replaces any
  failover, time-of-day or geographic routing the number had.
- `emergencyAddress`: every number listed at `emergencyAddressId`. A spare
  number takes it at once; a number in use has its IPND record changed
  shortly after, as with `PATCH /numbers/{number}`.

A number that is not yours is skipped. **`Idempotency-Key` is required**
(`400` without one): a retry with the same key returns the first call's
job instead of releasing or routing again.

The call does the work before it answers, and answers `202` with the
job, `done`, and every number's result; read it again with
`GET /numbers/bulk/{jobId}`. The job is saved as each number is done: a
call that stops part way leaves a job that reads `running`, with the
results of the numbers it reached.

numbers.description: The numbers, E.164 (`61299999999`, with or without `+`).

trunk.description: For `route`, required there and only there; the trunk's `sipUsername`.

emergencyAddressId.description: For `emergencyAddress`, required there and only there; one of your emergency addresses.

202.description: The job, with each number's result.

parameters.name: jobId
parameters.description: The `jobId` from `POST /numbers/bulk`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

What a `POST /numbers/bulk` call did to each number.

get.summary: Find the Numbering Area for an Address
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

The numbering areas (SZUs) that serve a street address, best match first,
as the portal's Order Numbers page finds them, so you can order a local
number for a customer's address. Search for the address with
`GET /addresses/search` and send its `fullAddress` as `address`; pass the
first `szu` to `GET /numbers/available`.

Our supplier answers this, which can take up to a minute. An address it
refuses answers `422` with its reason; when it cannot be asked, `503`.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: The `fullAddress` of a `GET /addresses/search` result.

200.description: The areas serving the address, best first. Empty when none was found.

percentMatch.description: How well the area matches the address, in percent.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Up to five numbers, or for a block the block you would get, that you can
order now, each with its monthly and setup price per number, as the
portal's Order Numbers page shows them. Our own stock first. Where we hold
none for an Australian geographic number, our supplier's offer, which
reserves nothing until you order it with its `offerId`; never inside a
bundle.

Hold a single number of ours with `POST /numbers/holds`, then order it.

parameters.name: szu
parameters.description: The numbering area, required for `fixed` and `nz_geographic`; from `GET /numbers/areas`.

parameters.name: blockSize
parameters.description: `1`, or `10` or `100` consecutive numbers for a geographic type.

parameters.name: bundle
parameters.description: The bundle you will order into: only numbers we hold are offered. A bundle that has been submitted answers `422`.

200.description: What you can order now. An empty `results` means nothing is available in this area.

blocksInStock.description: How many complete blocks we hold; null for a single-number search.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Hold one of our numbers from `GET /numbers/available` (a `stock` single)
for 24 hours while you finish the order, as picking a number in the
portal does, so nobody else can take it. Order it with `POST /numbers`
and the `holdId`. A hold cannot be extended; once `heldUntil` passes, the
order answers `422` with the code `hold_expired`, and you can hold the
number again if it is still free.

Your account may hold 50 numbers at once, counting numbers being
ordered. A hold past that answers `409` saying so, until one of them is
ordered or its hold ends. Ask us if you need more. A `409` also means
somebody else has just taken the number.

201.description: The number is held for you.

holdId.description: The hold, to order the number by.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Your number orders, newest first, each with its status, its numbers once
allocated, and its error if it failed.

>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

One number order, the `Location` an order answers with. Poll it from
`pending` until it is `completed`, with each number and its route, or
`failed`, with `error`. An order in a bundle is `draft` until the bundle
is released.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Who an Australian number was assigned to, who serves it now, its
numbering area, whether it is already porting and whether we already hold
it, for a batch of numbers, as the portal's Number Lookup shows. Use it as
the first step of a port, before asking the end user for paperwork.

It only reads, so a suspended account may still call it, as it may any
`GET`.

Each number counts against your account's daily lookup allowance, the
same one the portal uses. A batch that would go over it is refused whole
with `429`, the allowance in `error.allowance`, and `Retry-After` set to
the seconds until it resets at midnight Brisbane time.

429.description: Over the daily lookup allowance (`error.allowance`), or over the limit of requests per minute. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds.

error.reason: You have used 990 of your 1,000 daily number lookups, and this batch asks for 25 more. The allowance resets at midnight.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Every number port on your account, in and out, newest request first, as
the portal's Number Ports page lists them. A port-out (`direction: out`)
is a number leaving you for another carrier: it takes its customer's
calls with it when it goes, so filter on `direction=out` to watch them.

Filter by `direction`, by `group` (the portal's tabs: `active`,
`completed`, `rejected`), by `state`, by `number` (any number on the
port, including one inside a CAT C range) and by `needsAttention=true`
(ports stalled past their step's usual time, or past a date they carry:
a cutover that passed, a verification code that lapsed).

For a download, set `format=csv` or `format=ndjson` to stream every
matching port instead of paged JSON; `page`/`perPage` are then ignored.
`csv` has the portal's export columns (`reference`, `requested`,
`direction`, `numbers`, `state`, `losing_provider`, `end_user`,
`scheduled_for`, `completed`), with dates on your account's calendar, so
`group=active&format=csv` is the portal's export of its Active tab.
`ndjson` is one `results[]` item per line.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: The portal's tab: `active` (in flight), `completed` (`activated`, `ported_away`) or `rejected` (`rejected`, `cancelled`).

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Ports carrying this number, in E.164 or national form.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: `true` for only the ports that need a person to look at them (see `attention`).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Bulk export format. Omit for paged JSON; `csv` or `ndjson` streams every matching port as a download.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

200.description: A page of ports, or the download.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`: a header row with the portal's export columns, then one row per port.
Present only when `format=ndjson`: one JSON object per line, each identical to a `results[]` item.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Ask for numbers to be ported to you from another carrier, as the portal's
port request form does, with the same checks and the same refusals.

- `portType` picks the kind of port: `CatA` (one fixed-line number),
  `CatC` (a list of fixed-line numbers; an entry ending `#` is a range of
  10, `##` a range of 100), `Mob` (one mobile number) or `Inbound` (one
  13, 1300 or 1800 number). Every type but `CatC` takes one number.
- `trunk` (a `sipUsername` from `GET /trunks`) and `emergencyAddressId`
  (from `GET /emergency-addresses`) are where the numbers land when the
  port completes.
- The most recent bill from the losing provider, as a PDF of up to 8 MB,
  is required on every port except a prepaid mobile one, whose holder's
  `dateOfBirth` is the proof instead. Send the request as
  `multipart/form-data` to attach it.
- A mobile port needs `accountType`: `postpaid` with the losing carrier's
  `accountNumber`, or `prepaid` with `dateOfBirth`.
- `consents.portingAuthority` and `consents.terms` must be accepted;
  `consents.authorisedAgent` is recommended. Your API key is recorded as
  the one who gave them (its name, as it was then), not a user.
- To have the number's holder give the Porting Authority instead, send
  `authorityHolder` with their `name` and `email` and leave out
  `consents.portingAuthority` (any port but `Mob`). The port is saved in
  `awaiting_authority` and the holder is emailed a link
  (`confirmAuthority`, on `/ports/{reference}/delegations`) on your
  end-user portal. Their confirmation, with their name and position, is
  the port's Porting Authority and covers the Agent Authority; the port
  then moves to `requested` and we lodge it. They are reminded after 7
  days, and the port is cancelled after 14 without it. An account with
  no end-user portal is a `403` with `no_end_user_portal_access`.

A mobile port sends a verification code to the number straight away:
confirm it with `POST /ports/{reference}/confirm` within 30 minutes.
`verificationCodeSent: false` means it could not be sent yet; send one
with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code`.

A number the account may not port is a 422 on `numbers.0`: one that does
not match the port type, or a mobile number already on another open
port, or whose verification failed in the last day. An account that may
not place orders is a 403.

recentBill.description: The losing provider's most recent bill, PDF, up to 8 MB.

201.description: The port, in state `requested` (or `ppv_sent` once a mobile port's code has gone, or `awaiting_authority` when sent to the number's holder).

verificationCodeSent.description: On a mobile port, whether the verification code went to the number. Null on every other port.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

One port, as the portal's port page shows it: its real `state`, who it
is `waitingOn` and the `nextStep`, whether it needs `attention` and why,
its `history` step by step with dates, the cutover you asked for
(`preferredCutoverOn`) and the booked one (`scheduledFor`), and why it
stopped (`statusReason`). A mobile port carries its `verificationCode`
dates and the wrong codes it can still take.

post.summary: Confirm a Mobile Port's Verification Code
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

The six-digit code the mobile number's holder was sent, for a port in
state `ppv_sent`. A correct code moves the port to `ppv_validated` and we
lodge it with the carrier.

A refusal is a 422 on `code` whose message says what to do: the code is
wrong (with the attempts left), it has lapsed (send a fresh one with
`POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code`), or the port is not waiting
for a code. Five wrong codes per port, counted across every code sent,
reject the port. A 503 means the code could not be checked just then and
the attempt was not counted.

post.summary: Resend a Mobile Port's Verification Code
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Send a fresh verification code to the mobile number being ported, when
the last one lapsed or never arrived. The port stays waiting for the
code (`ppv_sent`). A code lasts **30 minutes**; the new one replaces the
old, which no longer works.

The five wrong codes a port can take are counted across every code sent,
so a resend does not give more tries: `verificationCode.attemptsRemaining`
on the port says how many are left. Resends count against your API rate
limit like any other write.

A port that is not a mobile port waiting for its code, or a number the
code cannot be sent to, is a 422 on `reference` whose message says why.

>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Withdraw a port-in you no longer want, before its cutover is locked in,
as the port-in terms allow and the portal offers. The port moves to
`cancelled` with `statusReason` saying you withdrew it, and the step is
sent as `order.statusChanged` like any other.

A port can be withdrawn in these states: `requested`, `submitted`,
`confirmed` (fixed line, 13/1300/1800), and `ppv_sent`, `ppv_validated`
(mobile). Once it is `scheduled`, or a mobile port is
`submitted_upstream`, the cutover is locked in: that, and a port that is
complete, rejected or cancelled by us, is a 409 with the reason. A
port-out is worked by our team and cannot be withdrawn here (409).
Withdrawing a port you already withdrew answers 200 with the port.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

The figures the portal's call history shows above its table, over the
same window and filters as `GET /voice/cdrs`: calls, answered calls,
minutes, cost, answer rate and average call length.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: On or after this datetime (ISO 8601). Defaults to 31 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: On or before this datetime (ISO 8601). Defaults to now.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: `unbilled`: the calls since the start of this month that are not on an invoice yet. Not with `from`.

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only this trunk's calls, by sipUsername.

parameters.name: invoice
parameters.description: Only the calls billed on this invoice of ours to you, by its `id` in your invoice list. Not one of yours is a 422.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search the source and destination numbers.

answerRate.description: Answered calls as a percentage of calls.

averageSeconds.description: The average length of an answered call.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

The scheduled call record exports, daily and monthly, each on or off, as
the portal's SFTP Access card shows them. Exports land on our SFTP server
under your SFTP login.

`sftpLogin` says whether you have a login and its username. The login is
created, rotated and withdrawn in the portal only; the password is never
returned. When the login's state cannot be read right now, `exists` and
`username` are `null`.

200.description: The exports and the SFTP login.

put.summary: Turn a Scheduled Call Record Export On or Off
put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Turns the daily or monthly export on or off, as the portal's SFTP Access
card does. The change is audited with the API key that made it. The SFTP
login itself is managed in the portal only. An unknown cadence is a `404`.

200.description: The export as it now stands.

parameters.name: cgrid
parameters.description: The call's `cgrid`, as `GET /voice/cdrs` lists it.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

One call detail record. Another account's call and an unknown id both
answer `404`.

>**Required Scope(s):** recordings:read

The recordings of calls on your trunks, newest first, as the Call
Recordings page of the portal lists them. Follow `nextCursor` for the next
page until it is `null`. Answers `403` while call recording is not
available on your account.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Recorded on or after this datetime (ISO 8601), or from the start of this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Recorded on or before this datetime (ISO 8601), or to the end of this date (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only this trunk's recordings, by sipUsername. A trunk that is not yours is a 422.

parameters.name: trigger
parameters.description: What started the recording. An unknown value is a 422.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search the caller ID number and name.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The recording's `id` (a uuid).

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** recordings:read

One recording, with `downloadUrl`: a link to the audio that works for
**5 minutes**. Fetch the recording again for a fresh link. Every fetch is
audited with the API key that made it.

Another account's recording, an unknown id and a recording whose audio is
no longer stored all answer `404`.

200.description: The recording and its download link.

downloadUrl.description: The audio file. Works for 5 minutes.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

The calls up now on your trunks, oldest first, as the trunk page of the
portal lists them under Concurrency. Filter to one trunk with `trunk`.

A call to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106) is listed with
`emergency: true`. It is never hung up: `POST /voice/calls/{callId}/hangup`
refuses it with `422 emergency_call`.

Follow `nextCursor` for the next page until it is `null`.

parameters.name: trunk
parameters.description: Only this trunk's calls, by its sipUsername. A trunk that is not yours is a 422.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of calls per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

callId.description: The call's id; hang it up with `POST /voice/calls/{callId}/hangup`.

trunk.description: The sipUsername of the trunk the call is on.

answeredAt.description: Null while the call is ringing.

emergency.description: True for a call to 000, 112 or 106, which is never hung up.

parameters.name: callId
parameters.description: The live call's `callId`, as `GET /voice/calls/active` lists it.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Ends one live call on one of your trunks: both parties are disconnected.
The call is billed for the time it was up. The hang-up is audited with
the API key that sent it.

**An emergency call (000, 112 or 106) is never hung up.** It answers
`422` with `error.code` `emergency_call`, and nothing is sent to the
network.

A call that has already ended, or is not on one of your trunks, answers
`404`.

202.description: The call has been ended.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's `id`, or its SIP digest username.

post.summary: Hang Up a Trunk's Live Calls
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Ends every live call on one of your trunks in one step, for example to
stop fraud: both parties are disconnected on each. Each call is billed
for the time it was up. The request is audited once, with the API key
that sent it and the counts. To stop new calls too, suspend the trunk
(`POST /trunks/{username}/suspend`) first.

**An emergency call (000, 112 or 106) is never hung up.** It is left up
and counted in `skipped`.

`failed` counts calls the network could not end; send the request again
with a new `Idempotency-Key` to retry them. A trunk with no live calls
answers `202` with every count `0`. A trunk that is not yours answers
`404`.

202.description: The trunk's calls have been ended, emergency calls aside.

trunk.description: The trunk as `GET /trunks` names it (its SIP username, else its `id`).

failed.description: Calls the network could not end.

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id, the `messageId` that `POST /sms` returned.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:read

One message on your account, with its `status`. The `Location` header of
`POST /sms` points here, so a client can send, then poll this until the
message is `delivered` or `failed`. A message held for review reads
`pending` with a `statusReason` until it is released or blocked.

A message on another account, or an inbound message held as a suspected
scam (one you never received), answers `404`. Reads are audited, with the
message id, never the text.

>**Required Scope(s):** sms:read

Every sender your account has asked for or holds, with its status: the
portal's **Approved Senders** list. Numbers you hold with us are approved
automatically and appear here too.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:send

Ask for a sender that `POST /sms` refused with `sender_not_approved`: a
number you control (ported elsewhere, say) or a sender ID of 3 to 11
letters and digits. It lands as `pending`, and can be used once our team
approves it. Sending again for your own pending or rejected request
updates it.

`422` when the sender is malformed, already approved, or held by one of
your end users.

sender.description: An E.164 number, or a sender ID of 3 to 11 letters and digits.

notes.description: What the sender is for, for our team's check.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request's `id` (a uuid), from `GET /sms/senders`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** sms:send

Take back one of your own pending requests; it reads `withdrawn`. A
request our team has already decided, or one an end user made, answers
`409` and is unchanged.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Every fax sent and received on your numbers, your end users' included,
newest first: the portal's **Fax History**. Metadata only, never the
document.

A page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results`. Pass `nextCursor`
back as `cursor` for the next page, until it is `null`.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: One of your numbers; only faxes received on or sent from it.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Part of the other party's number, as the portal's search.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Faxes received or queued at or after this time. A date alone means the start of that day.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Faxes received or queued at or before this time. A date alone means the end of that day.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Send from one of your numbers that is on a fax plan, to one or more
Australian landlines, mobiles and 13, 1300 and 1800 numbers: one fax per
destination, each billed per page. A fax cannot be recalled.

Send `multipart/form-data`. Documents are PDF or TIFF only, at most 5
of them, each at most 10 MB. A cover page, when it is on in your fax
settings, goes first and shows the subject, note and `replyEmail`.

**`Idempotency-Key` is required** (`400` without one): a retry with the
same key returns the first send's faxes instead of faxing again.

`202` with one fax per destination, `pending`. Follow each with
`GET /fax/documents/{id}` or the `fax.sent` and `fax.failed` webhook
events. `422` when the number is not yours or not on a fax plan, a
destination cannot be faxed, a document is the wrong type or too large,
there are too many, or a document fails the virus scan.

from.description: One of your numbers on a fax plan.

replyEmail.description: Shown on the cover page as who the fax is from, and sent the result by email. Leave it out for no result email.

documents.description: PDF or TIFF files, as `documents[]`, each at most 10 MB.

202.description: One fax per destination, queued.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

One fax on your account, by the id `GET /fax/documents`, `POST
/fax/documents` and the `fax.*` webhook events give it. Metadata only,
never the document. `404` for any other id.

>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Your fax domain and cover page: the portal's **Fax Settings**.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Set your fax domain or cover page; a field left out keeps its value.
`domain: null` goes back to the platform's domain. Check a new domain
with `POST /fax/settings/domain-check`.

`422` when the domain is not a hostname, is a shared platform domain, or
is held by another account.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Check your fax domain both ways, as **Check domain** in the portal: your
saved domain, or the one you give. Nothing is stored, so run it again
after changing your DNS. `422` when there is no domain to check.

It only reads, so a suspended account may still call it, as it may any
`GET`.

domain.description: A domain to check instead of the saved one.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Your account's list of countries its SIP trunks may call when
`International` is in their calling permissions. Every trunk follows it
unless the trunk has its own `allowedCountries`, and a new trunk follows
it too. An account that has never set a list allows every country.

The list applies to international calls only: calls to Australia and New
Zealand follow each trunk's calling permissions, high-risk destinations
stay blocked whatever the list says, and 000 always connects. New Zealand
is not in the list: a call to it is `NZMobile` or `NZNational`, never
international, so take those out of a trunk's `callingPermissions` to
stop it.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Replace your account's list. Every trunk that follows it uses the new
list from its next call; a trunk with its own `allowedCountries` keeps
its own. At least one country: to stop every international call, take
`International` out of the trunk's calling permissions instead. A list
naming `NZ` is a `422`: New Zealand follows `NZMobile` and `NZNational`.

allowedCountries.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes, each one of `availableCountries` (the United Kingdom is `GB`, not `UK`).

200.description: The list as it now stands.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The trunk's SIP digest username.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Lift the hold on a trunk that reached its daily spend cap, so its
outbound calls connect again now rather than at midnight Brisbane time.
The trunk then runs for the rest of the day at the same cap; changing the
cap arms it again. Raising `dailySpendCapExGst` above `spendTodayExGst`
also lifts the hold. A trunk that is not held is a 422. The hold never
stopped 000 or inbound calls.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns a paginated list of your residential lines, oldest first. A line
with `awaitingNumber: true` is billing but has no number yet, so it can
make and receive no calls. Filter by `endUser` for one end user's lines.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only the lines of this end user, by its public number. A number that is not one of your end users is a 422, not an empty list.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

200.description: A paginated list of residential lines.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Order a residential line on a plan. Every residential number is lodged
with the emergency register against a service address, so the order
needs one of your emergency addresses; the answer gives it back for
ordering the line's number.

**The line bills from now.** It cannot make or receive calls until its
number is ordered, and reads `awaitingNumber: true` until then. The
answer carries the line's SIP password, once: it cannot be read again.

name.description: A friendly name for the line.

emergencyAddressId.description: One of your emergency addresses (`GET /emergency-addresses`): where the line's number will be lodged. Another account's address, or an unknown one, is a 422.

endUser.description: The end user this line is for, by its public number. One of your end users that is not archived; any other number is a 422. Omitted or null makes the line your own.

201.description: The line was ordered. Includes the one-time SIP password.

sipPassword.description: The line's SIP password. Shown only in this response.

emergencyAddressId.description: The address sent, to order the line's number against.

notice.description: That the line bills now and takes no calls until its number is ordered.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The line's SIP username, as call records and numbers name it in `trunk`. A SIP trunk's username is a 404.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns one of your residential lines, with its live numbers.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Move an active line to the other plan, from today. The old plan's
monthly charge still applies to this billing period; the new one starts
today. A line that is not active, or a change onto the plan it is
already on, is a 422.

200.description: The line, on its new plan.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The line's SIP username. A SIP trunk's username is a 404.

get.summary: Get a Residential Line's Call Settings
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns the line's call forwarding, Do Not Disturb, anonymous call
reject and call waiting, and the kinds of number it may call.

patch.summary: Update a Residential Line's Call Settings
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Change any of the line's call settings; a setting left out keeps its
value. Turning forwarding on needs a `destination` of 6 to 15 digits.
The change reaches the line within a minute, and the portal and the end
user's star codes see the same settings. `callingPermissions` cannot be
changed here.

destination.description: Never 000, 112 or 106, in any form; that is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

200.description: The line's call settings as saved.

parameters.name: username
parameters.description: The line's SIP username. A SIP trunk's username is a 404.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns whether the line's mailbox is on, where its messages are
emailed, and what happens to a message once it is emailed. The PIN is
the end user's own and is not returned.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Turn the mailbox on or off and set where messages are emailed; a field
left out keeps its value. Send `email: null` to stop emailing. The PIN
cannot be set here: sending `pin` is a 422.

200.description: The line's voicemail settings as saved.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns your caller ID authorisation requests, newest first. Filter by
`status` for, say, the ones still pending.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: Page number to retrieve. Defaults to `1`.

parameters.name: perPage
parameters.description: Number of records per page. Defaults to `50`, maximum `200`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:create

Ask to present a number your account does not hold as a trunk's caller
ID. Send `multipart/form-data` with the number, why you need it, and
proof that you may use it (a PDF, PNG or JPEG up to 8 MB, such as a
recent bill for the number). We review it and email the account's
technical contact, or its notification address, with the outcome; the
decision also sends `callerId.statusChanged`.

A 422 on `number` means a 13, 1300, 1800 or 1900 number (never
presentable), a number your account can already present, or one with a
request already pending.

reason.description: Why you need to present this number.

evidence.description: Proof you may use the number. PDF, PNG or JPEG, up to 8 MB.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The request's `id` (a uuid).

get.summary: Get a Caller ID Authorisation Request
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Returns one request: its status, when it was made and decided, and the
reason for a rejection.

delete.summary: Cancel a Caller ID Authorisation Request
delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:delete

Withdraw a request we have not decided yet. It stays in the list as
`cancelled`. A request already approved, rejected or cancelled is a 422.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Your qualification batches, newest first: the ones sent here and the
ones uploaded on the portal's Batch Qualification page. `q` searches the
batch's reference. Each batch's rows are on `GET /data/sq/batches/{id}`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `createdAt` or `updatedAt`, `-` in front for descending.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Qualify up to 2,000 premises as one job, as the portal's Batch
Qualification page does with a CSV. Each row is a location id (`locId`,
LOC… or OPC…) or a street `address`, with your own `reference` for it.
For a premises whose port or line is in use, `avc` and `authorityDate`
carry the service id and customer authority date for a transfer, as the
CSV's `avc` and `authority_date` columns do.

The batch is accepted at once (`202`) and each row is qualified on our
side, usually within minutes: follow it with
`GET /data/sq/batches/{id}` until its `status` is `completed`. An
address that does not resolve to one location is `unresolved`, not a
refused batch.

Batches share the portal's allowance: ten batches an hour, and a number
of rows a day. A batch over either is refused whole with
`409 - sq_batch_allowance_exceeded`, the portal's words in `reason`, and
the rows left today in `remainingRows`; nothing in it is qualified or
counted. Creating orders from a batch is not offered.

reference.description: Your name for the batch. The portal shows the batch by it.

items.description: One premises. Give `locId` or `address`, not both.

locId.description: An NBN Location ID or an Opticomm Property ID.

address.description: A street address, resolved to its location first.

reference.description: Your reference for the row, given back with its result.

avc.description: For a transfer, the service in use at the premises, in any case.

authorityDate.description: For a transfer, the date the end user gave authority.

202.description: The batch is accepted and its rows are being qualified.

409.description: The batch is over your account's batch allowance.

error.reason: This batch has 500 rows, and this account has 120 of its 5000 rows a day left. Upload a smaller batch, or the rest tomorrow.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The batch's id.

get.summary: Read a qualification batch and its results
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

One batch, its progress, and one page of its rows in the order you sent
them, each with its result once qualified. `page` and `perPage` page the
rows. Another account's batch answers `404`.

rows.description: One page of the batch's rows.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:read

Your colocation services, newest first, as the portal's My Colocation
page lists them. `q` searches the service number.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `createdAt` or `updatedAt`, `-` in front for descending.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The colocation service's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:read

One of your colocation services. Another account's service answers `404`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The colocation service the work is at.

post.summary: Ask for remote hands at a colocation service
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:create

Ask our technicians for work at your rack, as the portal's Remote Hands
request does. Remote hands is billed per incident. The request is a
support ticket with the service linked: it is answered with the new
ticket, which you follow and reply to on `/tickets`, and it shows on the
portal's Support page.

Another account's service answers `404`; a decommissioned one `409`.

description.description: The work needed at the rack.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The colocation service the extra is for.

post.summary: Ask for an extra on a colocation service
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:create

Ask for another power outlet, cross-connect or network port, or a
bandwidth uplift, as the portal's Extras request does. We quote and
bill it. The request is a support ticket with the service linked: it is
answered with the new ticket, which you follow on `/tickets`, and it
shows on the portal's Support page.

Another account's service answers `404`; a decommissioned one `409`.

get.summary: List the sites you can order colocation at
get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:read

The sites that offer colocation, as the portal's order form lists them.
Pass a site's `id` as `siteId` on `POST /colocation/orders`.

label.description: The site as the portal names it.

defaultPowerAmps.description: The power a new service at this site includes, in amps, when the tier does not say.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** colocation:create

Order rack space at a site, as the portal's Order Colocation page does.
The order is recorded at once and we assign the rack and rack units; the
service then appears on `GET /colocation/services`.

An account that may not place orders (its credit, an onboarding check,
or a prepay balance short of the order) is refused with `403 -
forbidden` and the reason, as a data order is. A site that does not
offer colocation answers `422` naming `siteId`.

requestedPowerAmps.description: The power you need, in amps, when more than the tier includes.

201.description: The order, waiting for us to assign rack space.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

When the end user has moved into premises whose line or port is still in
use by someone else, and the old service's id cannot be given, order a
Connect Outstanding with a proof of occupancy instead: a lease, a utility
bill or similar showing the end user occupies the premises.

Send `multipart/form-data` with the document as `file`, a PDF, JPEG or
PNG up to 10 MB. The answer's `id` goes on the order as
`occupancyDocumentId` (on `POST /data/orders` and the NBN Connect
routes). Each document is used by one order and kept with it as
evidence, for as long as the order record is kept. It is stored
privately against your account and never served to anyone outside it.

A file of another type or over 10 MB is a `422`.

file.description: The document, a PDF, JPEG or PNG up to 10 MB.

201.description: The document, ready for an order to use.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Your bundles, newest first, each with its items in order. `q` searches
the reference and title.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `createdAt` or `updatedAt`, `-` in front for descending.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Start an empty bundle, as the portal's Start a bundle does. Add to it
through each item's own order route with its id: `bundleId` on
`POST /data/orders` and `POST /trunks`, and `bundle` on `POST /numbers`.
Each joins as a draft, and nothing is sent until you submit the bundle
with `POST /bundles/{id}/submit`.

Numbers and a trunk added after a data order start once the items above
them have completed, so nothing rings or bills before the service it runs
over; change that, and the order, with `PATCH /bundles/{id}/items/{itemId}`.

A bundle is submitted as a data order, so an account that may not order
data services is refused with a `403` here, before anything is added.

endUser.description: The end user the bundle is for, by its public number.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bundle's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

One of your bundles, with its items in order, each with its state and
what it is still waiting on. Another account's bundle answers `404`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:delete

Cancel a bundle nothing has left: its drafts are discarded and nothing
in it is sent. A bundle that has been submitted, or has an item already
sent, is a `409`; contact support for that.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bundle's id.

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: The item's `id`, as the bundle read shows it.

patch.summary: Move a bundle item, or set when it starts
patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Put an item at a place in the bundle (`position`, 1 is first; past the
end puts it last), and say whether it starts only once every item above
it has completed (`waitsForPrevious`). The first item waits for nothing,
and numbers on the bundle's own trunk always stay after it and wait for
it: a change that breaks either is a `422` and changes nothing. A bundle
that has been submitted is a `409`.

200.description: The item as it now stands.

delete.summary: Remove a draft from a bundle
delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:delete

Drop a draft from the bundle and discard it: a data order, numbers (their
hold is freed) or a trunk. Remove the numbers ordered for the bundle's
trunk before the trunk itself. Something already sent, or a bundle that
has been submitted, is a `409`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The bundle's id.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:create

Limit: 30 per minute for the account (carrier write).

Submit the bundle, as the portal's Submit All: every item that is ready
is sent now, each on its own, and the items that wait are sent as the
items above them complete. Read the bundle to follow each item. Sent
again, it sends anything added or made ready since.

A bundle with nothing ready to send, or one that has finished, is a
`409`. Its data orders go to the carrier, so the `Idempotency-Key` is
required and the call counts against the write limit.

202.description: The ready items are on their way.

released.description: The ids of the items sent now.

waiting.description: The ids of the items that follow once the items above them complete.

get.description:
Your VPN access groups, by name, with what each allows and how many
users it has.

post.description:
Create an access group. A `split` group needs at least one destination,
and none may name a reserved or Check Networks network: such a
destination is `422` naming `destinations`. A `full` group keeps none.

destinations.description: For a `split` group, the networks it reaches, as CIDRs or bare addresses.

patch.description:
Change a group's name, access mode, destinations or notes; a field left
out is kept. Every user in the group takes the change, and no profile
has to be downloaded again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The group's id.

delete.description:
Delete a group whose users are all removed or moved. Removed users
don't hold a group; a group that still has a live or suspended user
is `409` with the reason. A group with a dedicated egress IP has the
IP released, and its monthly charge ends on the day of the delete. If
the IP can't be released just now, the delete is `503` and nothing
changes: the group, its IP and its charge stay until you try again.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The group's id.

get.description: Your VPN users, by name. Removed users are not listed.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only this group's users, by the group's id. A group not on your account is `422`.

parameters.name: endUser
parameters.description: Only this end user's, by its number. An unknown number is `422`.

post.description:
Order up to 50 users in one of your groups, optionally for one of your
end users, as the portal's order form. Each is billed monthly from
issue at your seat price, shown in the answer. An account that may not
order is `403` with the reason: one your account manager has not
enabled for VPN, or one at its credit limit. A staff hold on the end
user is `409`. While you bill your end users, seats for an end user you
bill need a retail price for VPN users (a price, or a markup): until
then it is `422` on `endUser`, saying what to set.

The users are issued in the background, so the answer is `202`: they
are on GET /vpn/users as `provisioning` shortly after, and each
profile is ready to download a minute or so later (`profileReady`).

names.description: Each user's name, one user per name.

endUser.description: The end user the seats are for, by its number. They then appear on that end user's own portal, where it downloads and resets its profiles.

202.description: The users are ordered.

endUser.description: The end user's number; null when none.

seatPriceExGst.description: Each user's monthly price, ex GST. Null when no price is set for your account.

monthlyPriceExGst.description: What this order adds to your monthly bill, ex GST.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

patch.description:
Rename a user, move it to another of your groups, or give it to another
end user (null for none); a field left out is kept. Its certificate,
address and profile stay the same, so nothing needs downloading again.
A suspended user is `409`. So is a move to an end user you bill while
nothing prices a VPN user for them (a retail price or a markup).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

endUser.description: The end user's number, or null for none.

delete.description:
Revoke the user's certificate and stop its monthly charge, as the
portal's Remove. This cannot be undone: order a new user to replace it.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

get.description:
A link to download the user's OpenVPN profile (`.ovpn`), working for 5
minutes. The profile holds the user's private key, so it needs its own
scope, `vpn:credentials`, and each link given is recorded. `409`
while the profile is still being made (`profileReady` is false), or
while the user is suspended.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

What your usage has added to your bill with us for one month so far:
call charges, data and numbers, grouped as the bill groups them, with
each group's items, plus the month's usage in real units. These are the
figures the Usage page in the Wholesale Portal shows, worked out the way
the bill run will charge them; the bill itself is on
[List Invoices](#tag/Account/operation/list_invoices) once issued.

Months run on your bill's calendar: your account's time zone, the zone
your invoices are cut in (set in the Wholesale Portal's Company
Settings; Brisbane until you set another). A month already billed stays on the zone its invoice was cut
in. You can ask for this month or any of the eleven before it;
`daysRemaining` is how many days of the month are left after today,
`0` for a past month.

Amounts are dollars as decimal strings: each comes without GST, its
GST, and with GST (`...ExGst`, `...Gst`, `...IncGst`).

The units count every answered call, inbound and free ones included,
which the charges leave out.

Set `format=csv` for the Usage page's charges CSV: one row per item, then
each group's subtotal.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit for JSON; `csv` downloads the charges as CSV.

daysRemaining.description: Days of the month left after today; `0` for a past month.

groups.description: The charges, by the group the bill puts them in. Groups with nothing in them are left out.

smsMessages.description: SMS messages sent, counting each part of a long message.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. Columns `group`, `item`, `quantity`, `excl_gst`, `gst` and `incl_gst`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

One month's usage for each of your end users, in real units, with what
it has added to your bill with us so far. Every end user is listed,
alphabetically, including those with no usage; your own services, not
resold to an end user, come last with `endUser: null` when they have any.
These are the Usage page's "Usage by End User" figures.

Set `format=csv` for the Usage page's CSV of the same table (units only).

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit for JSON; `csv` downloads the table as CSV.

endUser.description: The end user's number, as `/end-users` names it; `null` for your own services.

chargesExGst.description: What this usage has added to your bill so far, without GST.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. Columns `end_user`, `voice_minutes`, `voice_calls`, `data_down_bytes`, `data_up_bytes` and `sms_messages`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

The data your services moved each day of one month, the curve behind the
Usage page's bar chart. Only days with usage are listed, oldest first.
Each day is a day on your bill's calendar, as `GET /account/usage`
describes it.

Set `format=csv` for the Usage page's CSV of the same days.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit for JSON; `csv` downloads the days as CSV.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. Columns `date`, `down_bytes`, `up_bytes` and `total_bytes`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

The business reports you can run, the ones on the Reports page of the
Wholesale Portal. Run one with
[Get Report](#tag/Account/operation/get_account_report). A report that
`takesPeriod` is worked out over a date window; the others are as at now.

key.description: The report's key, for Get Report.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

Runs one business report for your account, the same document the
Reports page downloads, as JSON, CSV or PDF. A key not on
[List Reports](#tag/Account/operation/list_account_reports) returns
`404`.

In JSON the report is a table: `columns` are its headings and each of
`rows` is one row of cells, already formatted as the download shows them
(dollars as decimal strings such as `"1234.50"`). `moneyColumns` lists
the indexes of the dollar columns. `kpis` are the headline figures, and
`sections` any small tables shown ahead of the main one.

`from` and `to` are read only by a report that `takesPeriod`; without
them it runs from the first of this month to today. They are calendar
dates on your account's time zone (Brisbane until you set one), whatever
`CN-Time-Zone` says: a day runs from midnight to midnight there, so the
end-user bill run at 04:00 on the 1st is in that month. `from` and `to`
come back as the dates asked for.

`asAt` is read only by `aged_receivables`: the report is as at the end
of that day in your account's timezone, leaving out invoices, payments
and credits dated after it. Without it the report is as at now.

`estimateRows` lists the indexes into `rows` of the rows that are an
estimate rather than invoiced figures: the margin report's "Usage so far
(not yet billed)" rows and its "Total with usage so far", which adds them.
Empty when no row is an estimate.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The report's key, from List Reports.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first day of the window, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The last day of the window, `YYYY-MM-DD`, included.

parameters.name: asAt
parameters.description: For `aged_receivables` only, the day the report is as at, `YYYY-MM-DD`; omit for now.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Omit for JSON; `csv` or `pdf` downloads the report.

subtitle.description: The period or as-at date the report covers.

from.description: The window's first day; `null` for a report that is as at now.

asAt.description: The day `aged_receivables` is as at; `null` for every other report.

estimateRows.description: Indexes into `rows` of the rows that are an estimate, not invoiced figures.

schema.description: Present only when `format=csv`. Any sections, then the main table.
Present only when `format=pdf`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:read

The usage alerts on your account, the ones under Notifications in
Company Settings. A usage alert watches your call spend today or this
month, your minutes this month or your SMS this month, on the whole
account or (for calls) one trunk. When it reaches its threshold we tell
the alert's own recipients, once for that day or month, and send a
[Usage Alert Triggered](#tag/Webhook-Events-Usage/operation/webhook_usage_alert_triggered)
event. Alerts are checked every 15 minutes.

Usage alerts are notices only: they never stop calls. Your credit limit
is what stops calls.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Adds a usage alert, up to 25 on an account. `recipients` lists who the
alert goes to (up to 10 addresses and 10 mobiles); only they are told.
One bad recipient refuses the whole request with `422`. Each channel in
`channels` needs someone on it: `email` at least one address, `sms` at
least one mobile, or the request is `422`. Left out, `channels` is the
ones your `recipients` reach; an empty list sends only the webhook
