event.

trunk.description: One of your SIP trunks, by its `sipUsername`, for a call metric only. Omit or `null` for the whole account.

threshold.description: Dollars without GST for a spend metric (`"50.00"`), otherwise a whole number (`"1000"`). At least one cent or one unit. A JSON number is taken too (`1000`); a string keeps the cents exact.

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Changes a usage alert. Send only the fields you change; `trunk: null`
moves it back to the whole account. A new `metric` in another unit
(spend to minutes or SMS, or back) needs a new `threshold` in that unit,
or the request is `422` and the alert is left as it was; between the two
spend metrics, or the two counts, the threshold is kept.
`recipients`, when sent, replaces the alert's whole list (`[]` empties
it); to add or remove one person, use the alert's `recipients` routes.
A change to `channels` or `recipients` that leaves a channel with nobody
on it (`email` with no address, `sms` with no mobile) is `422`.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The alert's `id` (a uuid).

threshold.description: As on create; a JSON number is taken too.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Removes a usage alert and its history.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The alert's `id` (a uuid).

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Adds one person to a usage alert: send `email` or `mobile`, not both. An
alert takes up to 10 addresses and 10 mobiles. Someone already on the
alert, or a mobile that is not an Australian mobile, answers `422`.
An alert that is not on your account answers `404`.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The alert's `id` (a uuid).

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** billing:update

Stops sending one usage alert to one recipient. A recipient that is not
on this alert, or an alert that is not on your account, answers `404`.
The last address of an alert sent by email, or the last mobile of one
sent by SMS, answers `422`: take that channel off the alert first.

parameters.name: alertId
parameters.description: The alert's `id` (a uuid).

parameters.name: recipientId
parameters.description: The recipient's `id` (a uuid).

patch.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Change the address printed on our invoices to you, your billing contact,
or both, as the Company Details page does in the portal and with the same
rules: a state is one of ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC or WA, a postcode
is four digits, and an email is a valid address.

Only what you send changes. A field left out of `billingAddress` or
`billingContact` keeps its value; a field sent as `null` clears it. A
billing contact with every field cleared is removed. Each change is
recorded in your account's audit log against this API key.

Your legal name, ABN, ACN and trading name are changed through support,
not here: sending `entityDetails` is refused with 422.

country.description: Left blank, an address is saved as in Australia.

200.description: Your billing details as they now stand.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

The Points of Interconnect where your account has a live data service,
each with how many of your services are live there, as the portal's
Utilisation page lists them. Read a POI's utilisation with
[Get POI Utilisation](#tag/Data-Utilisation/operation/get_data_poi_utilisation).

code.description: The POI's code, as NBN names it (`4IPS`), or `OPC-<state>` for Opticomm.

liveServices.description: How many of your data services are live at this POI.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

A POI's utilisation over a window, the series the portal's Utilisation
chart draws: the NNI's traffic (every supplier link into the POI,
summed) and the POI's traffic on its outer tag on our BNG, in Mbps, with
the NNI's planned capacity. Both are the whole POI, every customer's
traffic, so you can see whether congestion is ours before you raise a
fault.

The window is the last 24 hours unless you send `from` and `to`. It can
reach back at most 30 days, and its points are as far apart as the
portal's chart for that length: 5 minutes up to 24 hours, 30 minutes up
to 7 days, 2 hours up to 30 days.

A POI where your account has no live data service answers 404. When our
monitoring cannot be read the call answers 503; try again shortly.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: The POI's code, from [List POIs With Your Services](#tag/Data-Utilisation/operation/get_data_pois).

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The window's start, ISO 8601. At most 30 days ago. Default 24 hours before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The window's end, ISO 8601, not in the future. Default now.

capacityMbps.description: The NNI's planned capacity. Null when none is recorded.

currentNniPercent.description: The NNI's busier direction at the latest point, as a percent of capacity. Null without a capacity or a latest point.

currentBngPercent.description: The POI's BNG traffic, busier direction at the latest point, as a percent of capacity.

points.description: One point per step, oldest first. A value is null where nothing was recorded, never zero.

nniDownloadMbps.description: NNI traffic toward your end users.

nniUploadMbps.description: NNI traffic from your end users.

bngDownloadMbps.description: The POI's outer-tag traffic on the BNG, toward your end users.

bngUploadMbps.description: The POI's outer-tag traffic on the BNG, from your end users.

get.description:
Your account's audit trail, newest first: what your portal users did,
what your API keys did (named by the key), what each OAuth app you
connected did on your account (as `apiKey`, named by the app, and on no
other account's trail), and what our support staff did
on your behalf (as `Support`; the staff member is never named). The same
entries as the portal's Audit Log page, for feeding a security log system.

Paged by `page`, or by following `nextCursor` (pass it back as `cursor`
until it is `null`) to read every entry exactly once while new ones are
written. A cursor page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results`
only. `q` searches the action key and the IP address.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only entries at or after this time, an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only entries at or before this time. A date alone includes that whole day. Not before `from`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only these actions: one or several action keys, comma-separated (`user.login,user.password_changed`), at most 50.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: Only entries by this actor: a user's id (as `GET /account/users` names it), an API key's id, or `support` for our support staff. Anything else matches nothing.

total.description: Entries matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page or a page that was not full.

get.description:
The calls your API keys made in the last 30 days, newest first, for
debugging an integration: which failed, how long each took, and which
addresses used each key. The same list as the Recent API Calls panel on
the API Keys page. A call refused for its key (revoked, a missing scope,
an address not on the key's allowlist) is listed too; a call with no
valid token belongs to no account and is not.

Each entry is a summary only: never the request or response body, the
query string or a header. Paged by `page`, or by following `nextCursor`
(pass it back as `cursor` until it is `null`); a cursor page carries
`perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results` only.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Only calls at or after this time, an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Only calls at or before this time. A date alone includes that whole day. Not before `from`.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: Only calls by this key, by its `client_id`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only calls answered with these statuses: one or several, comma-separated, each a status (`404`) or a class (`4xx`, `5xx`). Anything else is `422`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Only calls whose path starts with this, with or without the `/v2` prefix (`/tickets` matches `/v2/tickets/TKT-10234`).

total.description: Calls matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page or a page that was not full.

get.description:
Every webhook event of the last 30 days on your account that one of your
endpoints subscribed to when it happened, oldest first, in the body a
delivery carries. An event no endpoint subscribed to, of any type, is not
kept and never appears here; an endpoint that is turned off still
counts. Use it to catch up after your receiver was down.

To catch up, pass the `eventId` of the last event you handled as
`after`, and follow `nextCursor` (pass it back as `cursor`) until it is
`null`. Events then arrive in the order they happened. Each carries the
same `eventId` as its deliveries, so a handler that de-duplicates on
`eventId` treats an event read here and one delivered as one. An event
older than 30 days is gone.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only these event types: one or several, comma-separated, each a type (`ticket.replied`) or a family (`ticket.*`). A type that does not exist is `422`.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only events at or after this time, an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only events after this one, by its `eventId`. An `eventId` that is not your account's, or is older than 30 days, is `422`: start again with `since`.

total.description: Events matching the query. Absent on a cursor page.

page.description: The page returned. Absent on a cursor page.

nextCursor.description: Pass back as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last page or a page that was not full.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event's `eventId`, from `GET /events` or a delivery.

get.description: One event of the last 30 days, in the body a delivery carries. An event that is not your account's, or is older than 30 days, is `404`.

parameters.name: eventId
parameters.description: The event's `eventId`, from `GET /events` or a delivery.

post.summary: Send an Event to an Endpoint
post.description:
Limit: 10 per minute for the account (webhook send), shared by test, redeliver, replay-dead and event re-send.

Sends one event of the last 30 days to one of your webhook endpoints, as
a new delivery. Use it for an event your receiver missed. Only an event
one of your endpoints subscribed to when it happened is kept, so only
such an event can be sent; it may go to any of your endpoints, including
one registered since.

The delivery carries the event's **own `eventId`** and its original
`occurredAt`, so a handler that de-duplicates on `eventId` sees the same
event, and the endpoint's next `sequence`. It is sent whether or not the
endpoint subscribes to the event's type, and while the endpoint is
disabled, as a redelivery is.

An endpoint that is not your account's is `404`. It is refused with `409`
while the endpoint holds 100 queued deliveries.

202.description: Queued

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:read

Every time a step of this port was handed to a person by a link, newest
first, with whether the link was used, cancelled or has expired.

200.description: A page of the port's delegations.

post.summary: Hand a Port's Step to a Person
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Email a named person a one-use link to do one step of this port, when
you cannot do it yourself. `confirmPort`: the holder of the mobile number
being ported enters the verification code texted to it, as
`POST /ports/{reference}/confirm` does; only a mobile port-in waiting
for its code (`ppv_sent`). `confirmAuthority`: the holder of the
fixed-line number reads the Porting Authority and confirms it with their
name and position, which is the port's Porting Authority and covers the
Agent Authority; only a port waiting for it (`awaiting_authority`, sent
with `authorityHolder` on `POST /ports`). Any other port is a `409`.

The link opens a page on your end-user portal, in your branding. The
person is emailed a code there first, then sees only the numbers being
ported and the step, and does it once. The link works for 7 days. When
it is used you get `delegation.used`.

Refused with `403` and the code `no_end_user_portal_access` when your
account has no end-user portal (turned off, or no domain).

The `Idempotency-Key` is required, so a retry after a timeout answers
with the first delegation and sends no second email.

One link is open per step at a time: while one is open (`sent` and not
expired), another for the same step is a `409`, to any address, and
sends nothing. Resend it, or cancel it and hand the step over again.

name.description: The person's name, used in the email.

email.description: Where the link, and then the code, are sent.

action.description: The one step the link allows.

201.description: The delegation; the link has been emailed.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** voice:update

Email the same person a new link, which works for 7 days from now. The
old link stops working at once, and any code sent for it with it. An
expired link can be resent; a used or cancelled one cannot (`409`), nor
one whose step is no longer open (`409`). A resend within 5 minutes of
the last email, or a sixth in a day, is a `429` with `Retry-After`, and
sends nothing.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:read

Every time a step of this order was handed to a person by a link, newest
first, with whether the link was used, cancelled or has expired.

200.description: A page of the order's delegations.

post.summary: Hand an Order's Step to a Person
post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Email a named person a one-use link to do one step of this order, when
you cannot do it yourself. `pickAppointment`: someone at the site picks
the technician's install time from the carrier's free slots and gives
the name and phone number the technician should call. Offered on an
NBN or Opticomm connect with no appointment yet, including an order
waiting for your appointment (`order.appointmentRequired`); any other
is a `409`.

The link opens a page on your end-user portal, in your branding. The
person is emailed a code there first, then sees only the site's address
and the free install times, and books one once. The appointment is put on the order as the
portal's Appointment card puts it; an order waiting for its appointment
is then sent to the carrier. The link works for 7 days. When it is used
you get `delegation.used`.

Refused with `403` and the code `no_end_user_portal_access` when your
account has no end-user portal (turned off, or no domain).

The `Idempotency-Key` is required, so a retry after a timeout answers
with the first delegation and sends no second email.

One link is open per step at a time: while one is open (`sent` and not
expired), another for the same step is a `409`, to any address, and
sends nothing. Resend it, or cancel it and hand the step over again.

name.description: The person's name, used in the email.

email.description: Where the link, and then the code, are sent.

action.description: The one step the link allows.

201.description: The delegation; the link has been emailed.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** data:update

Email the same person a new link, which works for 7 days from now. The
old link stops working at once, and any code sent for it with it. An
expired link can be resent; a used or cancelled one cannot (`409`), nor
one whose step is no longer open (`409`). A resend within 5 minutes of
the last email, or a sixth in a day, is a `429` with `Retry-After`, and
sends nothing.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none. Any token reads the key it was issued to.

The key the calling token belongs to: its name, scopes, IP allowlist,
end date and, while a rotation's overlap runs, when the old secret stops
working. Never a secret, and never another key.

A key belongs to your account, not to the user who made it: it keeps
working when that user leaves or changes role. Keys are created, rescoped
and revoked by an Owner or Admin under API Keys in the portal.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** none. Any token rotates the key it was issued to.

Gives the calling key a new secret, returned in this response only:
store it before anything else. Use it to roll a secret on a schedule
without an outage.

`rotationOverlapHours` (0 to 168, default 24) keeps the old secret
working for that long: both secrets mint tokens, and tokens from before
the rotation keep working, until `result.previousSecretExpiresAt`. A
token the old secret mints in the overlap ends with it. With `0`, the
old secret and every token minted with it stop at once, including the
token that asked. Rotating again ends the earlier overlap: only the
secret just replaced still works.

The account's Owners are emailed each time a key rotates itself.

An `Idempotency-Key` is required: a retry with the same key returns the
same new secret instead of rotating again.

rotationOverlapHours.description: How long the old secret keeps working, in hours.

200.description: The key, and its new secret.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Clears a staff user's second factor, for someone who has lost their
device. They set it up again the next time they sign in; on an account
that requires two-factor, they cannot go further until they do.

An Owner's two-factor cannot be reset through the API (`403`,
`owner_protected`): another
Owner resets it in the portal. `reset` is `false` when the user had no
second factor.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user's `id`.

reset.description: Whether there was a second factor to clear.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

For each notice a staff user can receive, the channels it can use and
the one they chose (`none` when they turned it off). Read only: each
user sets their own under Notifications in the portal.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The user's `id`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

The staff invitations not yet accepted, newest first, expired ones
included (`status: expired`) so you can resend them. `POST /account/users`
sends one, and its `inviteId` is the `id` here. Partner invitations are under `/partners/invites`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:delete

Withdraws an open staff invitation: its link stops working at once.

parameters.name: inviteId
parameters.description: The invitation's `id`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:create

Emails the invitation again with a fresh link, and starts its expiry
again. The old link stops working.

parameters.name: inviteId
parameters.description: The invitation's `id`.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Whether staff must use two-factor, and the addresses they may sign in to
the portal from: Company Settings > Security. Read only: an Owner or
Admin changes them in the portal. Each API key's own IP allowlist is on
`GET /account/api-keys/self`.

>**Required Scope(s):** `data:read` for disconnects, `voice:read` for plan changes; at least one

Every change booked on your account for a later date, in one list,
soonest first: a data service disconnect booked for a later day, and a
trunk plan or channel change waiting for the start of the next billing
cycle. Each can be cancelled with `DELETE /account/booked-changes/{id}`
before its date. A change that has taken effect, been cancelled or failed
on its date is no longer listed; `bookedChange.applied`,
`bookedChange.cancelled` and `bookedChange.failed` say when that happens.

A key lists only the kinds it may read: without `voice:read` there are no
plan changes, without `data:read` no disconnects. Asking for a `kind` the
key may not read is a `403`. The same change shows on the data service
and the trunk reads, as their `bookedChange`.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: One or both kinds, comma-separated. A value outside the set is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The booked change's id, as `GET /account/booked-changes` returns it.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** `data:delete` to cancel a disconnect, `voice:update` to cancel a plan change

Cancels a booked change before its date, so it does not apply: a
disconnect booked for a later day (the service stays live and billed),
or a trunk plan change booked for the next billing cycle (the trunk keeps
its current plan). It is the same cancel as the data service's and the
trunk's own (`DELETE /trunks/{username}/plan-change`), and sends
`bookedChange.cancelled`, beside `trunk.planChangeCancelled` for a plan
change.

A key without the cancelling kind's scope gets `403`. Another account's
change, and one already applied or cancelled, are `404`, as an unknown
id is. A disconnect that can no longer be cancelled is `409` with the
reason.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** the read scope of each type listed (`voice:read`, `sms:read`, `billing:read`, `data:read`); at least one

The account's background exports from the last 14 days, newest first,
of the types the key may read: without `voice:read` no `cdrs` exports
are listed, and so on. A ready one carries a fresh `downloadUrl`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: One or more states, comma-separated. A value outside the set is `422`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order by this field, `-` in front for descending. An unknown field is `422`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** the read scope of the type: `voice:read` for `cdrs`, `sms:read` for `sms`, `billing:read` for `invoiceLines`, `data:read` for `dataUsage`

Writes a large export in the background instead of one long streamed
response, and answers `202` with the export at once. Follow it with
`GET /exports/{exportId}`, or wait for `export.ready` (or
`export.failed`); a ready export carries a signed `downloadUrl`, good
for an hour, and its file is kept 7 days.

The rows are the streamed reads' own, so a file holds what `?format=` on
the list would have streamed for the same window and filters:

- `cdrs`: `GET /voice/cdrs`. Filters `trunk`, `endUser`, `direction`,
  `disposition`, `q`, `invoice`, `sort`.
- `sms`: `GET /sms`. Filters `direction`, `status`, `q`, `sort`.
- `invoiceLines`: each invoice issued in the window, one row per line as
  `GET /account/invoices/{invoiceId}?format=csv` has it. No filters.
- `dataUsage`: one row per data service per day, as
  `GET /data/services/{ref}/usage` buckets it (`serviceId`, `date`,
  `downloadBytes`, `uploadBytes`, `totalBytes`). Filter `serviceId`.
  Each day is a day on your account's time zone, the zone your bills
  are cut in. The export runs in the background, so `CN-Time-Zone`
  sets how `from` and `to` are read, not the days.

`from` is required and `to` defaults to now; the window is at most 93
days. A filter the type does not take, or a value the list would refuse,
is `422`. At most 3 exports run at once on an account: a fourth, while
3 are queued or running, is `409`.

to.description: The window's end. Now when absent.

filters.description: The list's own filters, by its query parameter names.

202.description: Accepted. The export is queued; `Location` names its read.

parameters.name: exportId
parameters.description: The export's id, as `POST /exports` returned it.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** the read scope of the export's type (`voice:read`, `sms:read`, `billing:read` or `data:read`)

The export's state, row count and size. While it is `ready` and its file
is kept (7 days), `downloadUrl` is a signed link to the file, good for
one hour; each read gives a new one, so read the export again when a
link has expired. Another account's export is `404`, as an unknown id
is; a key without the type's read scope gets `403`.

parameters.name: exportId
parameters.description: The export's id.

get.description:
The file of a ready export, through the signed `downloadUrl` that
`GET /exports/{exportId}` hands out. It needs no token: the signature is
the authority, and it lasts one hour. An expired or altered link is
`403`; read the export again for a new one. A file past its 7 days is
`410`.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: When the link stops working, as a Unix time. Part of the signed link.

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: The link's signature.

410.description: The export's file has been removed after its 7 days.

get.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

Your partners, by name, with the end users, products and permissions
each may reach: Company Settings > Partners.

>**Required Scope(s):** account:read

The partner invitations not yet accepted, newest first.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:create

Emails an invitation to a partner login. On accepting, the partner sees
only the end users and products named here; give it permissions after
with `PUT /partners/{partnerId}/scope`.

`endUsers` are end-user numbers on your account; `products` are product
ids on your retail price book. An unknown one is `422`. An email that
already has a login on your account, or an open invitation, is `422`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:delete

Withdraws an open partner invitation: its link stops working at once.

parameters.name: inviteId
parameters.description: The invitation's `id`.

delete.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:delete

Removes a partner: their login stops at once and they no longer see any
of your end users. Commission already earned is kept.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: The partner's `id`.

put.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

Replaces what a partner may reach. `endUsers` and `products` are both
required and replace the whole list (`[]` empties it). `permissions`,
when sent, replaces the partner's permissions; left out, they stay as
they are.

`endUsers` are end-user numbers on your account; `products` are product
ids on your retail price book. An unknown one is `422`.

parameters.name: partnerId
parameters.description: The partner's `id`.

post.description:
>**Required Scope(s):** account:update

**Sandbox only** (`https://api.checknetworks.dev`): production answers
`404`.

Wipes your sandbox account's orders, services, bills and callbacks and
starts its test addresses again, so a test run starts clean. Its users,
API keys and addresses are kept.

A sandbox can be reset 3 times in any 24 hours, from here and from API
Keys in the production portal together. Past that the reset is refused
with `429` and `Retry-After`, the seconds until the next is allowed.

resetsPerDay.description: How many resets are allowed in any 24 hours.

post.description: Sent when you call `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test` with no `eventType`, so you can check your endpoint receives and verifies deliveries. With an `eventType`, the test sends a sample of that event instead, in its own shape, with `test: true`.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a support ticket is raised on your account, from the portal, by our staff or through this API.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a public message is added to one of your tickets. `data.author` tells you who wrote it (`support`, `customer` or `api`). Internal Check Networks notes never emit this event.

post.description: Sent when a ticket's status changes — including the automatic re-open when a reply lands on a resolved ticket. `data.from` / `data.to` carry the transition.

post.description: Sent when our staff send one of your tickets back to you because they need something before they can go on: the ticket is set to waiting on you (`pending`), and the reply they send with it, the ticket's latest message from support, says what. It comes with `ticket.statusChanged`. A ticket set to `pending` any other way sends only `ticket.statusChanged`. Reply to the ticket to send it back to us.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a caller leaves a voicemail on one of your residential lines. It is sent for every new message, whether or not the mailbox also emails it.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

A hold never stops a 000 call, and inbound calls are not affected. Sent once per hold.

post.description: Sent when a plan or channel change takes effect on one of your trunks: a booked change on its effective date, or an upgrade at once. Use it to bill your end users for channels from the right day.

post.description: Sent when a change booked for a later date takes effect on its date: a trunk plan change on the 1st of the month, or a data disconnect booked for a later day, sent to the carrier that day (`service.disconnected` follows when the carrier confirms it). `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` listed.

The change is no longer listed and nothing changed; book it again if you still want it. `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` listed, plus the `reason`.

post.description: Sent when a background export (`POST /exports`) has its file. `data` is the export without its link: read `GET /exports/{exportId}` (the `resourceUrl`) for a signed `downloadUrl`, good for an hour.

post.description: Sent when Check Networks issues an invoice to your account. `data` carries the invoice summary. Invoices you raise to your own retail customers do not send this.

post.description:
Sent when one of your invoices is cancelled and its charges unwound — the counterpart to `invoice.issued`. The invoice is no longer owed: clear it from your receivables rather than carrying it as an open debt that nothing will ever settle.

`data.voidedAt` is when it was cancelled. A paid invoice is never voided — that is a refund or a credit note — so this only ever follows an `invoice.issued` you have already seen, and it fires once per invoice however many times a void is attempted.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent whenever a payment lands on your account, whether or not it settles an invoice — a part payment, an overpayment and a payment made before an invoice is issued all fire this.

`invoice.paid` only fires on FULL settlement, so this is the event to post receipts against if you are keeping a receivables ledger in step. `data.amount` is the payment and `data.balance` is your account balance after it, so you can reconcile without calling `GET /account/balance`.

amount.description: The payment amount, as a decimal string.

balance.description: Your account balance after this payment.

post.description: Sent when a payment that succeeded is taken back: a direct debit dishonoured or a card charged back. The invoices it paid are owed again, and `data.failureCode` / `data.failureMessage` carry the reason.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a PPPoE realm you requested is approved. The realm is live from that moment: logins are namespaced into it and PPPoE services can be provisioned.

post.description: Sent when a PPPoE realm you requested is not granted. `data.reason` carries why; the name is free for someone else, and you are welcome to request a different one.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when Opticomm reports the session of one of your RADIUS users on Opticomm's RADIUS. Opticomm gives it a minute or two after we ask, so when *Check Whether a User Is Online* or *Retrieve the Current Session* answers `202`, this event carries the answer and you need not poll. `data.session` is null when nothing is connected.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when one of your orders changes status, so you do not have to poll `/data/orders`. `data.from` / `data.to` carry the transition in the same words that endpoint publishes.

Orders move through more internal steps than the API publishes, and this event follows the published status — several internal steps share the status `InProgress`, and moving between them does not emit. You get one event per status change you can actually see.

Draft orders do not emit: they are not visible on `/data/orders` and have no order id to correlate against, so the first event for an order is the one where it becomes `InProgress`. The exception is an order waiting for your appointment or port (`order.appointmentRequired`, `order.ntdFull`): it is public under its PND, so if it is cancelled after 7 days unanswered, this event names that PND, with the reason. A held order (`order.delayed`) is public under its PND too: cancelling it sends this event naming the PND, `to: Failed`, with the reason.

Number ports (`orderType: numberPort`) are the exception to one event per status: a port sends this event on **every** step it takes, and again when its cutover moves, as our emails tell you. `step` is the port's real state (as `GET /ports/{reference}` reads it), `waitingOn` who it waits on, `scheduledFor` the booked cutover and `statusReason` why it stopped. A step that waits on you also sends `port.actionRequired`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent for an order held for a later submit time: when the hold starts, when its time changes, and when we hold it for you at its time because it could not be sent (for credit, because it was not ready, or because another order is open at the location). Nothing has been sent to the carrier. Subscribable while delayed orders are offered on your account.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when an order you placed with POST /data/orders needs a technician and no appointment was attached. The order is accepted and waits on our side; nothing is sent to the carrier until it has an appointment.

Read the order's timeslots (GET /data/orders/{orderId}/timeslots), reserve one on the network's appointment endpoint, and attach it with PATCH /data/orders/{orderId}. An order still waiting after 7 days is cancelled.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when an order you placed with POST /data/orders named no port and every port on the installed NTD is in use. We never order another NTD unasked, so the order waits on our side for you to choose:

- **A new NTD:** reserve an appointment from the order's timeslots and
  attach it with PATCH /data/orders/{orderId} (`appointmentId`).

- **Take over a port:** PATCH /data/orders/{orderId} with the port
  (`resourceId`), the service on it (`serviceId`, the AVC on NBN) and
  the `customerAuthorityDate`.


An order still waiting after 7 days is cancelled.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a number port arrives at a step only you can move: today, a mobile port-in waiting for the verification code its number's holder was sent (`action: enterVerificationCode`). Confirm it with `POST /ports/{reference}/confirm`, or send a fresh code with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code` once it lapses. The same step also arrives as `order.statusChanged`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when a service first comes up — a data service going live, or a SIP trunk becoming active. This is the event that tells you an order has turned into something usable.

`data.serviceType` says whether to read `data.serviceId` as a data service id or a trunk's `sipUsername`. Services migrated onto the platform from an existing environment do not emit this: they were already live for you, and the import is our records catching up.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a service is suspended and stops carrying traffic — including a suspension for non-payment, which is the most common reason a working service stops. Pair it with `service.resumed`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a suspended service is restored. Only emitted coming out of a suspension — a service going live for the first time sends `service.provisioned` instead.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a service is cancelled or terminated for good. Unlike `service.suspended` this is final — the service will not resume, and a replacement means a new order.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when the carrier tells us it will cease one of your data services on a future date, and no cease order of yours asked for it. Most are churns: the end user has moved to another provider. The service stays live, and billed, until `data.ceaseAt`, so there is time to warn your end user or reorder.

Sent once per date; if the carrier moves the date, it is sent again with the new one. `service.disconnected` follows on the day. A cease you ordered sends no `service.ceaseScheduled`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when a line test on one of your data services finishes: completed, cancelled or rejected. The carrier tells us when a test ends, so after `POST /nbn/diagnostics/avc/service_test` or `POST /opticomm/serviceTest` you need not poll. `data.result` is `Passed` or `Failed` where the carrier gives one; read the test by `data.testId` on `data.network`'s diagnostics endpoints for its measurements. A test still running sends nothing.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when a service health report on one of your data services is complete and stored, so after asking for one (`POST /nbn/service_health/service/{serviceRef}` or `POST /opticomm/serviceHealth`) you need not poll. Read it by `data.reportId` on `data.network`'s health endpoints. A report the carrier sends without being asked sends it too.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a technician appointment is committed to one of your orders. This is the first event for any appointment: a reserved slot is a hold that has not been committed and routinely lapses, so it is not announced, and every later appointment event follows a booking you have already been sent.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when a booked appointment's window moves. `data.previousSlotStart` and `data.previousSlotEnd` carry the window it used to hold.

Worth wiring up before anything else on this list: a reschedule most often originates with the carrier rather than with you, and a missed one means the technician arrives at an empty premises — a missed-appointment fee and a week's slip on the order.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a booked appointment is cancelled or expires. The order stays where it is — it simply has no appointment any more, and needs a new one booked.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description:
Sent when a network outage affecting services on your account reaches the register. `data` is the same body `GET /outages` returns, plus `yourAffectedServiceCount` and `yourAffectedServiceTypes`.

You are only sent outages that match your own services — the same matching `GET /outages` performs — so this and the read endpoint can never disagree about whether you are affected. Only reviewed, published entries are sent.

Planned maintenance is sent too, with `data.planned` true: when we first send its notice to your account.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when something a customer would be told about a running outage changes — the estimated restoration time, the affected area, the cause, the notes. Our own notification bookkeeping does not emit, so you will not receive one of these every time we send an email about the outage.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when the outage is resolved and services are restored. `data.resolvedAt` is when that happened.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when we raise a potential service degradation at a POI where you have a live data service: our interconnect there is busy and the extra capacity is delayed, so services may be slower at peak. They are not down, and it is not an outage. `data.expectedResolutionAt` is when we expect the capacity, and `data.yourAffectedServiceCount` how many of your services are there.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when the expected date, the affected POIs or what we tell customers changes. An account newly affected by the change is sent `degradation.opened` instead.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when the extra capacity is in place. `data.resolvedAt` is when.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when an EE fibre build quote linked to your account is priced. `data.quote` is the quote as `GET /nbn/quotes/{quoteId}` returns it, with the fibre build contribution in `quoteItem` and its validity in `validFor`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when the carrier holds a quote waiting on you: `data.quote.status` is `InProgress` with `subStatus` `Pending`, and `eventNote` gives the carrier's reason. Contact support so we can give the carrier what it needs.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a quote ends without a price: `data.quote.status` is `Rejected`, `Cancelled`, `Closed` or `Expired`. Request a new quote for the location with `POST /nbn/quotes`. A priced quote reaching the end of its `validFor` window sends nothing.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when an address on one of your IP transit services is blackholed, by you or by Check Networks (`data.placedBy`). Traffic to the address is dropped at our border from then on.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a blackhole is released before its expiry, by you or by Check Networks. Traffic to the address resumes.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a blackhole reaches its expiry and lifts by itself, within 15 minutes of `data.expiresAt`. Traffic to the address resumes; place it again if the attack is still running.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when an end user's charges this month reach 50, 85 or 100 per cent (`data.tier`) of the monthly spend limit you set on them, once per tier per month, from the daily check that emails the end user. It is sent whether or not the end user has an address to email. Spent is the same figure as Get End User Spend and the end user's Next Bill Estimate. Only for an account that bills its end users.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when you issue a credit note on one of your bills to an end user, including one that decides the end user's dispute in their favour. `data.endUser` names the end user by its number. Only for an account that bills its end users.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when an end user disputes one of your bills to them, from their portal. The disputed amount is not chased while the dispute is open. Only for an account that bills its end users.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when you decide an end user's dispute, in the portal or by API. `data.outcome` says how; a credit carries its amount and credit note, and `endUser.creditNote.issued` is sent for it too.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when a message arrives on one of your mobile numbers and is passed on, with its text (`data.message`). A message held as a suspected scam sends nothing unless our team releases it, when it is sent then. This is the only SMS event that carries the text.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when the delivery receipt for a message you sent says it reached the handset. `data.messageId` is the `messageId` from `POST /sms`.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when the delivery receipt for a message you sent says it could not be delivered, with the reason (`data.failureReason`).

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when a fax arrives on one of your numbers, after it is emailed or kept for the portal; `data.status` says which, or `failed` when it could not be passed on. Metadata only: never the document.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when a fax from one of your fax plans has gone through, with the pages sent.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent once when a fax from one of your fax plans has failed for good, with the reason. A busy line or no answer is retried first, and sends nothing until the last try fails.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

post.description: Sent when your account is suspended. From now, writes through this API answer `403` until it is reinstated; reads and webhooks keep working.

200.description: Acknowledged - any 2xx response marks the event as delivered.

OAuth2.description: OAuth2 access tokens are used for API access. An API key uses the client credentials flow. A registered OAuth app uses the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256) and its client secret: an Owner or Admin approves it on the consent screen in the wholesale portal, and its tokens act for that account within the scopes approved, until the account revokes it under Connected Apps. Access tokens last an hour. An app's refresh token is replaced on every use and lasts 30 days from that use, so an app left idle for 30 days must be connected again. Sending a replaced refresh token again within 60 seconds of its replacement is refused as `temporarily_unavailable`, a retry; after that it disconnects the app from the account. An app never gets a `safety:*` scope. See https://help.checknetworks.tools/api/oauth-apps/.
