status.description: HTTP status code for the error.

code.description: A stable code to branch on; `reason` is free text and may change. Each has an entry at `docUrl` saying what to do. A refusal says why: `key_revoked`, `key_expired`, `secret_rotated`, `scopes_changed` and `missing_scope` need a new key, token or scope; `ip_not_allowed` needs the caller's address on the key's allowlist; `account_suspended` and `account_inactive` need a person on your side; `owner_protected` is a change to an Owner (name, email, role, two-factor or removal), which a key, acting as an Admin, may never make; `app_disabled` and `app_access_revoked` (an OAuth app's token) mean the app must be connected again; `idempotency_in_progress` (with `Retry-After`) means retry later, and `idempotency_key_reused` means send the new request under a new key. The `carrier_` codes and the five before them are the canonical carrier errors, the same whichever carrier refused: `address_not_serviceable`, `duplicate_order`, `insufficient_capacity`, `auth_validation_failed`, `customer_authority_required` and `charge_acknowledgement_required` are a carrier refusing the request on its merits; `carrier_bad_request` is a carrier refusing it for any other reason (its own code is in `carrierCode`); `carrier_unauthenticated`, `carrier_rate_limited` and `carrier_unavailable` are our link to the carrier failing, so retry later; `carrier_unknown` is a carrier failure we could not classify. `caller_id_authorisation_required` is a trunk's caller ID that your account neither holds nor has had approved: ask for it with `POST /caller-id-authorisations`. `hold_expired` is a number order naming a hold that has run out: hold the number again. `no_end_user_portal_access` is a sign-in link asked for an end user who cannot use the end-user portal. `sender_not_approved` is a `POST /sms` from a sender your account has no approval for: request one with `POST /sms/senders`. `emergency_call` is a hang-up refused because the call is to 000, 112 or 106. `sq_batch_allowance_exceeded` is a qualification batch over your account's allowance: `remainingRows` says how many rows you may still send today. `no_live_session` is a session reset with nothing connected to drop, and `session_not_resettable` one on a network where a reset is not possible. New codes may be added: treat an unknown code by its `status`.

reason.description: Client-friendly reason for the error.

messageId.description: This request's id, the same as the `CN-Message-Id` response header. Quote it to support.

docUrl.description: The `code`'s entry on the error reference page.

carrierCode.description: The upstream carrier's own error code, where the failure was a carrier rejection of the request (e.g. NBN's RJ002003 or 001013). Absent when the error did not originate at a carrier.

remainingRows.description: On a `sq_batch_allowance_exceeded` error, the rows your account may still qualify by batch today; null when the day has no row limit and the refusal is the hourly batch count. Absent on every other error.

charge.description: On a `charge_acknowledgement_required` error, the charge the request would incur. Repeat the request accepting it to go ahead. Absent on every other error.

amount.description: The charge as a decimal dollar amount, without GST. Deprecated: read `amountExGst`, `amountGst` and `amountIncGst` instead.

amountExGst.description: The charge without GST, as a decimal dollar amount.

amountIncGst.description: The charge with GST, what the invoice will show.

contractEndsOn.description: When the contract the charge comes from ends.

period.description: On a recurring charge (call recording), how often it is billed: the amounts are per period.

consent.description: On a `charge_acknowledgement_required` error for call recording, the consent you accept by sending `acknowledgeRecording: true`. Absent on every other error.

holdId.description: On a `POST /numbers` that bought a number from our supplier but could not place the order, a hold on the number bought, until `heldUntil`. Order again with this `holdId` (same `type`, `szu` and `blockSize`) and the number is taken without buying it again. Absent on every other error.

heldUntil.description: When the `holdId` beside it runs out. Absent on every other error.

allowance.description: On a `rate_limited` error from `POST /numbers/lookup`, the account's daily number lookup allowance: how many it allows, how many were used today, and how many the refused batch asked for. It resets at midnight Brisbane time; `Retry-After` gives the seconds until then. Absent on every other error.

existingWebhookId.description: On a `409` from `POST /webhooks`, the endpoint already registered at that URL. Absent on every other error.

fields.description: On a `validation_failed` error, one entry per failed rule, naming the input it was about. Absent on every other error.

field.description: The input's name; nested inputs use dots, e.g. `address.postcode`.

reason.example: The location id field is required.

AddressMatch.description: An address from our copy of G-NAF.

gnafId.description: The G-NAF address id (`address_detail_pid`). Pass it to `GET /nbn/address/search?gnaf=` to find the NBN location.

roadNumber2.description: The end of a number range, such as 14 in 12-14.

confidence.description: G-NAF's confidence in the address, from -1 to 2. 2 means three or more contributing sources agree.

nbnLocId.description: The NBN location id, when we already know it.

opticommOpcId.description: The Opticomm property id, when the address is on Opticomm's network.

AccountBillingAddress.description: The address printed on our invoices to you (#4891), in the same shape as the account's `address`. Each line is null when not on file.

state.description: The state or territory. A change by API must be one of ACT, NSW, NT, QLD, SA, TAS, VIC or WA; an address our staff entered may hold another.

postcode.description: Four digits when changed by API.

country.description: Australia when an address is saved without one.

AccountBillingContact.description: Your billing contact (#4891), where invoices and billing notices go. Each field is null when not on file.

CreditPosition.description: Where your account stands with us, with the same meaning on a prepaid and a postpaid account. `amountOwed` includes GST, as your invoices do. The credit line is read as credit control reads it and the portal dashboard shows it: without GST, and credit used is what you owe plus usage not yet invoiced. Your services are held when `availableCredit` reaches zero.

amountOwed.description: What you owe us on invoices, less payments and credits, with GST. Positive when you owe us; negative when you hold credit with us.

creditLimit.description: Your credit limit with us, without GST. Two decimals.

creditUsed.description: How much of the credit limit is used, without GST: what you owe plus usage not yet invoiced. Never below `0.00`.

availableCredit.description: The credit limit less credit used, without GST. Below zero when you are over your limit.

creditUsedPercent.description: Credit used as a whole percentage of the limit, the figure the credit warnings at 80, 90, 95 and 100% are sent on.

Notice.description: A notice we sent you or one of your end users, and what happened to it. No message body is kept, so a notice is told by its kind and what it was about.

createdAt.description: When we sent it (or tried to).

kind.description: What the notice is, e.g. `invoice_issued`, `overdue_notice`, `outage_started`. New kinds may be added.

recipient.description: The address it went to. `Suppressed` for an end user whose contact details are withheld under a family violence record.

endUser.description: The number of the end user it went to, or null for a notice to you.

about.description: What the notice was about, or null.

type.description: `invoice`, `creditNote`, `outage` or `payment`; other notices name their own kind of record.

reference.description: The invoice or credit note number, the outage reference, or the payment's amount and date.

status.description: `suppressed` means not sent, because an earlier notice to the address bounced hard or was marked as spam.

error.description: Why it failed, bounced or was suppressed.

lastEventAt.description: The mail service's latest report on it (delivered, bounced).

BillingInvoice.description: One of our invoices to your account, as List Invoices returns it. Money is a decimal dollar string in `currency`. A priced figure carries three fields: without GST, the GST, and with GST.

id.description: The invoice's id, as `GET /account/invoices/{invoiceId}` takes it. Opaque: compare it, never parse it.

createdAt.description: When the invoice was created, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the invoice last changed, in UTC.

type.description: Always `invoice`. An explicit discriminator matching the `type` field on /account/credit-notes rows.

total.description: This invoice's new charges with GST. Deprecated: read `totalIncGst`.

totalExGst.description: This invoice's new charges without GST.

totalGst.description: The GST on this invoice's new charges.

totalIncGst.description: This invoice's new charges with GST.

currency.description: The currency of the invoice amounts.

periodStart.description: The first day of the period the invoice bills.

periodEnd.description: The last day of the period the invoice bills.

previousBalance.description: The balance carried onto this invoice from before it, with GST, as the invoice prints it.

amountPaid.description: The payments applied to this invoice so far, with GST, as the portal's invoice page lists them.

amountDue.description: What is still owed on this invoice now, with GST. `0.00` once it is paid or void. A part-paid invoice shows what is left.

amountDisputed.description: The part of `amountDue` an open dispute holds off collection and reminders, with GST. `0.00` when nothing is disputed.

paidAt.description: The date the invoice settled. `null` while any amount is still outstanding, and cleared again if a payment is later dishonoured and the invoice reopens. This is the settlement date of the payment that closed the invoice, not the time it was recorded.

PaymentCharge.description: A card or direct debit charge we started on your account, from autopay or Pay Now in the portal. While `inFlight`, it has not reached your balance yet: do not pay the same invoice again.

invoiceId.description: The invoice the charge pays, when it pays one.

methodLabel.description: The stored method as the portal names it.

amount.description: The charge, with GST like the invoice it pays.

status.description: `initiated` and `pending` are in flight. `succeeded` moves to List Payments once it settles. `errored` means the provider's answer was lost; the charge is retried with the same key, so it cannot be taken twice.

BillingLineDetailRow.description: One row behind an invoice line. `kind` says which fields it has: a `call` (the calls a usage line charges) or a `burst_settlement` (the 95th percentile behind a transit burst line).

dialled.description: The number dialled, E.164 without the `+` (`call`).

included.description: The call was inside an included allowance, so it charged nothing (`call`).

chargeExGst.description: The call's charge without GST, to 4 decimal places as rated (`call`).

billedMbps.description: The whole Mbps above the commit that was billed.

BillingInvoiceLine.description: One line of an invoice: what it charges, the service, end user and period it bills, and the rows behind it.

id.description: The line's public id, for its detail route and a dispute's `lineId`.

product.description: The product the line charges for, as the invoice names it.

unitPrice.description: The unit price without GST, to up to 5 decimal places. Deprecated: read `unitPriceExGst`.

unitPriceExGst.description: The unit price without GST, to up to 5 decimal places.

unitPriceGst.description: The GST on one unit; `0.00` on a GST-free line.

total.description: The line total with GST. Deprecated: read `totalIncGst`.

tax.description: The GST on the line. Deprecated: read `totalGst`.

totalGst.description: The GST on the line, as the invoice charged it.

totalIncGst.description: The line total with GST. Lines add up to the invoice's `totalIncGst`.

serviceType.description: The kind of service the line bills. Null for an account-level line, or a service the API does not read.

serviceRef.description: The service, named as its own routes name it: a data service's `GET /data/services/{ref}`, a trunk's SIP username, a fax plan's or VPN user's id, a transit service's number. Null for an account-level line.

serviceCategory.description: The broad category the line bills under.

endUser.description: The end user's number when the service belongs to one of your end users.

group.description: The section of the invoice the line prints under.

invoiceGroup.description: The name of the invoice group you placed the line's service in, as it stood when the invoice was built. Null for a line in no group, which prints under Other.

invoiceGroupId.description: The invoice group's public id, as GET /account/invoice-groups names it. Null once the group has been removed.

invoiceLabel.description: The service's own billing label when the invoice was built.

poNumber.description: The purchase order number in effect for the line, the service's own or else its group's.

costCentre.description: The cost centre in effect for the line, the service's own or else its group's.

periodStart.description: The first day the line bills for. Null for a one-off charge.

periodEnd.description: The last day the line bills for.

detail.description: The rows behind the line, as the portal opens them: the calls a usage line charges, or a transit burst settlement. At most 50; `detailHref` pages the rest.

detailTotal.description: How many rows are behind the line in all.

detailHref.description: Where to page every row when there are more than `detail` carries; null otherwise.

InvoiceGroupSection.description: One section of an issued invoice: an invoice group's lines and subtotal, as the group stood when the invoice was built. Lines in no group are the Other section, with a null `groupId`. Money is in dollars; the subtotal is split ex GST, GST and inc GST.

groupId.description: The group's public id; null for Other.

lineIds.description: The public ids of the section's lines, as `lineItems[].id`.

BillingPayment.description: A payment we received on your account, with the invoices it settled.

id.description: The payment's id, as the `payment.*` webhook events name it in `paymentId`. Opaque: compare it, never parse it.

createdAt.description: When the payment was recorded, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the payment last changed (a reversal), in UTC.

type.description: Always `payment`, the discriminator beside invoice rows (`type: invoice`) and credit-note rows (`type: credit_note`). `amount` is unsigned, so treat a payment as a credit by its `type`, not its sign.

status.description: `applied` once the payment is on your account; `reversed` when your bank later dishonoured it and the amount was taken back off.

amount.description: The payment in dollars, as a decimal string with two decimals. A payment has no GST of its own: it pays invoices whose totals include GST, so read it as GST-inclusive.

method.description: How it was paid: `bank_transfer`, `bpay`, `cheque`, `cash`, `offset` or `other` for a payment our billing team recorded, otherwise the direct-debit gateway that reported it.

reference.description: The payment reference as it reached us, if any.

invoices.description: The invoices this payment settled, oldest first, and how much of each.

invoiceId.description: The invoice's `id`, as on List Invoices.

amount.description: The part of this payment applied to that invoice, in dollars with GST.

receiptHref.description: Our receipt for this payment as a PDF (Get Payment Receipt).

PricingItem.description: One product at the price you pay us, as the portal's Pricing page shows it, with any volume tiers and the tier your current quantity sits in.

displayName.description: The Friendly/Display Name of the Product/Service

setup.description: The upfront price without GST. Deprecated: read `setupExGst`.

rate.description: The recurring price without GST. Deprecated: read `rateExGst`.

rateExGst.description: The recurring price without GST. On a tiered product, the first tier's price; `tiers` has the rest.

increment.description: The Billing Interval/Period for the Product/Service

tiers.description: Volume tiers, lowest first. Empty for a flat price.

from.description: The first quantity this tier's price applies to.

to.description: The last quantity, or null for the top tier.

heldQuantity.description: How many you hold now, on a tiered product; null otherwise.

currentTier.description: The tier `heldQuantity` sits in, counting from 1; null for a flat price.

AccountUser.description: A staff login on your wholesale account.

id.description: The user's id, for the user's own routes.

twoFactorEnabled.description: Whether the user has a second factor set up.

lastLoginAt.description: When the user last signed in to the portal, in UTC.

createdAt.description: When the login was created, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the login last changed, in UTC.

Layer2Destination.description: A Layer 2 link destination — one of your active customer-interconnect outer VLANs (S-Tags), where a Layer 2 service can be handed off to you.

interconnectRef.description: The customer interconnect this destination belongs to.

outerVlan.description: The outer VLAN (S-Tag) at the handoff.

poiCode.description: The Point of Interconnect code. `0NAT` is a reserved code for a single-tag interconnect — one outer VLAN carries all your services across every POI and carrier, rather than a separate tag per POI — and therefore serves both NBN and Opticomm.

poiName.description: The Point of Interconnect name (null for a `0NAT` destination).

carriers.description: The carrier network(s) this destination serves.

isDefault.description: Whether this is the default destination on its interconnect.

SuspensionTakesEffect.description: On a suspended data service, how soon the suspension takes effect: `within 15 minutes` for a service we cut, `within 1 business day` for an Opticomm L3 service, which the carrier suspends for us, and `cannot be suspended yet` for a service handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect, which keeps passing traffic. Null while the service is not suspended.

ExternalRef.description: Your own reference for this object, such as your customer or job id, so you need not keep a map from our ids to yours. Up to 64 letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`. Unique on your account for each kind of object (two trunks cannot share one, but a trunk and a ticket can); matched exactly by the list's `externalRef` filter. Set it on create or with PATCH; send null to clear it. Null when none is set.

Metadata.description: Your own key-value pairs on this object: at most 20 keys, each up to 40 letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`, each value text of up to 255 characters. We store them and send them back on reads and webhooks; we never act on them. A map you send replaces the one held; send `{}` or null to clear it. An empty object when none is set.

BookedChangeRef.description: The change booked on this service or trunk for a later date, as `GET /account/booked-changes` lists it in full, or null when none is. `DELETE /account/booked-changes/{id}` cancels it.

DataService.description: One of your data services, on any network, in one shape. Fields we do not hold for a service are null.

id.description: The product reference: an NBN PRI, or an Opticomm product. Use it, or `serviceId`, to address the service.

href.description: Link to this service on the Check Networks API.

network.description: The network that delivers the service.

serviceId.description: The service reference on the network, such as an NBN AVC.

status.description: Where the service is. A connect still in flight is an order, not a service.

speed.description: The speed of the service's plan, in Mbps.

locationId.description: The premises the service is at, an NBN location id or an Opticomm one.

poi.description: The NBN point of interconnect the service is carried through, where we hold it.

plan.description: The plan you are billed for, by our SKU and name; before the service has a plan, the SKU it was ordered on, with `name` null.

customerReference.description: Your own reference for the service.

tags.description: Your own tags on the service, in the order you set them (PUT /data/services/{ref}/tags). A Connect's tags are carried to the service it builds.

radiusUser.description: The service's RADIUS user reference, for the RADIUS endpoints (GET /data/radius/{ref}).

endUser.description: The retail customer you assigned the service to, by its public number, or null.

endUserName.description: That end user's name, or null.

endUserDetail.description: Present only with `expand=endUser`: the end user in full, or null when the service has none.

endUser.description: The end user's public number, as `endUser`.

externalReference.description: Your own reference for the end user.

requestedAt.description: When the service was ordered. The list opens newest first on this.

updatedAt.description: When the service last changed.

DataOrderSummary.description: One order as a row of GET /data/orders: enough to act on without reading each order. The whole order is GET /data/orders/{orderId}, its `href`.

id.description: The order ID: the carrier's, or a Check Networks PND for an order the carrier does not have yet. The same ID the order read takes.

href.description: Link to the whole order.

status.description: "InProgress" covers everything still moving, including an order waiting for you.

statusReason.description: Why a failed order failed, or what an order waiting for you or for Check Networks needs. As on the order read.

locationId.description: The premises the order is for (LOC

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as supplied when the order was placed.

salesReference.description: The same value as `orderReference`, the order's sales reference.

serviceId.description: The service the order produced (AVC

endUser.description: The end user the order is for, by its public number, or null.

endUserName.description: That end user's name, or null.

actionRequired.description: What the order waits for from you, or null: `appointmentRequired` or `ntdFull`. The order read has the detail.

tags.description: Your own tags on the order.

updatedAt.description: When the order last changed.

service.description: Present only with `expand=service`, the order's service in the shape of the service list, or null before there is one.

MetadataInput.description: Your own key-value pairs, as `Metadata` describes them. The map you send replaces the one held; `{}` or null clears it.

DataOrderCreate.description: A Connect order for any data network. Take each value from the Service Qualification for the location (GET /data/sq/{locId}).

locId.description: The premises: an NBN Location ID (LOC…) or an Opticomm Property ID (OPC…). The location decides which network and product the order is placed as.

bandwidthProductSku.description: One of the `availablePlans` SKUs from the Service Qualification.

orderReference.description: Your own reference for the order. Sending the same reference again returns the order it already placed rather than placing a second one.

tags.description: Your own tags on the order, carried to the service it builds (see PUT /data/services/{ref}/tags). Each is trimmed, at most 255 characters, matched ignoring case; at most 20. Checked before anything is sent to the carrier. A retry under the same `orderReference` keeps the tags the order was placed with.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the data service this order builds, held on the order and set on the service when it is built (see PATCH /data/services/{ref}). One another of your data services holds, or another open order holds for its service, is a 422 before anything is sent to the carrier. A retry under the same `orderReference` keeps the reference the order was placed with.

metadata.description: Your own metadata for the data service this order builds, set on it when it is built.

informedConsent.description: Confirms the End User has given Informed Consent for the order.

resourceId.description:
(Optional) One of the `resources` from the Service Qualification: the NTD or OTD port, or the copper pair, the service runs on.
Leave it out and we choose: the next free port on an installed NTD; on copper, the one spare pair, or a new line where there is none. Where no NTD is installed, the order waits for an appointment (`order.appointmentRequired`). Where every port is in use, it waits for you to choose a new NTD or a port to take over (`order.ntdFull`): we never order a second NTD unasked. Required on copper with more than one spare pair.

appointmentId.description: (Optional) An appointment you reserved for this location, where the order needs a technician. Without one, such an order waits for it (see `order.appointmentRequired`).

preferredAppointmentDate.description: (Optional) The first day you would like a technician, should the order need one: today or later, on your account's time zone (or the one you sent in `CN-Time-Zone`). The order's timeslots read (GET /data/orders/{orderId}/timeslots) starts here.

potsInterconnect.description: (Conditional, copper) The Full National Number (FNN) or Unconditioned Local Loop (ULL) of the phone service being transitioned. Required for an Active Service Class 12 pair, and must not be sent otherwise.

priorityAssist.description: (Optional) Sent to the carrier as its priority assist flag. "true" is accepted only for an `endUser` on our Priority Assistance register; otherwise the order is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist` before anything is drafted. A `newEndUser` is never on the register.

endUser.description: (Optional) The end user the service is for, by its public number. The service, its charges and its usage are then theirs, as an order placed in the portal for them. One of your end users that is not archived; any other number is a 422 and no order is placed.

occupancyDocumentId.description: (Optional) On an NBN Connect Outstanding, the `id` of a proof of occupancy uploaded with `POST /data/occupancy-documents`, instead of the old service's id: evidence that the end user occupies the premises. It is kept with the order, and each one is used by one order: a retry with the same `orderReference` may name it again. A retry after a call that stopped before the order was sent keeps it with the order before sending it, unless the order already keeps one. Not with `serviceRef`; another account's, or one another order used, is a 422.

bundleId.description: (Optional) An open bundle to add the order to, as a draft that is placed when the bundle is submitted. A bundle that has been submitted, or is not yours, is a 422.

newEndUser.description: (Optional) A new end user to make and order for in this one call, instead of `endUser`; never both. It takes the same fields and rules as creating an end user. Both parts are checked before anything is made; if the order is refused, the end user is not kept and the answer is the order's 422. The end user's welcome email goes only once the order is accepted. A retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same end user and order. The response's `endUser` is the new end user's number.

endUserType.description: (Optional) What the carrier is told the premises is. Left out, it is taken from the end user's own type, as the portal does.

addons.description: (Optional) The add-on products to sell with the service, each with a quantity. Only the add-ons the portal offers for the chosen plan may be sent; any other is a 422. Left out, the order carries the plan's default add-ons, as the portal ticks them; an empty list carries none. Each starts billing when the carrier accepts the order.

productId.description: The add-on product's public id, as an order's `addons` show it (GET /data/orders/{orderId}).

restorationSlaSku.description: (Optional, NBN) The restoration SLA, one the chosen plan allows at this location; the standard SLA when left out. Refused on an Opticomm order.

staticIp.description: (Optional) A static IPv4 address rather than one from the dynamic pool. A monthly charge applies.

ipv6.description: (Optional) IPv6 (a framed /64 and a delegated prefix). Free, and on unless you turn it off.

install.description:
(Optional) How the service reaches the premises:

- `existing`: on a port or pair already there (`resourceId`, or the one we choose).
- `new`: a new NTD, OTD or copper pair, where the Service Qualification offers a new install.
- `additional`: another NTD, OTD or pair beside the ones in use, where it offers an additional install.
- `fibreUplift`: not yet available through the API; order it in the portal.

A `new` or `additional` install takes no `resourceId` and needs a
technician appointment, on NBN and Opticomm alike: without an
`appointmentId` the order waits for one (`order.appointmentRequired`).
It is a 422 where the location does not offer it.

transferType.description: (Optional) Take over a service another provider has at the premises, in this one call. On NBN, as the NBN order routes take it, with `serviceRef` and `customerAuthorityDate`. On Opticomm, `Service Transfer` or `Service Transfer Reversal` with `customerAuthorityDate` and no `serviceRef`.

serviceRef.description: (Conditional, NBN transfer) The AVC of the service being taken over.

customerAuthorityDate.description: (Conditional, transfer) The day the end user authorised the transfer. Required with `transferType`. Today or earlier, on your account's time zone (or the one you sent in `CN-Time-Zone`).

DataOrder.description: An order for a data service, in carrier-agnostic form.

id.description: The order ID: the carrier's, or a Check Networks PND for an order the carrier does not have yet: one waiting for your appointment or port (see actionRequired), or an NBN order awaiting Check Networks validation (see statusReason). That PND keeps finding the order after the carrier gives it an ID.

href.description: Link to this order on the Check Networks API.

type.description: What the order does.

status.description: Where the order has got to. "InProgress" covers everything still moving, including an order awaiting an appointment.

statusReason.description: Why a failed order failed. For an InProgress NBN order that NBN could not accept as Check Networks sent it, "Awaiting Check Networks validation": the fault is ours, nothing is needed from you, and Check Networks will correct and resubmit it; it ends Failed only if it cannot be placed. For an order waiting for you, what it needs (see actionRequired). Null otherwise.

actionRequired.description: What an order waiting for you needs, or null. Nothing has been sent to the carrier; answer it with PATCH /data/orders/{orderId}.

reason.description: "appointmentRequired": a technician is needed; attach an appointment. "ntdFull": every port on the NTD is in use; attach an appointment for a new NTD, or name a port to take over.

demandType.description: The appointment type a technician visit for this order needs.

expiresAt.description: When the order is cancelled if it is still waiting.

preferredAppointmentDate.description: The first day you would like a technician, as you placed the order.

locationId.description: The premises the order is for (LOC

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as supplied when the order was placed.

salesReference.description: The same value as `orderReference`, the order's sales reference.

serviceId.description: The service the order produced (AVC # or OVC #), once the carrier has assigned one.

appointmentId.description: The appointment attached to this order, if any.

tags.description: Your own tags on the order, as placed with POST /data/orders. They are carried to the service it builds.

endUser.description: The end user the order is for, by its public number, or null.

endUserName.description: That end user's name, or null.

endUserType.description: What the carrier was told the premises is.

address.description: The premises as qualified, or null where we hold no address for the location.

poi.description: The Point of Interconnect the service is delivered through.

name.description: Our product's name for the plan, as the portal names it; null where no product sells the SKU.

restorationSlaSku.description: The restoration SLA ordered (NBN), or null for the standard one.

addons.description: The add-ons sold with the service.

staticIp.description: Whether a static IPv4 address was ordered.

ipv6.description: Whether IPv6 was ordered; null where the order does not say.

price.description: The monthly charge and the one-off charges the order will start: the plan and each add-on times its quantity, at your prices. Null for a key without `billing:read`, or where the plan is not priced for you.

contacts.description: The contacts given for the install; null where the order holds none.

customerRequiredDate.description: The carrier's customer required date, where it has one.

events.description: The order's timeline, oldest first: its state changes, the carrier's progress and appointment updates, and its notes.

createdBy.description:
Who placed the order: the portal user's name, or the name of the API
key that placed it through `POST /data/orders`. Null where we hold
neither (an API order placed before 21 Nov 2026).

service.description: Present only with `expand=service`: the service the order is for, in the shape of the service list (GET /data/services), or null before there is one.

BundleItem.description: One item of a bundle: a data order, a number order or a voice trunk, in the bundle's order.

id.description: The item's own id: a data order's carrier order id once placed, else its `PND` reference; a number order's `id`; a trunk's id in the bundle, which `POST /numbers` takes as `trunk` to put numbers on it.

href.description: Where the item is read on its own: the data order once the carrier has it, the number order, or the trunk once it is set up. Null until then.

label.description: What the portal calls the item.

position.description: Its place in the bundle; 1 is first.

waitsForPrevious.description: Whether it starts only once every item above it has completed. Numbers on the bundle's own trunk always do.

state.description: `draft` until it is released, `inProgress` once it has been sent, then `completed`, or `failed` when it ended without completing.

waitingFor.description: The ids of the items above it it is still waiting on.

outcomeReason.description: Why it ended without completing, or null.

DataOrderAnswer.description: What an order waiting for you needs: an appointment, or a port to take over. Send `appointmentId` or `resourceId`.

appointmentId.description: An appointment you reserved from the order's timeslots (GET /data/orders/{orderId}/timeslots). On an NTD with no free port, a technician installs another NTD on it.

resourceId.description: On an NTD with no free port: the port to take over, from the Service Qualification's `resources`.

serviceId.description: The service on that port, taken over by this order (the AVC on NBN).

customerAuthorityDate.description: When the End User authorised taking the service over. Required with `serviceId`.

DataProvisioningRecord.description: A provisioning request: what was configured for a service, what we allocated for it, and whether it is live yet.

href.description: Link to this provisioning request on the Check Networks API.

orderId.description: The order this provisioning belongs to.

status.description: Pending while the carrier is still working the order; Complete once the service is built and everything below is final.

deliveryMode.description: How the service is handed to you.

protocol.description: The Layer 3 session protocol. Null for Layer 2.

staticIp.description: Whether the IPv4 address is held stable. Null for Layer 2.

ipv6.description: Whether IPv6 is provisioned. Null for Layer 2.

handoff.description: Layer 2 only — the interconnect this service hands off on.

cTag.description: Layer 2 only — the inner VLAN. Your chosen one while pending, the allocated one once complete.

pppoeUsername.description: PPPoE only — the login the CPE dials with, once it exists.

serviceId.description: The service this produced (AVC

id.description: The provisioning request reference — track it on GET /data/provisioning/{ref}.

orderNumber.description: The order the configuration was applied to.

deliveryMode.description: How the service will be handed to you.

protocol.description: The Layer 3 session protocol. Null for Layer 2.

staticIp.description: Whether the IPv4 address is held stable. Null for Layer 2.

ipv6.description: Whether IPv6 will be provisioned. Null for Layer 2.

pppoeUsername.description: PPPoE only — the full login the CPE dials with, once it exists. Null until the carrier accepts the order and the service is built.

sTag.description: Layer 2 only — the outer VLAN (S-Tag) your service is handed off on.

cTag.description: Layer 2 only — the inner VLAN (C-Tag) for this service. Null until it is allocated, unless you chose one.

status.description: Whether the service is built. Pending while the carrier is still working the order; Complete once it is done and the tags are final.

handoff.description: Layer 2 only — the interconnect in use, or the string `accountDefault` when your default destination for the POI was chosen.

DataServiceDetail.description: One of your data services, with its live status.

contract.description: The service's contract term, as the portal's Contract Term card shows it: when it ends, and what disconnecting today would charge, the plan's and every add-on's together. Null for a service with no term. For another cease date, GET /data/services/{ref}/disconnect-quote.

earlyTerminationChargeExGst.description: Dollars, ex GST. `0.00` once the term has ended, or when the charge was waived.

earlyTerminationChargeWaived.description: True when we waived the early termination charge: the charge is `0.00` though the service is still in its term, and a disconnect charges nothing.

session.description: Whether the service is connected right now. Null for a service that is not Live.

status.description: `Available`: `online` answers. `Unavailable`: the network did not answer just now; try again. `OnRequest`: this network has no live status we can read without starting a test there; ask GET /data/radius/{ref}/online with the service's `radiusUser`. `NotOnOurRadius`: the service is handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect and never logs on to our RADIUS, so it has no live status here.

online.description: Whether a session is up. Null unless `status` is Available.

DataServiceUsage.description: One month of a service's data usage, by day. Usage is reported, never charged.

from.description: The start of the billing month, on your bill's time zone (or the one you sent in `CN-Time-Zone`), with its offset.

to.description: The end of the billing month, or now for the current month, on the same zone as `from`.

complete.description: False for the current month, which is still counting.

allowanceBytes.description: The plan's included data, if it has a figure; null for unlimited.

days.description: One entry per day with usage, oldest first.

date.description: The day, on the same zone as `from`.

NetworkOutage.description: One entry from the Check Networks outage register, as published under the Telecommunications (Customer Communications for Outages) Industry Standard 2024 (Part 4), or a planned maintenance window you were sent notice of. Field values match the public register at https://status.checknetworks.tools. For a planned window, `startedAt` and `estimatedRestorationAt` are the window's start and end, and `additionalInfo` describes its impact.

reference.description: The Check Networks outage reference

title.description: Short plain-English description of the outage

type.description: Whether the outage is planned maintenance or an unplanned outage

severity.description: For an unplanned outage, its class under the Standard: `major` (at least 100,000 services or a whole State, for more than 60 minutes) or `significant_local` (at least 1,000 regional or 250 remote services, for more than 6 or 3 hours). Null for planned maintenance.

status.description: Whether the outage is still in progress or has been resolved

startedAt.description: When the outage began, in UTC like every time the API returns

resolvedAt.description: When service was restored. Null while the outage is open.

estimatedRestorationAt.description: Current estimate for restoration. Null when no estimate is available yet — absence of an estimate is itself meaningful and is not a placeholder.

timezone.description: IANA timezone of the affected area, for showing the UTC times in local time

affectedSites.description: Our own sites affected (a data centre or exchange), by name. Absent for planned maintenance.

premisesAffected.description: Number of premises affected. Null where Check Networks has no technical visibility of the count, and always null for planned maintenance.

responsibleParty.description: The carrier or carriage service provider responsible for resolving the outage. Null where Check Networks is itself responsible.

cause.description: High-level cause. The literal value `withheld` means a cause is known but has been withheld from publication; null means no cause is recorded yet.

causeNatural.description: Whether the cause relates to a natural event or weather

additionalInfo.description: Any further published detail about the outage

firstPublishedAt.description: When this register entry was first published

lastRectifiedAt.description: When this register entry was last corrected, if it has been

yourAffectedServiceCount.description: How many of your services this outage hit, from the footprint we recorded when it was published; 0 when it reaches your area but none of your services. Null for planned maintenance, where we do not record which services a window touches.

yourAffectedServices.description: Each of your services this outage hit, including those of your end users, so you can tell them. Null for planned maintenance.

service.description: The service's reference (a data service id, trunk or number).

address.description: The service address. Null when it is masked (`addressMasked`), or when we hold none.

addressMasked.description: True when the address is withheld because the end user is protected by a family violence safety record, as the End Users list in the portal withholds their contact details.

endUser.description: The end user the service belongs to, by its public number. Null for a service you hold yourself.

ServiceDegradation.description: A Potential Service Degradation: the link at the service's point of interconnect is near capacity, so the service may be slower at peak, but is not down. It is not an outage under the Standard, so it carries no register fields.

startedAt.description: When we opened it, in UTC.

estimatedRestorationAt.description: When we expect the extra capacity to be in place; null until we have a date.

area.description: The affected points of interconnect, e.g. `Sandbox (0SND)`.

additionalInfo.description: What end users may notice until the capacity is added.

url.description: Where the status site lists it.

id.description: The test's id, the carrier's reference for it.

test.description: The test's code, as `GET /data/services/{ref}/diagnostics/types` lists it.

status.description: Where the test is, from either carrier's own states: `accepted` (asked for, not yet started), `in_progress`, `completed`, `cancelled` (also a test whose result never came) or `rejected` (the carrier refused it).

result.description: `passed` or `failed` once the carrier says; `none` until then, or for a test with no pass or fail.

DataServiceHealthReport.description: One health report on a data service, in the same shape on every network. `overall` is the result the portal's service page shows.

id.description: The report's id. Read it again on GET /data/health/{id}.

serviceId.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product).

network.description: The access network the service is on.

status.description: `pending` until the carrier answers. The `serviceHealth.reportReady` webhook says when a report is complete.

overall.description: The report's overall result, as the portal shows it. Null while pending, or when the carrier gave none.

summary.description: The carrier's summary of the report, when it gives one.

alertMessage.description: The carrier's alert, when the report raised one.

requestedAt.description: When the report was asked for.

checks.description: Each measurement in the report, empty while pending. An NBN report lists its Connectivity, Performance and Stability roll-up first, under `Overview`.

category.description: The group the measurement is in, as the carrier names it.

name.description: The measurement, as the carrier names it.

result.description: The measurement's result; null when the carrier gave none.

unit.description: The value's unit, when it has one.

DataRadiusUser.description: A RADIUS user. There is one per service.

href.description: Link to this user on the Check Networks API.

username.description: The username the service authenticates with.

realm.description: The realm the username sits in. Null where the service authenticates on its access circuit rather than a login.

authentication.description: How the service authenticates. An IPoE service has no password: the access circuit is the identity.

serviceId.description: The service this user belongs to.

detailSource.description: Whose RADIUS authenticates the service, and so where the detail below comes from. `checknetworks`: our own RADIUS, answered from what we hold. `kinetix`: Kinetix's RADIUS, read live from Kinetix on every request. `carrier`: another carrier's RADIUS, which cannot be read, so the detail is unavailable. `handoff`: the service is handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect and never logs on to our RADIUS, so there is no detail and `online` is null.

detailAvailable.description: False when the detail could not be read (Kinetix did not answer, or the carrier's RADIUS cannot be read). The detail fields are then null; the rest of the record is still given.

online.description: Whether the user has a session up right now. Null when the detail is unavailable.

ipAddress.description: The IPv4 address assigned to the service. Behind CGNAT this is the inner 100.64.0.0/10 address; see publicAddress.

staticIp.description: Whether the IPv4 address is static.

publicAddress.description: The shared public IPv4 address, when the service is behind CGNAT. Null for a service with its own public address.

publicPortRange.description: The ports of publicAddress this service holds, when behind CGNAT.

ipv6Address.description: The IPv6 WAN address. On our own RADIUS the service is given a WAN /64 instead, given here in CIDR form.

ipv6DelegatedPrefix.description: The IPv6 prefix delegated to the service's router.

lastAuthentication.description: The latest authentication. Null when none is recorded.

reason.description: Why a reject happened (for example no_live_service or bad_credential), on our own RADIUS. Null on an accept, and from Kinetix.

recentDropouts.description: Sessions that ended within the recent window (five days).

DataRadiusNotChecked.description: The service is on Opticomm's RADIUS and no session check is held for it. Reading never asks Opticomm: ask for a check with `POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check`, then read again once it completes.

retrievedAt.description: Always null, as no check is held.

message.example: This session has not been checked at Opticomm recently. Ask for a check with POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check, then read it here once it completes.

DataRadiusNotOnOurRadius.description: The service is handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect and never logs on to our RADIUS, so there is no session here to read: neither online nor offline.

message.example: This service is handed to you at layer 2 on your interconnect and never logs on to our RADIUS, so we hold no session for it.

DataRadiusSession.description: A live RADIUS session. Traffic is named from the end user's point of view: what they sent is the upload.

id.description: The RADIUS user reference this session belongs to.

username.description: The username the session authenticated with.

source.description: Where the session was read from. `checknetworks`: our own RADIUS accounting. `kinetix`: Kinetix's RADIUS, read live on this request. `opticomm`: Opticomm's session history from the latest session check, as at `lastSeenAt`.

startedAt.description: When the session came up. Null if the carrier does not give it.

lastSeenAt.description: When we last heard accounting for the session. For a `kinetix` session, the time of this read. For an `opticomm` session, when Opticomm reported it.

durationSeconds.description: How long the session has been up. For a `kinetix` session, counted from `startedAt`, and null when that is. For an `opticomm` session, as Opticomm reported it.

ipAddress.description: The address assigned to the session.

uploadBytes.description: Traffic sent by the end user. Kinetix reports traffic to two decimal places of a unit (27.38 GB), so a `kinetix` figure is that amount in bytes, with GB taken as 10^9. Null if the carrier gives no figure.

downloadBytes.description: Traffic sent to the end user, converted from Kinetix's figure the same way as `uploadBytes`.

id.description: The service's product reference (PRI, Opticomm product).

endUser.description: The end user's public number, or null when none is assigned.

downloadBytes.description: Bytes sent to the end user in the month.

uploadBytes.description: Bytes the end user sent in the month.

allowanceBytes.description: The plan's monthly allowance, or null for an unlimited plan.

percentUsed.description: The total as a percentage of the allowance, to one decimal place; null with no allowance.

complete.description: False for the current month, which is counted up to now.

id.description: The location ID as queried (LOC… or OPC…).

href.description: URL of this qualification.

network.description: The access network the qualification ran against.

locId.description: The premises' NBN Location ID — equal to `id` for NBN queries; resolved via the address crosswalk for Opticomm queries, null when the premises has no resolvable NBN footprint.

serviceable.description: Whether the premises can be served on the network.

status.description: The carrier's own serviceability status for the premises.

serviceClass.description: The carrier's serviceability class, where reported.

primaryAccessTech.description: Primary access technology (e.g. FTTP, HFC, FTTC).

alternativeTech.description: (NBN) The alternative technology the carrier plans for the premises, where reported (e.g. Fibre at an upgrade-programme FTTN/FTTC premises).

upliftAvailable.description: True when the premises is FTTN/FTTC with Fibre as the alternative technology AND the carrier confirms Fibre Uplift eligibility. The full uplift document is served by /nbn/service_qualification/fibre_uplift.

additionalInstallAvailable.description: True when every port or copper pair at the premises is in use and the carrier will install another device or pair for a further service. NBN: order a connect with `ntdId` (or `copperPairId`) set to `NEW` and a Standard Install appointment. Opticomm: order a connect naming no OTD, with an Additional Install appointment. The subsequent installation charge applies.

newDevelopmentChargeApplies.description: (NBN) True when the carrier's New Development Charge applies at the premises. Null where the network does not report it.

poi.description: (NBN) The Point of Interconnect serving the premises.

resources.description: The in-ground access resources a service can be provisioned on — NTD/OTD ports and copper pairs. Empty when the technology needs no resource pick (e.g. a new-install fibre premises).

status.description: A port is `Free` or `Used`. A copper pair is `Line In Use` (a service runs on it) or `Line Not In Use` (a spare pair), in nbn's own words.

installFeeApplies.description: (Copper pairs) True when a subsequent installation charge applies to activating this pair.

serviceIdMatch.description: Present on NBN Service Transfer queries — true on the one resource carrying the supplied serviceRef.

siteRestrictionError.description: (NBN Service Transfer) The carrier's rejection of the supplied serviceRef (RJ002003…), null when the transfer validated or no serviceRef was supplied.

enterpriseEthernet.description: The NBN Enterprise Ethernet check at the premises — null when no NBN footprint is resolvable or the check was unavailable.

availablePlans.description: The carrier-sellable bandwidth products at the premises — the SKUs the order endpoints accept. Empty when the lookup is unavailable.

otherNetwork.description: The same premises on the other network, where both NBN and Opticomm serve it: that network's qualification exactly as `/data/sq/{locId}` answers for its own ID (without an `otherNetwork` of its own). Null when the premises is on one network only, when that network does not answer, or on a transfer check (`serviceRef`), which is about the asked network only. Order on whichever network is serviceable with the plan you want.

GeographicAddress.description: An nbn address as Kinetix returns it: each field only when nbn holds it, coordinates as strings.

href.description: Link to this address, `/nbn/address/{locId}`, on this API. Present only when the carrier sent a link.

formattedAddress.description: Human-readable single-line form of the address.
formattedAddress.example: Lot 708 16 De Vecchi Cl, Edmonton, QLD

lotNumber.description:
The Lot number is a reference number allocated to a property for subdivision administration purposes prior to road numbering.

Usage: Where an official Road number has not been assigned, this field may be used for postal purposes as well as the physical identification of an address site.

planNumber.description: The deposited plan number allocated to a property for subdivision administration purposes prior to road numbering in addition to the Lot number.

roadNumber1.description:
Identifies the number of the address in the road or thoroughfare and for a ranged address is the start number.
The data element may include an alphabetic prefix. The data element may include an alphabetic suffix.

roadNumber2.description:
Identifies the last number for a ranged address in the road or thoroughfare.
The data element may include an alphabetic prefix. The data element may include an alphabetic suffix.
This data element is used for ranged street numbers otherwise it is left blank.

roadName.description:
The name of the road/thoroughfare applicable to the address site or complex.
Only the road name should be stored in this data element.

roadTypeCode.description: The abbreviation code used to distinguish the type of road/thoroughfare applicable to the address site/complex.

roadSuffixCode.description: The abbreviation code used to represent the suffix of road/thoroughfare applicable to the address site/complex.

localityName.description: The name of the locality/suburb of the address.

postcode.description:
The Australian numeric descriptor for a postal delivery area, aligned with locality, suburb or place

*Mandatory if stateTerritoryCode not provided

stateTerritoryCode.description:
The State or Territory code of the address.

*Mandatory if postcode not provided

secondaryComplexName.description:
Name associated with a building or area within a complex site.
This data element may represent the name given to an entire building within an address site that has its own separate address.

unitTypeCode.description:
Sub dwelling unit type code.
Within a complex, an abbreviation used to distinguish the type of an address found within a building / sub-complex or marina.

unitNumber.description:
Sub-dwelling unit number.
Within a complex, a number used to distinguish an address found within a building / sub-complex or marina.
The data element may include a leading alphabetic prefix. The data element may include a trailing alphabetic suffix.

levelTypeCode.description: Within a complex, an abbreviation used to distinguish the floor or level of a multi-storey building/sub-complex.

levelNumber.description:
Within a complex, the number of the floor or level of a multi-storey building/ sub-complex.
The data element may include a leading alphabetic prefix. The data element may include a trailing alphabetic suffix.

addressSiteName.description:
Synonyms: Building property name, Primary Complex name

The official place name or culturally accepted common usage name for an address site, including the name of a building, homestead, building complex, agricultural property, park or unbounded address site. This data element represents the name given to an entire building or address site

complexRoadNumber1.description: Within a complex, identifies the number of the address in the road or thoroughfare and for a ranged address is the start number.

complexRoadNumber2.description: Within a complex, identifies the last number for a ranged address in the road or thoroughfare.

complexRoadName.description:
Within a complex, the name of the road /thoroughfare of the address. Within a Road name it is possible to find what appears to be a Road type (eg. The Boulevard).
It is also possible to have a null Road type.

complexRoadTypeCode.description: Within a complex, an abbreviation used to distinguish the type of road / thoroughfare of the address.

complexRoadSuffixCode.description: Within a complex, an abbreviation representing the suffix of the road/ thoroughfare of the address.

locationDescriptor.description: Additional descriptor that further identifies the location.

latitude.description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the address, as a decimal string.

longitude.description: Geographic longitude coordinate of the address, as a decimal string.

id.description: Unique NBN Reference for the location

When the value is 'less than 3Mbps' or '3 Mbps to less than 6 Mbps', then either a Forecast Date or Comment will be provided. priorityLink.description: Indicated whether the cell is connected via a priority upgrade link. Valid values: Yes, No, Upgrade. When the value is No, forecastDate and comment is not required. However, when the link is an upgrade, the upgrade has been completed but the link is still reporting an Average 28 Day Busy Hour Link Packet Loss of 0.25% or greater (typically due to the 28 day average not yet reflecting the post-upgrade link performance).

state.description: The current state of the order as per the nbn Product Order state model, plus one Check Networks state. PendingReview: the order passed Check Networks' checks but nbn could not accept it as Check Networks sent it. The fault is ours and nothing is needed from you: Check Networks will correct and resubmit it. Until nbn gives it an Order ID its id is a Check Networks PND, which GET /nbn/orders/product/{orderId} accepts and keeps accepting afterwards. It ends Cancelled if it cannot be placed. A genuine refusal (for example informed consent not evidenced, or no NTD capacity) is never PendingReview: the order is refused with a 422.

restorationSlaSku.description:
(Optional) Product SKU of the Service Restoration SLA.
If omitted, the Standard SLA ("NBN-SLA-TC4-STD") is applied.
Indicates how quick NBN responds should this service be affected by an issue, depending upon the SLA Region.
Response times are Business Hours unless a (24/7) SLA is selected.
Enhanced or Premium SLAs may incur an additional monthly cost.
Bundled SLA Product SKUs will only be accepted when provided with an eligible Bandwidth Product SKU.
Use the Product Qualification > Eligible Restoration SLA Products API to find selectable options for the Location (LOC #).

orderReference.description:
Your Reference Number for this order. Max of 35 characters.
Only alphabetic characters ("a-Z"), numbers ("0-9"), underscores ("_"), hyphens ("-") and periods (".") are allowed.

EXAMPLES:
 - "New.Foo_BAR-2020-09-20"
 - "ExampleCompanyName"
 - "JaneCitizen-123456"
 - "Reseller.EndUser.123456"

endUserRef.description:
NOT ACCEPTED: supplying this field returns 422. The platform assigns the End User; this API has no End User (Party) records.
The Reference (EUP #) of the End User to associate this Order to.

EXAMPLES:
 - "EUP000000000000"

priorityAssist.description:
(Optional) Whether Priority Assistance is required.
Defaults to "false" if value not set.
Only specify "true" where the end user is eligible for a Downstream Priority Assistance Service in accordance with NBN Co's Wholesale Broadband Agreement.
"true" is accepted only for a customer on our Priority Assistance register; otherwise the order is refused with a 422 on `priorityAssist` before anything is drafted.

ntdId.description:
The Reference Number of the Network Termination Device (NTD) to place the order against.
Specify "NEW" in this field to order a New NTD, but only if there are no free ports on any existing NTDs at the premises.

appointmentId.description:
(Conditional) NBN Appointment ID to attach to this order.
An Appointment with Demand Type "Standard Install" is required
when `ntdId` is "NEW" — a technician attends to install the NTD.
Taking a port on an NTD that is already installed requires no
appointment.

unidPortId.description:
(Conditional) The Port ID for the UNI-D Resource. Required for Service Transfers or where you want to specify an exact port.
NBN will assign the next available port where this field is not supplied or is `null`.

transferType.description:
(Conditional) Service Transfer Type.
Only applicable to, and is mandatory for Service Transfers.
 - "Service Transfer" - transfer an existing nbn service from another provider to you.
 - "Service Transfer Reversal" - recover an existing service that was incorrectly transferred away from you.
 - "Connect Outstanding" - connect a new service over a line that still has an existing active service not controlled by the End User.  This requires time to legally cancel the existing service.

occupancyDocumentId.description: (Optional, ours) On a Connect Outstanding, the `id` of a proof of occupancy uploaded with `POST /data/occupancy-documents`: evidence that the End User occupies the premises. It is kept with the order and used by that order only: a retry with the same `orderReference` may name it again. Another account's, or one another order used, is a 422.

serviceRef.description:
(Conditional) Service ID (AVC #) for Service Transfer.
Only applicable to, and is mandatory for, Service Transfers.

IMPORTANT > Validate the AVC # against the CPI # or NTD + UNI Port using the SQ Single Site API first.

customerAuthorityDate.description:
(Conditional) Date the Customer authorised this order, as `YYYY-MM-DD` (a date-time is read as its date). Must be within the last 45 calendar days only.
This is only applicable to Service Transfers and required if `transferType` is "Service Transfer" or "Connect Outstanding".

informedConsent.description: Verification that the End User has provided Informed Consent for this order to be placed.

overlapPeriod.description:
(Optional) The overlap period for Service Transfers.
For use when transferring a service to a new UNI-D Port.  The number of hours after Order Completion during which the service will be active on both the old and new ports.  The End User infrastructure should be updated during this period.
Only applicable to Service Transfers.

fromPortId.description:
(Conditional) The UNI-D Port ID of the existing service. Specify the new Port ID via `unidPortId`.
Only applicable to Service Transfers and is mandatory if the `overlapPeriod` value is "4".

vlanMode.description:
(Optional) The VLAN Mode determines which Product Template will be used when ordering this connection.

IMPORTANT> Do not specify unless explicitly needed.

When this field is not specified, "Default-Mapped" will be the assumed value.
Intended mainly for transitioning existing "Tagged" PPPoE services without needing to change the client CPE configuration.

IMPORTANT> You cannot change this value with a Modify Order. Instead, the service must be cancelled and reordered, potentially bringing the service down for 24-48 hours.

uniVlanId.description:
(Conditional) Required if `vlanMode` is "Tagged"
The UNI VLAN ID # used to tag the service traffic.
The value should be between 1 and 4094.

serviceabilityClass.description:
The servicability classes are:

0 - Planned to be serviced by Fibre in the future (boundary status isnt In Service yet)
1 - Serviceable by Fibre, no drop or NTD in place
2 - Serviceable by Fibre, drop in place, no NTD in place
3 - Serviceable by Fibre, drop and NTD in place
4 - Planned to be serviced by Wireless
5 - Serviceable by Wireless, CPE not installed
6 - Serviceable by Wireless, CPE installed
7 - Planned to be serviced by Satellite
8 - Serviceable by Satellite, Satellite - NTD not installed
9 - Serviceable by Satellite, Satellite - NTD installed
10 - Planned to be serviceable by Copper
11 - Serviceable by copper, active node present
12 - Serviceable by copper, jumpering is required
13 - Serviceable by copper, infrastructure in place
20 - Planned to be serviced by HFC, outside plant does not exist
21 - Serviceable by HFC, the location has a street TAP but requires a lead-in, PCD, internal tie cable, and wall-plate/socket
22 - Serviceable by HFC, the location has a street TAP, lead-in & PCD in place, but no internal tie-cables with wall plates/sockets
23 - Serviceable by HFC, the location has a wall-plate/socket but no HFC NTD
24 - Serviceable by HFC, Location has a wall-plate/socket & HFC NTD and is Ready to Connect
30 - Planned to be serviceable by FTTC
31 - Serviceable by FTTC, no line available (NCD required)
32 - Serviceable by FTTC, cut-in required (NCD required)
33 - Serviceable by FTTC, cut-in complete (NCD required)
34 - Serviceable by FTTC, infrastructure in place (Check NCD status)

Example "YYYY-MM-DD".

Exactly two classes of difference from the carrier's response: Check Networks' account and interconnect identifiers are removed, and hyperlinks point at this API instead of the carrier. `externalId` carries YOUR reference (Check Networks holds its own reference with the carrier, so two customers can never collide on one value).

href.description: Link to this order on the Check Networks API.

Check Networks sets the carrier account fields itself (`billingAccount`, `accessSeekerContact`, `productOffering`, `relatedParty`, and interconnect identifiers such as `ovcId`); a request carrying any of them is rejected with `400` rather than silently overridden. `externalId` is YOUR reference — Check Networks presents its own reference to the carrier.

realizedResource.description: Physical resource requests — a Connect may name the NTD port (productSpecification `OUID` + `portId`).

oacIds.description: Your affected services (OAC ids) — only yours.

OpticommOutagePosition.description: The carrier's own npis-networkoutage position answer for a service — upstream's `NoOutage`, `CurrentOutage` or `FutureOutage` body, verbatim. A service with no outage carries only `currentOutage: false`; the id arrays appear only when the carrier sends them.

OpticommProductRecord.description: A product record inside an Opticomm inventory document — the carrier's own shape, minus Check Networks' account and interconnect identifiers. Records nest: an NTD (OTD) record carries its ports (OUI) as `productRef` entries of its own.

connectedToOui.description: The NTD port (OUI #) the access service rides.

OpticommProduct.description: An Opticomm service — the carrier's own npis-product-inventory `Product` document, relayed as Opticomm produces it. The differences from the carrier's response: Check Networks' account and interconnect identifiers are removed, hyperlinks point at this API, and a service we hold suspended carries `suspensionTakesEffect`. `name` carries YOUR reference (the carrier-side name is Check Networks' own).

id.description: The Product Instance (OPI #) — the product key across this API.

href.description: Link to this product on the Check Networks API.

status.description: The product lifecycle status, as the carrier holds it.

Absent otherwise.

name.description: Your reference for the service.

productRef.description: The realised records under this product — access service (OAC), NTD (OTD) and, nested within it, the NTD ports (OUI).

place.description: The property the service is delivered at.

href.description: Link to the property on the Check Networks API.

OpticommServiceHealthReport.description: The carrier's own npis-service-health report fields, from the latest callback. The carrier-side correlation key is Check Networks' own and is omitted — the wrapper carries YOUR reference.

OpticommHealthCategory.description: One health category from the carrier's report, verbatim.

status.description: RAG.

Upstream has no report read — reports arrive only by callback — so this read is a Check Networks extension; `serviceHealth` and `healthCategory` are absent until the report lands. `requestStatus` is Check Networks' own request lifecycle: upstream has no failure state, so a failed request is visible here rather than masquerading as InProgress.

OpticommSiteRestriction.description: The qualification body — the property's serviceability, features, charges, boundaries, NTD/port inventory and technology, exactly as the carrier answers them. Upstream resource links that do not resolve here (`supportingProduct[].href`, `supportingResource[].href`, product catalog hrefs) are omitted; `siteRestriction.href` points at this API's own address resource.

href.description: The qualified property on this API.

name.description: The property's display address.

serviceabilityStatus.description: Serviceable / Rejected, as upstream enumerates it.

supportingProduct.description: Product instances already at the property. `serviceProviderId` names the RSP the end user deals with today and is kept; the upstream `href` is not resolvable here and is omitted.

supportingProductFeatures.description: Feature availability at the property, as one object: the carrier's swagger declares an array, but the live carrier sends one object, and this API relays what the carrier sends. `productAvailability` is present only when the request asked for it (`?productAvailability=true`).

productAvailability.description: The bandwidth products orderable at the property, by Opticomm's product code.

supportingRelatedLocationFeatures.description: Charges, activity flags and demand/transfer availability.

supportingResource.description: The NTD (OTD) inventory — device, bandwidth, UNI ports.

OpticommSiteQualification.description: The carrier's own npis-service-qualification `SiteQualification` document — an integration built against Opticomm reads it unchanged. Served from Check Networks' qualification cache (fresh until 01:00 Sydney the next day); a request carrying `customerAuthorityDate` is always answered live. `href` points at this API's own resources.

href.description: This qualification on this API.

NumberRoutingStep.description: One route in a number's routing chain. The first step takes the call; each step with a `failover` hands it to the next step when it fails. A chain has at most 4 steps. A `time_of_day` step picks a destination by the time, and a `geographic` step by where the caller is (13, 1300 and 1800 numbers only); each falls back to `fallback`. Their destinations are plain routes, not another time-of-day or geographic step. A step read back always carries `routeType`, `routeTarget`, `disconnectResponse`, `redirectCallerId`, `label` and `failover`; a step sent needs only `routeType`, and a field left out is read as null (`disconnectResponse` as `hangup`).

routeType.description: Where this step sends the call. `route_to_server` is set by Check Networks only: a chain that has one is read here but cannot be sent back. `fax2email` needs the number on a fax plan.

routeTarget.description: Per `routeType`: a trunk's `sipUsername` or its `id` (sent as either; read back as the `sipUsername`, or the `id` for a trunk with none, such as an IP-authenticated trunk), a phone number, a SIP URI (`sip:` or `sips:`, not a private or reserved address) or an email address. Null for `disconnected`, `time_of_day` and `geographic`. A phone number is never 000, 112 or 106, in any form (`+61000`, `0061112`, `1831000`): that is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

disconnectResponse.description: For `disconnected`: what the caller hears. `hangup` when you send none. Null for every other route type.

redirectCallerId.description: For `redirect`: the caller ID the forwarded call shows, the original caller's (the default) or this number. Null for every other route type.

label.description: Your name for this step; null for none.

failover.description: When the call moves on to the next step. Null on the last step, and on a step that never fails over.

trigger.description: `afterSeconds`: after `seconds` of ringing unanswered. `whenUnreachable`: when the destination cannot be reached.

seconds.description: For `afterSeconds`: one of 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 120 or 180 (or a value Check Networks already set on this chain). Null for `whenUnreachable`.

timezone.description: For `time_of_day`, required there and only there; the time zone its windows are in.

windows.description: For `time_of_day`, required there and only there; checked in order, the first match takes the call.

days.description: The days of the week, 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday).

start.description: HH:MM, 24-hour. A window may cross midnight (22:00 to 06:00).

rules.description: For `geographic`, required there and only there; checked in order, the first match takes the call.

mode.description: `state`: callers in `states`. `area`: callers from mobile originating location (MOLI) codes in `molis`, or fixed numbers in the standard zone units in `szus`.

fallback.description: For `time_of_day` and `geographic`, required there; where the call goes when no window or rule matches.

SmsDelivery.description:
Where a mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered. A number with no method still receives and stores its messages (`GET /sms/{number}`); they are just not forwarded.

Every webhook request is signed: the `X-Signature-256` header is `sha256=` and the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed with the number's secret. Compare it in constant time and reject a request that does not match.

method.description: How messages are forwarded. Null when they are not.

vendor.description: The payload shape of a webhook: `generic` (our own), `3cx` or `yeastar`. Null unless `method` is `webhook`.

destination.description: The webhook URL (a public HTTPS address) or the email address. Null when `method` is null.

secretSet.description: Whether a signing secret is stored. The secret itself is never returned on a read.

secret.description: Only in the answer to the `PATCH` that generated it: the new signing secret. Store it now; it is not returned again.

DidNumber.description: A phone number on your account.

description.description: A label or description for this number. Null when you have not set one.

routeType.description: How incoming calls to this number are routed first: the first step of `routing`. Null for unrouted numbers. `route_to_server` is not yet generally available.

routeTarget.description: The target for the first route (trunk sipUsername, redirect number, SIP URI or fax email); null for disconnected, unrouted and composite routes.

trunkType.description: On a `trunk` route, where `routeTarget` is found: `trunk` at `GET /trunks/{username}`, `residentialLine` at `GET /residential-lines/{username}`. Null on every other route.

routingSteps.description: How many routes the number's chain has: the first route and its failovers. 0 for an unrouted number.

hasAdvancedRouting.description: True when the chain has a failover, or its first route is time of day or geographic. A `PATCH` with `routeType` on such a number answers `409` unless it sends `replaceRouting: true`.

routing.description: The whole routing chain, first route first, as the portal shows it. Send it back, changed, as `routing` on `PATCH /numbers/{number}`.

faxEnabled.description: Whether this number takes faxes: true while it is on one of your fax plans (`faxPlanId`). Only such a number can be routed to `fax2email`.

faxPlanId.description: The `id` of the fax plan this number is on (`GET /fax/plans`); null when it is on none.

smsEnabled.description: Whether this number can send and receive SMS (a mobile number you hold).

smsDelivery.description: Where this mobile number's inbound SMS are delivered. Null for any number that is not a mobile number.

status.description: `releasing` while a release is being carried out; once it is done the number is gone.

emergencyAddressId.description: The `id` of the emergency address this number is listed at (`GET /emergency-addresses`). Null until one is linked. A change to a number in use shows here once the register has been updated, a moment after the call.

ipnd.description: The last IPND record sent for this number and what the IPND said about it; null when none has been sent. The IPND record is the number's address, uploaded to the national database after the fact: it never changes how a call is routed or connected, and a call to 000 goes through whatever it says. A rejected record needs the emergency address fixed so emergency services are given the right one.

status.description: `waiting` until the IPND answers; `accepted`; `rejected` when it refused the record, with the reasons in `errors`; `fileRejected` when the whole upload it was in was refused, so the record itself is not at fault.

lastSubmittedAt.description: When the record was uploaded; null while it waits to go.

directoryListing.description: Whether the record lists the number in the public directory, as the emergency address's list code sets it: `unlisted`; listed at the service address; or listed at a separate directory address. Null when the address is no longer on the account.

errors.description: Each code the IPND returned, explained. Empty when there were none.

code.description: The IPND's code, as its manager writes it.

meaning.description: What it means, in plain words.

fixInAddress.description: True when a field of the emergency address needs correcting.

portOutCode.description: A mobile number's port-out code from the carrier. Your end user gives it to their new provider to move the number away. It is an identifier, not a password. Null on a fixed number, or when the carrier has not given one.

endUser.description: The end user who holds this number, by its public number: the one it is tagged to, or else the end user of the trunk it is on. Null when the number is your own.
