monthlyCost.description: Monthly recurring cost for this number as a decimal dollar amount, without GST. Null when no hosting product prices this number's category, which is not the same as free. Deprecated: read `monthlyCostExGst`, `monthlyCostGst` and `monthlyCostIncGst` instead.

monthlyCostExGst.description: The monthly cost without GST, as a decimal dollar amount. Null, with the other two, when nothing prices this number.

monthlyCostGst.description: The GST on the monthly cost; `0.00` on a GST-free account.

createdAt.description: When the number was added to the account's stock, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the number last changed, in UTC.

NumberOrder.description: A number order. Accepted is not done: an order is recorded `pending`, the numbers are allocated and routed in the background, usually within a minute, and the order ends `completed` with its numbers or `failed` with `error`. An order inside a bundle is a `draft`, holding nothing, until the bundle is released.

status.description: `draft`: in a bundle, waiting for it to be released. `pending`: being set up. `completed`: the numbers are yours, listed in `numbers`. `failed`: nothing was allocated; `error` says why. `cancelled`: taken out of its bundle, or the bundle was abandoned.

type.description: The number type ordered.

szu.description: The numbering area of a geographic order; null for other types.

blockSize.description: How many consecutive numbers the order is for.

spare.description: True when the numbers were ordered spare: on no trunk, routed to Disconnected until you set their route.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk the numbers go on. Null for a spare order.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the numbers are listed at; null for a spare order.

routeType.description: Where the order said calls go: `trunk` rings the trunk, `redirect` forwards to `routeTarget`, `sip_address` sends to a SIP URI, and a spare order is `disconnected`.

routeTarget.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`, the forward number or the SIP URI; null when spare.

bundle.description: The bundle the order is in, when it was placed in one.

error.description: Why a `failed` order failed, or why a `cancelled` one was cancelled, in plain words. Null otherwise.
error.example: No complete block of 10 numbers (e.g. X0–X9) is available.

numbers.description: The numbers allocated, once `completed`, each with the route it has now. Empty until then.

routeType.description: How the number's calls are routed, as `GET /numbers/{number}` shows it.

routeTarget.description: The route's destination, as `GET /numbers/{number}` shows it.

EmergencyAddress.description: The address emergency services are given for a number, with the customer it is listed under. In Australia this is the number's IPND (Integrated Public Number Database) listing, and every Australian number needs one linked before it can be routed. Link a number to an address with `emergencyAddressId` on `PATCH /numbers/{number}`. Fields are the IPND's own, with its lengths.

id.description: The address's identifier, as `emergencyAddressId` on a number names it.

country.description: The country whose emergency register lists the address. `AU` is the only value today; it may be omitted when creating one.

label.description: Your name for the address. Unique on your account.

listCode.description: How the listing appears in directories: `LE` listed entry, `UL` unlisted, `SA` listed with the address suppressed.

usageCode.description: Who uses the service: `R` residential, `B` business, `G` government, `C` charity, `N` not available.

findingNameSameAsCustomer.description: Whether the directory finding name is the customer's name. When false on an `LE` or `SA` listing, `findingName1` is required.

name1.description: The customer's surname or business name.

serviceAddress.description: Where the service is used, which is the address emergency services are sent to. Give a `streetName` or a `buildingProperty`.

gnafPid.description: The G-NAF address detail PID, the `gnafId` of a `GET /addresses/search` result. Sent on a create or an update, it fills every other service address field from that address in the shape the IPND record needs (building, unit, level, street number and suffix, street name and type, locality, state, postcode), as the portal's address search does; a field sent beside it wins over the filled one. An unknown PID answers `422` on this field. The answer shows the filled address.

directoryAddress.description: The address printed in directories. On an `LE` or `SA` listing that does not use the service address, `locality`, `state`, `postcode` and a `streetName` or `buildingProperty` are required.

gnafPid.description: The `gnafId` of a `GET /addresses/search` result. Sent, it fills the directory address's street number, street name and type, locality, state and postcode from that address and sets `sameAsService` to false, unless those fields are sent beside it. An unknown PID answers `422` on this field.

liveNumbers.description: How many of your numbers are listed at this address. It cannot be deleted while any are.

FaxPlan.description: A fax plan. A number sends and receives faxes only while it is on an open plan.

kind.description: `bundle` is the Fax Bundle: one number, pages included in the monthly fee. `service` is the fax service: any number of numbers, a monthly fee for each, and a charge for each page sent.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the plan is for, or null when it is your own.

numbers.description: The numbers on the plan now, as E.164 digits.

createdAt.description: When the plan was opened, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the plan last changed, in UTC.

CallingPermission.description: A calling-permission class that can be applied to a trunk. `AUEmergency` and `AUFreecall` are always enabled and cannot be removed; the remaining classes are opt-in per trunk, subject to the ceiling the wholesaler has configured.

TrunkNumberFormat.description: How an Australian number is written on calls delivered to a trunk. `national`: `0` plus the national number (`0755501234`). `international`: with a plus (`+61755501234`). `internationalDigits`: international digits only, with no plus (`61755501234`).

TrunkIpEntry.description: One entry on a trunk's IP ACL.

id.description: The entry's id, as `DELETE /trunks/{username}/ips/{ipId}` takes it.

ipAddress.description: The allowed address in CIDR form (a single host is `/32`, or `/128` for IPv6), or the host name when `type` is `host`.

type.description: `cidr` for an address or range; `host` for a host name, which is resolved on its DNS TTL and allows the addresses it resolves to.

description.description: A label for this IP entry.

createdAt.description: When the entry was added, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the entry last changed, in UTC.

id.description: The trunk's public id. Every trunk has one, including a trunk set up without a SIP credential, so every `/trunks/{username}` endpoint accepts it in place of the SIP username. Trunk events carry it as `trunkId`. The internal database id is never exposed.

name.description: A friendly name for this trunk.

description.description: An optional description for this trunk.

authMethod.description: The SIP authentication method. A trunk is always `both`: it accepts either registration with its credential or a source IP on its IP ACL. The other values remain for compatibility and are not returned for a trunk.

sipUsername.description: The trunk's platform-generated SIP digest username. Every `/trunks/{username}` endpoint accepts it, as it accepts `id`. Null on a trunk set up without a SIP credential, which authenticates only by IP: address that trunk by its `id`.

sipDomain.description: The SIP domain for this trunk.

type.description: The trunk's plan. This is what decides the price: on `ultimate` each channel is a recurring billed assignment, on `payg` the channels are a ceiling and outbound calls are metered per use.

channels.description: Maximum concurrent calls allowed on this trunk. On `ultimate` this is also the number of channels billed.

maxInternational.description: Maximum concurrent international calls. **Null means no trunk-level limit** — the trunk inherits your account's cap rather than being capped at zero. Setting it to `0` is a different thing entirely: that blocks international calling on this trunk. A limit applies only while `International` is among `callingPermissions`; without it this is null.

activeCalls.description: Calls up on the trunk now, as the portal's Concurrency card counts them. `GET /voice/calls/active?trunk=` lists them.

recordingEnabled.description: Whether call recording is on. When it is, every call on the trunk is recorded.

callingPermissions.description: The calling-permission classes applied to this trunk (its call barring). `AUEmergency` and `AUFreecall` are always listed: 000 and freecall numbers are never barred.

defaultCallerId.description: The default outbound caller ID presented for calls from this trunk.

forcePrivateCli.description: Whether all outbound calls present as Private/Anonymous regardless of the caller ID set.

forceOutboundCli.description: Whether every outbound call presents `defaultCallerId`, whatever caller ID the PBX sends.

defaultState.description: The default registration state for this trunk. Null when none is set.

status.description: A `suspended` trunk makes and receives no calls: new outbound calls are refused, and calls to its numbers are refused before they reach your PBX. It still places 000 (and 112 and 106) calls, and for an hour after one, calls to its numbers are delivered so the emergency service can call back. See `suspendedBy`.

suspendedBy.description: Who suspended the trunk, while `status` is `suspended`. `account`: you did (in the portal or with `POST /trunks/{username}/suspend`), and you can resume it. `checkNetworks`: we placed a hold (for example for non-payment or fraud), which only we lift; `POST /trunks/{username}/resume` answers 409. Null when the trunk is not suspended.

calledNumberFormat.description: How the dialled number is written in the Request-URI and To of calls delivered to this trunk. `national` is an Australian number as `0` plus the national number (`0755501234`); a number that is not Australian is delivered as digits only.

callerNumberFormat.description: How an Australian caller's number is written in From on calls delivered to this trunk. A number's own inbound format, where set, overrides this for calls to that number. An overseas or withheld caller is delivered as received.

provisioningState.description: Whether the trunk's latest change (to the trunk, its SIP credential or its IP ACL) has reached every customer SBC. `pending` until the next network reload, which runs every minute; `active` once every SBC has it. A new trunk reads `pending` at first: wait for `active` before a test call.

provisionedAt.description: When the voice network was first confirmed to hold the trunk's latest change. Null while `provisioningState` is `pending`.

internationalHold.description: An international-cap hold on the trunk, or null. While it is in force the trunk's international calls are refused; calls within Australia, and 000, still go. Raise a support ticket to have it released.

capMinutes.description: The trunk's international minutes cap for the period.

trippedMinutes.description: The international minutes the trunk had made when the hold was placed.

pendingPlanChange.description: A plan or channel change booked for the next billing cycle, or null. A downgrade made with `PATCH /trunks/{username}` is booked this way; `DELETE /trunks/{username}/plan-change` cancels it.

direction.description: Which way the change moves the trunk from its current plan and channels.

type.description: The plan the trunk moves to.

channels.description: The channels billed after the change; 0 on `payg`.

effectiveOn.description: The date the change takes effect, the start of the next billing cycle.

connection.description: What a PBX needs to connect to the trunk, as the portal's Trunk Configuration panel shows it.

registrar.description: The host name the PBX registers to and sends calls to.

udpTcpPort.description: The SIP port for UDP and TCP.

srtpRequired.description: Whether the trunk requires SRTP. When it does, the PBX must use TLS on `tlsPort`.

codecs.description: The codecs offered, in preference order.

dtmfMode.description: How DTMF digits travel between the network and the PBX.

dtmfWarning.description: A warning when `dtmfMode` is `inband`, which loses digits on some calls. Null otherwise.

numberFormat.description: The form the called number arrives in, as `calledNumberFormat`.

allowList.description: The addresses to allow through your firewall for this trunk, read from DNS. Returned by `GET /trunks/{username}` only, not on the list. Empty when DNS could not be read.

endUser.description: The end user this trunk belongs to, by its public number; its calls are billed to that end user. Null when the trunk is your own.

allowedCountries.description: This trunk's own list of countries it may call (ISO 3166 alpha-2), or null when it follows your account's list.

effectiveAllowedCountries.description: The countries this trunk's international calls may reach: its own list, else your account's. A call to any other country is refused. Calls to Australia and New Zealand follow `callingPermissions` (New Zealand is `NZMobile` and `NZNational`, and is never in a list), high-risk destinations stay blocked whatever the list says, and 000 always connects.

followsAccountList.description: True when the trunk has no list of its own and follows your account's.

dailySpendCapExGst.description: The trunk's daily spend cap, ex GST, as a dollar string; null is no cap. The cap is measured on our rated cost to you for the trunk's outbound calls since midnight Brisbane time.

spendTodayExGst.description: The trunk's outbound calls today, ex GST, since midnight Brisbane time. A call counts when it ends, so calls still up are not in it yet.

spendCapHeld.description: True while the trunk is held for reaching its daily spend cap: its outbound calls are refused, all but 000 and 1800. Inbound calls are not affected.

spendCapReleasesAt.description: When the hold lifts by itself, the next midnight Brisbane time. Null when the trunk is not held. Release Spend Cap Hold lifts it sooner.

ips.description: IP ACL entries for this trunk. Empty when the trunk authenticates only by registration.

createdAt.description: When the trunk was created, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the trunk last changed, in UTC.

TransitBlackhole.description: A blackhole on one address of an IP transit service. All traffic to the address is dropped at our border until the blackhole expires or is released.

id.description: The blackhole's ID. Use it to release the blackhole.

serviceNumber.description: The IP transit service the address belongs to.

address.description: The blackholed address, IPv4 or IPv6.

route.description: The address as the host route that is dropped, a `/32` or a `/128`.

reason.description: The reason you gave when you placed it. Always `null` on one Check Networks placed.

placedBy.description: `customer` when your portal user or API key placed it, `staff` when Check Networks did.

expiresAt.description: When the blackhole lifts by itself. One you place always has an expiry; one Check Networks places may have none.

releasedAt.description: When it was released or expired. `null` while it is in force.

Cdr.description: One call detail record, as `GET /voice/cdrs` lists it and `GET /voice/cdrs/{cgrid}` reads it.

cgrid.description: A unique id for this call. Use it to de-duplicate, and to read one call with `GET /voice/cdrs/{cgrid}`. A re-rated call keeps its id.

source.description: The originating number or SIP URI.

callerId.description: The caller ID that was presented, digits only, as the portal shows it. Null when the caller withheld it or none was presented.

cost.description: Call cost as a decimal dollar amount, without GST. Deprecated: read `costExGst`, `costGst` and `costIncGst` instead.

costExGst.description: The call's cost without GST, as rated.

costGst.description: The GST on the call; `0.00` on a GST-free account.

rerated.description: Whether the call was re-rated after it was first priced. A re-rated call is listed once, at its new price in `costExGst`, `costGst` and `costIncGst`, and counted once in the summary.

previousCostExGst.description: The price before the most recent re-rate, without GST: the price the call had just before its current one. A call re-rated more than once has only that one here. Null when it was not re-rated.

previousCostGst.description: The GST on `previousCostExGst`. Null when the call was not re-rated.

previousCostIncGst.description: The price before the most recent re-rate, with GST. Null when the call was not re-rated.

answerTime.description: When the call was answered. Null if unanswered.

disposition.description: The call's final state. `blocked` means the call never reached a carrier (barred call class, high-risk prefix, account hold or insufficient credit) — distinct from `failed`.

sipCauseCode.description: The SIP response code that ended the call, when the call reached SIP signalling.

callClass.description: The permission class the dialled destination fell into (e.g. AUMobile, International).

trunk.description: The sipUsername of the trunk (as returned by `GET /trunks`) this call belongs to; null for a call with no trunk.

trunkType.description: Where `trunk` is found: `trunk` at `GET /trunks/{username}`, `residentialLine` at `GET /residential-lines/{username}`. Null with no trunk.

endUser.description: The end user of the call's trunk, by its public number; the call is billed to that end user. Null for your own trunk or a call with no trunk.

createdAt.description: When the call record was written, in UTC.

updatedAt.description: When the call record last changed (a re-rate), in UTC.

NetworkOutages.description: Check Networks outages affecting your account's services, in the list envelope every list uses.

queryDateTime.description: When this query was received, in UTC

total.description: Number of outages matching the query

perPage.description: The number of outages per page

TicketCategory.description:
The ticket's category — what kind of work it is, used for routing and for
filtering the list.

Declared in one place and referenced everywhere a category appears
(filter, create, and the ticket body), so the values you may send are
always exactly the values you can be returned.

`security_incident` is a first-class category rather than a technical
ticket with a note, because the ticket register doubles as the
security-incident register.

`remote_hands` is on-site hands-and-eyes work at a facility.
`scam_traceback` is a scam-call traceback handed to a wholesale client to
continue tracing their own end customer; both are raised by us and appear
on your tickets, so an integration filtering the list must expect them.
`scam_report` is yours to raise: a scam call or SMS, or a spoofed number,
reported by you or your customer.

TicketComplaint.description: The complaint and its clocks, null when the ticket is not a complaint. A complaint about one of your end users is yours to handle under the Telecommunications Consumer Complaints Handling Standard: acknowledge it by `acknowledgeDueAt`, answer an urgent one by `urgentResponseDueAt`, resolve it by `resolutionDueAt`, and answer a TIO case by `tioDueAt`. The due times count in working days from when the complaint was received.

urgent.description: An urgent complaint has a shorter resolution deadline.

receivedAt.description: When the complaint arrived, which the deadlines count from.

acknowledgedAt.description: When the complaint was acknowledged to the consumer, or null while it has not been.

urgentResponseDueAt.description: Set when the consumer asked for urgent handling; null otherwise.

resolutionDueAt.description: When the complaint must be resolved. Not the support target of the same name on the ticket.

outcome.description: How the complaint ended, once recorded. Record it with the resolve on `PATCH /tickets/{ticketRef}`.

tioReference.description: The TIO's case reference, once a TIO case is logged.

tioDueAt.description: When the response to the TIO is due, once a TIO case is logged.

reference.description: The public ticket reference, e.g. `INC-7K3F9Q`. Use this to address the ticket in all other endpoints.

status.description: `open` and `pending` are active states; `resolved` and `closed` are closed-out. `pending` means Check Networks is waiting for your reply, and the response time clock is stopped until you reply. Replying to a resolved/closed ticket re-opens it.

endUser.description: The end user the ticket is about, by its public number. Null when the ticket is your own.

relatedService.description: What the ticket is linked to, by the same public reference `POST /tickets` takes: a data service's PRI (its AVC when it has none), a trunk's SIP username (its id when it has none), a number in E.164 without the `+`, or an invoice number. Null when the ticket is linked to none of these.

isComplaint.description: Whether the ticket is a complaint. `complaint` carries its deadlines.

updatedAt.description: When the ticket last changed, in UTC.

lastActivityAt.description: Bumped on every message and state change — the list sorts by this, newest first.

awaitingCustomerReply.description: True while the ticket is `pending`, waiting on your reply.

resolveBlockedReason.description: Why the ticket cannot be resolved now, or null. A refused resolve answers 422 with the same `code`.

canReopen.description: Whether `PATCH` with `status=open` would re-open the ticket (it is resolved or closed).

TicketFaultChecklist.description: The checklist answers given. A question left unanswered is absent.

newService.description: The service was connected recently and has never worked.

devicesPowered.description: The end user's devices are powered on, and have been restarted.

cabledDirectly.description: The router (or phone) is cabled straight to our equipment, with nothing between.

siteAvailability.description: When someone is at the site to let a technician in.

inductionNeeded.description: A technician needs a site induction before they can enter.

endUser.description: The end user the ticket is about, by its public number. One of your end users that is not archived; any other number is a 422. Omitted or null raises the ticket as your own.

relatedService.description: Optionally link the ticket to one of your services, or to one of your invoices for a billing question. The reference is validated against your account.

ref.description: The record's public identifier: an NBN service reference (AVC/PRI) for `data`, the trunk digest username for `trunk`, the phone number for `number`, or the invoice number for `invoice`. An invoice must be one of yours that has been issued (issued, paid or void); a draft is a 422.

isComplaint.description: Raise the ticket as a complaint: its deadlines start from now, as `POST /tickets/{ticketRef}/complaint` would start them.

complaintUrgent.description: With `isComplaint`, raise it as an urgent complaint. Ignored without it.

fault.description: The fault, on a `technical` ticket about a data service, trunk or number: required there, and refused on any other ticket. There is no limit on open fault tickets for one service unless we set one; a service at it is refused with `fault_ticket_limit`, so add to the open ticket instead.

type.description: For a data service: `speed`, `dropouts`, `noConnection`, `noService` or `other`. For a trunk or a number: `noDialTone`, `noCalls`, `callQuality`, `noInternational`, `nuisanceCalls`, `hardware` or `other`. Any other is a 422 on `fault.type`.

testRefs.description: Tests and health checks you have run on this data service: a test's `id` from `POST /nbn/diagnostics`, or a health check's `hrId`. One of another service, or unknown, is a 422 on `fault.testRefs.{n}`. A trunk or a number has none to link.

siteContact.description: Who our technician calls about access to the site.

preferredAppointment.description: When suits the site for a technician, in your words.

additionalContacts.description: Email addresses to copy on our emails about the ticket.

TicketFaultTestRef.description: A test or health check linked to a fault ticket.

ref.description: The test's id (`GET /nbn/diagnostics/{id}`) or the health check's `hrId`.

TicketFaultSiteContact.description: Who to contact at the site, when one was given.

TicketFault.description: A fault ticket's fields, as raised with `POST /tickets`. Null on a ticket that is not a fault ticket.

serviceKind.description: `data` for a data service, `voice` for a trunk or a number: the list `type` is from.

testRefs.description: The tests and health checks of the service you linked.

additionalContacts.description: Email addresses copied on our emails about the ticket.

TicketMessage.description: One public entry in a ticket's conversation thread.

id.description: The message's id, as the `ticket.replied` webhook names it in `messageId`. Opaque.

kind.description: `reply` is a human message; `event` is a system timeline entry (e.g. a status change).

author.description: Display label for the author: `Support` for Check Networks staff, the user's name for portal users, `API` for messages posted via this API, `System` for event entries.

updatedAt.description: The same as `createdAt`; a message is never edited.

attachments.description: Attachment metadata. Download the content from `GET /tickets/{ticketRef}/attachments/{attachmentId}`.

isInline.description: True when the file is embedded in the message body (referenced as `cid:<id>`), rather than listed alongside it.

Ticket.description: A support ticket with its public conversation thread.

escalation.description: Your latest escalation with `POST /tickets/{ticketRef}/escalate`; null until you escalate. Each one is also on the thread.

firstResponseDueAt.description: When our first response is due, under your support targets. The clock counts business hours (around the clock for an `urgent` ticket) and stops while the ticket is `pending`.

resolutionDueAt.description: When we aim to resolve the ticket, on the same clock. A complaint's own resolution deadline is `complaint.resolutionDueAt`.

messages.description: The public conversation thread, oldest first. Internal Check Networks notes are never included.

TicketsSummary.description: The ticket report's figures over a range, as the portal's Support Reports page shows them.

total.description: Tickets raised in the range.

open.description: Of those, the ones still `open` or `pending`.

byStatus.description: Tickets by status, every status listed, zeros included.

byPriority.description: Tickets by priority, every priority listed, zeros included.

byCategory.description: Tickets by category, every category listed, zeros included.

volumeByMonth.description: Tickets raised each month of the range, oldest first, months with none included.

firstResponseMetPercent.description: The percentage of tickets with a first response that had it by the target. Null when none in range had both.

resolutionMetPercent.description: The percentage of resolved tickets resolved by the target. Null when none in range had both.

averageFirstResponseMinutes.description: The average minutes from raising a ticket to our first response, over the tickets that had one.

averageResolutionMinutes.description: The average minutes from raising a ticket to its resolution, over the resolved ones.

count.description: Tickets in range with a satisfaction rating.

average.description: Their average rating, 1 to 5, to two decimal places. Null when none were rated.

OutageSubscription.description: An email address or Australian mobile subscribed to our outage notices for your account. It is `pending` until the person follows the link they are sent, and only then are notices sent to it.

address.description: The email address in lower case, or the mobile in E.164.

scope.description: Which outages it is told of.

status.description: `pending` until the person confirms by the link; `active` after.

Watch.description: A subscription that emails one or more people when something we track changes. The human-facing counterpart to a webhook.

id.description: The watch's identifier — use this to fetch or remove it.

reference.description: What is being watched: an order reference (the carrier's, e.g. `OPO000000230683`, or ours, `PND…` — both address the same order), a technician appointment reference, a service identifier (a carrier service id, or a trunk's SIP username), or an outage reference.

referenceType.description: The kind of thing `reference` names, worked out from the reference itself — you never send it. It tells you which group in `GET /watch/event-types` applies to this watch. Treat it as an open set rather than an enum you switch on exhaustively: more kinds land on this same endpoint over time.

supplier.description: The carrier the watched reference belongs to, filled in from the order. Null on a watch that is not carrier-specific.

eventTypes.description: Which events this watch notifies on. Null — the default — means every event.

emails.description: Where notifications are sent. Lowercased and de-duplicated on save.

status.description: `disabled` is what removing a watch produces — the record is kept, and watching the same reference again re-enables it.

lastNotifiedAt.description: When this watch last caused an email to be sent.

updatedAt.description: When the watch last changed, in UTC.

EventTypeItem.description: One event you can subscribe to. `GET /webhooks/event-types` and `GET /watch/event-types` both list items of this shape.

value.description: The value to send: in a webhook's `events`, or in a watch's `eventTypes`.

label.description: How this event is described to a reader, as the notification emails name it.

referenceType.description: The kind of watched thing this event applies to, matching a watch's own `referenceType`. Null on the webhook list: a webhook is not about one kind of reference.

WebhookEventType.description:
A subscribable webhook event type, or `*` for every event.

Declared in one place and referenced by both the subscription request and
the subscription you get back, so anything you can be told about is
something you can subscribe to. (They drifted apart once: five order and
service events reached the response list while the request list still
rejected them, which left a generated client unable to subscribe to
events the same spec said existed.)

`ping` is deliberately absent — it is sent only by
`POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test`, regardless of what the subscription
covers, so it is not something to subscribe to.

WebhookFilters.description: Limits an endpoint to some services or end users. An event about a service is sent when its service is in `serviceIds` or its end user is in `endUserIds`. An event about no service or end user (an invoice, a ticket) is sent only when the endpoint names its type in `events`, not through `*`. Empty lists, or no filters, mean every event the endpoint takes.

serviceIds.description: Services by the id their events carry in `data.serviceId`: a data service's id, a trunk's `sipUsername`, a transit or colocation uuid.

WebhookSubscription.description: A registered webhook endpoint. The signing secret is returned once — at registration or rotation — and is never readable afterwards.

id.description: The endpoint's id, as `/webhooks/{webhookId}` takes it. Opaque.

url.description: Your HTTPS endpoint. Must resolve to a public address (port 443 or 8443).

events.description: Subscribed event types, or `["*"]` for all events.

isActive.description: Endpoints are disabled automatically after 20 consecutive dead deliveries (each delivery is 6 attempts over ~8.6h). While disabled, events are still recorded as `dead` deliveries with zero attempts rather than dropped. Re-enable with a PATCH once your endpoint is healthy, then replay dead deliveries to catch up.

consecutiveFailures.description: Dead deliveries in a row; the endpoint is disabled automatically at 20. Resets to zero on a successful delivery or re-enable — the dead deliveries themselves remain in the delivery history.

disabledReason.description: Why the endpoint is off: `auto` after 20 dead deliveries in a row, `manual` when you turned it off. Null while it is on.

lastDeliveredAt.description: When a delivery last succeeded, or null if none has.

lastError.description: Why the latest dead delivery failed. Cleared by the next successful delivery.

previousSecretExpiresAt.description: After a secret rotation, when the previous secret stops signing deliveries. Null when no rotation window is open.

updatedAt.description: When the endpoint last changed, in UTC.

sequence.description: A counter for the deliveries to this endpoint: each delivery queued for it takes the next number. A redelivery or a replay is a new delivery, so it takes a new, higher number, and an old event sent again sorts after newer ones. Do not order events by it: order them by `occurredAt`, which a redelivery keeps, and use `eventId` to drop repeats.

WebhookDelivery.description:
One attempted delivery of one event to one endpoint. Rows are written before
the delivery is attempted and are never removed, so the history survives a
failed endpoint — and the endpoint being deleted.

id.description: The delivery id. Use it to redeliver. Opaque.

webhookId.description: The endpoint it went to, as `GET /webhooks` names it.

eventId.description:
The event's id, as sent in the `eventId` field of the delivered payload.
A redelivery carries the SAME `eventId` as the attempt it replays, so
handlers that de-duplicate on it treat the replay as the same event.

status.description:
`queued` is in flight, `delivered` was acknowledged with a 2xx, and
`dead` exhausted its retries.

attempts.description: Delivery attempts made so far for this record.

responseCode.description: HTTP status your endpoint returned on the last attempt, if it answered.

lastError.description: Why the last attempt failed — the transport or HTTP error we saw.

payload.description: The event body that was POSTed to your endpoint.

updatedAt.description: When the delivery record last changed (an attempt), in UTC.

EndUserAddress.description: An Australian street address, as the End User form in the portal takes it.

EndUser.description:
One of your end users: a customer of yours who uses your services. Named
by its number (`endUser`), which every other end-user call takes.

**Family violence safety.** While an active safety record suppresses the
end user's contact details, `contactsMasked` is true and the contacts and
both addresses are null, exactly as the portal masks them. Only
`POST /end-users/{endUser}/contacts/reveal` returns them, on the
`safety:read` scope, and every reveal is audited.

endUser.description: The end user's number. Every end-user call names the end user by it.

name.description: The person's name, or the contact name for a business.

businessName.description: The legal business name. Set for a business end user only.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the end user, such as its id in your CRM. Find an end user by it with `GET /end-users?externalRef=`.

status.description:
`suspended`: its voice services are cut off (a 000 call still goes
through). `archived`: a former end user, put away; it can be restored.

suspendReason.description: The reason given when it was suspended. Null unless `status` is `suspended`.

lastVerifiedAt.description: When a one-time code sent to the end user last proved who was on the call (`POST /end-users/{endUser}/verification-codes`). Nothing requires it.

contactsMasked.description: True while a family violence safety record withholds the contacts and addresses below.

billingEmail.description: Where bills go, when not to `email`.

billingSameAsService.description: True when bills go to the service address. Null while the contacts are masked.

billingAddress.description: The billing address. Null when it is the service address.

usageNotificationMethod.description: How the end user is told about their data usage.

paymentTermsDays.description: Days to pay their bills. Null uses your default.

invoiceFormat.description: Summary or detailed bills. Null uses your default.

timezone.description:
The end user's own time zone: their bills are cut on it, and their
portal shows times in it. Null is your zone. Change it with
`PATCH /end-users/{endUser}`; a change applies from their next billing
period.

creditLimit.description:
A credit limit for your own records, in dollars including GST. Nothing
reads it: it stops no call and no service. Null is none.

spendLimit.description:
A monthly spend limit, in dollars including GST. The end user is
emailed when the month's bill reaches 50, 85 and 100 per cent of it.
Nothing is stopped. Null is none.

notes.description: The free-text notes on the end user's details. Your notes history is `/end-users/{endUser}/notes`.

EndUserDetails.description:
The details of an end user that create and update share, as the End User
form in the portal takes them. Send `null` to clear a field.

businessName.description: The legal business name. Required for a business end user; ignored for a residential one.

tradingName.description: Kept for a business end user only.

abn.description: An ABN, checked with the ATO check digit. Spaces are allowed. Kept for a business end user only.

acn.description: Kept for a business end user only.

externalRef.description: Your own reference for the end user, such as its id in your CRM.

invoiceDelivery.description: How their bills are sent. On a create, left out or null takes your default.

usageNotificationMethod.description: How they are told about their data usage. On a create, left out or null is email.

paymentTermsDays.description: Days to pay their bills. Null uses your default.

creditLimit.description: Dollars including GST, for your own records; nothing reads it. Null is none.

spendLimit.description:
A monthly spend limit, in dollars including GST. The end user is
emailed at 50, 85 and 100 per cent of it; nothing is stopped. Null is
none.

EndUserSettings.description: An end user's own defaults for the calls to their lines, whether they get billing texts, and whether you bill them through the platform.

blockInternationalInbound.description: Block calls from overseas numbers to their lines, by default.

allowNzInbound.description: While international calls are blocked, still let New Zealand (+64) callers through.

billingSms.description:
Whether they get the billing texts you have switched on (payment
reminders, final notices, receipts, failed automatic payments). False
when they asked you to stop them; their billing emails still go.

isBilled.description:
Whether you bill them through the platform. False for an end user you
bill some other way: they get no bill from it, and their services need
no retail price. What we bill you does not change. Every end user
starts billed.

EndUserNote.description: One of your own notes on an end user. The end user never sees it.

author.description: Who wrote it. A note added through the API names the key, as "<key name> (API key)".

EndUserSafetyRecord.description:
A family violence safety record on an end user (F2025L00664). Legal
obligations attach to this data: see the End users safety help page. While
one is active with `suppressContactDisclosure`, the end user's contacts are
masked on every other read.

safePostalAddress.description: Where their bills are posted under `safe_post`, never the end user's own address. Stored encrypted, and returned only on these safety-record reads (`safety:read`), as the safe number and email are. Null: none recorded.

billDelivery.description: How the end user wants their bills while the record is active: `safe_email` emails bills and billing notices to `safeContactEmail` only; `safe_post` sends none and alerts you to post them to `safePostalAddress`; `portal_only` sends none, and they read their bills in the portal; `none` sends no bills or billing notices. Null: bills follow `agreedCommunicationMethod`.

billDeliveryNote.description: Anything more about how they want their bills.

billDeliveryRequest.description: The same as `billDeliveryNote`. Deprecated: read `billDelivery` and `billDeliveryNote`.

identifiedBy.description: The portal user who raised it; null when raised by API (the audit log names the key).

retentionExpiresAt.description: Set on close; the earliest the record may be disposed of.

EndUserSafetyRecordInput.description: A safety record's own fields, with the portal's rules. On a change, a field left out stays as it is.

safePostalAddress.description: Where their bills are posted under `safe_post`. A PO Box is fine. Null clears it. `safe_post` with no safe postal address on the record is refused (422, on `safePostalAddress`).

billDelivery.description: How the end user wants their bills; see the record's `billDelivery`. `safe_post` needs a `safePostalAddress`.

billDeliveryRequest.description: Sets `billDeliveryNote`. Deprecated: send `billDelivery` and `billDeliveryNote`; ignored when `billDeliveryNote` is sent.

EndUserLogin.description: A login to the end user's own portal.

EndUserLoginInvite.description: An invite to the end user's portal not yet accepted or revoked. One that ran out is listed with `expired` true, so you can resend it.

EndUserRepresentative.description: Someone the end user has authorised to act for them (IGN017). Only an active one confers authority.

authorities.description: The areas they may act on. `full` covers every area and is then the only one listed.

EndUserService.description: A service an end user owns, or a number they hold.

reference.description:
The reference the service's own calls take: a data service's service
reference, a trunk's SIP username, a number, an IP transit service's
number, a fax plan's id, a hosted PBX's id. A closed hosted PBX is not
listed.

label.description: A name that helps tell it apart, such as a data service's username or a number's label.

status.description: The service's own status, as its own calls show it.

suspensionTakesEffect.description: For a suspended data service, how soon the suspension takes effect, as on GET /data/services/{ref}. Null for any other service.

assignmentId.description:
The billed assignment the service carries, when it has one. End it with
`DELETE /end-users/{endUser}/services/{assignmentId}`. Always null for a
number.

endsOn.description: The last day the assignment is billed, once it has been ended.

EndUserImport.description:
One end-user import, as the portal's Import page lists it. The counts are
null while it is `processing`. A `failed` import stopped part-way: its
counts are of the rows it wrote, and the rest of the `total` were not run.

status.description:
`processing` on the queue, `finished`, or `failed` when its run
stopped part-way or had not started an hour after it was queued
(then nothing was written). Import the rows not run again: those already
made are skipped as duplicates.

source.description: Where it was sent from, `api` or the portal (`wholesale`).

filename.description: The file's name, or null for rows sent as JSON.

total.description: The rows read from the file.

skipped.description: Rows passed over as duplicates of an end user already there, or of a row earlier in the file.

failed.description: Rows not made because a check failed (a missing name, a business with no business name, a bad email, an invite with no email) or an unexpected error.

EndUserImportDetail.description: One end-user import with each row's outcome, as the portal's import page shows it.

rows.description: Each row read, in file order. Empty while the import is `processing`.

rowNumber.description: The line in the file, or the row's place in `rows` counting from 1.

endUser.description: The end user made from this row, by number.

email.description: The row's email. Null while a family violence safety record withholds the contacts of the end user made from it.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or failed, or what went wrong after it was made (an invite that could not be sent).

NotificationSettings.description: Where automated mail goes, and the usage notices sent to your residential end users.

notificationEmail.description: The address automated mail goes to, such as a NOC alias. Null sends it to your primary or billing contact (`fallbackEmail`).

fallbackEmail.description: Where mail goes while `notificationEmail` is null.

enabled.description: Whether your residential end users are told at 50%, 85% and 100% of their data allowance. Off by default: they go out under your name, and SMS is billed to you.

smsSender.description: The approved sender the SMS go as; null sends email only.

availableSenders.description: The approved senders you may send as.

PortalBranding.description:
The end-user portal's branding, as Portal Branding shows it in the
portal. The same values theme the end-user portal and the emails your end
users are sent.

displayName.description: The brand name end users see. Empty until first set.

brandColor.description:
Filled under white text, so it must reach 4.5:1 contrast against
white. Null uses the platform's colour.

supportHours.description: Free text, such as "Mon to Fri, 8am to 6pm", in the portal footer.

afterHoursPhone.description: A fault number for outside those hours, in the portal footer.

ticketsEnabled.description: Whether end users may raise tickets in the end-user portal.

emailLogoPosition.description: Where the logo sits in emails to end users.

logos.description:
Where to download each logo (with your token), or null when none is
set.

light.description: The main logo, also the logo on your end users' invoices.

dark.description: The logo shown in dark mode.

PortalDomain.description:
The end-user portal's custom domain: the hostname claimed, the DNS records
to publish for it, and where its verification stands.

status.description:
`pending` until both records check out; `verified` once they have and
the portal answers on the domain; `failed` when the claim expired
unverified (claim the domain again for a new TXT record).

live.description: Whether the end-user portal is served on this domain now.

records.description: The records to publish at your DNS host.

lastCheck.description: The record's result at the last verify.

checkedAt.description: When the records were last checked.

checkError.description: What the last check found missing.

expiresAt.description:
When an unverified claim stops holding the domain (seven days after
it was made). Null once verified.

DfvSupportChannel.description:
A way for an affected person to reach you (s18). The statement needs at
least two different types, and one that reaches a person.

connectsToIndividual.description: Reaches a person. Always false for a web form.

DfvStatement.description:
Your own domestic and family violence statement (F2025L00664, ss16-18), shown
on your end-user portal once published, else ours. Approval by your most
senior executive and publishing are done in the portal, at `portalUrl`.

safetyCommitment.description: s17(2)(a), your safety policies and procedures.

continuityCommitment.description: s17(2)(b), staying connected and reversing restrictions.

nonPaymentCommitment.description: s17(2)(c), non-payment and financial hardship assistance.

contactInstructions.description: s17(2)(d), how to contact you for assistance.

supportOrganisations.description: Your own wording, shown beside the six statutory support services.

interimNotice.description: Shown until `supportAvailableFrom`; changing it keeps approval.

approval.description: Null until approved, and again after a wording change.

outstanding.description: What stands between the statement and publishing.

portalUrl.description: The portal page where the statement is approved and published.

ComplaintsProcess.description:
Your own complaints-handling process and network outage
complaints-handling process (Consumer Complaints Handling Industry
Standard 2018, s8(1)(f), s10A, s10B), shown on your end-user portal once
published, else ours. Approval by a named person and publishing are done
in the portal, at `portalUrl`.

outageProcessSummary.description: s10B, how you handle complaints about a network outage.

approval.description: Null until approved, and again after a summary change.

outstanding.description: What stands between the process and publishing.

portalUrl.description: The portal page where the process is approved and published.

CreditAlertRecipient.description: One person who receives credit warnings, by email or by SMS.

CreditAlertSettings.description: Your credit warning settings, as the portal's Credit Alerts page holds them.

thresholds.description: The percentages of your credit limit a warning is sent at.

fallbackEmail.description: Where warnings go while there are no recipients, your billing contact.

InvoiceDispute.description: A dispute you raised on one of our invoices, and where it is up to.

invoiceId.description: The invoice's `id` (a ULID), as `GET /account/invoices` gives it.

lineId.description: The line disputed, by its public id as the invoice's `lineItems[].id`, or null for the invoice as a whole.

status.description: Where the dispute is up to, as the portal shows it.

ticketRef.description: The support ticket the dispute opened.

creditNoteId.description: The credit note it was resolved with, if any.

InvoiceGroup.description: A named section of an invoice: a site, a department or a cost centre. The account's own groups section our invoice to you; an end user's section the invoices you send that end user. Changes apply from the next invoice; an issued invoice keeps the groups as they were.

name.description: Unique among the owner's groups, ignoring case. At most 100 characters.

description.description: The billing description printed under the group's heading.

poNumber.description: The purchase order number printed with the group, unless a service sets its own.

costCentre.description: The cost centre printed with the group, unless a service sets its own.

serviceCount.description: How many services are in the group.

InvoiceGroupInput.description: A group's fields. On create, `name` is required; on update, only the fields sent change, and a blank or null description, PO or cost centre clears it.

InvoiceService.description: A service's place on one owner's invoice: its invoice group (at most one) and its own billing label, PO number and cost centre, which override the group's. The service is named as invoice lines name it.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the service is set on, if any.

invoiceGroupId.description: The group the service is in, by its public id. Null for none, which prints under Other.

invoiceLabel.description: The service's own billing label, printed with its lines.

poNumber.description: The service's own PO number. Null uses its group's.

costCentre.description: The service's own cost centre. Null uses its group's.

PartnerCommissionRun.description: One month's commission for one of your partners. Figures are stored without GST; each carries its GST and the figure with GST. `gstShown`, beside the results, says which the portal shows.

partnerId.description: The partner's user id, as on GET /account/users.

basis.description: What the rate was applied to.

payableExGst.description: Commission less clawbacks, what the partner is paid.

PartnerCommissionClawback.description: Commission taken back because revenue it was paid on was reversed: a credit note, a write-off or a dishonoured payment. It comes off the partner's next runs until `remaining` is zero.

sourceRunId.description: The run that paid the commission now taken back, by its public id.

remainingExGst.description: What is still to come off.

RetailInvoice.description: An invoice you issued to one of your end users. Never one of the invoices Check Networks issues to you: those are on /account/invoices. Money is a decimal dollar string, each amount as ex-GST, GST and inc-GST.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

status.description: `held` only on a final invoice that answered held for approval; the lists never carry a held invoice (see /end-users/invoice-approvals).

final.description: True on an end user's final invoice.

amountPaid.description: What has been paid against this invoice, inc. GST.

amountDue.description: What is still owed on it, inc. GST.

remindersPausedUntil.description: While payment reminders on this invoice are paused, the day they start again.

remindersPauseReason.description: The reason given for the pause. On the single invoice only.

RetailPayment.description: A payment applied to an end-user invoice. Money is a decimal dollar string.

method.description: `recorded` for one you recorded; otherwise the gateway that took it.

appliedToInvoice.description: The part of it applied to this invoice. A payment can cover several invoices, oldest first.

paidOn.description: The day it was paid, on your account's time zone.

RetailCreditNote.description: A credit note you issued to one of your end users, the only correction to one of their invoices. Money is a decimal dollar string.

lines.description: On the single credit note only.

EndUserLedgerEntry.description: One transaction on an end user's account. Money is a decimal dollar string, inc. GST unless named otherwise.

reference.description: The document number, where there is one.

direction.description: `debit` adds to what they owe; `credit` takes off it.

balance.description: The running balance after this transaction.

paidOn.description: On an invoice, the day it was paid in full.

HardshipCase.description: An end user's financial hardship case: an arrangement in force, or an application under assessment. Money is a decimal dollar string.

id.description: The case's public id, as `/end-users/{endUser}/hardship/{caseId}` takes it.

status.description: `proposed` is an application under assessment; `active` an arrangement in force.

options.description: The assistance agreed, from the options you offer (/retail/hardship-options).

pauseAutopay.description: Whether automatic payments are paused while it is open.

assessmentDueAt.description: The deadline to assess an application, in business days on your calendar.

instalmentAmount.description: On a payment plan, each instalment.

EndUserDispute.description: An end user's dispute of a charge on an invoice you issued them. While it is open the disputed amount is not collected.

id.description: The dispute's public id, as `/end-users/disputes/{id}` takes it.

invoiceLineId.description: The line disputed, by its public id, or null for the bill as a whole.

raisedBy.description: Who raised it, by kind (for example the end user's own portal login).

inProgress.description: A decision is queued and has neither landed nor failed.

error.description: Why the last decision could not be completed. Retry sends it again.

creditNoteId.description: On a credited dispute, the credit note (/end-users/credit-notes/{id}).

RetailPriceBookItem.description:
One product in your retail price book: what your end users are charged for
it. Prices are held ex-GST; the GST and the price with GST are worked out
under your own tax settings and the product's GST treatment.

id.description: The price's public id, used to change or remove it.

priceExGst.description: The price each period (a month, or a year for an annual product), ex-GST.

setupFeeExGst.description:
The setup fee, ex-GST. Null when none is set, so the setup fee falls
back to your default markup on ours; "0.00" is a free connection.

effectiveFrom.description: The day the price applies from. Every end user on the product moves to it then.

planId.description:
The product's default call plan, one of your own published plans. It
prices calls for end users whose service has no plan of its own. Null
for none.

RetailPlan.description: One of your own call plans for your end users. A plan is versioned: published versions never change, and every edit goes to the plan's one draft, which is opened from the latest version on the first edit. A published version prices calls from its `effectiveFrom` date.

code.description: The plan's code, unique across all plans.

archived.description: An archived plan cannot be given to another service. Services already on it keep being rated by it.

workingVersion.description: The version an edit starts from: the draft, else the version in effect, else the latest. Null for a plan with no version yet.

effectiveVersion.description: The published version that prices calls today, or null.

draftVersion.description: The open draft, or null when there is none.

assignedServices.description: How many of your end users' services the plan is pinned to.

status.description: `superseded` is a published version a later one has replaced from its effective date. It still prices calls made before then.

effectiveFrom.description: The date the version prices calls from. Null on a draft.

notes.description: Where the version came from, such as the card it was copied from.

RetailPlanDestination.description: One destination on a call plan version: the calls to numbers starting with `prefix` (the longest matching prefix wins). Each rate is shown ex-GST, its GST, and with GST, as your end user's invoice will bill it under your own tax settings. Rates are dollar amounts to up to 5 decimal places.

prefix.description: The number prefix, in E.164 digits without the `+`. It names the destination on every version.

connectionFeeExGst.description: The charge for each answered call, ex-GST.

minimumChargeExGst.description: The least an answered call costs, ex-GST.

firstIncrementSeconds.description: The first billing increment, in seconds.

subsequentIncrementSeconds.description: Each billing increment after the first, in seconds.

RetailPriceSourced.description:
The price that will bill today, ex-GST with its GST, and where it comes
from: `service_price` (this service's own price), `retail_book` (your
price book), `default_markup` (your markup on what we charge you) or
`unpriced` (nothing prices it: it bills nothing and holds the end user's
invoice for you to approve).

EndUserServiceBilling.description:
How one service you have given an end user bills. Its own price and setup
fee, when set, win over your price book; null means the book applies.
Prices are ex-GST, with the GST worked out under your tax settings.

planId.description: The call plan pinned to this service, one of your own, by its public id. Null uses the product's default plan.

priceExGst.description: This service's own price each period, ex-GST. Null when the price book applies.

setupFeeExGst.description: This service's own setup fee, ex-GST. Null when the price book applies; "0.00" is free.

notBilled.description:
True when the whole service, its fees and its usage, is left off the
end user's invoices. Our invoice to you is not changed.

endsOn.description: The last day the service is billed to the end user, once ended.

EndUserCharge.description:
One of your own charges on an end user's bill. The amount is ex-GST;
GST is added on the invoice.

kind.description: Recurring bills each month in advance; once-off bills once, on the next invoice.

priceExGst.description: The amount each month (recurring) or once, ex-GST.

startsOn.description: The start date (recurring) or the date of the charge (once-off).

endsOn.description: The last day a recurring charge bills. Null for no end, and for a once-off charge.

billFrom.description: The first day a recurring charge bills from. Null for a once-off charge.

invoiced.description:
True once a held or issued invoice carries it. A once-off charge can no
longer change or be removed then; a recurring one can change only its
description, amount (for months not yet charged) and end date, and is
ended rather than removed.

RetailInvoiceSettings.description: The settings printed on every invoice to your end users, as Retail Settings sets them in the portal. The logo is set under the portal's branding and domain settings, not here.

displayName.description: The business name your end-user invoices are issued by. Null for your account's name.

abn.description: Your ABN, printed on each tax invoice: 11 digits, which must pass the ATO check digit. Spaces are accepted on a write and stored as bare digits.

defaultTermsDays.description: Days to pay for an end user with no terms of its own. Null for 14 days.

defaultInvoiceDelivery.description: The invoice delivery a new end user starts with.

invoiceCopyEmail.description: Blind-copied on each end-user invoice email. Null sends no copy.

defaultInvoiceFormat.description: Summary or detailed invoices, for an end user with no choice of its own. Detailed lists each call under its usage line.

invoiceNumberPrefix.description: Leads every end-user invoice and credit note number. Null for none.

invoiceNextNumber.description: The next number of one running sequence across all your end users, shared by invoices and credit notes. Null numbers each invoice by end user and month. Each bill run moves it on.

remittanceText.description: The bank transfer details printed on each invoice.
remittanceText.example: BSB 062-000, account 1234 5678, reference your invoice number.

bpayBillerCode.description: Your own BPAY biller code, 3 to 10 digits.

RetailReminderSchedule.description: When your end users are reminded of an overdue invoice. Reminders only: no end user is suspended automatically.

enabled.description: Whether overdue end users are reminded at all. Off until you turn it on.

reminderDays.description: Days after the due date the first reminder is sent.

finalNoticeDays.description: Days after the due date the final notice is sent. Must be after the first reminder.

sendNotices.description: Whether the reminders are emailed to the end user. Off for a wholesaler that chases its end users through its own system: the reminder stages are still recorded.

RetailNotice.description: A notice your end users receive that you may reword.

key.description: The notice's key, used in its path.

group.description: The notices are grouped as in the portal.

description.example: Sent to an end user with each invoice from your bill run, the invoice PDF attached.

reworded.description: Whether you have saved your own wording. False sends the Check Networks default.

requiredContent.description: The placeholders that must stay in the subject or the body.

tokens.description: Every placeholder the notice offers. Any other placeholder is refused.

body.description: The body in effect, in Markdown. A statutory footer, where a notice has one, is added on every send and is not part of it.
body.example:
Hi {{ customer_name }},

Your invoice **{{ invoice_number }}** from {{ brand }} is attached.

default.description: The Check Networks default wording, which a reset goes back to.

body.example:
Hi {{ customer_name }},

Your invoice **{{ invoice_number }}** from {{ brand }} is attached.

RetailPaymentGateway.description: One payment gateway you take your end users' card or direct debit payments through. No key, webhook secret or callback address is ever returned.

connected.description: Whether keys for this gateway are saved.

status.description: `verified`: the keys passed our check when they were last saved or the gateway was switched back on. `unverified`: they did not, so end users are not offered it. `disabled`: you switched it off and its keys are kept. Null when not connected.

working.description: Whether end users are offered this gateway now (its status is verified).

supportedMethods.description: The payment methods this gateway can take.

enabledMethods.description: The payment methods you have turned it on for. Empty when not connected.

verifiedAt.description: When the keys last passed our check. Null when they never have, or after a failed check.

lastCheckedAt.description: When we last checked the keys, whether or not they passed. The keys are checked when they are saved or the gateway is switched back on. Null when no check has been recorded.

lastError.description: Why the last check failed, as the portal shows it: the gateway's own reason and its HTTP status, or why it could not be reached. Null when it passed or none has run. Never contains key material.

EndUserSpend.description: An end user's spend this month against the monthly spend limit you set on them. Spent is their Next Bill Estimate so far, with GST: the same figure their spend alerts and your portal show. The limit is an alert only; nothing is stopped when it is reached.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

month.description: The calendar month, in the billing time zone (Australia/Brisbane).

limit.description: The monthly spend limit, in dollars, GST-inclusive.

spentExGst.description: Spent so far this month without GST, in dollars.

spentIncGst.description: Spent so far with GST: the figure compared with `limit`.

percent.description: Whole per cent of the limit spent, rounded down.

tiersReached.description: The alert tiers (50, 85 and 100 per cent) reached this month.

usageExcluded.description: Call usage is not in `spent` yet, as on the end user's Next Bill Estimate; the figure is their services and charges only.

EndUserUsageRecord.description: A record of usage you rated yourself, billed on your end user's next invoice. Money is a dollar string. The unit price is to up to five decimal places of a dollar; the amount is the quantity times the unit price, rounded up to the cent, as the invoice bills it. GST is worked under your own tax settings and the record's `gst` treatment.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

description.description: What the usage was, as it is printed on the invoice.

quantity.description: How much, to up to four decimal places.

unitPriceExGst.description: The price of one unit, ex GST.

unitPriceIncGst.description: The price of one unit with GST.

amountExGst.description: Quantity times unit price, ex GST, rounded up to the cent.

gst.description: The GST treatment: `gst` adds GST, `free` and `exempt` add none.

reference.description: Your own reference for the record, unique on your account.

service.description: The end user's service the usage relates to, if you named one: its `assignmentId` from List an End User's Services.

billed.description: Whether a held or issued invoice carries it. A billed record can no longer be removed.

EndUserUsageInput.description: One record of usage you rated yourself. The unit price is in dollars, ex GST, as the portal takes it. A record can come to at most $999,999.99.

usageDate.description: The day of the usage. Not in the future, and not in a bill period the end user already has a held or issued invoice for.

description.description: What the usage was. On a summary invoice, records with the same description, unit, unit price and GST treatment are one line; on a detailed invoice each record is its own line.

quantity.description: How much, above 0, to up to four decimal places.

unitPrice.description: The price of one unit in dollars, **ex GST**, from 0, to up to five decimal places.

gst.description: The GST treatment. `gst` when left out.

reference.description: Your own reference for the record, unique on your account: a record with a reference already added is refused, so you can resend safely.

service.description: One of the end user's services the usage relates to, by its `assignmentId` from List an End User's Services.

XeroStatus.description: Your own Xero connection, as Integrations → Xero in the portal shows it: whether it works, what still stops a push, and how much is waiting.

configured.description: Xero can be connected here. `false` means connecting is not available at the moment.

connected.description: An organisation is connected and Xero still accepts the connection.

needsReconnect.description: Xero no longer accepts the connection (it expired, or was removed in Xero). Nothing is sent until you connect again in the portal.

pushFrom.description: Only documents from this date on are sent: the day you connected. Earlier ones are taken to be in your books already.

pushPayments.description: Whether payments you record are sent too, as well as invoices and credit notes.

problems.description: What still stops a push, in words: a mapping not chosen yet, or an account or tax rate archived in Xero since. Empty when ready. Fix these with Set Xero Mapping.

chartError.description: Why your chart of accounts could not be read from Xero just now, when it could not. `problems` is then empty.

counts.description: How many end-user ledger entries are in each state.

waiting.description: Not tried yet. The nightly push, or Send Now, sends them.

unmatched.description: Waiting on a Xero contact for the end user. Link one with Link Xero Contact.

partial.description: Sent in part: the next push finishes them.

failed.description: Xero refused them. `reason` on each says why; the next push tries again.

lastPushAt.description: When an entry was last sent or tried, by any push (nightly, the portal's Send Now or this API).

lastError.description: The newest reason Xero gave for refusing an entry still failed or sent in part.

message.example: The document date cannot be before the period lock date.

XeroQueueEntry.description: One end-user ledger entry that has not reached Xero: the end user, the document it is for, and why.

entryId.description: The ledger entry's public id, as the end-user ledger names it.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

kind.description: What the entry is: `invoice_charge` (an invoice), `credit_note`, `payment`, `payment_reversal` (a dishonour or chargeback) or `adjustment`.

direction.description: A debit adds to what the end user owes you; a credit takes from it.

invoiceNumber.description: The end-user invoice the entry is for, when it is one.

creditNoteNumber.description: The end-user credit note the entry is for, when it is one.

amountExGst.description: The entry's amount without GST, in dollars. Unsigned; `direction` carries the sign.

reason.description: Xero's reason, or ours, for the entry not being in Xero. `null` while waiting.
reason.example: The document date cannot be before the period lock date.

attempts.description: How many times a push has tried it.

XeroChoice.description: One account or tax rate your Xero chart of accounts offers.

code.description: The account code or tax type to send in Set Xero Mapping.

XeroMapping.description: Which of your Xero organisation's accounts and tax rates your end-user documents use. Every value is an account code or tax type from your own chart of accounts (`choices`); nothing is assumed, so nothing is sent until the mapping is complete.

revenueDefault.description: The sales account every invoice line goes to unless its product or charge has its own.

products.description: A sales account for a product's lines, by product ID, in place of `revenueDefault`.

charges.description: A sales account for one of your own charges, by charge ID, in place of `revenueDefault`.

paymentDefault.description: The account payments are received into, unless their gateway has its own. Needed only when `pushPayments` is on.

payments.description: A clearing account per way an end user pays (`manual`, `stripe`, `square`, `gocardless`), in place of `paymentDefault`.

tax.description: The Xero tax rate for GST lines (`taxed`), GST-free lines (`free`) and lines with no GST (`none`).

pushPayments.description: Whether payments you record are sent to Xero too.

choices.description: What your chart of accounts offers for each kind of mapping today.

problems.description: What still stops a push. Empty when ready.

EndUserXeroContact.description: The Xero contact an end user's documents go to.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

contactId.description: The Xero contact's ID, or `null` when none is linked.

TrunkCredential.description: A trunk's SIP digest credential, with its password in plain text. Store the password securely: the answers that carry it are not cached.

username.description: The SIP digest username, which also addresses the trunk on `/trunks/{username}`.

TrunkSourceRestrictions.description: Where a trunk's SIP credentials may be used from. A call that authenticates with the credentials from anywhere else is refused, so a stolen password is no use elsewhere. Both lists empty means no restriction. The trunk's IP list (`/trunks/{username}/ips`) is separate: it lets calls in without registering.

cidrs.description: Public source addresses or CIDR ranges, IPv4 no wider than `/24` and IPv6 single hosts (`/128`). A bare address is stored as `/32` or `/128`.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, upper case. The United Kingdom is `GB`, not `UK`.

NumberBulkJob.description: One bulk number change and what happened to each number.

status.description: `done` once every number has its result. A release is then queued, and the number reads `releasing` until it is gone. `running` while the call is still working through the numbers; a job left `running` stopped part way (the call timed out), and `results` are the numbers it reached.

done.description: How many numbers were changed (a release asked for).

skipped.description: How many were left alone, each with its reason.

failed.description: How many could not be changed just now; try those again.

results.description: One per number, in the order sent.

reason.description: Why it was skipped or failed; null when done.
reason.example: This Number Is Suspended By Check Networks; Contact Support To Lift It

NumberOffer.description: A number, or the start of a block, you can order now, with its price per number. The price is the monthly price at the tier your holding of this type reaches with these numbers, as your invoice will charge it.

number.description: The number, or the first number of the block, as E.164 digits with no `+`.

lastNumber.description: The last number of the block; the same as `number` for a single number.

source.description: `stock`: a number we hold. Hold a single one with `POST /numbers/holds` and order it with the `holdId`; order a block by its type, area and size, which takes this block. `supplier`: a number our supplier offers where we hold none; order it with `offerId`. Nothing is reserved with the supplier until you order.

offerId.description: For a `supplier` number, the reference to order it by; null for `stock`.

monthlyPriceExGst.description: The monthly price per number without GST, in dollars. Null when no price applies.

setupPriceExGst.description: The one-off setup fee per number without GST, in dollars. Null when none applies.

NumberLookupResult.description: What the number register says about one Australian number, as the portal's Number Lookup shows it.

number.description: The number as it is dialled in Australia.

assignedCarrier.description: The carrier the number's block was assigned to.

currentCarrier.description: The carrier that serves the number now. It differs from `assignedCarrier` when the number has ported.

portedActionIndicator.description: The register's ported action indicator. A blank is a real state; null means the register has no entry.

alreadyPorting.description: Whether a port of the number is in progress. Null when the register could not say; `reason` says why (for a mobile, it is not an Australian fixed line).

heldByUs.description: True when the number is already on our books.

portable.description: A hint only, from `alreadyPorting` and `heldByUs`: false when we hold the number or a port is already in progress, true when neither, null when the register could not say. It is not a check that a port will be accepted.

reason.description: The register's own explanation, when it gave one.

asAt.description: How current the answer is, the register file's date or the time it was asked.

PortState.description:
A number port's real state: the step it is at, not a summary. The same id
is a port's `state` on `GET /ports` and its `step.id` on the port webhooks.
Each state waits on one party (`waitingOn`):

| State | Track | `waitingOn` |
|---|---|---|
| `awaiting_authority` | fixed line, 13/1300/1800, sent to the holder | `wholesaler`: the number's holder confirms the Porting Authority by the emailed link; resend it if they need a new one. Cancelled after 14 days without |
| `requested` | every port-in | `us`: we check the request and send it to the losing carrier |
| `submitted` | fixed line, 13/1300/1800 | `losingCarrier`: with the losing carrier for approval |
| `confirmed` | fixed line, 13/1300/1800 | `us`: approved; we book the cutover |
| `scheduled` | fixed line, 13/1300/1800 | `losingCarrier`: the cutover is booked; the number moves on the day |
| `ppv_sent` | mobile | `wholesaler`: enter the verification code the number's holder was sent |
| `ppv_validated` | mobile | `us`: we lodge it with the carrier |
| `submitted_upstream` | mobile | `losingCarrier`: lodged; waiting for the number to move |
| `port_out_requested` | port-out | `us`: our team reviews the gaining carrier's request |
| `port_out_approved` | port-out | `gainingCarrier`: approved; waiting for the gaining carrier to take the number |
| `activated` | port-in, finished | null: the number is live on our network |
| `ported_away` | port-out, finished | null: the number has left |
| `rejected` | finished | null: refused; `statusReason` says why |
| `cancelled` | finished | null: withdrawn or cancelled; `statusReason` says why |

PortWaitingOn.description: Who the port is waiting on now, so you can tell whether to act or wait: `wholesaler` (you: a verification code to enter), `us` (Check Networks works the next step), `losingCarrier` (the carrier the numbers are leaving, on a port-in) or `gainingCarrier` (the carrier taking the number, on a port-out). Null once the port has finished. See `PortState` for the party each state waits on.

PortOrder.description: A number port, in or out, as the portal's port page shows it: its state, who it is waiting on, its history step by step, the cutover and why it stopped. Named by `reference`. Times are ISO 8601 with an offset; dates are on your account's calendar.

reference.description: The port's reference, as `GET /ports/{reference}` takes it.

direction.description: `in` brings the numbers onto your account; `out` is a number leaving you for another carrier, which our team works with the gaining carrier.

portType.description: The kind of port-in: `CatA` one fixed-line number, `CatC` a list or range of fixed-line numbers, `Mob` a mobile number, `Inbound` a 13, 1300 or 1800 number. Null on a port-out.

numbers.description: The numbers on the port in E.164 digits. A CAT C range keeps its wildcard tail: `#` is 10 numbers, `##` is 100.

stateName.description: The state's name, as the portal shows it.

group.description: The portal's tab for the port: `active` (in flight), `completed` (`activated` or `ported_away`) or `rejected` (`rejected` or `cancelled`).

nextStep.description: The next step in plain words. Null once the port has finished.
nextStep.example: Enter the verification code the number's holder was sent.

attention.description: Why the port needs a person to look at it, or null: a cutover date passed without the number moving, a verification code that lapsed, or a step that has taken longer than it should.
