stateEnteredAt.description: When the port entered its current state; null once finished.

preferredCutoverOn.description: The cutover date you asked for, if any. The carriers set the real one.

scheduledFor.description: The booked cutover, once the carriers have set it; on a port-out, the agreed date.

completedAt.description: When the number went live on our network, or left it on a port-out.

statusReason.description: Why the port was rejected, withdrawn or cancelled, in plain words. Null otherwise.
statusReason.example: The account number does not match the losing carrier's records.

portOutResponseCode.description: On a port-out, the industry response code we gave the gaining carrier: `000` approved, otherwise the reason it was refused. Null on a port-in.

losingProvider.description: The provider the numbers are leaving, on a port-in.

carrierReference.description: The losing carrier's reference for the port, once it has one.

endUserName.description: The legal holder of the numbers, as given on the request.

endUser.description: The end user of the trunk the numbers land on, by its number; null for your own trunk.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk the numbers land on.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the numbers are listed at once live.

contact.description: Who we email about a port-in. Null on a port-out.

type.description: `sp` the service provider, `cr` the customer's representative.

verificationCode.description: A mobile port's verification code. Null on every other port. A code lasts 30 minutes; a fresh one can be sent with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code`. Five wrong codes per port, counted across every code sent, reject the port.

sentAt.description: When the latest code was sent; null if none has gone yet.

expiresAt.description: When the latest code lapses, while the port waits for it.

expired.description: True when the code lapsed before it was entered.

attemptsRemaining.description: Wrong codes the port can still take.

history.description: What has happened to the port, oldest first, as the portal's port page lists it.

PortInRequest.description: A port-in request, as the portal's port request form takes it.

numbers.description: The numbers to port, in E.164 or national form. One, except on `CatC`.

trunk.description: The `sipUsername` of the trunk the numbers land on.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the numbers are listed at.

endUserName.description: The legal holder of the numbers with the losing provider.

contactName.description: Who we email about the port.

contactType.description: `sp` the service provider, `cr` the customer's representative.

preferredCutoverOn.description: A cutover date you would like, after today on your account's time zone (or the one you sent in `CN-Time-Zone`). The carriers set the real one.

accountNumber.description: Mobile postpaid only, and required there.

dateOfBirth.description: Mobile prepaid only, and required there.

authorityHolder.description: Send the port to the number's holder to give the Porting Authority, instead of giving it in `consents`. Any port but `Mob`. The port is saved in `awaiting_authority` and the holder emailed a link on your end-user portal.

CdrExport.description: One scheduled call record export to our SFTP server.

description.description: When the export runs and what it covers.

id.description: The recording's public id; fetch it with `GET /voice/recordings/{id}`.

trunk.description: The sipUsername of the trunk the call was on.

trigger.description: What started the recording, such as the trunk's always-on setting or an on-demand request.

retentionExpiresAt.description: When the recording is deleted under the retention period.

SmsMessage.description: One SMS sent from or received on your account.

id.description: The message's id, as `POST /sms` returned it in `messageId`.

from.description: The sender, a number in E.164 format or a sender ID.

to.description: The recipient number in E.164 format.

message.description: The message body. Blank once the text is no longer held (90 days, or 7 days after delivery).

status.description: `delivered` and `failed` are final. `pending` means the message may still move: queued, awaiting a delivery receipt, or held for review; `statusReason` says which.

statusReason.description: Present only where the status alone is ambiguous.

SmsSender.description: A sender your account has asked for or holds: a number you control, or a sender ID (3 to 11 letters and digits). Numbers you hold with us are approved automatically; anything else is checked by our team first.

status.description: `pending` until our team decides it; only an `approved` sender can be used with `POST /sms`. `revoked` is a sender that left your account; `withdrawn` is a request you took back.

endUser.description: The end user the sender belongs to, by its public number. Null when it is your own.

FaxDocument.description: One fax sent or received on your numbers, as Fax History in the portal shows it. Metadata only: never the document or a link to it.

id.description: The fax's id, as the `fax.*` webhook events carry it in `faxId`.

number.description: Your number the fax was received on or sent from.

remoteNumber.description: The other party's number; null when it was withheld.

pages.description: Pages received or sent. 0 until a sent fax has gone through.

status.description: Received: `received`, then `emailed` (sent on by email), `delivered` (kept for the portal) or `failed`. Sent: `pending` (queued), `rendering`, `dialing` and `sending`, then `sent` or `failed`. A busy line or no answer is retried, so a fax can go back to `pending` before it fails for good.

failureReason.description: Why it failed; null unless `status` is `failed`.
failureReason.example: The destination fax number is busy.

endUser.description: The end user's account number when the fax is theirs; null when it is yours.

createdAt.description: When the fax was received, or queued to send.

completedAt.description: When it finished arriving, or finished sending; null until then.

FaxSettings.description: Your fax domain and cover page, as Fax Settings in the portal.

domain.description: Your own fax domain: end users email faxes to `<number>@` it, and received faxes and send results are emailed from it. Null for the platform's domain.

enabled.description: Whether a cover page goes ahead of each fax sent. It is a page sent, and billed as one.

company.description: The company name on the cover page.

footer.description: The line at the foot of the cover page.

FaxDomainCheck.description: A fax domain checked both ways. Nothing is stored.

inbound.description: Whether mail to `<number>@` the domain reaches us, from its public MX records. `ok`: delivered to us directly. `forwarding`: it points elsewhere, which works if that mail is forwarded to us; send a test fax by email to be sure. `fail`: no MX record. `error`: the lookup failed.

outbound.description: Whether mail from the domain is accepted. It cannot be read from here, so it is always `unknown`: ask us to confirm it.

AllowedCountries.description: Your account's list of countries its trunks may call.

allowedCountries.description: ISO 3166 alpha-2 codes, sorted. Every country until you set a list.

availableCountries.description: Every country a list can name, by name. Australia and New Zealand are not among them: calls to either are never international, and New Zealand's follow each trunk's `NZMobile` and `NZNational` permissions.

name.description: A friendly name for the line.

username.description: The line's SIP username, which its phone registers with. This is the line's identifier: every `/residential-lines/{username}` endpoint addresses it by this value, and call records and numbers name it in their `trunk` field with `trunkType: residentialLine`.

sipDomain.description: The SIP domain the line's phone registers to.

plan.description: The line's plan. `payg` meters calls; `ultimate` includes Australian calls to landlines and mobiles in a higher monthly price.

status.description: The line's status. A suspended line makes and receives no calls, except 000 and an emergency callback within the hour.

endUser.description: The end user this line is for, by its public number; null for a line that is your own.

numbers.description: The line's live numbers, E.164 digits without the `+`.

awaitingNumber.description: True while the line has no live number. It bills from the day it is ordered but cannot make or receive calls until its number is ordered, as the portal's Residential Lines list shows with Awaiting Number.

defaultCallerId.description: The number the line presents on outbound calls. It is set to the line's own number when that number lands on the line; null until then.

ResidentialLineSettings.description: A residential line's call settings: the same settings its end user can change from the phone with star codes (*72 and *73 forwarding, *78 and *79 Do Not Disturb).

forwarding.description: Forward every call to another number.

destination.description: The number calls are forwarded to, 6 to 15 digits. Required to turn forwarding on; null while forwarding is off. Never 000, 112 or 106, in any form (`0061000`, `1831112`): that is a `422`, "Calls can’t be diverted to an emergency number (000, 112 or 106)."

doNotDisturb.description: Send every incoming call straight to voicemail.

anonymousReject.description: Refuse incoming calls that withhold their number.

callWaiting.description: Let a second call through while the line is on a call.

callingPermissions.description: The kinds of number the line may call. Shown for reference; set by us, not changeable here.

ResidentialLineVoicemail.description: A residential line's mailbox. The PIN is the end user's own, set in the end-user portal or by phone, and is never read or set here.

enabled.description: Whether unanswered calls go to the mailbox.

email.description: Where each new message is emailed; null for none.

attachAudio.description: Attach the recording to the email. A line with no mailbox yet reads true, the value a new mailbox gets when it is turned on.

deleteAfterEmail.description: Delete the message once it is emailed. Only takes effect with an `email` set; without one it reads false.

number.description: The number asked for, E.164 digits without the `+`.

reason.description: Why you want to present the number, as you sent it.

status.description: `pending` until we decide it. `approved`: the number can be set as a trunk's default caller ID. `rejected`: it cannot; `decisionNote` says why. `cancelled`: you withdrew it.

decidedAt.description: When it was approved, rejected or cancelled; null while pending.

decisionNote.description: Why a rejected request was refused; null otherwise.

evidence.description: The proof sent with the request. The file itself is never returned. Both fields are null on a request made before 21 November 2026.

name.description: The file's name as it was sent.

DataSqBatch.description: A batch of premises qualified as one job (#4848): the API's form of the portal's Batch Qualification page, which lists the same batches.

href.description: URL of this batch.

reference.description: Your name for the batch, as you sent it. A batch uploaded in the portal carries its file name.

status.description: `completed` once every row has its result. Rows are qualified one by one on our side, usually within minutes; poll this batch to follow it.

total.description: Rows in the batch.

done.description: Rows with a result, whatever it is.

unresolved.description: Rows whose address did not resolve to one location.

failed.description: Rows the carrier could not qualify after retries. Not a verdict on the premises: qualify it on its own with `GET /data/sq/{locId}`.

DataSqBatchRow.description: One row of a qualification batch and its result.

rowNumber.description: The row's place in the list you sent, from 1. For a batch uploaded in the portal, its line in the file.

reference.description: Your reference for the row, as you sent it.

input.description: The location id or address you sent.

status.description: `unresolved` is an address that did not resolve to one location; `failed` is a qualification the carrier could not answer after retries, not a verdict on the premises.

resolvedAddress.description: The address the row resolved to.

detail.description: The result in words, as the portal shows it, such as `FTTP · class 3 · port available`.

qualification.description: Once the row resolved to a location, its qualification summary in the field names of `GET /data/sq/{locId}`. Follow `href` for the full qualification. Null until then, and for an unresolved row.

href.description: URL of this location's full qualification.

id.description: The site's code, as `GET /colocation/sites` lists it.

ColocationSellUnit.description: The tier: a full rack, a half rack, or 1, 2, 4 or 10 rack units. Full and half racks are priced by quote.

ColocationService.description: One of your colocation services, rack space at one of our sites.

serviceNumber.description: The service's number, as the portal and your invoices show it.

position.description: The rack units the service holds, bottom up, as the portal shows them.

powerAmps.description: The power included with the service, in amps.

ColocationOrder.description: A colocation order. We assign the rack and rack units, and the service then appears on `GET /colocation/services`.

OccupancyDocument.description: A proof of occupancy you uploaded: what was sent, and the order that used it. The file itself is kept privately with us and never served back.

name.description: The file's name, as it was sent.

used.description: Whether an order has used it. Each document is used once.

orderId.description: The order that used it, or null.

Bundle.description: A bundle: data orders, numbers and a voice trunk ordered together, in sequence, as the portal's Bundles page.

reference.description: The bundle's reference, as the portal shows it.

status.description: `draft` until something in it has been sent, `inProgress` while its items run, then `completed` or `cancelled`.

submitted.description: Whether it has been submitted. A submitted bundle takes nothing more and is not rearranged; the items that wait are released as the items before them complete.

blockedReason.description: Why the bundle could not move on at its last attempt, or null.

endUser.description: The end user the bundle is for, by its public number, or null.

VpnGroup.description: A VPN access group. Its users may reach what it allows.

accessMode.description: `split`: only `destinations` go through the tunnel. `full`: all the user's internet traffic does.

destinations.description: For a `split` group, the networks its users reach through the tunnel, as CIDRs; a bare address is a /32. Empty for a `full` group.

dedicatedEgressIp.description: The group's own public address on the internet, when we have given it one (billed monthly). Ask support for one.

userCount.description: The group's users, not counting removed ones.

VpnUser.description: A VPN user, with its own certificate and profile, billed monthly.

cn.description: The certificate's name. It never changes, through a rename or a move.

state.description: `provisioning` until its profile is ready, then `active`. `suspended` while we hold it (for an unpaid account): its profile is not released.

endUser.description: The number of the end user the seat is for, when you resell VPN; null when none.

endUserName.description: That end user's name; null when none.

vpnIp.description: The user's address inside the tunnel, once issued.

profileReady.description: Whether GET /vpn/users/{id}/profile will give a link now.

UsageAlertMetric.description: What a usage alert watches. `callSpendToday`: call charges today, without GST. `callSpendMonth`: call charges this month, without GST. `minutesMonth`: minutes of answered calls this month. `smsMonth`: messages sent this month. Days and months run on the Brisbane calendar our bill runs on. Only the call metrics can be limited to one trunk.

UsageAlertRecipient.description: One person a usage alert goes to, by email or by SMS. Each alert has its own list.

mobile.description: An Australian mobile, as stored (E.164 digits without the `+`).

UsageAlert.description: A usage alert: when the metric reaches the threshold, we email and text the alert's own recipients once for that day or month, and send a `usageAlert.triggered` webhook event.

trunk.description: The SIP trunk the alert watches, by its `sipUsername`; `null` watches the whole account. Only the call metrics take a trunk.

threshold.description: Dollars without GST for a spend metric (`"50.00"`), otherwise a whole number of minutes or messages (`"1000"`).

currency.description: The threshold's currency for a spend metric; `null` otherwise.

channels.description: How the alert's recipients are told. Empty sends only the webhook event.

recipients.description: Who this alert goes to, oldest first: up to 10 addresses and 10 mobiles. Only these people are told; there is no fallback to your billing contact or your credit alert recipients, so an alert with none sends only the webhook event.

lastFiredAt.description: When the alert last went off; `null` if it never has.

lastFiredPeriod.description: The day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or month (`YYYY-MM`) it last went off for.

UsageAlertRecipientInput.description: One recipient: send `email` or `mobile`, not both. A mobile may be written in any usual form (`0491 570 006`, `+61491570006`); one that is not an Australian mobile answers `422`.

AuditLogEntry.description:
One entry in your account's audit trail: something one of your portal
users, one of your API keys or our support staff did on your account. The
same entries your portal's Audit Log page shows. Entries are never changed
or removed.

action.description: What was done, as a key. New keys are added as the platform grows.

actionLabel.description: The action in words, as the portal shows it. The wording can change.

type.description: `user` is one of your portal users, `apiKey` one of your API keys, and `support` our support staff acting on your behalf (signed in as one of your users). The staff member is never named.

id.description: For a `user`, their id as `GET /account/users` names it; for an `apiKey`, the key's id (its `client_id`). `null` for `support`.

name.description: The user's name, the key's name as it is now, or `Support`.

email.description: A user's email address; `null` for any other actor.

target.description: What it was done to, when the entry names one. `ref` is its public id where it has one (an end user's number, a trunk's or user's id, an invoice's id, a ticket's reference), else `null`.

ip.description: The address the action came from. `null` when our support staff did it, and when none was recorded.

changes.description: What changed, by field: each value has the `from` and `to` as text, `—` where a value was not set. Empty when the entry records no change.

context.description: Further detail, by label, as text. Internal identifiers are never included. Empty when there is none.

ApiCall.description:
One call one of your API keys made: a summary, kept for 30 days. It never
holds the request or response body, the query string or any header.

id.description: The call's `CN-Message-Id`. Quote it to Support to find the call.

keyId.description: The key that made it, its `client_id`.

keyName.description: The key's name as it is now; `null` once the key is gone.

route.description: The endpoint, as a pattern (`/v2/tickets/{ticketRef}`), so calls to the same endpoint group together. `null` for a path no endpoint matched.

path.description: The path called, without the query string.

status.description: The HTTP status we answered.

durationMs.description: How long we took to answer, in milliseconds.

ip.description: The address the call came from.

createdAt.description: When the call was made, in UTC.

apiVersion.description: The API version the event's `data` follows: `2`, as the `/v2` paths. Fields are only ever added to an event within a version, so ignore ones you do not know.

livemode.description: `false` when the event comes from the sandbox, so you can send both to one endpoint and tell them apart.

test.description: `true` for a delivery you asked for with `POST /webhooks/{webhookId}/test`: a ping, or a sample event whose `data` describes nothing real. Do not act on it.

accountId.description: The account the event belongs to, as `clientNumber` on `GET /account`.

resourceUrl.description: Where to read the current state of what the event is about. Events can arrive late or out of order, so re-read it rather than trusting the event alone. Null when there is no single resource to read, and on a test.

WebhookFeedEvent.description:
One event from the feed (`GET /events`): the body a delivery of it
carries, with the same `eventId`, so a handler that de-duplicates on
`eventId` treats a feed event and a delivery of it as one. `sequence` is
`null`: each endpoint numbers its own deliveries. Kept for 30 days, and
only when one of your endpoints subscribed to it.

eventId.description: The event's id, as every delivery of it carries.

eventType.description: The event type, as `GET /webhooks/event-types` lists them.

occurredAt.description: When the event happened, in UTC.

sequence.description: Always `null` in the feed; a delivery carries its endpoint's sequence.

data.description: The event's `data`, as the event's own schema under `webhooks` describes it.

StepDelegation.description: One step of a port or a data order handed to a named person by a one-use emailed link. The link and the email code are never returned: only the person they were sent to can use them.

action.description: The one step the link allows. `confirmPort`: the mobile number's holder enters the verification code texted to it, on a mobile port-in waiting for it (`ppv_sent`). `pickAppointment`: someone at the site picks the install time, on a data order with no appointment yet. `confirmAuthority`: the fixed-line number's holder confirms the Porting Authority with their name and position, on a port waiting for it (`awaiting_authority`).

portReference.description: The port, for `confirmPort` and `confirmAuthority`; null otherwise.

orderId.description: The data order, for `pickAppointment`; null otherwise.

name.description: The person's name, as you gave it.

email.description: Where the link and the code went.

status.description: `sent`: the link works. `used`: the person did the step; the link works no more. `cancelled`: you cancelled it. `expired`: 7 days passed unused; resend it for a new link.

type.description: A portal user or an API key handed it over.

name.description: The user's or the key's name.

sentAt.description: When the current link was sent (the last resend).

expiresAt.description: When the current link stops working, 7 days after it was sent.

resendCount.description: How many times the link was sent again.

codePassedAt.description: When the person last passed the email code on the current link.

ApiKey.description: The calling API key: its own details, never a secret and never another key. A key belongs to your account, not to the user who made it.

clientId.description: The key's client id, the one you send to `POST /oauth/token`.

scopes.description: The scopes the key may ask for.

ipAllowlist.description: The addresses and CIDR blocks the key may be used from. Empty is anywhere.

expiresAt.description: When the key stops working, in UTC; `null` for a key with no end date. An Owner or Admin sets it in the portal. The account's Owners are emailed 14 days and 1 day before.

previousSecretExpiresAt.description: While a rotation's overlap runs, when the old secret and its tokens stop working, in UTC; otherwise `null`.

NotificationPreferences.description: A staff user's notice choices, as on their Notifications page: for each notice they can receive, the channels it can use and the one they chose. Read only: each user sets their own in the portal.

channels.description: The channels this notice can use.

channel.description: The channel chosen, or `none` for a notice turned off.

AccountInvite.description: An open invitation to a staff login on your account. Accepting it makes the login. Partner invitations are under `/partners/invites`.

role.description: The role the login gets on accepting.

status.description: `expired` once its link no longer works; resend it for a fresh link.

AccountSecurity.description: Your account's security settings, as on Company Settings > Security. Read only: an Owner or Admin changes them in the portal.

requireTwoFactor.description: Whether every staff login must use two-factor to sign in.

signInIpAllowlist.description: The addresses staff may sign in to the portal from. Empty is anywhere. This is the portal's list; each API key has its own.

createdBy.description: The name of the user who added it.

BookedChangeSide.description: One side of a booked change. A disconnect moves `status` (from the service's status now to `Cancelled`); a plan change moves `plan` and `channels`.

status.description: The data service's status, as `GET /data/services` names it; null on a plan change.

plan.description: The trunk's plan; null on a disconnect.

channels.description: The channels billed on the trunk, 0 on `payg`; null on a disconnect.

BookedChange.description: A change booked on your account for a later date: a data service disconnect booked for a later day, or a trunk plan change waiting for the start of the next billing cycle. `from` and `to` say what changes, each with all three fields, null where the kind does not change it.

kind.description: `disconnect`: a data service disconnect booked for a later day. `planChange`: a trunk plan or channel change booked for the next billing cycle.

serviceId.description: The data service's `id`, as `GET /data/services/{ref}` takes it; or the trunk's `sipUsername`, else its `id`.

trunkId.description: The trunk's `id` for a plan change; null for a data service.

effectiveOn.description: The day it takes effect: a disconnect goes to the carrier at the start of that day, Sydney time; a plan change applies on that day, the 1st of a month.

type.description: `user`: one of your portal users. `apiKey`: one of your API keys. `checkNetworks`: our staff, at your request. `system`: booked by the platform itself.

name.description: The user's or the key's name; null for Check Networks and the platform.

ApiExport.description: A background export (`POST /exports`): its state, and once it is `ready` the file's size, its row count and a signed link to download it. The webhook events carry the same fields without the link.

type.description: What it holds.

state.description: `queued` until a worker picks it up, `running` while the file is written, then `ready` or `failed`.

filters.description: The list filters it was started with.

rowCount.description: The rows in the file, once it is ready.

sizeBytes.description: The file's size in bytes, once it is ready.

failureReason.description: Why it failed, in words to act on. Null unless `failed`.

expiresAt.description: When the file is removed, 7 days after it was ready.

downloadUrl.description: While it is ready and kept, a signed link to the file, good for one hour and needing no token. Each read gives a new one; an expired link answers `403`. Only on the API's reads, not in webhook events.

PartnerProductRef.description: A product on your retail price book.

Partner.description: A partner: a login that sees only the end users, products and permissions you give it.

id.description: The partner's id, as in the commission routes.

endUsers.description: The end users the partner may reach, by end-user number.

products.description: The products the partner may sell.

permissions.description: What else the partner may do for its end users.

PartnerInvite.description: An open invitation to a partner login.

endUsers.description: The end users the partner will reach, by end-user number.

WebhookTicketEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `ticket.*` events. `data` carries the ticket's header (its reference, subject, status, priority, category, times and your own reference) plus the fields of the event. For the whole ticket, as you may act on it now, read `resourceUrl` (`GET /tickets/{ticketRef}`).

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

data.description: Exactly what every ticket event sends, and the event's own fields. What depends on who reads the ticket (`canResolve`, `actions` and the like) is on the ticket read only.

reference.description: The public ticket reference, as `GET /tickets/{ticketRef}` takes it.

status.description: The ticket's status after the event.

lastActivityAt.description: The ticket's last message or change.

messageId.description: `ticket.replied` only — the new message's `id`, as `GET /tickets/{ticketRef}` lists it.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

cgrid.description: The call record's id, as `cgrid` on `GET /voice/cdrs`.

serviceId.description: The trunk's sipUsername, as `GET /trunks` and the trunk events name it. Null for a line with no SIP credential.

tenantHandle.description: Deprecated; use `serviceId`. The trunk or line's internal handle. Removed in the next release.

direction.description: `outbound` — a call your PBX placed to a carrier. `inbound` — a call a carrier delivered to your PBX.

costExGst.description: The rated charge without GST, as a dollar string. The same figure as `costExGst` on the CDR endpoints.

totalCents.description: Deprecated: use `costExGst`. The rated charge in cents without GST, sent for one more release and then removed.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The trunk's sipUsername, as `GET /trunks` and the trunk events name it. Null for a line with no SIP credential.

tenantHandle.description: Deprecated; use `serviceId`. The voice tenancy's internal handle. Removed in the next release.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

cgrid.description: The call the recording belongs to, as `GET /voice/cdrs/{cgrid}` names it.

serviceId.description: The trunk the call was on, by its SIP username: the `sipUsername` `GET /trunks` returns and the `serviceId` the trunk events carry.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`, or its `id` when it has no SIP credential.

trunkId.description: The trunk's `id`, which every trunk has.

lastSeenAt.description: When the trunk was last registered or sending OPTIONS. On `trunk.down` that is when it went quiet.

WebhookCallerIdEvent.description: A caller ID authorisation request approved or rejected.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

id.description: The request's public id, as `GET /caller-id-authorisations/{id}` takes it.

callerId.description: The number asked for, E.164 digits without the `+`.

status.description: `approved`: the number can now be set as a trunk's default caller ID. `rejected`: it cannot; `reason` says why.

reason.description: `rejected` only — why the request was refused.

WebhookVoiceHoldEvent.description: The delivery for `voice.hold.placed` and `voice.hold.released`. A hold never stops a 000 call.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

holdType.description: `spendVelocity` and `callingPattern` pause the account's new outbound calls until we release the hold. `internationalCap` refuses one trunk's international calls until we release it. `dailySpendCap` refuses one trunk's outbound calls, all but 000 and 1800, until midnight Brisbane time or until you release it or raise the cap.

serviceType.description: `voice` for a trunk's hold; null for an account hold.

serviceId.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`; null for an account hold.

unit.description: What `threshold` and `measured` count: international minutes, or dollars ex GST. Null, with both figures null, for an account hold.

threshold.description: The cap the hold tripped at, as a string in `unit`.

measured.description: What the trunk had used when the hold tripped, in `unit`.

windowSeconds.description: The rolling window the figure was measured over; null for a daily cap, measured since midnight Brisbane time.

releasesAt.description: When a `dailySpendCap` hold lifts by itself; null for the others, which we release.

releaseReason.description: On `voice.hold.released`: `released` by us or by you, `cap_raised` when you raised the daily cap above today's spend, `midnight` when a daily cap hold lifted by itself.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

number.description: The number, E.164 without `+`, as `GET /numbers/{number}` takes it.

serviceId.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`: the trunk it was assigned to on `number.assigned`, the one it was on for the others. Null when the number was on no trunk.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

emergencyAddressId.description: The emergency address the refused record was built from.

status.description: `rejected`: the IPND refused this number's record. `fileRejected`: it refused the whole file the record was in, so the record is not at fault and Check Networks sends it again. As on the number's `ipnd`.

errors.description: The IPND's codes, each explained, as on the number's `ipnd.errors`.

fixInAddress.description: True when fixing the emergency address clears it.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The trunk's `sipUsername`, or its `id` when it has no SIP credential.

previousType.description: The plan the trunk was on when the change was booked.

previousChannels.description: The channels billed before the change; 0 on `payg`.

type.description: The plan the change moves the trunk to.

channels.description: The channels billed after the change; 0 on `payg`.

effectiveOn.description: When the change takes effect: the start of the next billing cycle for a booked change, today for an upgrade that applied at once.

WebhookBookedChangeEvent.description: The delivery for `bookedChange.applied` and `bookedChange.cancelled`: a change booked on your account for a later date took effect on its date, or will no longer happen. `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` listed; `resourceUrl` is the data service or trunk it changes.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

WebhookBookedChangeFailedEvent.description: The delivery for `bookedChange.failed`: a change booked on your account for a later date reached its date but could not be made. `data` is the entry `GET /account/booked-changes` listed, plus the `reason`; `resourceUrl` is the data service or trunk it was to change.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

reason.description: Why the change was not made. For a disconnect, the carrier's reason for refusing it, as the order shows it. For a plan change, a plain reason; contact us with the change's `id` for the detail.
reason.example: The plan change could not be applied to the trunk. Contact us with the change's id.

WebhookExportEvent.description: The delivery for `export.ready` and `export.failed`: a background export (`POST /exports`) has its file, or could not be written. `data` is the export as `GET /exports/{exportId}` shows it, without the download link; `resourceUrl` is that read, which hands out a fresh link.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

WebhookInvoiceEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `invoice.*` events. The event type — not a field — carries which one it is; `occurredAt` is when it happened.

`invoice.issued` when an invoice is finalised, `invoice.paid` when it is settled in full, `invoice.voided` when it is cancelled and its charges unwound. A voided invoice is no longer owed — clear it from your receivables rather than carrying it as an open debt. Voiding is idempotent, so the event is emitted once however many times a void is attempted.

Platform (wholesale) invoices only: your own retail billing is your ledger and never emits here.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

totalExGst.description: The invoice's own charges without GST, as a dollar string. The same figure as `totalExGst` on `GET /account/invoices`.

totalGst.description: The GST on those charges, as the invoice states it.

totalCents.description: Deprecated: use `totalIncGst`. The invoice total in cents (inc. GST), sent for one more release and then removed.

voidedAt.description: When the invoice was cancelled. Present on `invoice.voided` only.

WebhookPaymentEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `payment.succeeded`, `payment.failed` and `payment.reversed`. Every one carries the same keys, whether the money came from a charge against an invoice (`source: charge`) or a credit top-up (`source: topup`, with `paymentId`, `invoiceId` and `invoiceNumber` null). `failureCode` / `failureMessage` are set on `payment.failed` and `payment.reversed` only.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

paymentId.description: The payment's `id`, as `GET /account/payments` lists it. Null until the money is in, so on `payment.failed`, and on a top-up.

invoiceId.description: The `id` of the invoice this payment was applied to, as `GET /account/invoices` gives it. Null for a payment not made against an invoice, so on a top-up.

amount.description: The amount charged, GST-inclusive, as a dollar string. A payment has no GST split of its own: the GST is on the invoices it pays.

amountCents.description: Deprecated: use `amount`. The charged amount in cents, sent for one more release and then removed.

gateway.description: The payment gateway that processed the charge.

source.description: `charge`: a stored method charged against an invoice. `topup`: credit bought for the account, with no invoice behind it.

failureCode.description: `payment.failed` and `payment.reversed` only: the gateway's decline, error or dishonour code.

WebhookCreditNoteEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `creditNote.issued`: a credit note we issued against one of your invoices, whether by our staff or as the outcome of a dispute. The credit is on your account balance from that moment. Credit notes you issue to your own end users never send this; they send `endUser.creditNote.issued`.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

invoiceId.description: The `id` (a ULID) of the invoice the credit note corrects, matching `GET /account/invoices`.

totalExGst.description: The credit without GST, as a dollar string.

reason.description: Why it was issued, as the credit note states it.

WebhookDisputeEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `dispute.raised` and `dispute.decided`: a dispute on one of our invoices to you, raised by you (in the portal or by API) or by our staff for you. While it is open, the disputed amount is not collected or chased. Disputes your end users raise on your bills to them never send these; they send `endUser.dispute.raised` and `endUser.dispute.decided`.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

invoiceId.description: The disputed invoice's `id` (a ULID), matching the /account/invoices endpoints.

invoiceLineId.description: The line disputed, when the dispute names one, by its public id as the invoice's `lineItems[].id`.

amountDisputed.description: The amount disputed, GST-inclusive as it appears on the invoice, as a dollar string. It has no GST split of its own until it is credited.

reason.description: `dispute.raised` only: the reason given.

outcome.description: `dispute.decided` only. `resolved_credited`: a credit note was issued (and `creditNote.issued` sent). `resolved_no_change`: closed with nothing owed either way, such as a withdrawn or duplicate dispute. `rejected`: the charge stands and is collected as normal.

amountCreditedExGst.description: `dispute.decided` only: the credit without GST, or null when nothing was credited.

creditNoteId.description: `dispute.decided` only: the `id` (a ULID) of the credit note issued, when credited.

WebhookInvoiceOverdueEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `invoice.overdue`: one of your invoices past its due date, at the payment reminder we have just sent. One event per overdue invoice the reminder covers, at each of the two reminders (`reminder`, then `warning`), once each per overdue spell. Sent whether or not you receive the overdue emails.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

invoiceId.description: The invoice's `id` (a ULID), matching the /account/invoices endpoints.

amountDue.description: What the reminder asks you to pay on this invoice, GST-inclusive, as a dollar string: the amount due less anything held by an open dispute.

daysOverdue.description: Days past the due date, on the Brisbane calendar.

reminderStage.description: `reminder`: the first overdue notice. `warning`: the later notice that services may be suspended.

WebhookPaymentMethodEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `paymentMethod.expiring`: a card you pay us with expires soon, so add a new one before it does. Sent once for each expiry date, alongside the email. Your end users' cards never send this.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

paymentMethodId.description: The card's public id, as `GET /account/payment-methods` returns it.

label.description: The card as the portal shows it.

expiryMonth.description: The last month the card can be charged, as `YYYY-MM`.

isDefault.description: Whether it is the card we charge by default.

WebhookPriceRiseEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `priceRise.noticed`: notice that the price of a product you hold goes up, sent with the email once per notice. `changes` lists each rise, with the date it takes effect and the services it reaches, so you can reprice your own end users or pass the notice on.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

items.description: One rise. A recurring price carries `oldPrice*` and `newPrice*`; a metered price carries `oldUnitPrice*` and `newUnitPrice*`. The side a product is not priced on is null. Unit prices go to 5 decimal places.

productId.description: The product's public id, as the retail price book returns it.

subscriptionId.description: The product subscription that is billed, by its public id.

serviceId.description: A data service's id or a trunk's `sipUsername`, as the service events name them; null for a subscription not tied to one service.

WebhookCreditEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for `credit.thresholdReached`, `credit.callsBlocked` and `credit.callsRestored`. Credit is checked every minute: credit used is what you owe us plus usage not yet invoiced, and available credit is your credit limit less that. All three figures are without GST, as credit control works them out.

A block stops new outbound calls on your trunks. It never stops a call to 000.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

threshold.description: `credit.thresholdReached` only: the percentage of your credit limit now used, one of the warning levels you set, or 100 when calls are about to be blocked.

creditUsed.description: What you owe plus unbilled usage, without GST, as a dollar string.

availableCredit.description: `creditLimit` less `creditUsed`, without GST. Zero or less blocks new calls; it goes below zero when you are over.

WebhookUsageThresholdEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `usage.thresholdReached`: one of your end users' data services has used 50, 85 or 100% of its monthly allowance. Sent once for each of those levels in a month, whether or not the end user could be told (one with no contact details still sends it), while usage notices are on for your account.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The data service's id, as the service events name it.

endUser.description: The end user's number.

usedBytes.description: Data used this month when it was crossed.

billingMonth.description: The allowance month, `YYYY-MM`, on your account's calendar.

WebhookUsageAlertEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `usageAlert.triggered`: one of the usage alerts you set passed its threshold. Sent once per period (the day for `callSpendToday`, the month otherwise, on the Brisbane calendar our bill runs on), with the email and SMS the alert chose. An alert is a warning only: nothing is blocked.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

alertId.description: The alert's id, as `GET /account/usage-alerts` lists it.

trunk.description: The trunk's `sipUsername` when the alert is on one trunk; null for the whole account.

threshold.description: The alert's figure: dollars without GST for a spend metric ("50.00"), otherwise a whole number of minutes or messages ("500").

value.description: The period's usage when the alert fired, in the same unit as `threshold`.

currency.description: `AUD` for a spend metric, null otherwise.

period.description: The day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or month (`YYYY-MM`) it fired for.

WebhookRealmEvent.description: The outcome of a PPPoE realm request.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

reason.description: `data.realm.rejected` only — why the realm was not granted.

WebhookRadiusSessionEvent.description: An Opticomm RADIUS user's session, retrieved from Opticomm.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

online.description: Whether Opticomm reported a session up.

session.description: The current session, as *Retrieve the Current Session* gives it; null when nothing is connected.

PortStep.description: A port state as the port webhooks name it.

name.description: The state's name, as the portal shows it.

WebhookOrderEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `order.statusChanged`. `data.from` / `data.to` carry the transition, in the same status words `/data/orders` publishes — an order moving between internal steps that share one published status does not emit, so you get one event per status change rather than one per internal step. A number port (`orderType: numberPort`) is the exception: it emits on every step and on a moved cutover, with the step in `step`.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

from.description: The previous published status, or null when the order had not been published before (a draft order is not visible on `/data/orders`, so its first event has no `from`).

statusReason.description: Why the order failed. Present only when `to` is `Failed`. On a `numberPort`, why it was rejected, withdrawn or cancelled.

portReference.description: On a `numberPort`, the port's own reference, as `GET /ports/{reference}` takes it. Absent on other order types.

step.description: On a `numberPort`, the step the port is now at: its real state, as the port read's `state`. Absent on other order types.

previousStep.description: On a `numberPort`, the step before this event. The same as `step` when the event is a moved cutover (`scheduledFor` changed).

scheduledFor.description: On a `numberPort`, the booked cutover (on a port-out, the agreed date), once there is one.

portOutResponseCode.description: On a port `out`, the industry response code we gave the gaining carrier: `000` approved, otherwise why it was refused.

orderType.description: What kind of order this is. `data` is a carrier connect/disconnect order on `/data/orders`. `numberPort` is a number moving between carriers — see `numbers`, and note that a port OUT reaching `Completed` means the numbers have left you.

direction.description:
Which way a `numberPort` is moving the numbers. `in` brings them onto your account; `out` takes them off it. Present on `numberPort` only.

**Read this together with `to`.** On an `out` port, `Completed` means the numbers have LEFT you — the opposite of what `Completed` means on every other order. Branch on `direction`, not on the fact that something finished.

network.description: The carrier delivering the order. Null on a `numberPort`: a port has a losing carrier and a gaining one, and naming either as "the network" would be wrong half the time. See `losingCarrier` and `gainingCarrier`.

losingCarrier.description: Who the numbers are moving FROM, on a `numberPort`. On a port `in` this is the customer's previous provider; on a port `out` it is us. Null when we hold no name for them.

gainingCarrier.description: Who the numbers are moving TO, on a `numberPort`. On a port `in` this is us. On a port `out` it is **null**: we buy wholesale rather than porting as a carrier, so the receiving carrier reaches us by email and is not recorded — null means we do not know it, not that there isn't one.

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as supplied when the order was placed.

salesReference.description: The same value as `orderReference`, under the name your own reference has on trunks, numbers and services (`externalRef`).

serviceId.description: The service the order produced, once one exists. Null until the carrier has allocated it — expect it to be populated by the time the order reaches `Completed`. Always null on a `numberPort`, which moves an existing number rather than producing a service.

numbers.description: The numbers on a `numberPort`, in E.164. Absent on other order types.

WebhookOrderDelayedEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `order.delayed`: an order held for a later submit time. Sent when the hold starts, when its time changes, and when we hold it for you at its time because it could not be sent (`heldForAction`). Nothing has been sent to the carrier. Once it is sent, `order.statusChanged` follows as for any order; a cancelled held order is announced there under its PND. A booked disconnection never sends this event.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

delayedOrderId.description: The held order's PND, as /data/orders/delayed and /nbn/orders/delayed name it.

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as supplied when the order was placed.

submitDateTime.description: When the order will be sent; null while it is held for you.

heldForAction.description: True when the order was not sent at its time and needs you: fix the cause and submit it now, give it a new time, or cancel it.

heldReason.description: Why the order was not sent, while heldForAction is true.

WebhookOrderAwaitingEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `order.appointmentRequired` and `order.ntdFull`: an order you placed with POST /data/orders is waiting for something only you can give. Nothing has been sent to the carrier. Answer it with PATCH /data/orders/{orderId}; an order still waiting after 7 days is cancelled, with `order.statusChanged`.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

orderId.description: The order's id until the carrier has it: a Check Networks PND. It keeps finding the order on /data/orders/{orderId} afterwards.

locationId.description: The premises the order is for (LOC

orderReference.description: Your own reference, as supplied when the order was placed.

statusReason.description: What the order needs from you.

demandType.description: The appointment type a technician visit for this order needs, as the order's timeslots read uses it.

expiresAt.description: When the order is cancelled if it is still waiting.

WebhookPortActionRequiredEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `port.actionRequired`: a number port has arrived at a step only you can move. Today that is a mobile port-in waiting for the verification code its number's holder was sent. The same step also arrives as `order.statusChanged`.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

portReference.description: The port's reference, as `GET /ports/{reference}` takes it.

orderId.description: The id `order.statusChanged` names the same port by.

action.description: What is needed. `enterVerificationCode`: confirm the code with `POST /ports/{reference}/confirm`. `openPort`: read the port for what it needs.

actionDescription.example: Enter the verification code the number's holder was sent.

expiresAt.description: When the verification code lapses (30 minutes after it was sent). A fresh one can be sent with `POST /ports/{reference}/verification-code`.

WebhookServiceEvent.description: The delivery envelope for the `service.*` lifecycle events. The event type — not a field — carries which thing happened; `data.status` is where the service ended up. `data.serviceType` tells you which surface the service belongs to, and therefore how to read `data.serviceId`.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

serviceType.description: `data` for a data service (NBN, Opticomm), `voice` for a SIP trunk, `transit` for an IP transit circuit, `colocation` for a rack or part-rack with its power.

serviceId.description: How to address the service. For `data`, the service id used by the data endpoints. For `voice`, the trunk's `sipUsername`, or its `id` when it has no SIP credential — never a numeric id. For `transit` and `colocation`, the service's uuid, which is what the portal shows.

trunkId.description: On a `voice` event only: the trunk's `id`, which every trunk has. Absent for other service types.

externalRef.description: On a `data` or `voice` event only, your own reference on the service or trunk.

metadata.description: On a `data` or `voice` event only, your own metadata on the service or trunk.

status.description: Where the service ended up. `data` and `transit` services report `Live`; `voice` trunks and `colocation` services report `Active`; all four use `Suspended` and `Cancelled`.

previousStatus.description: Where it was before, or null when the service had no prior state (a newly provisioned service).

reason.description: Why it changed. `nonPayment` for a suspension or restore under the payment rules; `fraud` or `scam` for a suspension our staff recorded as fraud or a scam, on you or one of your end users, and for its lift; `customerRequest` for a change you asked for (a disconnect you ordered, a trunk you paused, an agreed hardship pause); `carrier` for one the carrier made, such as a cease we did not order; `staff` for an operator hold or other staff action. A fraud cap on a trunk holds its international calls without changing the service, so it sends no `service.*` event. More values may be added: treat one you do not know as `staff`.

source.description: Who made the change: our `staff`, you (the `wholesaler`, in the portal or this API), the `carrier`, or the platform itself (`system`, such as the payment reminder ladder).

WebhookServiceCeaseScheduledEvent.description: The carrier will cease one of your data services on a future date, and you did not ask for it.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

serviceId.description: The service id used by the data endpoints.

ceaseAt.description: When the carrier will cease the service. It stays live, and billed, until then.

carrierReference.description: The carrier's own reference on its notice (an order id, or Opticomm's product instance id), or null when it gave none.

WebhookDiagnosticCompletedEvent.description: A line test on one of your data services finished.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

testId.description: The test's reference, as the diagnostics reads take it (`GET /nbn/diagnostics/{testRef}` or `GET /opticomm/diagnostics/{testRef}`).

serviceId.description: The service id used by the data endpoints.

network.description: Which network's diagnostics endpoints read the test.

testType.description: The test, by the name the diagnostics reads give it.

status.description: How the test ended.

result.description: Whether the test passed, or null when there is no pass or fail: a cancelled or rejected test, an inconclusive one, or a result the carrier has not yet given us. Read the test for its measurements.

reason.description: The carrier's note on the outcome, when it gave one.

WebhookServiceHealthReportReadyEvent.description: A service health report on one of your data services is ready.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

reportId.description: The report's reference (HRI #), as the health reads take it (`GET /nbn/service_health/report/{hrId}` or `GET /opticomm/service_health/{hrId}`).

serviceId.description: The service id used by the data endpoints.

network.description: Which network's health endpoints read the report.

overall.description: The report's overall condition as the carrier gives it, such as `Green`, `Amber` or `Red`; null when it gave none.

readyAt.description: When the report was stored and became readable.

WebhookAppointmentEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `appointment.*` events. The event type — not a field — carries which one it is.

Carrier-neutral: an NBN and an Opticomm appointment arrive in the same shape, with `data.network` naming whose technician it is, so you handle appointments once rather than per carrier.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

appointmentId.description: The carrier's appointment reference, matching the appointment endpoints.

status.description: The appointment's status in the words the appointment endpoints publish, never the carrier's raw string.

previousStatus.description: What it was immediately before this change.

slotStart.description: The appointment window, relayed as the carrier's own ISO-8601 string with its offset intact — the time your end user was told, not a normalised UTC rendering of it.

previousSlotStart.description: The window this appointment used to hold. Present on `appointment.rescheduled` only, so you can find the booking in your own calendar rather than guessing which one moved.

orderId.description: The order the appointment belongs to, in the same reference `/data/orders` publishes. Null for an appointment not yet attached to an order.

locationId.description: The carrier's location identifier for the premises.

WebhookOutageData.description: An unplanned outage in an `outage.*` event: the outage as `GET /outages` publishes it, with `planned` false and `yourAffectedServiceCount` and `yourAffectedServiceTypes` added.

reference.description: The register reference for this outage.

timezone.description: The zone the timestamps above are rendered in.

cause.description: `withheld` where the cause is not disclosable — said explicitly rather than sent as null, so it is not mistaken for missing data.

yourAffectedServiceCount.description: How many of YOUR services fall in the outage's scope — including services attributed to your own retail end-customers, which are yours to relay to. Lets you tell "one site" from "everything you have in that area" without cross-referencing your inventory.

yourAffectedServiceTypes.description: Which service families of yours are affected.

WebhookMaintenanceData.description: Planned maintenance in an `outage.*` event, as the public status page shows it.

impact.description: What customers will notice during the window.

url.description: The maintenance on the public status page.

WebhookOutageEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `outage.*` events. The event type — not a field — carries which one it is.

`data` is the same outage body `GET /outages` returns, plus two fields telling you how much of it is yours. You only receive an outage that affects services on your account, matched the same way the read endpoint matches them, so a push and a poll can never disagree about whether you are affected.

Only reviewed, published register entries are ever sent — an auto-detected outage awaiting staff review is not.

Planned maintenance is sent on the same three events with `data.planned` true and the maintenance body instead: `outage.opened` when we first send you its notice, `outage.updated` when the window or what we tell customers changes or the work starts, and `outage.closed` when it is completed or cancelled. You receive maintenance whose notice we sent to your account.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

eventType.description: `outage.opened` when an entry reaches the register while still running, `outage.updated` when something a customer would be told changes (the estimated restoration time, the affected area, the cause, the notes), `outage.closed` when services are restored. Notification bookkeeping does not emit — you will not get an `outage.updated` every time we send an email about it.

data.description: An outage when `planned` is false, planned maintenance when it is true.

WebhookDegradationData.description: A potential service degradation, as the public status page shows it, plus how many of your data services are at its POIs.

area.description: The affected points of interconnect, e.g. `Sandbox (0SND)`.

impact.description: What customers may notice until the capacity is added.

expectedResolutionAt.description: When we expect the extra capacity to be in place; null until we have a date.

url.description: The degradation on the public status page.

yourAffectedServiceCount.description: Your live data services at the affected POIs.

WebhookDegradationEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `degradation.*` events. The event type — not a field — carries which one it is.

A potential service degradation is not an outage: our interconnect at a POI is busy and the extra capacity is delayed, so data services there may be slower at peak times, but they are not down. You receive one when you have a live data service at one of its POIs.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

eventType.description: `degradation.opened` when we first tell you of it, `degradation.updated` when the expected date or what we tell customers changes, and `degradation.closed` when the capacity has been added.

WebhookQuoteEvent.description:
The delivery envelope for the `quote.*` events. The event type, not a field, carries which one it is.

Each account linked to the quote is sent its own event, carrying its own `externalId` (the reference it gave when it requested the quote), never another account's.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.
Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.
Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

tier.description: The tier this event is for. Each is sent once a month.

WebhookEndUserCreditNoteEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `endUser.creditNote.issued`: a credit note you issued on one of your bills to an end user, by hand, as a service credit or as the outcome of the end user's dispute. It is on the end user's account from that moment. Credit notes we issue to you send `creditNote.issued` instead. Only for an account that bills its end users.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

endUser.description: The end user the credit note is for, by its number.

invoiceId.description: The `id` (a ULID) of the bill the credit note corrects, matching `GET /end-users/invoices/{id}`.

totalExGst.description: The credit without GST, as a dollar string.

reason.description: Why it was issued, as the credit note states it.

WebhookEndUserDisputeEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `endUser.dispute.raised` and `endUser.dispute.decided`: a dispute an end user raised on one of your bills to them, from their portal, and your decision on it (in the portal or by API). While it is open, the disputed amount is not chased. Disputes on our invoices to you send `dispute.raised` and `dispute.decided` instead. Only for an account that bills its end users.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

endUser.description: The end user who raised it, by its number.

invoiceLineId.description: The line disputed, when the dispute names one, by its public id.

amountDisputed.description: The amount disputed, GST-inclusive as it appears on the bill, as a dollar string. It has no GST split of its own until it is credited.

reason.description: `endUser.dispute.raised` only: the reason the end user gave.

outcome.description: `endUser.dispute.decided` only. `resolved_credited`: a credit note was issued to the end user (and `endUser.creditNote.issued` sent). `resolved_no_change`: closed with nothing owed either way. `rejected`: the charge stands and is chased as normal.

amountCreditedExGst.description: `endUser.dispute.decided` only: the credit without GST, or null when nothing was credited.

creditNoteId.description: `endUser.dispute.decided` only: the credit note issued, when credited.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

messageId.description: The message's id: `messageId` from `POST /sms`, and the id `GET /sms/messages/{messageId}` reads.

from.description: The sender, a number in E.164 format or a sender ID.

to.description: The recipient number in E.164 format.

status.description: As `GET /sms/messages/{messageId}` reports it.

statusReason.description: Present where the status alone is ambiguous, else null.

sentAt.description: When the message was sent or received.

at.description: When it arrived, or when the delivery receipt settled it.

failureReason.description: Why it was not delivered. In `sms.failed` only.

WebhookFaxEvent.description: The delivery for `fax.received`, `fax.sent` and `fax.failed`. Metadata only: never the document or a link to it.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — one emit shares one id across all your endpoints, so use it to deduplicate.

faxId.description: The fax's id, as `GET /fax/documents/{id}` reads it.

number.description: Your number the fax was received on or sent from.

remoteNumber.description: The other party's number, when known.

faxPlanId.description: The fax plan a sent fax went out under, or the plan the receiving number is on. Null when there is none.

status.description: `sent` or `failed` for a sent fax. For one received: `delivered` (kept for the portal), `emailed`, or `failed` (it could not be passed on; `failureReason` says why).

at.description: When the fax was received or sent.

WebhookAccountEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `account.suspended` and `account.reinstated`: your own account. While it is suspended, writes through this API answer `403`; webhooks keep coming.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

status.description: Where the account ended up.

reason.description: On `account.suspended`, the reason we gave you by email.

WebhookEndUserEvent.description: The delivery envelope for the `endUser.*` events. Light by design: it names the end user and what changed, not the new values, so read the end user to sync it (`data.full` is always `false`). For an end user under a safety flag, the reference and the names of changed contact fields are withheld, as the portal withholds them, and `data.detailsWithheld` is `true`.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

reference.description: Your own reference for the end user, or null when it has none or it is withheld.

changedFields.description: On `endUser.updated`, the names of the fields that changed, such as `name` or `billingEmail`. The values are not sent.

full.description: Always `false`. The event is a pointer; read the end user for its details.

detailsWithheld.description: `true` when the end user is under a safety flag and contact details are withheld.

WebhookEndpointDisabledEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `webhook.endpointDisabled`: another of your endpoints was turned off after 20 dead deliveries in a row. Sent to your other endpoints that take it, never to the one turned off.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

webhookId.description: The endpoint turned off: its public id, as `GET /webhooks` names it and `GET /webhooks/{webhookId}` takes it.

WebhookDelegationEvent.description: The delivery envelope for `delegation.used`: a person you handed one step to by a one-use link (`POST /ports/{reference}/delegations`, `POST /data/orders/{orderId}/delegations`) passed the email code and did the step. Sent once per link. Read the port or the order for its new state.

eventId.description: Unique per emitted event — use it to deduplicate.

delegationId.description: The delegation's id, as the delegation calls give it.

portReference.description: The port's reference, for `confirmPort` and `confirmAuthority`; null otherwise.

orderId.description: The data order's id, for `pickAppointment`; null otherwise.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists, but doesn't accept this HTTP method.

TooManyRequests.description: Over a rate limit (see Rate Limits): the call's own, its API Client's or its account's. Wait for `Retry-After` seconds.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. On every `429`.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The calls the limit that refused this one allows in its minute.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: The calls left under that limit; `0` here.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: When that limit starts again, as a Unix time.

InternalServerError.description: Something failed on our side. If it persists, contact Support with the `CN-Message-Id`.

ServiceUnavailable.description: We, or the carrier's system, are briefly unavailable. Retry shortly.

Unauthorized.description: The access token is missing, expired or invalid.

Forbidden.description: Your token doesn't carry the scope this endpoint needs.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The request failed validation. `fields` names each input that was wrong.

error.reason: The location id field is required.

fields.reason: The location id field is required.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or had invalid parameters, or the carrier refused it. For a carrier refusal, `code` says which and `carrierCode` holds the carrier's own code.

invalid.summary: Our own check refused the request

error.reason: The provided AVC does not exist

NotFound.description: Nothing by that identifier exists on your account.

Conflict.description: The resource isn't in a state that allows this right now.

error.reason: Satisfaction has already been submitted for this ticket.

BadGateway.description: We couldn't reach the carrier, and the request was not processed. Retry shortly.

DataRadiusRetrieving.description:
Retrieving. The service is on Opticomm's RADIUS, and Opticomm gives its sessions only as a diagnostic result that arrives a minute or two after we ask. A session check is on its way.

Ask again after `Retry-After` seconds; reading never asks Opticomm again. Or subscribe to `data.radius.sessionRetrieved`, which carries the answer when it arrives. If Opticomm never answers, a new `POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check` after five minutes asks again.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking again.

testId.description: On `POST /data/radius/{ref}/session-check` only: the Session History test's reference. Absent when the test was started elsewhere and is not yet known here.

message.example: We are retrieving this session from Opticomm. Check again in a minute or two, or subscribe to the data.radius.sessionRetrieved webhook to be told when it arrives.

NotImplemented.description: This endpoint is Coming Soon and not yet available.

NotInSandbox.description: Answered only by the API sandbox (`api.checknetworks.dev`): this call acts on our live network, which the sandbox never reaches. Production never answers it.

TicketResult.description: The ticket as it now stands.

EndUserResult.description: The end user, as it now stands.

Page.name: page
Page.description: The page to return, from `1`. A value that is not a whole number of at least 1 is refused with `422 - validation_failed` naming `page`, never changed.

PerPage.name: perPage
PerPage.description: Rows per page: a whole number from `1` to `200`, `50` when left out. A value outside that range, or not a whole number, is refused with `422 - validation_failed` naming `perPage`, never reduced or rounded.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The `nextCursor` of the previous page. Walks the list newest first from where that page ended, so a row added meanwhile is neither repeated nor skipped. A cursor page carries `perPage`, `nextCursor` and `results` only; `page` is ignored. A cursor this list did not issue, or one sent with `sort`, is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

Q.name: q
Q.description: Search: rows whose searchable fields contain this text, ignoring case. Each list's description names the fields it searches. At most 100 characters; a longer value is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

UpdatedSince.name: updatedSince
UpdatedSince.description: Only rows changed at or after this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time, such as `2026-11-01` or `2026-11-01T09:00:00Z`. A date alone means the start of that day (UTC). A value that is not ISO 8601 is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

CreatedFrom.name: createdFrom
CreatedFrom.description: Only rows created at or after this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone means the start of that day (UTC). A value that is not ISO 8601 is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

CreatedTo.name: createdTo
CreatedTo.description: Only rows created at or before this time: an ISO 8601 date or date-time. A date alone includes the whole of that day (UTC). A value that is not ISO 8601 is refused with `422 - validation_failed`.

IdempotencyKeyRequired.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyRequired.description: **Required.** A unique value for this operation, such as a UUID, so that retrying it never does the work twice. Without it the request answers `400`. Sending the same key and the same request again returns the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. See Idempotency, above.

IdempotencyKeyOptional.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKeyOptional.description: Optional. A unique value for this operation, such as a UUID, so that retrying it never does the work twice. Sending the same key and the same request again returns the stored response with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. See Idempotency, above.

Tag.name: tag
Tag.description: Only rows carrying this tag, matched whole, ignoring case. Repeat it (`tag=Site%2012&tag=Brisbane`, or `tag[]=`) and a row must carry every one. A tag may hold a comma, so values are never split. A blank tag, or one over 255 characters, is `422`.

ExternalRef.name: externalRef
ExternalRef.description: Only the object holding this `externalRef`, matched exactly (case counts). Up to 64 letters, digits, `_`, `.` or `-`; another value is refused with `422 - validation_failed`. A reference no object holds gives an empty list.

NbnProductType.name: productType
NbnProductType.description: (Optional) Only the products of this traffic class, as each product's own `productType` shows it: `EE` for Enterprise Ethernet, `TC4` for every other product. Any other value is `400`: `TC1` and `TC2`, which no product reports, and a product family, which is filtered with `techType`.

NbnTechType.name: techType
NbnTechType.description: (Optional) Only the products of this product family, as each product's `technology` shows it: `NFAS` (fibre), `NCAS` (copper), `NWAS` (fixed wireless), `NHAS` (HFC), `NSAS` (satellite) or `EEAS` (Enterprise Ethernet). Any other value is `400`.

SmsFrom.name: from
SmsFrom.description: (Optional) Only messages sent on or after this time (ISO 8601). A date alone means the start of that day. An invalid value returns `422`.

SmsTo.name: to
SmsTo.description: (Optional) Only messages sent on or before this time (ISO 8601). A date alone means the end of that day, so the day is included. An invalid value returns `422`.

SmsSearch.name: q
SmsSearch.description: (Optional) Only messages whose sender, recipient or text contains this, as the portal's search does.

SmsStatus.name: status
SmsStatus.description: (Optional) Only messages with this `status`. Any other value returns `422`.

SmsExportFormat.name: format
SmsExportFormat.description: Bulk export format. Omit for paged JSON; `csv` or `ndjson` streams every message the other filters match as one download, newest first, and `page`/`perPage` are ignored. Each row has `id`, `sentAt`, `direction`, `from`, `to`, `message`, `parts`, `status` and `statusReason`. An unrecognised value returns `422`.

EndUserPath.name: endUser
EndUserPath.description: The end user's number. An end user of another account answers 404, as an unknown number does.

PortReferencePath.name: reference
PortReferencePath.description: The port's reference. Another account's port answers 404, as an unknown reference does.

UsageMonth.name: month
UsageMonth.description: The month, as `YYYY-MM`: this month (the default) or one of the eleven before it, on your bill's calendar (your account's time zone). Any other month returns `400`.

DelegationIdPath.name: delegationId
DelegationIdPath.description: The delegation's id, from its create or list. One on another object answers 404.

DataOrderIdPath.name: orderId
DataOrderIdPath.description: The order's id, as GET /data/orders gives it (the carrier's, or the PND while it waits for you). Another account's order answers 404.

ApiVersion.description: The API version that answered. `2` on every response, from `/v2` and the unprefixed paths alike (see Versioning).
